reviews.reasons:
I checked the ledger digest's do-not-repeat and untested lists, the progress log, screen.py and the scr-gate479 launch line. C04 does not repeat anything already tried. It is new in two ways.

(1) Mechanism and node. The registry and launcher checks are new N12 infrastructure. Neither the ledger nor the log has a recipes file, a resolved-flag record, a duplicate-flag rejection or an argparse-default warning. The faults it targets are real:
- scr-gate479's stdout.log passes --turnover-every twice, at positions 35 and 61 (10 from main_args, then 5; argparse keeps the last).
- screen.py builds every screen on lab.json main_args plus hand-stacked flags.
- Section 9 of analysis.md lists the argparse defaults that differ from the adopted recipe as clutter.

(2) A factor that was never varied: whether the resetcap stack is present under the z-gate. Every run with select_z > 0 carried the full stack. The H25 do-not-repeat entries are all stacked variants: scr-gate479, scr-gatevs479, scr-t60gate479 and scr-jsearch479. The H25 and H26 verifiers name this ablation as missing. The H32 verifier asks for scr-gate479 with and without the floor, and here that is one branch of the bisection. H16 (practice) and H40 (turnover) were never isolated under the gate.

Closest overlap: H40's do-not-repeat list includes "joint removal of practice games + wide turnover + protection (scr-draft, #130) without separating the factors". C04 is also a joint removal, but it is different in three ways:
- It runs under the gate (scr-draft was ungated --select c3).
- It starts from 479 (scr-draft started from 460).
- It also drops the floor, group changes and cap, and it commits to a bisection if the result is not null.
That keeps it distinct only if the bisection is binding.

Other checks:
- The arms are matched: same snapshot, --reseed 2, 20 iterations.
- The kill rule is concrete.
- The design respects rule 3 and the self-discovery rules. It adds no priors and only removes knobs.

Weaknesses that do not change the verdict:
- Like 25 of the 27 earlier screens, it forks from a wall state. A null result only shows the knobs are inert at 479, not that they do nothing from scratch, which is where Stage 3 would run.
- 'adopted-bare' is lab.json main_args. That keeps --turnover-every 10 --turnover 0.15 (non-wide), --swaps 6 and --shaping 0.1, so 'bare' still has plain turnover.
required_changes: Make the bisection binding, not optional. If gate-bare differs from scr-gate479 beyond 2x the A/A band, run the planned split before any conclusion is drawn. Otherwise the result is a second unseparated joint removal, which H40's do-not-repeat list rules out (scr-draft, #130).

Define 'adopted-bare' explicitly in the registry as lab.json main_args with no additions. Its turnover is --turnover-every 10 --turnover 0.15, non-wide, so the diff should read 'every 5 to 10, wide+protect off', not 'turnover off'. Record that --swaps 6 and --shaping 0.1 stay in.

Limit the pruning claim to the 479 wall state. A null result supports dropping the knobs at that fork only. Before the knobs are removed from the frozen Stage 3 recipe, there must be at least one fresh-start check, the planned fractional factorial or a single fresh-start bare-vs-stack pair. Running it should not depend on whether two levers interact.

In the bisection, keep the floor in its own branch or as a one-factor follow-up. The H32 verifier names the floor/no-floor ablation under the gate as the cheap decisive test, and it should be answerable from this work and not left confounded with group changes and wide turnover.

reviews.reasons:
The registry part is sound infrastructure and needs no statistical justification. The critic's clutter list (stacked-recipe provenance, argparse defaults that differ from the adopted recipe, the duplicated --turnover-every) supports it directly. The delta-debug experiment as written is only partly diagnostic.

(1) A null cannot separate the rivals. From the 479 wall state, almost every intervention has stayed within the A/A band of its matched control. Finding 1301 says only the gate, 40-turn draws and Monte Carlo value targets ever separated. H-load-bearing names its mechanism as "practice and the varied field keeping the pilot general" (#137). That mechanism is slow and acts on how the pilot forms. A 20-iteration fork from a state the stack itself produced tests whether the flags keep the state, not whether they shape it. So H-load-bearing also predicts "within A/A" at this horizon. The design's claim that "a null is strong evidence for pruning" for the Stage 3 recipe overreaches. A null licenses only "inert at the 479 gated state over 20 iterations". Stage 3 runs from scratch, and the fresh-start leg is currently conditional only on an interaction being found.

(2) The noise bands are not calibrated to the gated regime. The distance A/A RMS (2.6) comes from ungated forks. The 15-deck type band comes from ungated A/A type sizes (33/19, 48/44, 74/72). Under the gate the largest type ran 12-26, so a doubling would fall inside the band. No gated A/A exists for type size or wall-core decks: gatevs479 at 36 vs gate479 at 23 was read as "within A/A" with no measured gated noise. scr-gate479 also ran on older code, and t60gate479 shows that earlier "controls" were not concurrent matched controls. One run against one historical run, on code that has changed, cannot place a difference against noise.

(3) Multiple readouts. Load-bearing is declared on "a difference beyond 2x the A/A band on any of" four to six readouts: distance, type, wall-core decks, moves, acc-prop and the walls verdict. That inflates the false-positive rate for H-load-bearing. Results between 1x and 2x the band are not assigned to either rival.

(4) The readout does not match the node. Practice (H16) and the varied field are pilot-node levers. The only pilot readout is the final-pilot walls verdict, and it has no predicted direction or band. There is no pilot competence check against a fixed panel (bar 0.06).

(5) The kill rule is uncalibrated. "More than 20 wall-core decks above gate479 at 490" has no noise reference: gate479's Chansey+Snorlax decks went 54->73, and ungated runs reached 78-85. Killing at 490 also throws away the 490-499 window that the primary distance readout needs.

(6) The resolved diff may confound the comparison. screen.py builds gate479 on the lab's pre-#127 main_args. "adopted-bare" may therefore also differ in swaps, draft margin, lr, draft-lr, epochs or shaping, not only in the seven stacked flags. If so, a difference cannot be pinned on the stack.

Fixing (2) costs nothing extra in slots: the machine runs 3 screens at once, and this needs only 3 concurrent runs.
required_changes: Run a concurrent, current-code replicate of the gate479 recipe (same 479 fork, a new reseed) alongside gate-bare. Preferably also run a second gate-bare seed, which uses all 3 slots for about 1.6 slot-hours each. Use the two gate479 runs as the gated A/A band for distance, largest type and wall-core decks, instead of the historical scr-gate479 and the ungated noise bands.

Pre-register one primary readout (window-mean distance over 490-499) and one co-primary readout (wall-core decks at 499). State the decision rule: inert if |delta| is at most the gated A/A difference (floor 2 x 2.6 cards); load-bearing if it exceeds 2x that; anything in between gets one more seed. Treat moves, acc-prop and type as secondary readouts that cannot by themselves declare load-bearing.

Narrow the inference from a null: it licenses only 'inert for keeping the 479 gated state over 20 iterations'. Before any knob is pruned from the Stage 3 from-scratch recipe, require a fresh-start bare-vs-stack check at matched iterations, at least 40. This check must run whether or not an interaction is found.

Add pilot-node readouts for the practice and varied-field levers: the final-pilot walls verdict, with a stated direction and band under #137, plus a pilot competence score on a fixed deck panel, judged against the 0.06 bar. Either justify 20 iterations as long enough for a pilot-generality effect to appear, or extend the run to 30.

Calibrate the kill rule. Set the wall-core threshold from the concurrent gated replicate, or from the ctl479-vs-resetcap spread, rather than a fixed 20. Do not stop before 499 unless the gap is beyond 2x the calibrated noise for 3 consecutive iterations, so the primary 490-499 window is kept.

Before launch, have the registry print the fully resolved flag diff between gate-bare and gate479, including screen.py's inherited pre-#127 main_args. Confirm that only the seven stacked flags differ, or list every other differing flag as a confound and match it.
Express the type-size band in the gated regime, either relative to the size or taken from the gated A/A, not the ungated 15 decks.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: no violation. The candidate only removes knobs and adds launch infrastructure. Human lists are used only in the readouts (distance, wall-core), the registry works for any game, and it supports rule 3 (simple, one frozen recipe for Stage 3). The diagnosis matches the code and logs:
- notes/scripts/screen.py builds every screen on runs/lab/lab.json main_args plus extra flags appended after `--`, with no check for duplicates. scr-gate479's screen.jsonl passes --turnover-every 10 and then 5; argparse keeps the last value, so 5 was used.
- The rl/metagame.py argparse defaults are the pre-adoption values: lr 1e-4, swaps 3, draft-lr 1e-3, draft-margin 0.5, shaping 0, select-z 0, candidates 4. A hand launch would pick these up silently.

The fork path is sound for the bare arm, with one effect to state up front:
- --fork-from loads the net, the heads and the population.
- --draft-h-in-floor and --draft-group-p are Drafter constructor arguments, not saved state, so dropping them at the fork takes effect immediately.
- Adam starts fresh from a population snapshot, the same as in gate479, so the two arms match.
- --select keeps the season cands.
- gate-bare does keep the adopted turnover every 10 at 0.15 from main_args; the design should say this explicitly.
- Dropping the floor makes the inherited head draw sharper at once. That is a real immediate effect, not drift, and the bisection should expect it.

Costs are underestimated:
(1) Iteration time. scr-gate479's own log shows 289-352 s per iteration, about 5.3 min, not 4.7. Removing the 250 practice games saves perhaps 10%, so 20 iterations take about 1.7-1.9 slot-hours.
(2) Code: 3-4 h is low.
- Each flag needs its value, the log entry it came from and its status. Back-filling that from progress-log.md for about 25 flags takes roughly 1 h.
- The "ledger families of changed flags" check needs a flag-to-family map kept in the repo. The ledger lives only in the session scratchpad, so this is a hand mapping.
- No script in notes/scripts computes wall-core decks; one has to be written to read the population snapshots.
- The "final-pilot walls verdict (C07 protocol)" depends on another candidate's tooling, which is not costed here.
Realistic total: 5-6 h, or 4 h if the ledger-family lookup is deferred.
(3) The conditional follow-ups are not costed. A one-step bisection is 2 more runs, about 3.5 slot-hours. A 2^(4-1) fractional factorial "in a fresh-start regime" is 8 from-scratch arms: at about 5 min an iteration and 50+ iterations each, that is 30-40+ slot-hours, roughly 12 h of the whole 3-screen machine. It needs its own costing and go/no-go, not an aside.

Measurement details:
- scr-gate479 saved snapshots at 484, 489, 494 and 499. The kill check at 490 has no matching snapshot, so it must use 489, and gate-bare must launch with --keep 5.
- The A/A band (ctl479 vs resetcap) comes from the 3-candidate, no-gate rule. The gate arm (1 candidate, z 1) may have different variance, so a null near the band edge is weaker than claimed.

Value is high: the critic flagged reproducibility and pruning as real clutter, and this run is cheap.
required_changes: Re-cost gate-bare at about 5.3 min an iteration (measured in scr-gate479's stdout.log: 289-352 s), about 1.7-1.9 slot-hours for 20 iterations, not 1.6.

Re-cost the code at 5-6 h: about 1 h to back-fill each flag's source and status from progress-log.md, plus a flag-to-ledger-family map kept in the repo (the ledger lives only in the scratchpad), plus a new wall-core counting script over the population snapshots. Alternatively, defer the ledger-family pre-launch lookup to cut this to about 4 h.
Launch gate-bare with --seed 1 --reseed 2 --keep 5 so its snapshots land on scr-gate479's 484/489/494/499, and move the kill check from 490 to 489 to match a saved snapshot.

State that gate-bare keeps the adopted main_args turnover (every 10, 0.15) and that dropping --draft-h-in-floor changes the inherited head's draws at once (the floor is a Drafter constructor argument, not saved state).

Cost the bisection separately (2 more runs, about 3.5 slot-hours). Do not make the fresh-start 2^(4-1) factorial part of this candidate: it is 8 from-scratch arms, 30-40+ slot-hours, and needs its own proposal and go/no-go.
Either include the C07 final-pilot walls verdict tooling in the cost or drop that readout and keep window-mean distance, largest type, wall-core decks, moves and acc-prop.
Note that the A/A band comes from the ungated 3-candidate rule (ctl479 vs resetcap); treat a gate-bare null within about 1.5x that band as a weak result, not proof that the stack is inert.

title: Kill-horizon calibration on the existing logs: do early readings predict final ones, node by node?
rivals: H-short-horizon: early arm-minus-control differences do not predict final ones, so 1-13-iteration screen kills and one-segment pilot stops were uninformative
H-early-informative: early differences predict final ones; the kills were justified
H-node-specific: selection mechanics show at once; shape and type relapse non-monotonically and need about 1.5 relapse times; pilot effects need several segments
design: Offline on runs/screens/*/log.jsonl, checkpoint type counts, runs/lab branch logs and lab card events. (1) Arm-minus-matched-control differences at +3, +5, +10 and the end (>= +16) for every pair with a stated control (about 16: vs479, league479, turns40/70/120, lamv479 and gate479 vs ctl479; gatevs and t60gate vs gate479; jsearch479 vs t60gate479; resetcap, gamma and judge2 vs reset; resetent vs resetcap; anchor vs resetent) on smoothed top-12 distance, largest type, wall-core decks, deck-out share and moves; Spearman between early and final differences. (2) Relapse time constants per run (distance minimum to min+5; h_in < 1 to largest type > 50). (3) Lab: segment-1 vs segment-2 Elo and competence for every two-segment card (aux, deep6, hist4, ent02, vq4-b, deckcross-w, slotbind-w, exit arms, margin0, lr2, draftlr3 ...). (4) Truncate surviving runs where killed screens stopped (1, 2, 7, 8, 11, 13) and score how often a kill there matches the survivor's final verdict.

predictions.predicted: Spearman(+5, final) <= 0.4 for distance and type; lab segment-1 vs segment-2 Elo rho <= 0.3 with >= 3 sign flips; truncated verdicts at <= 8 iterations match final ones <= 60% of the time
rho >= 0.7 for distance, type and Elo; truncation agreement >= 85%
rho >= 0.8 for moves and held-back counts from +1; rho <= 0.4 for distance before about 1.5 relapse times (relapse 10-16 iterations from 479, S03); pilot Elo rho <= 0.4 at one segment

readout: Minimum horizons per metric and node, relapse time constants, and the killed screens reclassified as 'decided' or 'untested'.
noise_and_power: About 16 correlated arm-control pairs (two fork states): Spearman SE about 0.26, enough to tell >= 0.7 from <= 0.3; lab n about 10-14 cards. Survivorship bias: killed runs have no final value, so step (4) uses truncated survivors.
kill_rule: Analysis only; none.
cost: About 1.5-2 h of agent time, CPU only.
distinct_from: Methodology idea 8 (not run) and H62's untested 'truncated-curve ranking'. The lab had a two-segment rule for pilot cards, but screens from #128 on set kill horizons by eye; no family measured early-to-final agreement.
rules_check: Log analysis only; no training, no human data.
value: Sets node-matched kill rules before the next screens (composition drift early-readable; type and shape claims need about 1.5 relapse times; pilot changes need 2-3 segments) and reclassifies early-killed arms (scr-judge, scr-judge-select, scr-select, scr-draft, scr-typecap, scr-resetent10, scr-practice1k) for the do-not-repeat lists.
merged_from: scratch: Kill-horizon calibration on the existing logs: do early readings predict final ones, node by node?

reviews.reasons:
I found no repeat. C05 is a measurement of the experimental method (node N12) that nobody has run before. I checked every N12 family (H42, H61-H66) and grepped notes/progress-log.md for spearman, early/final, kill horizon, truncat, short-horizon, relapse time, rank agreement and minimum horizon. The only Spearman hit is #34-35 (builder scorers on held-out decks), which has nothing to do with this. No entry measures whether early arm-minus-control readings predict final ones.

How it compares with the overlapping families:
- **H62** ("Short screens and lab forks can rank pilot changes"): the families sharing H62's mechanism tested whether short forks can *detect* pilot changes, using A/A sigma and ladder reruns. The verifier lists "truncated-curve ranking" as explicitly untested. C05 measures early-to-final agreement itself, across screen and lab metrics. That is a factor H62 never varied. None of H62's do-not-repeat items is rerun: there are no new one-seed screens and no SPRT-at-first-look decisions.
- **H42** (population shape swings): its do-not-repeat list bans reading shape from single forks over fewer than 40 iterations. C05 measures how long that window has to be, so it does not break the rule. H42's untested multi-seed A/A is a separate experiment that C05 does not duplicate.
- **H64 / H65** (the yardsticks themselves) and **H66** (faults ending runs): C05 uses their metrics but does not re-validate them.
- **Source idea:** this is methodology research idea 8 (research_notes/methodology.md, line 392), marked [keep] in research_index.md line 208. It was never executed.

So C05 is distinct both in mechanism (calibrating kill horizons and truncated-verdict agreement) and in a factor never varied (the horizon at which screens and lab cards are read).

Non-blocking notes:
- **Step (2) is mostly done already.** ledger_meta.json has per-run relapse fields (distance minimum + 5, type > 50) for the 479 forks and the lab branches. Its aa_noise block already gives the A/A distance RMS (1.7-4.8) and the one-iteration jitter (about 1.9). Reuse these rather than recompute them, and use the smoothed (3-iteration) relapse reading, as aa_noise recommends.
- **Low correlation can come from null effects.** Several pairs (vs479, league479, turns70, turns120, gatevs, t60gate) end within A/A noise of their controls (S-regularities: RMS 1.7-2.6). A low early-to-final Spearman among them would show there was no effect to predict, not that short horizons mislead. Report rho separately for the pairs whose final difference exceeds about 2x A/A RMS (gate479, turns40, lamv479). Otherwise H-short-horizon would win by default.
- **Stopping reasons need sorting.** The killed screens should be reclassified as "decided" or "untested" only after separating those killed by shutdown or memory faults (H66: 019, 017-m, practice1k, resetent10) from those killed by eye for no movement.

This is cheap, CPU-only log analysis with no rules problem, and it targets a real gap: S03 and analysis section 4 say kill rules must depend on the node, but no family has measured early-to-final agreement. The readouts mostly match their nodes: moves and type counts for selection, distance and shape for drafting, Elo and competence for pilot cards. As written, though, the main statistic cannot tell the rivals apart, for five reasons.

(1) Range restriction makes a low rho ambiguous. By the ledger's own regularities, most of the roughly 16 pairs are true nulls inside A/A noise on distance: vs479 (RMS 1.7), league479, turns70, turns120, gatevs, t60gate, anchor and gamma. Only gate479 (types), turns40 and lamv479 separate. A Spearman taken across pairs whose true effects are about 0 is low whatever the horizon. So rho(+5, final) <= 0.4 is predicted both by H-short-horizon and by "early readings are fine, there is just nothing to detect". The same applies to lab Elo: most two-segment cards were judged neutral, with Elo sigma about 8.8 and segment swings of about 40 Elo, so a segment-1 vs segment-2 rho <= 0.3 with sign flips is the expected result under every rival. This is the "every outcome predicted by all live hypotheses" failure in correlational form.

(2) "Final" is itself short-horizon. The logs show the arm runs end at 13-20 iterations: anchor 13, turns40 13, vs479, turns120 and lamv479 16, most others 20. Only reset, resetcap, resetent and gamma reach 32-40. The design's "end >= +16" is not met for every pair. The final reading sits at about 1-1.5 relapse times (S03: 10-16 iterations), so the analysis can at best test +5 against +16-20. It cannot test whether the 20-iteration screens were themselves killed too early, which is the substantive version of H-short-horizon.

(3) Smoothed windows overlap. A 3-iteration smoothed reading at +10 shares data with an end at +13, so rho(+10, final) is inflated mechanically.

(4) The power claim is optimistic. The pairs are not independent: there are two fork states, ctl479 is shared by six arms, and resetent is a parent of anchor. Effective n is well below 16. Fisher SE is about 0.28 at n=16, so 0.7 vs 0.3 is at best about 1.5 SE apart. The thresholds 0.4/0.7/0.8 between rivals cannot be resolved.

(5) Step 4 lacks a pre-stated verdict rule and a reference set. Survivors are a selected sample, and most of their final verdicts are "noise". Agreement with a "null" final is easy, so 85% agreement would be uninformative unless it is scored separately on survivors with real effects.

H-node-specific is the most diagnostic rival, because it predicts a contrast between metrics within the same pairs. It should be the primary test, stated against A/A-normalised reliability rather than raw rho.
required_changes: Replace the raw cross-pair Spearman as the primary statistic with horizon-specific signal-to-noise against A/A. At each horizon h, compare the spread of arm-minus-control differences with the A/A difference spread at the same h (scr-ctl479 vs scr-resetcap, plus lab 001/002 and the near-A/A pairs). Report reliability = (Var_arms - Var_AA) / Var_arms per metric and horizon. A low rho then counts as evidence for H-short-horizon only if the early differences exceed A/A but fail to predict the final ones.

Add explicit positive and negative controls with written predictions. Positive controls are the known separated effects: gate479 type 23 vs 74, lamv479 distance +3.7/+9.5, turns40 Energy -3.5 and steps -56. For each, state the earliest horizon at which its sign and beyond-A/A status match the final, and what each rival predicts. Negative control: the A/A pair's early-to-final 'difference' correlation, which all rivals predict to be about 0.

Score verdict agreement, not rank correlation. Fix the three-way verdict rule in advance: worse beyond A/A, within noise, better beyond A/A, using smoothed distance > ~5 or 2x A/A RMS, type > 50, and the competence bar 0.06. Report agreement separately for pairs whose final verdict is a real effect and for pairs whose final verdict is null, so that agreement on nulls cannot inflate it.

Use non-overlapping windows. Early readings use iterations <= h, the final uses only the last 3 iterations, and h + window must be below the final window. Use the same per-pair final horizon, and drop or flag pairs that end before +16 (anchor, turns40).

State that the analysis can only calibrate horizons up to about 20 iterations, with 30-40 only for reset, resetcap, resetent and gamma. Restrict any claim that a kill was too early to that range, and for longer horizons use the 4 long runs (truncated at +5, +10 and +20 vs +30-40) as the test.

Account for dependence. Cluster by fork state and shared control, and compute the CIs by bootstrap over clusters or by permutation within control groups. Do not quote SE 0.26 for n=16. Relax the rival thresholds to what the effective n can resolve, or make the within-pair metric contrast the primary test: moves and type counts readable at +1-3, distance needing >= 1.5 relapse times. This is H-node-specific, and it is paired, so it has more power.

For the lab, compute segment-1 vs segment-2 reliability against the lab A/A segment swings (Elo sigma ~8.8, swings ~40) rather than raw rho over mostly neutral cards. Include at least one card with a known large effect, if any exists, as a positive control. Otherwise state that the lab data can only bound reliability and cannot decide H-short-horizon for the pilot.

reviews.reasons:
The rules check passes. This is offline log analysis with no training input. The human shape is used only as the evaluation distance, as notes/scripts/screen_watch.py already does with HUMAN=[13.5,28,18]. Nothing in it is game-specific, so it carries over to MTG. It needs no screens and no GPU, so it fits the machine budget. It is a useful step before more screens are run. The data on disk is thinner than the design assumes, though, and the power claims are overstated.

(a) Per-iteration metrics are fully available. runs/screens/*/log.jsonl has these fields every iteration: shapes, z, ids, endings, select.moved/held_back, draft.h_in, shape_quartiles, best and turnover. Top-12 shape distance, deck-out share, moves and h_in can therefore be read at +1, +3, +5 and so on, reusing screen_watch.line().

(b) Card-level metrics (largest type, wall-core decks) need decklists. Those exist only in the population snapshots (save-every 5, pruned) and in checkpoint.pt.
- 479 forks have them at +5, +10 and +15, plus +20 only for ctl479, gate479, gatevs479 and league479. vs479, lamv479, turns120, turns70, jsearch479 and t60gate479 stop at it0494. turns40 stops at it0489.
- 460 forks have them only at 469, 479, 489 and sometimes 499, which is +9, +19, +29 and +39. So reset, resetcap and gamma cannot be read at +3, +5 or +10, judge2 has only 469 and 479, and resetent has no 499.
- Type and shape relapse times can therefore only be bracketed to 5- or 10-iteration bins.

(c) Pair counts.
- There are 15 arm-control pairs, not about 16. Seven share ctl479 and three share reset, so the differences have correlated errors and the effective n is far below 15. The claimed Spearman SE of about 0.26 does not hold.
- turns40 (13 iterations) and anchor (13 iterations) cannot supply a final reading at +16 or later; vs479 and lamv479 reach only +16.

(d) The lab is smaller than claimed.
- Only 7 pilot cards have two or more rungs: 003-vq4-b, 005-aux, 009-deckcross-w, 009-hist4, 010-ent02-b, 031-slotbind-w and 032-lr2.
- deep6, deep6-b and the exit, memattn, lamturn and shapeon arms have one rung each (rebased, failed-early or error).
- Meta cards add 2-4 rungs each: margin0, margin0-n, swaps6, turnover30-b, practice, practice10, hin2, hin3, draftlr3, league3-copy, league3-m and exploit.
- With n=7 pilot cards, rho <= 0.3 or >= 0.7 cannot be told apart, and failed-early cards are survivorship-censored.

(e) The cost of 1.5-2 h is underestimated. Snapshot decoding with type and wall-core classification, the A/A-band computation and the per-fork-group bootstrap make it about 2.5-3.5 h of agent time.

title: Adversarial fidelity audit of the human side: the 2000 procedure rules and the human lists' most-played cards, with a paired re-probe per fault
rivals: F1 faithful: no deviation in the 2000 procedure rules or the human field's cards changes play materially; H02 closes for both sides
F2 a fault slows or weakens the lists: a procedure rule or high-frequency human card is implemented against the 2000 text in a way that matters against the walls
design: #139's procedure for the other side: one agent reads each rule and card in code against the printed text (notes/data/cache/tcgdata) and the 2000 rulebooks and Compendium rulings (C02 Q4), writing a scripted engine check per claim; an adversarial verifier reproduces each claimed deviation. Scope: the procedure rules env/engine.js uses (ryuu-play Rules with first-turn draw, the opponent's optional extra card per mulligan, the 2003 Confusion rule, a simultaneous win as a draw) and the most-played human cards not covered by #139 or #92: Scyther, Hitmonchan, Electabuzz, Jigglypuff and Wigglytuff, Ditto's Transform against Chansey and Snorlax (Ditto is in 11 of 24 lists; copying 120 HP or Thick Skinned matters exactly here), Mewtwo promo, Magmar, Item Finder, Scoop Up, Rocket's Sneak Attack, Lass, Nightly Garbage Run, Switch, Rainbow Energy. Each confirmed deviation touching the human field gets a flagged fix and a paired re-probe (wall set A vs the 24 lists, greedy, 1,152 games on identical deals, before and after).

predictions.predicted: only cosmetic or out-of-field deviations; any re-probe moves the walls' score by < 0.02
>= 1 deviation in a high-frequency human card or a procedure rule whose re-probe moves the walls' score >= 0.03 toward the lists

readout: Each claim verified or refuted with a reproduction; per fix, the paired change in the walls' score against the 24 lists and in the lists' Prize-win turns.
noise_and_power: The audit is deterministic (scripted checks). A paired re-probe on identical deals has a difference SE of about 0.01-0.015 at 1,152 games (0.03 is 2-3 SE); games stay identical up to the first decision a fix changes.
kill_rule: Stop when every rule and card in scope has a verified or refuted entry; skip the re-probe for a deviation that never fires in 200 traced human-vs-wall games.
cost: About half a day of agent time on CPU (the #139 pattern); about 10 min per re-probe. Engine fixes are submodule commits needing Evan's go-ahead (C33 D7), so they stay behind flags.
distinct_from: H02 was refuted only for the walls' cards and end rules (#139); its do-not-repeat bars re-auditing the walls' cards, PlusPower/Gust/Computer Search (#92), 'once during your turn' Powers (#62) and the enumerator-oracle check (#5), none in scope. #1's 22/23 dated rulings and 1,926 card-data checks tested data and single rulings, not the human field's cards adversarially or the 2000 procedure rules (critic).
rules_check: Environment fidelity: the engine plays the printed 2000 game; no human data in training; auditing rules and card text is game-agnostic practice.
value: Closes the last open fidelity question on N1 before the deviation is blamed on the process: F2 means part of the walls' edge rests on an engine fault; F1 lets C13, C16 and C34 be read without that caveat. Low prior, low cost.

reviews.reasons:
Diagnostic, and the readout fits the node. F1 and F2 predict different things on a deterministic readout: a claim is either reproduced or refuted. The paired re-probe is the right way to measure a fix's effect on N1, and the experiment is cheap, runs on CPU and stays outside the H02 do-not-repeat list (#139 audited the walls' side, #92 PlusPower/Gust/Computer Search, #62 the Powers). It is not the 'relapses like the control' kind of design, so I would keep it. Five statistical and design problems need fixing first.

(1) The noise estimate is wrong for the in-scope rules that fire in every game. The paired SE of 0.01-0.015 holds only while games stay identical. After the first changed decision, the coin-flip/RNG stream and the rest of the game diverge, so a game where the fix fires contributes roughly independent variance. The SE of the difference is then about sqrt(f*2p(1-p)/n). With f near 1 (first-turn draw, the mulligan extra card) and p about 0.7, that is about 0.019 at 1,152 games. So 0.03 is about 1.5 SE, not 2-3. The fix is to estimate the SE from discordant pairs and to size n by the measured firing fraction f.

(2) Multiplicity. About 20 rules and cards could each get a re-probe. A one-sided test at about 2 SE would then be expected to produce about 0.4-1 false F2 call. There is no correction and no confirmation run.

(3) The decision threshold does not match the stated value. The walls score about 0.72 greedy against the lists, and #147 brings them to parity only with search plus 50-60-turn draws. A 0.03 shift would confirm a fault but would not change how C13, C16 or C34 are read. No threshold is set for 'part of the walls' edge rests on an engine fault', and no combined all-fixes probe catches several sub-threshold fixes adding up.

(4) The F2 prediction is one-directional ('toward the lists'). A fix could instead strengthen the walls, and the 0.02-0.03 band belongs to neither rival, so some outcomes have no reading.

(5) A third explanation is not separated out. The greedy pilot was trained on the faulty engine, so a fixed rule or card may be underused, for example a Ditto that copies Chansey's 120 HP or Thick Skinned, or a corrected opening draw. A null re-probe would then be read as F1 when it really means F2 with the effect hidden by the pilot's training.

Two smaller points. The 2003 Confusion rule and the simultaneous-win draw were already flagged as minor deviations in #139. Re-auditing them repeats work; they should go straight to a re-probe. The 'lists' Prize-win turns' readout has no prediction for either rival, although game length is the E x P link that JF2 and #147 point to. The kill rule fits a deterministic audit; short-horizon bias does not apply because nothing is trained.
required_changes: Recompute the paired SE from discordant pairs, using each fix's measured firing fraction f. For rules that fire in nearly every game (first-turn draw, the opponent's extra card per mulligan, the Confusion rule), use 2-4 deal seeds (2,304-4,608 games) so that 0.03 is at least 2.5 SE. Report f and the number of decisions changed for each fix.
Control multiplicity. Use Holm across all re-probed fixes, or require any fix that crosses the threshold to replicate on a fresh deal seed before F2 is declared.
Make the test two-sided. State predictions for fixes that move the walls' score away from the lists, and assign the 0.02-0.03 band (for example 'inconclusive, replicate').

Add one combined re-probe with every confirmed fix on together, so that sub-threshold fixes that add up are caught. Add a decision threshold tied to the value claim, for example a combined shift of at least 0.10 or the walls dropping below 0.60 greedy before C13, C16 and C34 must be re-read under the fixed engine.

Add a third explanation and test it: the fix matters but the pilot trained on the old engine cannot use it. For any fix that fires in at least 10% of games, or whose |delta| is at least 0.02, run a short pilot fine-tune on the fixed engine (about 10-20 iterations) and re-probe, so a null result is not read as F1 by default.

Do not re-audit the 2003 Confusion rule or the simultaneous-win rule that #139 already flagged; send them straight to the paired re-probe. Give each rival an explicit prediction for the lists' Prize-win turns, for example F2 predicting the median falls by at least 1 turn.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: no violation. Checking the engine against the printed 2000 text is about fidelity to the game, not a training input. Choosing which cards to audit by how often they appear in the human lists is diagnostic use of those lists, which is allowed. A procedure audit of this kind would carry over to MTG.

Feasibility and cost: the scope and the prior-work claims are not accurate against the repo, and the fix-and-re-probe step is underestimated.

(1) Much of the scope has already been tested adversarially. notes/sts-2000-engine-check.md section 7 and notes/scripts/ryuu_sts_cards_tests.js (68/68) cover the following:
- Ditto: D1-D21, including copied HP, type, Weakness, retreat, passive-Power copying, the Asleep/Confused/Paralyzed exceptions, Toxic Gas, and Ditto vs Ditto.
- Mewtwo promo: M1-M15.
- Cross-card cases: X1-X15, including Rainbow Energy from hand vs from the discard, Defender and Energy Removal on a transformed Ditto, and the KO check using the copied HP.
notes/scripts/ryuu_rulings_tests.js also names Scyther, Hitmonchan, Electabuzz, Jigglypuff, Wigglytuff, Item Finder, Scoop Up, Sneak Attack, Lass and Switch. The candidate's distinct_from cites only #1's 22/23 rulings and 1,926 data checks, and misses both suites. That makes the Ditto/Mewtwo part, and probably most of the vanilla attackers (Scyther, Hitmonchan, Electabuzz, Magmar), a near-repeat.

(2) Two of the four procedure items are known results. #139 already found and verified the 2003 Confusion rule and the simultaneous-win-is-a-draw rule; it also found the Maintenance order, Thick Skinned and ending-label deviations. H02's ledger entry lists 'fix the minor deviations and rerun the walls probe' as the open variant. Re-auditing these repeats #139. The open work is the flagged fix plus the paired re-probe.

(3) The real gaps are smaller than the candidate's list: the setup and turn procedure (first-player draw and turn-1 attack/Trainer legality in 2000, the mulligan extra-card option and its count, the Basic-placement order) and the cards neither suite covers (Nightly Garbage Run, the Wigglytuff Do the Wave bench count, Magmar, plus whatever a grep of both suites shows untested).

(4) The cost of fixes is missing. Each fix means editing ryuu-play TypeScript, rebuilding packages/*/dist, and adding a runtime toggle plumbed through env/engine.js → env/game.js → runner/remote_worker. That is about 1-2 h per fix on top of the audit. The submodule is shared with up to 3 live screens, so a rebuild with default-on behaviour would silently change the engine under them.

(5) The re-probe is feasible. walls_vs_humans.js and the Node ONNX pilot exist (#139). 1,152 greedy games in ~10 min is plausible on 16 threads. The paired SE claim holds for identical deals. 'Wall set A' should name the snapshot (#139 used scr-resetcap 499 greedy) so before and after are comparable to #139's 0.702.

Value is low-prior but cheap once trimmed, and it closes H02 for the human side.

Protect live screens. Every fix must default off. After the rebuild, run the seeded-2000 trace_hash check (#46/#62, e332007...) with flags off to prove the engine is byte-identical before any running screen's workers restart. Do not commit to the submodule without Evan's go-ahead (uncommitted working-tree edits behind default-off flags only).

Name the re-probe's wall snapshot and agents exactly (#139: scr-resetcap population_it0479-derived walls at 499, greedy, walls_vs_humans.js on #137's deals) so before and after compare with #139's 0.702 baseline. State the games per pair (1,152 = 3 walls x 24 lists x 16).

title: Zero-training judge zoo: wall-naive checkpoints, matched from-scratch pairs and a skill trace on the walls' verdict (deck-out payoff, exposure, card familiarity, Energy-count bug, open decklists, encoder)
rivals: H-payoff (H2/H5): any competent pilot paid 1 for deck-out wins rates the walls high without meeting them; pilot-v2's 0.24-0.26 is its deck-out-0 training (#147's attribution)
H-exposure (H1, F2): only pilots that played the walls rate them high (co-adaptation)

Familiarity confound: the a4-tok family and pilot-scratch never played Snorlax JU, Potion Energy or Recycle (none is in the 56-card human pool) and may fail with the walls whatever the payoff; the abl pilots know these cards
H-human-side (H19): the walls win because the lists are misplayed; a human-list specialist on their seat pulls the walls below 0.55
H-count-bug: the live attached-Energy count bug (token_model.py:367, aux slot*8+copies read as a count) tilts the judge to Energy-heavy walls
H-open-decklists: seeing the opponent's full list (OPP_DECKLIST) favours denial and stall
H-architecture (A1): the deck-free cross encoder favours walls (Snorlax decks 30 -> 88 with it)
H-weak: these pilots are too weak to separate decks
Null: no factor moves the verdict beyond the training-seed band
design: No training. Loop notes/scripts/probe_matchups.py (--pilot, --pilot-b exist) over checkpoints that load under the current token bounds (checked with token_net on one worker): the 3 walls of scr-resetcap 499 (#829/#796/#809, runs/probe/walls_resetcap499.json) vs the 24 lists, greedy, judge on both seats, seed 11 (#137/#147 deals). (a) runs/abl pilots, all from scratch, deck-out wins 1, lr 3e-4, on runs/abl/matchups.json (meta-99's drafted full-pool decks: Snorlax JU in 143, Potion Energy in 285, Full Heal Energy in 295 of 477, never the 460+ walls), 16 a pair (1,152 games): base and base-s2 at it19/39/59/79 (seed band), base-cont, ent-cont, explore-cont at it19/39, explore10 and -s2 at it39/79, and the it39 arms slot-bind (the only pilot ever trained with the corrected count), no-deck (decklist tokens masked), deck-cross (deck-free encoder plus deck cross-attention), cand-self, ability-text, deck-inter, deck-cross-sb, gae1 (near floor); skill covariates already measured (#73, #74, #82: Elo vs pilot-v2, SimpleBot on archived lists; base it79 +80/0.418, base-cont +135/0.514, ent-cont +140/0.475). (b) Card-unfamiliar human-field lineage (pilot-v2's 278-card table, max_tok 128), 32 a pair (2,304): a4-tok it249 (250 iterations on the 24 lists, deck-out 1, 44% deck-outs on the field, no count features), #33's matched pair deckout-w1 / deckout-w0 it14 (a4-tok + 15 iterations at 1 / 0), pilot-scratch it249 (deck-out 0, random field-card decks, #42); pairings X/X, a4-tok on walls + resetcap499 on lists, and the reverse. Human-free twin: the walls vs 12 wide decks under X/X. Log the walls' deck-out share, share past turn 40 and game length per pairing. References on the same deals: own/own 0.720, own/v2 0.761, v2/v2 0.237, v2/own 0.233 (#137); pilot-v2 0.264, 499 pilot 0.722 (#147).

predictions.predicted: abl verdict rises with skill (Spearman >= 0.5 with either covariate and along the base lineage); base-cont, ent-cont, base-s2 it79 >= 0.55 with most wall wins by deck-out; a4-tok/a4-tok and w1/w1 >= 0.55 with >= 50% deck-out wins, w0 >= 0.08 below w1, pilot-scratch <= 0.35, the wide twin the same way (decisive: these pilots never met the walls)
every pilot <= 0.40, no skill trend (Spearman <= 0.2), w1 - w0 within +/-0.05, walls' deck-out share under these pilots <= 20%

a4-tok family <= 0.35-0.40 regardless of payoff while abl pilots >= 0.55; with the walls the a4-tok family takes >= 40% of games past turn 40 yet scores <= 0.40, and a4-tok on the walls' seat is no better than X/X
resetcap499 on walls + a4-tok on lists <= 0.55 (vs 0.720) opens the lever; >= 0.65 closes H19 (pilot-v2 there gave 0.761)
slot-bind it39 below base it39 by >= max(0.05, 2x |base - base-s2|)
no-deck it39 below base it39 by the same margin
deck-cross it39 above base it39 by the same margin
all pilots in 0.45-0.55 with no trend
every matched pair inside the seed band

readout: Walls' mean score vs the 24 lists per judge and pairing, within-pair differences, Spearman against skill; deck-out share, share past turn 40, length; human-free twin. Absolute levels read only beside each judge's human-list strength (abl eval_split; a4-tok 93% vs SimpleBot; deckout-w0/w1 93.0/95.5%).
noise_and_power: 1,152 games: binomial SE about 0.013; 2,304 games over 72 pairs: pair-clustered SE about 0.025, judge differences about 0.03 (0.35 vs 0.55 about 6 SE apart; w1 - w0 of 0.08 about 2.7 SE). The binding noise for (a) is training seed (|base - base-s2|; if > 0.08, single-seed pairs resolve only >= 0.16); about 25 checkpoints give Spearman SE 0.2-0.27. abl pilots are weak on the lists (0.27-0.38 vs SimpleBot at 40, #74) and met Energy-heavy, stall-prone decks (about 35% deck-outs), so only pairs and trends are read; only a high verdict is decisive for H-payoff.
kill_rule: Probe base-cont it39, ent-cont it39, base-s2 it79 first; if all fall in 0.45-0.55, stop the abl sweep and rely on W (C30). Drop a judge with > 2% errors or 5,000-decision caps. Do not read a pair whose pilots differ by > 0.1 vs SimpleBot. A checkpoint failing the GPU path is exported to ONNX and run with walls_vs_humans.js on #139's 576 deals. Run C17 only if (b) lands in the H-exposure or confound band or in 0.40-0.55.
cost: About 47k greedy games, about 1 h GPU at about 13 games/s (RL_GPU_SHARE 0.15, beside screens) plus about 45 min of scripting. No training, no screen slot.
distinct_from: #137/#147 swept population pilots and pilot-v2 (H18/H22 do-not-repeat); the critic notes a payoff-1 pilot that never met the walls was never in any sweep; none of (b) judged the walls since #127; H19's verifier lists a4-tok on the human side and H52's the matched deck-out 0/1 judge pair as untested (#33 read only card values); H58 judged slot binding and H57's no-deck screen (#73-74) only on Elo; A1 untested. Not H20: nothing enters the loop.
rules_check: Evaluation and diagnosis with existing checkpoints; the a4-tok family (human lists) and pilot-scratch (their 56-card pool) are diagnostic judges only and never enter training; human lists are probes with the human-free twin beside them.
value: The cheapest first split of why the judge pays the walls. Decisive H-payoff closes evaluation-regime fixes that keep the deck-out payoff (reset or frozen judges, panels: C39), sends judge work to strength plus the turn cut (C13, C16, C20, C38, C33), and says Stage 3 will re-find stall, so the round-rule question precedes Stage 3 compute. H-exposure or the confound sends the question to C17, then C39; a fresh rule-compliant pilot is then a fair judge. The seat swap settles H19. Count-bug, no-deck and encoder pairs pre-read C08, C09 and A1; nulls retire links cheaply.

reviews.reasons:
C07 does not rerun anything on a do-not-repeat list. Its new factor is which pilot judges: none of its judges has ever judged the walls. I checked the families it could overlap.

- **H18, H22, #147 (judge sweeps).** The do-not-repeat lists forbid further sweeps of population (scr-*) pilots and the four own/v2 pairings (#137). C07 uses neither. runs/probe/judge/ holds only scr-* pilots and pilot-v2. There is no probe of an abl pilot, a4-tok, deckout-w0/w1 or pilot-scratch. All four were trained under the plain result, either from scratch or on the human lists, and never met the walls. The critic (ledger_meta research_mode_collapse and the N4 comment) names this as the confound under F2: the population judges' rating is mixed up with pilot-v2's deck-out-0 training. No pilot paid 1 for a deck-out win that never met the walls has ever been probed.

reviews.reasons:
The readout fits the node. The candidate targets the judge (N4), and the walls' score vs the 24 lists under each pilot is a judge readout. It needs no training, and the checkpoints exist: I checked that runs/abl/{base,base-s2,...} have it19/39(/59/79), that runs/a4-tok, runs/deckout-w0 and runs/deckout-w1 (it4/9/14) and runs/pilot-scratch are present, and that runs/probe/walls_resetcap499.json exists. Several of its contrasts have never been run, and they separate the rivals cleanly. The best ones are the seat swap (resetcap499 on the walls, a4-tok on the lists: <=0.55 vs >=0.65, against pilot-v2's 0.761) and a4-tok X/X high vs low. The full run costs about 1 h of GPU and takes no screen slot. The statistics have five problems.

(1) The design calls a high abl verdict "decisive for H-payoff", but H-weak predicts the same outcome. The abl pilots are weak and slow on the lists (0.27-0.38 vs SimpleBot) and were trained among stall-prone decks, about 35% of which deck out. #139 shows the walls win through slowness: 0.36 at <=40 turns, 0.78 past 40. So a slow pilot on the human seat lets the walls win by deck-out whatever payoff it was trained on. The H-weak prediction of 0.45-0.55 is assigned arbitrarily. In (a), H-payoff and H-weak/slow therefore predict the same absolute level.

(2) Exposure is also confounded in (a). The abl pilots met Snorlax JU decks in 143 of 477 matchups, so "never met the walls" holds only partly. Training length and skill both co-vary with exposure to stall decks along each lineage, so a skill trend cannot separate payoff from exposure.

(3) The seed band is estimated from a single |base - base-s2| difference. That number is noisy, and when it comes out small the threshold collapses to the 0.05 floor, which invites false positives for slot-bind, no-deck and deck-cross. The candidate already has 4 base/base-s2 pairs and 4 explore10/-s2 pairs but does not pool them.

(4) The Spearman cutoffs (>=0.5 vs <=0.2, with SE 0.2-0.27) are only about 1.2 SE apart. The 25 checkpoints are nested in lineages, so the effective n is lower still. The skill covariates exist for only some checkpoints (#73/#74/#82).

(5) The cleanest payoff contrast, deckout-w1 vs w0, differs by only 15 fine-tune iterations. The predicted 0.08 gap is about 2.7 SE at 32 games a pair, and the true effect of 15 iterations is probably smaller, so this contrast is underpowered.

In (b), a low a4-tok result is predicted by both H-exposure and the familiarity confound. The split proposed through the past-turn-40 share is post hoc, but routing that case to C17 is acceptable.

The kill rule (three probes in 0.45-0.55) rests on the miscalibrated H-weak band. Short-horizon bias does not apply because there is no training. The whole run is cheap, so the rule should not be allowed to drop the cheap architecture pairs.

About 20 contrasts are read at about 2 SE each, so roughly one false positive is expected without a correction.
required_changes: Re-derive the predictions for (a): a high absolute verdict from slow or weak pilots is predicted by both H-payoff and H-weak. Log human-side speed for every judge, as the median turn of the lists' prize wins (lists vs the wide twin, or a small human-vs-human subset on the same deals). Report the walls' score restricted to games ending <= 40 turns next to the full score. A high (a) verdict counts for H-payoff only if it persists in the <= 40-turn games or after conditioning on speed. Drop the 0.45-0.55 band as the H-weak prediction.

Make deckout-w1 vs deckout-w0 the primary decisive payoff contrast. Raise it to 64-96 games a pair on the same deals (about 5-7 min of GPU). Add the it4/it9/it14 dose-response for both arms. Compute the paired difference SE by bootstrap over deals and wall-list pairs, and pre-register the effect needed (>= 3 paired SE).

Estimate the training-seed band from every available seed pair: base/base-s2 at it19/39/59/79 and explore10/-s2 at it19/39/59/79, giving 8 differences. Set the margin for the slot-bind, no-deck and deck-cross contrasts to max(0.05, 2*sqrt(2)*sigma_seed), not 2x one observed difference.

Replicate each architecture contrast (slot-bind, no-deck, deck-cross vs base) at both it19 and it39, since both checkpoints exist. Read a lever as live only if the sign and the margin hold at both checkpoints.

Measure the skill covariate (SimpleBot on the archived lists, same deals and protocol) for every checkpoint in the sweep before reading any trend. Use a within-lineage trend or a mixed model instead of a pooled Spearman across nested checkpoints. Do not treat the Spearman >= 0.5 / <= 0.2 cutoffs as decisive.

Add each abl checkpoint's training exposure to stall decks as a covariate: the share of training games against Snorlax JU or Potion-Energy decks before that iteration, from matchups.json and the logs. This separates H-exposure from H-payoff inside (a).
Pre-register the primary contrasts: w1-w0, the seat swap, a4-tok X/X, and the three architecture pairs. Apply Holm (or a similar) correction across them. Treat all other cells as descriptive.
Restrict the kill rule to the abl skill trace. Always run the architecture pairs and arm (b). State how 5,000-decision caps and errors are scored (excluded vs draw) and report their rate per judge.
