title: The live attached-Energy count bug: zero-training sensitivity tests (channel mean-ablation, metamorphic Bench swap), then an isolated fix with an A/A
rivals: R1 distorts: with slot_bind off, count_features reads an ENERGY token's raw aux, slot*8 + copies (env/tokens.js:125; rl/token_model.py:367; count_features on in the PILOT), so 2 Energy on slot 5 reads 42 and threshold features saturate for every Bench slot; only the own Active gets a true count and slot features count Energy cards (DCE once). This skews Energy reading, hurting the typed-cost human attackers (Hitmonchan FFC, Electabuzz LC, Magmar, Articuno, Rain Dance) while Chansey and Snorlax pay colorless costs
R2 inert: the 256-way aux embedding learned each (slot, copies) code and the slot totals suffice; #116's neutral warm-started slot binding stands
R3 opposite channel: the walls read opposing Energy through the same bug to aim Energy Removal, so a fix helps the walls more
design: Step 1, forward passes only; pilots scr-resetcap 499 and pilot-v2 (bug) with 031-pilot-slotbind-w (corrected counts) as positive control; recorded main-phase states from human-vs-human games (evaluation), population games and the 499 pilot's walls-vs-list games: (i) mean-ablate the ENERGY tokens' count input on 2,000 states and measure value change and greedy-choice flips overall and on attach, retreat and attack decisions, against a control ablation of a non-Energy count channel of similar variance; (ii) metamorphic test on 10,000 states: swap two Bench Pokemon with all attachments (rules-neutral), re-encode, compare |dV| for Energy-moving swaps vs Energy-free swaps vs a relevant change (+1 Energy of the Pokemon's type), on both Benches. Step 2 only under R1: the fix computes ENERGY count features from owner_and_count's copies (aux - 8*slot; aux embedding kept; no slot embeddings or same-slot bias, unlike --slot-bind). Distil three students with rl/warmstart.py from scr-resetcap 499 on the same teacher games (#98's recipe: 400+ games, 2+ epochs): fix, bug seed 1, bug seed 2 (A/A); train each 15 iterations on the shared human-free pilot testbed (scr-resetcap 499 population decks, best decks of other types from main seg_0160-0320 and screen snapshots, wide decks; no run that saw human lists), reused by C09 and C35-C37. Step 3 if the fix moves the judge: a fork pair from population_it0479.pt with scr-gate479's flags and --reseed 2, fixed vs unfixed pilot, 20 iterations.

predictions.predicted: Step 1: flips on >= 3% of Energy-related decisions and |dV| >= 0.03, well above the control ablation; Energy-carrying swaps |dV| >= 2x Energy-free and >= 50% of the +1-Energy change, slotbind-w <= 1.3x. Step 2: the fix cuts human-vs-human deck-outs >= 3 points beyond the bug-1/bug-2 gap, most in typed-cost archetypes, and lowers the walls' verdict >= 0.03 through the lists' seat. Step 3: the fixed fork's pilot rates the walls >= 0.05 lower, median Energy >= 2 lower and >= 10 fewer Chansey+Snorlax decks at 499
flips < 1% and |dV| < 0.01 like the control; Energy/no-Energy ratio <= 1.3 and irrelevant/relevant <= 0.2 for every pilot; Step 2 not run
Step 2: the walls' verdict rises >= 0.03, with the gain on the walls' seat (#137 decomposition)

readout: Step 1: flips and |dV| by decision class; |dV| ratios with bootstrap CIs per Bench. Step 2: human-vs-human tempo by typed vs colorless-leaning archetype (C10 panel); walls' verdict with seat decomposition; puzzles. Step 3: verdict per fork, drafted shape, Chansey+Snorlax count.
noise_and_power: Step 1 is deterministic per state: 2,000 states give SE < 0.002 on mean |dV| and about 0.4 points on flips; about 5,000 swaps per class give a +/-0.1 CI on the median ratio. Step 2: deck-out SE about 1.4 points (1,024 games), verdict SE 0.013 (1,152); fork noise from the two buggy students. Step 3: 479 forks reproduce type trajectories (S03); distance A/A RMS 2.6, median Energy 0.8.
kill_rule: Stop after Step 1 under R2. Stop Step 2 at 10 iterations if fix and bug differ by less than the bug-1/bug-2 gap on every readout. Stop Step 3 at 10 iterations if the forks are within A/A on distance and the Chansey+Snorlax count and the probe differs by < 0.03.
cost: Step 1 about 2-3 h (scripts plus minutes of GPU). Step 2 about 3 h of distillation plus 3 x 15 iterations at about 1 min and 1 h of evaluation. Step 3 about half a day of code and warm start plus 2 forks x 20 iterations, about 2.5 h in two slots.
distinct_from: H58 (do-not-repeat) tested slot binding cold and warm on Elo and competence only (#106, #113, #116), with walls (the decks least exposed to the bug) and with owner embeddings and same-slot bias bundled; its verifier notes the fix was never measured on Energy or deck shape. C07's slot-bind pair is a from-scratch proxy. Critic's top untested #7 and coverage gap 'Energy-count input encoding'.
rules_check: A fix to an existing input, not shaping: a per-entity count of attached cards is generic to card games. Human lists are evaluation decks only.
value: Energy count is the failure's own axis. R1: adopt the one-line fix with a warm start before further pilot or judge work, since every judge result builds on it, and re-read anomaly A2 (Haymaker loses despite Weakness). R2/R3 close the item in analysis section 9 with a measured answer.
merged_from: chain: Perception-link swap for the live attached-Energy count bug: mean-ablation of the corrupted channel, then an isolated fix fork; pilot: The attached-Energy count bug: does the pilot misread typed Energy on Benched and opposing Pokemon, slowing the typed-cost human decks while the colorless walls need only the slot total?

reviews.reasons:
The closest family is H58 (slot binding, N11). Its do-not-repeat list is: --slot-bind cold or warm; deck-cross-sb from scratch at 40 iterations; growing slot_bind with no warm start (#83/#106, -201); and warm-started slotbind-w decided on walls competence (#113/#116). C08 reruns none of these.

It is distinct on three counts:
(a) Node/diagnostic. Step 1 is a zero-training sensitivity test: mean-ablation of the ENERGY count channel against a matched control channel, plus a metamorphic Bench swap. Grep of progress-log.md finds no ablation, perturbation or metamorphic test of the count input. #70's pilot_ablation covered architecture switches, not this input. So Step 1 is new in kind.
(b) Never-varied factor: isolation. In every H58 test (#71, #73/74, #106, #116) the count correction came bundled with slot/owner embeddings and the per-head same-slot bias. The isolated fix (aux - 8*slot for ENERGY count features only, aux embedding kept, no new embeddings or bias) was never built. Grep for count fix, aux % 8 and corrected count only hits #71's bundled slot_bind description.
(c) Never-measured readout. H58's verifier states the fix was never measured on Energy count or deck shape. #116 was judged on walls competence and Elo only. C08 reads human-vs-human deck-outs by typed vs colorless archetype, the walls' verdict with seat decomposition, and drafted Energy plus the Chansey+Snorlax count.

Protocol do-not-repeats are respected:
- Warm start uses rl/warmstart.py at 400+ games and 2+ epochs, satisfying H60's ban on about 40 games and 1 epoch, and avoids cold-growing a non-identity change (H57/H60).
- A bug-seed A/A pair is included, which addresses the single-seed screens of H58 and H57.

H55, H56 and H57 overlap only through the architecture node and share no configuration. It also fills the critic's 'Energy-count input encoding' coverage gap and analysis section 9's live-bug item.

One protocol risk remains, in Step 3. H60's do-not-repeat bans 'reading a single fork's population deck shape as evidence for a pilot architecture' (#104, retracted by #109/#112, where two forks of one state split 8 vs 23-29 Trainers). Step 3 is one fixed vs unfixed fork pair read on median Energy and the Chansey+Snorlax count. S03 (479 forks reproduce type trajectories) and the A/A RMS partly answer this, but the design should add explicit replication.
required_changes: Step 3: do not decide on a single fixed vs unfixed fork pair's deck shape (H60 do-not-repeat, #104 retracted by #109/#112). Run at least two seeds per arm, or add an unfixed-vs-unfixed A/A fork from population_it0479.pt with the same flags. Require the drafted-shape gap (median Energy, Chansey+Snorlax count) to exceed that A/A spread before attributing it to the fix.

State explicitly that Step 2's fix is ENERGY-token count correction only (no owner/slot embeddings, no same-slot attention bias, not the --slot-bind flag), so it cannot be confused with H58's do-not-repeat '--slot-bind cold or warm'.

reviews.reasons:
This is worth running. The bug is live in code. In rl/token_model.py:367, count_features gets aux_in when slot_bind is off, and env/tokens.js:125 sets an ENERGY token's aux to i*8+min(v,7). It sits on the failure's own axis, closes a coverage gap the critic flagged, and its Step-1 cost is small. Step 1 can tell R1/R3 apart from R2, and the readouts fit the nodes: pilot probes for the pilot change, then the judge verdict, then deck shape. But several parts are not diagnostic as written.

(1) The mean-ablation in Step 1(i) measures how much the pilot relies on the channel, not whether it misreads it. With slot_bind off, aux (the 256-way embedding plus the a/8 term) is the only route by which an ENERGY token tells which slot it is attached to. Ablating it removes that attachment information under every hypothesis. Within a slot, a/8 = slot + copies/8 is lossless. So >=3% flips is predicted by R2 as well as R1, and a non-Energy count channel of matched variance does not control for the lost slot identity. The real mechanism R1 would need is poor generalisation on rare (slot, copies) codes, such as 4 typed Energy on an opposing Bench slot. Ablation does not test that, and the candidate never states it.

(2) The metamorphic swap in Step 1(ii) is confounded by importance. Pokemon carrying Energy are usually the attackers, so any leftover non-invariance to position will be larger for them under every hypothesis. Every pilot sees the slot ordering through the per-slot numeric features, and slotbind-w also has per-slot owner embeddings. slotbind-w is also a poor positive control: it is an older, separately distilled pilot, so its age, teacher and architecture differ along with the count fix.

(3) R3 makes no Step-1 prediction, although it is also a misreading hypothesis. Step 1 could separate R1 from R3 by side and decision class: R3 is opponent-slot sensitivity on Energy Removal targeting, R1 is own-Bench sensitivity on attach, retreat and attack. The readout has no Energy Removal or discard-targeting class.

(4) Step 2 is underpowered and uses an unreliable noise bar. The 'bug-1/bug-2 gap' is a single draw of the A/A difference, not a variance, and could be near zero by chance. The verdict threshold of 0.03 with SE 0.013 per arm (SE of the difference about 0.018) is about 1.6 SE. The deck-out threshold of 3 points with SE 1.4 per arm (difference SE about 2.0) is about 1.5 SE. R1 and R3 differ only in the sign of a verdict shift that sits inside about ±2 SE.

(5) In Step 3, the 'unfixed' arm must be a distilled bug student, or the fork confounds the fix with distillation. One fork per arm from 479 tests escape, not prevention. The 10-iteration kill rule fires on 'within A/A on distance and C+S' just when the relapse is still forming (S03: 10-16 iterations), so it is biased toward a false null. The A/A spread of type sizes mid-trajectory reaches 14 (33/19), so a C+S threshold of 10 is inside the noise before about iteration 495.

The idea is sound and cheap. The design needs the changes below before its outcomes can be read.
required_changes: Replace or supplement the Step-1(i) ablation with a direct test of misreading. Fit linear or MLP probes on the pilot's per-token or per-slot hidden states to decode (a) typed Energy copies on each slot and (b) whether each slot's attacks can be paid. Report accuracy by slot (own Active, own Bench, opposing Active, opposing Bench) and by how often each (slot, copies) aux code appears in training data. Prediction: R1 shows accuracy dropping on Bench and opposing slots and on rare codes; R2 shows flat accuracy across slots. If the ablation is kept, ablate only the count_features projection for ENERGY tokens and leave the aux embedding intact, so slot-attachment information is not removed, and say so.

Normalise the metamorphic test per state. Use swap |dV| divided by that state's own '+1 Energy of the Pokemon's type' |dV|, or stratify swaps by that relevant-change magnitude, so that Energy-carrying swaps are not inflated simply because those Pokemon matter more. Add a positional-baseline arm: swap two Pokemon with identical attachments. This measures each pilot's non-invariance to position on its own.

Use matched positive and negative controls. Run Step 1 on the Step-2 students too: the fixed student against bug seeds 1 and 2, all distilled from the same scr-resetcap 499 teacher. Make that comparison the primary one; slotbind-w becomes a secondary reference. To keep Step 1 zero-training, the fixed student can be distilled first, which costs minutes.

Give R3 a Step-1 prediction and a decision class: sensitivity concentrated on opposing-slot ENERGY tokens and on Energy Removal or Super Energy Removal target choices. Give R1 its own: concentrated on own Bench, and on attach and retreat. That lets Step 1 separate R1 from R3, not only {R1, R3} from R2.

Step 2 power: use at least 2 fix seeds and 2 bug seeds, or bootstrap the A/A variance, instead of a single bug-1/bug-2 gap. Raise the game counts or use paired games with shared deals and swapped seats (common random numbers), so a verdict difference of 0.03 is at least 2.5 SE of the difference and a deck-out difference of 3 points is at least 2.5 SE.

Step 3: the unfixed fork must use a bug student distilled the same way. Run at least 2 reseeds per arm, or add an A/A fork pair. Use the A/A type-size spread at the same iteration (up to 14 mid-trajectory) as the bar for the Chansey+Snorlax count. At iteration 10, kill only on the probe (verdict difference < 0.03); evaluate deck shape and C+S at 20, past the 10-16 iteration relapse window. If affordable, add a prevention fork from an earlier, non-wall state.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: no violation. Fixing how an existing input is encoded is generic to card games (a per-entity count of attached cards). It carries to MTG and is not shaping. Human-vs-human states and human-list verdicts appear only as diagnostic readouts. The testbed is explicitly human-free.

Bug premise verified in the code. env/tokens.js:125 pushes ENERGY tokens with aux = i*8 + min(v,7). PILOT in rl/metagame.py:133 has count_features True and slot_bind False. rl/token_model.py:367 therefore feeds count_features(aux_in): raw slot*8+copies goes into the a/8 and a/32 scales and the thresholds 1..40. owner_and_count (token_model.py:43) already computes the correct copies and is export-safe, because slot_bind already uses it. So the fix is about one line plus a config flag.

R2 is plausible, and the design should say why. The 256-way aux embedding gives each (slot, copies) code its own vector, and slots[o+10] carries the slot's Energy-card total. The information is present; only the ordered count features are corrupted. This makes Step 1 the right gate.

Assets exist:
- runs/screens/scr-resetcap/population_it0499.pt and population_it0479.pt
- runs/screens/scr-gate479
- runs/pilot-v2
- runs/lab/branches/031-pilot-slotbind-w/warm.pt and checkpoint.pt
- rl/warmstart.py, which records teacher rollouts with rec:true, so state recording for Step 1 reuses existing paths

Machine: Step 2's three students and Step 3's two forks fit within the 3-screen, 2.7 GB / 3.5 GB budget.

Costs are underestimated:
1. Step 1 at 2-3 h is optimistic. The metamorphic swap must be done in token space. SLOT tokens sit at positions 1-12, and the slot feature rows are added by position (token_model encode: cat[g, s, pad]). So a swap must permute the SLOT card ids, the slot feature blocks, and the slot index in UNDER/TOOL aux and in the ENERGY aux (slot*8). The +1-Energy edit must change both the ENERGY token's copies and slots[o+10]. Decisions also need classifying as attach, retreat or attack from candidate kinds. Realistic cost is 4-6 h.
2. Step 2 needs more than the one-line fix. The new cfg key (e.g. energy_count) must be threaded through:
   - the TokenPointerNet cfg
   - the rl/train.py argument and its config-key list at about line 460
   - rl/gpu_matrix.py:35-38
   - rl/crossplay.py:35
   - the ONNX/puzzle export path
   - rl/tests.py

   That is about 2-3 h.
3. The 'shared human-free pilot testbed' does not exist, and Step 2 as written does not cost it:
   - rl/metagame.py has no frozen-draft or pilot-only mode; --fixed-decks is a 30% diagnosis share, and --freeze-pilot freezes the wrong side.
   - rl/train.py --matchups-file can train on fixed decks, but --init-from loads ckpt["model"] and builds the net from argparse flags. rl/warmstart.py writes a metagame checkpoint with "net" and "config".
   - The glue to build and validate the testbed is about half a day, unless C09 or C35 pays for it first.
   - The '~1 min an iteration' is unverified.
4. Step 3's warm start is not specified. The 499 students cannot be dropped into a 479 fork, so both arms need distilling from 479's pilot (fixed and unfixed, for symmetry).

Design notes:
- (a) The mean-ablation should target the count_proj input only, not the aux embedding, and say so.
- (b) slotbind-w also has owner embeddings, so Energy-free swaps move it too. The prediction that its ratio is about 1 or below 1.3 is the right expectation, but it comes from a different line (lab 360), not from 499.
- (c) Adoption should not depend on human-list movement. The fix corrects a bug, so it should be adopted on human-free non-inferiority (Elo against the bug arms and the A/A, and the puzzles), with the human readouts kept as diagnosis.
required_changes: Raise Step 1 to about 4-6 h. Spell out the token-space swap: SLOT token positions 1-12 together with their position-added slot feature rows; the slot index inside UNDER/TOOL aux and ENERGY aux (slot*8+copies); and the +1-Energy edit to both the ENERGY token's copies and slots[o+10].

Specify that the mean-ablation replaces only the count_features/count_proj input of ENERGY tokens. The 256-way aux embedding still distinguishes (slot, copies) and should be left intact or ablated as a separate arm. The control channel is a non-Energy count (e.g. HAND copies) of matched variance.

Add the Step 2 code cost (about 2-3 h): a new config flag threaded through the TokenPointerNet cfg, the rl/train.py argument and config-key list (~line 460), rl/gpu_matrix.py, rl/crossplay.py, the ONNX/puzzle export, and a rl/tests.py case that checks the Bench ENERGY count equals copies.

Cost the human-free testbed explicitly (about half a day) unless C09 or C35 builds it first. rl/metagame.py has no frozen-draft mode, and rl/train.py --init-from expects ckpt['model'], not a metagame checkpoint's 'net' and 'config'. Measure the per-iteration time before committing to 3 x 15 iterations.
Step 3: distil both fork arms (fixed and unfixed) from population_it0479's pilot with rl/warmstart.py, and include this in the half-day estimate.

Make adoption of the fix rest on human-free non-inferiority (Elo against both bug students beyond the bug-1/bug-2 gap, and the puzzles). Human-vs-human tempo and the walls' verdict stay diagnostic readouts, not the adoption criterion.

Note that slotbind-w's owner embeddings make Energy-free swaps move it too, and that it comes from the lab-360 line. Read it only as a ratio control, not as a matched positive control for absolute |dV|.

title: Open decklists: does seeing the opponent's whole list, which a 2000 player lacked, power the walls' stall plan?
rivals: R1 information leak: OPP_DECKLIST tokens (env/tokens.js:142, every decision) let the walls' pilot track the opponent's remaining Energy and resources, which a denial and deck-out plan uses more than a prize race
R2 irrelevant: play and verdicts do not depend on the opponent's list (#73: hiding both lists did not hurt)
R3 out of distribution: masking a stream the pilot always saw damages both seats, so a zero-shot probe cannot answer
design: Make list visibility per seat (env/env.js visibleDecks already honours showOpponentDecklist; make it per player and pass it through the Runner and gpu_matrix). Step 1: #147's protocol (3 walls of scr-resetcap 499 x 24 lists x 16 games, identical deals, greedy, the 499 pilot) in four arms: shown to both seats, hidden from the walls' seat, hidden from the lists' seat, hidden from both; plus C10's human-vs-human 8x8 panel with lists hidden from both. Step 2, if Step 1 shows R1 or R3: fine-tune two copies 10 iterations on C08's human-free testbed, one never shown the opponent's list, one control; rerun the walls verdict under each.

predictions.predicted: hiding the list from the walls' seat lowers their score >= 0.05 more than hiding it from the lists' seat lowers the lists'; the walls' deck-out wins fall; Step 2's hidden-list pilot rates the walls >= 0.05 lower
both seat effects <= 0.03 and within +/-0.03 of each other
each single-seat mask costs its own seat > 0.10, so Step 2 is needed

readout: Walls' verdict in the four arms (the interaction measures the asymmetry); the walls' wins by ending; human-vs-human pace with lists hidden.
noise_and_power: 1,152 games an arm: SE 0.013; paired deals put the asymmetry's SE at about 0.02, so 0.05 is detected at about 85% power.
kill_rule: Close under R2 (asymmetry < 0.03, both effects < 0.03). Under R3 run Step 2 only when a testbed slot is idle.
cost: About 1 h of code and 45 min of GPU for Step 1; Step 2 about 1.5 h on one GPU process.
distinct_from: #73-74's no-deck screen hid both lists from scratch for 40 iterations on the old joint encoder, judged vs SimpleBot, never on the walls or one seat (C07's no-deck pair is its zero-training pre-read). --no-deck-tokens hides own and opponent lists together; decklist dropout and H57's attention variants differ. The never-varied factor is per-seat visibility of the opponent's list.
rules_check: Evaluation-only probe; game-agnostic (opponent lists are hidden information in most card games). If R1 holds, hiding opponents' lists is a game-definition choice for Evan (C33 D6).
value: R1 gives a rule-faithful environment fix removing an information advantage behind the walls; R2 closes the open item in analysis section 9 in about two hours.
merged_from: pilot: Open decklists: does seeing the opponent's whole list, information a 2000 player lacked, power the walls' stall plan?

reviews.reasons:
I compared C09 with every family it could overlap and found no repeat. It is distinct in a factor that was never varied: per-seat visibility of the OPPONENT's list only, measured on the walls' verdict.

Overlaps I checked:
(1) H57, attention variants (N11). The no-deck screens #73-74 used --no-deck-tokens (deck_tokens=False), which masks the player's own unseen cards (MY_UNSEEN) and the opponent's list (OPP_DECKLIST) together for both seats. They trained from scratch for 40 iterations on the old joint encoder and were judged against SimpleBot and pilot-v2 ladders. They never touched the walls, the human-list panel or a single seat. H57's do-not-repeat list names --cand-self, --ability-text, --cross-layers, deck-inter, slot binding, vq4, memattn and depth. It does not name opponent-list masking. Decklist dropout (#73/74 Next) was never run, and C09 does not run it either.
(2) H60, deck-free board encoder (N11). That family is about where the deck stream enters the network. Visibility of the opponent's list was never varied there.
(3) The cosine probe in #65 (progress-log ~1465). It measured how the draft head reads decks, not play or verdicts.
(4) H03, H51, H52 and H23 (the stall and deck-out families). They vary reward, the clock and judging, never what the pilot can see.

A grep of progress-log.md for showOpponentDecklist, OPP_DECKLIST, opponent list and hidden list finds nothing after #74. ledger_meta.json's coverage gaps list this as an open gap ("Open decklists favour resource-denial plans"), saying only #73/#74 touched it. The four-arm seat design (shown to both, hidden from the walls, hidden from the lists, hidden from both), the paired deals, the walls' wins by ending and the human-vs-human pace with lists hidden have never been run. env/env.js and env/runner.js already have a whole-environment showOpponentDecklist flag, but no logged run ever used it, so the per-seat plumbing is new.

One caution for the designers, not a repetition problem. #65 found that removing the opponent's list pushes the pilot's deck encoding off its training distribution (cosine 0.36, against 0.64 with a list present, and "the glob bytes do not matter"). That makes R3 a likely outcome of a zero-shot mask. A cheap extra arm would keep Step 1 informative: give the walls' seat a wrong list (a random other list from the field) instead of no list. This keeps the stream in distribution while removing the true information. If the swapped-list arm moves the walls as much as the hidden arm, the effect is out-of-distribution damage (R3); if only the hidden arm moves them, the true information mattered (R1). This is optional and does not affect distinctness.

Diagnostic value is real and cheap. Per-seat visibility of the opponent's list has never been varied: #73-74 hid both lists from scratch on the old joint encoder. The change is small. env/env.js visibleDecks already gates OPP_DECKLIST (kind 10) on one flag, and rl/token_model.py masks deck kinds (9, 10) together, so a mask on kind 10 alone, applied per seat, is enough for a zero-shot probe. The readout is matched to the node: a pilot-side change is read out by the pilot playing fixed decks, and no drafting readout is used. R1 and R2 do predict different outcomes, so this is not a "relapses like the control" design.

Diagnosticity and statistics problems:

(1) Step 1 cannot separate R1 from R3 as written. Masking a stream the pilot always saw is out of distribution. That damage can itself be asymmetric: the walls' long stall games have roughly twice as many decisions conditioned on a corrupted deck encoding, so errors compound there. So "walls lose >= 0.05 more" is predicted by R3-with-asymmetric-fragility as well as by R1. Step 1 can close R2, and it can gate Step 2. It cannot confirm R1. One addition fixes this zero-shot: a decoy arm that gives the seat a wrong, in-distribution list (a random other human list) in place of removing tokens. If the pilot really uses the list (R1), the decoy hurts that seat as much as hiding it, or more. If the damage is pure distribution shift (R3), the decoy costs about 0 while hiding costs more than 0.10.

(2) The estimand is muddled. The readout says the interaction measures the asymmetry. The asymmetry is the difference of the two single-seat effects: 2*S_shown - S_wallsHidden - S_listsHidden, all in the walls' score. The interaction from the 2x2 (the both-hidden arm) tests whether the two effects add. Both should be pre-registered separately.

(3) The power figure is optimistic. With identical greedy deals, each paired difference has variance of about q/n, where q is the rate of games whose result changes between arms. At q around 0.3, each single-seat effect has an SE of about 0.016, and the asymmetry, combining two such effects, about 0.023. That gives about 70% power to detect 0.05 one-sided, or about 60% two-sided, not 85%. The effects also vary across 72 wall-list pairings, and only 3 walls carry the claim about the walls' plan, so the SE should come from a cluster bootstrap over the 24 lists.

(4) The R2 close is a point-estimate rule. "Both effects < 0.03" with an SE of 0.016-0.023 does not establish equivalence. It needs a confidence-interval rule: close only if the upper 90% bound of the asymmetry and of the walls' own-seat effect are both below 0.05. Results falling between 0.03 and 0.05 need a stated action.

(5) The outcome space is not fully mapped. Symmetric use (both seat effects of about 0.06 and equal) and the reverse asymmetry (the lists' seat relies on the list more) match no rival. Add an R4, symmetric use, so that every outcome maps to a conclusion.

(6) The turn limit must be fixed. R1's mechanism is deck-out stalling, and #147 shows the walls' score depends strongly on T. Step 1 should run with no limit as the primary arm, and the paired-deal rate q should be measured: RNG use can diverge after the first changed decision, which weakens the pairing.

(7) Step 2 is underpowered and biased against R1. One seed per arm at 10 iterations sits against an A/A seed noise of about 8.8 Elo (sigma), and a reseeded no-change run already moved -13.3 Elo, while 0.05 in score is about 17 Elo. A list-blind fine-tune is also a general handicap: a deck-blind pilot grown cold lost 54 Elo in #98. Lower skill favours the walls (link P), so the walls' rating would rise and could mask R1. Step 2 needs 2 seeds per arm, the competence check (bar 0.06) on both copies, and a stated kill rule.

(8) The human-vs-human pace panel with both lists hidden needs a shown-lists baseline from the same run, with the same deals. Otherwise any change in pace cannot be attributed to the lists.
required_changes: Add a decoy-list arm to Step 1, giving the walls' seat and the lists' seat each a wrong, in-distribution opponent list (a random other human list), so the zero-shot probe separates R1 (information used: the decoy hurts as much as hiding, or more) from R3 (distribution shift: the decoy costs about 0, hiding costs more than 0.10).

State that an asymmetry from Step 1 alone does not confirm R1. Asymmetric damage from distribution shift (long stall games compound a corrupted deck encoding) predicts the same sign. R1 can be confirmed only by the decoy arm or by Step 2.
Pre-register the estimands. Asymmetry = 2*S_shown - S_wallsHidden - S_listsHidden, in the walls' score. Report the interaction (additivity, using the both-hidden arm) separately.

Recompute power from the measured paired-discordance rate q and a cluster bootstrap over the 24 lists (and report the 3 walls separately). The likely power is about 60-75% for 0.05, not 85%. Either raise the games per pairing or accept 0.06 as the detectable effect.

Replace the point-estimate R2 close with a confidence-interval rule: close only if the upper 90% bound of the asymmetry and of the walls' own-seat effect are both below 0.05. State the action for results between 0.03 and 0.05.
Add R4 (symmetric use: both seat effects above 0.03 and equal) and the reverse-asymmetry outcome, so that every outcome maps to a conclusion.

Fix the turn limit: no limit as the primary arm (the deck-out mechanism), optionally plus T=60. Log the share of games that end by deck-out and the length distribution per arm. Verify that identical seeds keep deals and coin flips paired after decisions diverge.

Step 2: run 2 seeds per arm, check both fine-tuned copies against the competence bar (0.06), and note that a general skill loss in the list-blind copy biases the walls' verdict upward (against R1). Add an explicit Step 2 kill rule, such as stopping if the list-blind copy's competence drops more than 0.06.
Run the human-vs-human pace panel with a shown-lists baseline on the same deals, in the same run.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: clean. Step 1 is evaluation only. The human lists are opponents in a probe, exactly as in #147 and JF2, and never a training input. Step 2 trains only on C08's human-free testbed. Hiding the opponent's list is game-agnostic: an opponent's list is hidden information in MTG as well. It is not shaping, because it removes information rather than adding a game-specific signal. Adopting it as a game-definition change needs Evan's decision, which the candidate already notes.

Cost: overestimated, not underestimated, and the proposed build path is more work than needed.
(1) The #147 protocol is notes/scripts/probe_matchups.py on the GPU, not a 45-minute run. runs/probe/judge/resetcap499.log shows 1,152 games in 98 s (11.7 games/s, capped at 2 workers). Four arms plus an 8x8 human panel are about 10 minutes of GPU.
(2) Plumbing per-seat visibility through env.js, runner.js, remote_worker.js and gpu_matrix is unnecessary. remote_worker.js builds its Runners without showOpponentDecklist at lines 151, 202, 230, 306 and 365. The seat also alternates per game (iSeat), so the hide flag would have to follow the deck, not the player id. probe_matchups.py already supports --pilot-b, which uses models {0,1} with per-deck slots: the A decks always get model 0 and the B decks model 1, whatever the seat. A model-side flag is enough. In rl/token_model.py encode(), next to the existing deck_tokens mask at ~line 351, add mask &= tok_kind != 10 (OPP_DECKLIST only; MY_UNSEEN is kept, since a real player knows their own list). Load the same 499 checkpoint with that config override as pilot or pilot-b. The four arms are then the four combinations of masked and unmasked models. This is about 30 minutes of code including a rl/tests.py check that outputs do not depend on kind-10 tokens.
(3) The same flag serves Step 2. Add it to TokenPointerNet.config(), the train.py config key list (~line 461) and a metagame.py argument. Then training games need no env change at all.
(4) Step 2 is two fine-tunes (masked plus a control), each 10 iterations at about 6 minutes, so about 1 h on two of the 3 screen slots or about 2 h serially. "1.5 h on one GPU process" understates it slightly. It also depends on C08's testbed existing; without it, it falls back to forking 499, a wall state, which tests escape rather than cause.

Statistics: greedy play on identical deals is deterministic. The existing resetcap499.json (0.722) is the shown-to-both arm, and rerunning it is a free determinism check. Pairing per game makes the ~0.02 SE on the asymmetry plausible.

Caveat: the live attached-Energy count bug (token_model.py:367) affects all arms equally, so it does not confound the contrast. The readout should still note it.
required_changes: Implement the per-seat hide model-side, not env-side: add an option to TokenPointerNet.encode that masks only OPP_DECKLIST (kind 10) tokens, keeping MY_UNSEEN. Run the four arms through probe_matchups.py's existing --pilot / --pilot-b per-deck model slots, which follow the deck across seat swaps. Drop the env.js / Runner / remote_worker / gpu_matrix plumbing (remote_worker.js never passes showOpponentDecklist to its Runners, and the seat alternates per game).
Add a rl/tests.py check that, with the flag on, outputs do not change when kind-10 tokens change but do change with MY_UNSEEN.

Correct Step 1's cost to about 30 min of code and about 10 min of GPU (1,152 games in 98 s per runs/probe/judge/resetcap499.log). Reuse runs/probe/judge/resetcap499.json as the shown-to-both arm and rerun it once as a determinism check.

Step 2: put the flag in TokenPointerNet.config(), the train.py config keys and a metagame.py argument. Cost it as two 10-iteration processes (about 1 h on 2 screen slots, or about 2 h serially). Make it conditional on C08's testbed; forking 499 instead tests escape from the wall, not its cause.

In the readout, note that the attached-Energy count bug (token_model.py:367) is present in every arm, and that adopting hidden opponent lists in training is a game-definition change for Evan to approve.

title: Human-field tempo ladder and a powered competence panel: human-vs-human games at SimpleBot, greedy and one-turn-search strength (is the lists' slow play, 27-35% deck-outs, an in-turn skill gap?)
rivals: R1 in-turn tactics: the field is slow because the pilot misplays inside the turn (setup before attack, PlusPower/Gust lines); one-turn search already fixes this at play time (Trainer-first 60 -> 85-88%, PlusPower 31 -> 81%, #96)
R2 beyond the turn: slowness is multi-turn (Energy development, attacker sequencing) or from the objective (a deck-out win pays like a prize win); one-turn search cannot reach it
R3 deck-resource myopia: search speeds the prize race but burns the deck faster, as human-side search did against the walls (deck-outs 31% -> 51%, #139)
design: Evaluation only. (a) Panel: regenerate win-this-turn puzzles with env/tools/puzzles.js from 4,000 seeded heuristic games on the 24 lists (about 10x #92's 408: about 970 Trainer-first, 160 PlusPower-only, and a class led by prompt-opening Trainers such as Gust and Energy Removal), classed by the winning first move; add a line-scored mode (the agent plays the whole turn, prompts included, under fixed heads and tails, and must win; today's scorer checks only the first move). (b) Ladder: 8 lists, one per archetype (Marshall Haymaker, Lieu Wigglytuff, Guiao Hitmonchan/Magmar, Savage Sponge, Viray Rain Dance, Morris Electabuzz/Mr. Mime, Knight Clefable, Diamond Articuno/Hitmonchan/Scyther), all 64 ordered pairs x 16 = 1,024 games on fixed seeds, same seeds at every rung: SimpleBot both seats (pace reference: 14% deck-outs, 134 decisions a game, #32); pilot-v2 greedy; scr-resetcap 499 greedy; scr-ctl479 499 greedy (near-A/A of resetcap: same 479 state, reseed 2); scr-resetcap 499 with one-turn psearch k4 d4 on both seats, GPU-served (C03); later a CRN k8 d2 rung. Every rung is also scored on the panel; search is the positive control the competence score never had (H65).

predictions.predicted: searched vs greedy: Prizes taken per side by game turn 20 up >= 0.5, median prize-win turn down >= 5, deck-outs from about 35% to <= 22%; searched agents solve >= 80% of line-scored PlusPower and Gust-led puzzles
pace moves < 0.3 Prizes by turn 20 and deck-outs < 3 points, though search lifts first-move puzzle scores as in #96
pace up >= 0.5 Prizes by turn 20 but deck-outs flat or up, with more draw-Trainer plays per game

readout: Per rung: deck-out share, median prize-win turn, Prizes per side by turn 20, share won by Prizes before turn 30, decisions per game; per-class puzzle solves, first-move and line-scored; the ctl479-resetcap gap as the fork-noise band.
noise_and_power: 1,024 games: deck-out SE about 1.4 points; paired rungs about 1.6-1.8 (5 points at about 85% power, 8 at > 99%); pace SE about 0.05 Prizes. Puzzles: 160 PlusPower-only SE 0.037 (+0.10 at about 75%); 970 Trainer-first SE 0.016. The A/A band is expected at 2-4 points, never measured.
kill_rule: Stop the searched rung after 512 games if deck-outs are within +/-3 points and pace within +/-0.2 Prizes of greedy (R2). Skip the CRN rung unless C03 shows CRN changes searched choices.
cost: Puzzle generation 1-2 CPU-hours in two processes (#92); line scoring about 2 h of code; greedy and SimpleBot rungs 3-5 min each; searched rung 25-30 min GPU-served (#148: 200 searched games in about 320 s). About 4 h; no screen slot.
distinct_from: JF2 (#149) played the lists against each other greedy only; #139/#146/#147 searched only walls-vs-list games (H05/H22 do-not-repeat); #50 searched one seat against SimpleBot and read win rate; #92/#96 scored 408 puzzles by first move only (H06/H65 do-not-repeat: re-scoring them on measured checkpoints). New: human-vs-human search on both seats, pace metrics, powered and line-scored classes, an A/A band ('more puzzles per class' and 'positive control' are H65 untested).
rules_check: Evaluation and diagnosis only: lists are evaluation decks and puzzle sources; SimpleBot is a coarse reference (H61); endings and Prize pace are game-agnostic.
value: Decides which pilot investments the field needs: R1 -> search distillation (C37) and searched judging (C38); R2 -> horizon and objective levers (C35, C36, C12); R3 -> a deck-resource-aware leaf value. Builds the panel (line-scored classes, tempo metrics, A/A band) that C08, C09, C11, C12, C22 and C35-C37 read instead of deck-shape stall rules (analysis section 4).
merged_from: pilot: Human-field tempo ladder: is the human lists' slow play (27-35% deck-outs in H-H games) an in-turn skill gap? H-H games at SimpleBot, greedy and one-turn-search strength, plus the powered competence panel every pilot test needs

reviews.reasons:
Checked C10 against every family it could overlap (H03, H05, H06, H11, H14, H18, H19, H21, H22, H23, H49-H53, H61, H62, H65) and against progress-log #17, #32, #50, #92, #96, #139, #141, #145-#149. It does not rerun anything on a do-not-repeat list. It is distinct in configuration and in what it reads out.

1. Which games are searched. Every searched game in the log so far was walls vs human lists (#139 human seat, #145-147 both seats, one or two turns; H05, H19 and H22 do-not-repeat), or one seat against SimpleBot read by win rate (#50). Nobody has run one-turn psearch on both seats of human-list vs human-list games. Grep finds psearch only in #50, #96, #139 and #145-147.

2. What is measured. This is the first test of the slowness #149 found (Found 3: 27-35% deck-outs in H-H games, the prize-race deficit). It asks whether that slowness is an in-turn skill gap. The readouts are new: deck-out share, Prizes per side by turn 20, median prize-win turn, and share won by Prizes before turn 30. JF2 ran the same H-H field greedy only. `rl/gpu_matrix.py` and the JF2 jsons store only endings counts and decisions per game, with no per-game turn or Prize data. So the greedy rungs have to be replayed with pace logging. That is not a repeat, and at 3-5 min a rung it costs little.

3. The panel. The H65 verifier lists both "more puzzles per class" (only #92's 408 exist: 16 PlusPower-only, 97 Trainer-first) and "a positive control" as genuinely untested. Line-scored whole-turn puzzle solving is new: today `puzzles.js score` checks only the first move. Three do-not-repeat entries are respected:
- H06 "re-scoring the A2 puzzles on measured checkpoints": the candidate generates a new, larger set and adds a new scoring mode.
- H05/H06 "psearch k4/k8 on A2 puzzles at 220": the candidate uses different checkpoints and line scoring.
- H65 "distilled-search puzzle inflation": the candidate uses no training at all.

4. The A/A band from ctl479 vs resetcap at 499 has never been measured for pace, and H62 lists A/A calibration with more replicates as untested.

5. Rules. It is evaluation and diagnosis only, so rule 1 holds:
- The human lists serve as evaluation decks and puzzle sources only.
- SimpleBot is used only as a coarse pace reference, which is allowed under H61. It is not used as a fitness or adoption signal.
- The puzzles are not trained on, which avoids the human-prior exclusion in the H06 verifier.

6. Confounds to note, not repetition problems:
(a) The attached-Energy count bug is live (analysis section 9, `token_model.py:367`). It may make the pilot misread its own Energy development, which is exactly R2's multi-turn channel. The readout should name it as a confound of R2, or add one slot-bind pilot rung if one exists.
(b) The pilot sees both decklists. This does not affect this design.

7. Cost and readout fit. The design takes no screen slot. Its kill rule is specific to the node, as analysis section 4 asks.
required_changes: Optional, not required for distinctness: add a line to the readout naming the live attached-Energy count bug (rl/token_model.py:367, slot_bind off) as a confound that could pass for R2 ('beyond the turn', Energy development). If a slot-bind pilot checkpoint at a comparable strength exists (#116), add it as a greedy rung; if not, record the caveat.

Optional: the JF2 jsons (runs/probe/jf2_human24_*.json) hold only endings counts and decisions per game. State that the greedy rungs are replayed with per-game turn and Prize logging, not taken from JF2, so the work is not double-counted as new.

reviews.reasons:
Diagnosticity is good. The three rivals predict different outcomes on the main paired readout (searched vs greedy on the same checkpoint, lists and seeds). R1 predicts pace up and deck-outs down a lot. R2 predicts pace and deck-outs flat while first-move puzzle scores rise. R3 predicts pace up with deck-outs flat or up and more draw-Trainer plays. Not every outcome is predicted by all live hypotheses, and the puzzle panel is correctly framed as a positive control (search must visibly change play) rather than as a discriminator, since R1 and R2 both predict a lift there.

Node match is right. This is a pilot question read on pilot readouts (pace, endings, in-turn puzzles) with the decks held fixed, and it does not use deck-shape or SimpleBot-as-fitness readouts (H61 and H63 are respected). Rules are respected: the lists and puzzles are used for evaluation only and nothing feeds training. It is distinct from the do-not-repeats (#139/#145-147 were walls vs lists; #96 was first-move only on 408 puzzles), and it fills H65's untested gaps (more puzzles per class, a positive control).

Power checks out roughly. At p=0.35 and n=1,024, the deck-out SE is 1.5 points, so an unpaired difference has SE about 2.1. The claimed paired 1.6-1.8 is credible only through stratification by ordered pair, because the trajectories diverge after the first differing decision, so the fixed seeds give little true common-random-number pairing. Even at SE 2.1, R1's predicted drop of 13 or more points is detected easily. The 5-point claim at 85% power is optimistic, closer to 65-80%. The pace SE of about 0.05 is plausible. The kill rule is calibrated against R1's large predicted effect and does not wrongly kill R3, which requires pace to move. Short-horizon bias does not apply because nothing is trained. The kill saves only about 13 GPU-minutes, so it is optional.

Weaknesses:
(1) R2 bundles two mechanisms that this readout cannot separate: multi-turn horizon (Energy development, sequencing) and the objective (a deck-out win pays like a prize win). They lead to different levers (C35/C36 vs C12), so an R2 result would not say which pilot investment to make.
(2) The live attached-Energy count bug (token_model.py:367, slot_bind off) is a confound for R2. One-turn search with the same bugged value net cannot fix misread Energy counts, so a flat result would read as 'beyond the turn' when the cause is a feature bug.
(3) 'Median prize-win turn' conditions on games won by Prizes. If search turns deck-outs into late prize wins, it can rise while play gets faster. It should not be a decisive metric.
(4) The thresholds leave intermediate outcomes unassigned (e.g. deck-outs -7, pace +0.3), and there are many readouts without a pre-registered primary. That invites post-hoc reading.
(5) One ctl479-resetcap pair is n=1 for a fork-noise band (H62 warns against bars from 1-2 A/A forks). For the main searched-vs-greedy contrast, the relevant noise is game sampling, which a bootstrap over pairs and seeds gives directly.
(6) Line-scored puzzles involve hidden draws as well as coin flips. Fixed heads and tails is not enough: deck order must be fixed, solvability must be verified under that fixed order, and the searched agent's determinizations must not see the true order.
(7) The deck-out share depends heavily on the pairing (Clefable and Sponge lists may stall by design). Tempo-vs-tempo pairs are the cleanest test of 'fast decks played slowly'.
required_changes: Pre-register one primary contrast and a full decision table covering intermediate outcomes. Primary: searched minus greedy on scr-resetcap 499, deck-out share and Prizes per side by turn 20, paired by ordered pair x seed, with SE from a bootstrap over pairs. Map every cell of (pace change: <0.2 / 0.2-0.5 / >=0.5) x (deck-out change: down >=5 / within +/-5 / up >=5) to R1, R2, R3 or 'inconclusive', and do not read R2 on a flat result unless the search rung shows its own instrumentation working: the decision-change rate from greedy plus the puzzle positive control.

Split R2 with an endings readout. For deck-out games, record the Prize differential at the end and whether the deck-out winner was behind on Prizes, plus turns with no attack while an attack was legal. Objective-driven stalling predicts winners who were behind and deliberate passes. Horizon limits predict deck-outs with even Prizes and slow Energy build-up (turn of the first fully powered attacker).

Handle the live attached-Energy count bug. Add a rung with a slot_bind pilot (corrected count, #116) at greedy and searched strength if a comparable checkpoint exists. If none does, state explicitly that an R2 verdict cannot exclude the feature bug, and report turns-to-first-powered-attacker per rung.

Do not use 'median prize-win turn' as a decisive metric, because it conditions on the outcome. Use unconditional pace instead: Prizes by turn 10/20/30 and a restricted mean time to the 6th Prize, with deck-outs and draws treated as censored.

Report deck-out share stratified by pair type: tempo-vs-tempo (Haymaker, Hitmonchan/Magmar, Rain Dance, Electabuzz/Mr. Mime, Wigglytuff), and pairs involving Clefable, Sponge or Articuno. Make the tempo-vs-tempo stratum the main readout for 'fast decks played slowly', and check it has enough games (~25 ordered pairs x 16 = 400; SE about 2.4 points).

Make line-scored puzzles deterministic. Fix deck order and coin outcomes from a stored seed, verify that each puzzle is solvable under that exact fixed state, and make sure the searched agent's determinizations re-sample hidden cards and never read the true order. Report first-move and line scores per class with binomial CIs.
Treat the ctl479-resetcap gap as descriptive only (n=1). Do not set a noise bar from it. Use the analytic or bootstrap SE for every within-checkpoint contrast.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: pass. The design is evaluation and diagnosis only. The 24 lists are used as evaluation decks and as the source of the puzzles. HeuristicAgent (generation) and SimpleBot (the pace rung) are reference bots and never touch training. Prize pace, game endings and win-this-turn puzzles carry over to MTG. Nothing feeds a draft or PPO signal. One condition: the panel may rank pilot variants between runs, as s1 did in the lab. It must never become an in-run selection or reward term.

Feasibility: the parts all exist, but the 4 h estimate is too low (realistic: about 7-9 h of code and checks plus 2-4 CPU-hours), and the instrumentation the readouts need is missing. Checked against the code:
(1) env/tools/puzzles.js generate exists and splits across processes (--start), but --max defaults to 300 per process, so 4,000 games need --max raised. No timing for #92's 400 games is recorded, so the 1-2 CPU-hour estimate is unverified. The DFS replays from base at every node inside a prompt (NODE_LIMIT 4000), and with 3 screens running only about 4 threads are free.
(2) score asks for the first move only. The line-scored mode is new code: hand the agent the replayed env with the coin fixed (fixedRng heads, then tails); play the agent's own choices through the whole turn, prompts included; score both coins. It must also settle three things the generator settles implicitly. (a) Opponent decisions inside the turn, such as a new Active after a knockout: score them adversarially (every option must still lose), as winsWith does. (b) Draw Trainers (Bill, Oak, Gambler and the rest of UNPROVABLE): under a fixed shuffle the deck order is known, so a line can 'win' on luck the agent could not see. Mask these or report them apart. (c) An oracle self-check: replaying a stored winning line must score 100%. Realistic cost is 3-4 h, not 2.
(3) The ladder readouts are not recorded. runner.js returns turns, ending and final prizesLeft only. 'Prizes per side by game turn 20' needs a prize snapshot at a set turn (copy the valueAtTurn hook at runner.js:134). R3's 'draw-Trainer plays per game' needs a per-game count of Trainer plays by card class. rl/gpu_matrix.py: plays only unordered i<j pairs (mirrors are filled with 0.5, so the 8 mirrors of '64 ordered pairs' need explicit pairs); does not pass judgeSearch or mark jobs search:true (remote_worker.js supports both since #148, but gpu_matrix never sends them); and its main() writes no per-game rows. env/tools/matrix.js (the SimpleBot rung) drops ending and turns from its results. About 2 h in all.
(4) The searched rung: #148 played 200 searched games in about 320 s with 4 workers beside a screen, so 1,024 human-list games take about 25-45 min, more under GPU and CPU contention. Using 14 workers would crowd the 3 screens' CPU. 'No screen slot' holds only if it runs with about 4 workers or in a gap between screens. Puzzle scoring with psearch runs on CPU ONNX: about 4,000 puzzles x 4-5 pilots x (first-move + 2 coins line-scored), roughly 1-2 CPU-hours more. scr-ctl479 499 needs an ONNX export; resetcap499.onnx and pilot-v2 it349 exist.

Statistics: the puzzle SEs (0.037 and 0.016) assume independent puzzles. The generator keeps several consecutive endgame positions per game, so SEs must be a cluster bootstrap by game, after removing near-duplicates. Otherwise the 160 PlusPower-only puzzles are worth fewer than claimed. The ladder SEs and the kill rule are reasonable, and so is the ctl479-resetcap A/A band. Note: that band also includes training-path divergence over 479-499, not only seed noise.

The diagnostic is distinct from #92/#96 (first move only, 408 puzzles), #139/#146/#147 (walls only) and JF2 (greedy only). It is worth running.
required_changes: Re-cost at about 7-9 h of code and checks plus 2-4 CPU-hours (generation, and psearch puzzle scoring on every rung), not 4 h. Time one 400-game generate part first (it equals #92's whole run) before committing to 4,000 games, and pass --max above the default 300.

Add the missing instrumentation to the scope and cost: a per-seat prize snapshot at game turn 20 in env/runner.js (copy the valueAtTurn hook) carried into the remote_worker.js result rows; per-game Trainer-play counts by card class (for R3); ending and turns kept in env/tools/matrix.js (SimpleBot rung); in rl/gpu_matrix.py, explicit mirror pairs, judgeSearch with search:true jobs (both seats PolicySearchAgent, k4 d4), and a per-game results dump.

Define the line-scored mode exactly: fixed-coin heads and tails both required; opponent decisions inside the turn scored adversarially (every option must lose), as winsWith does; draw Trainers in UNPROVABLE either masked or their lines reported apart, since a fixed shuffle leaks deck order; an oracle self-check that replaying a generator's winning line scores 100%.
Compute puzzle-class SEs by cluster bootstrap over source games, after removing near-duplicate consecutive positions. Restate the PlusPower-only power from that bootstrap.
Run the searched rung with about 4 workers, alongside screens (expect 30-45+ min), or in a gap between screens. Do not claim 'no screen slot' at 14 workers.
State that panel scores rank pilot variants between runs and are never an in-run selection or reward input. Export scr-ctl479 499 to ONNX for the puzzle rungs.

title: Prompt decisions: is the pilot's Trainer devaluation decided inside the Trainer's prompt (Gust target, Energy Removal target, Computer Search fetch)?
rivals: R1 prompt incompetence: the pilot answers prompts badly, which would explain why only prompt-free draw Trainers (Oak, Bill, Gambler: 0.64-0.76 on #92's panel) beat basic Energy while search, disrupt and tempo groups score 0.36-0.52, and why a prize follows Gust on only 0.7% of Gust turns (#92)
R2 main-phase timing: prompt answers are near best; the loss is when the card is played (#92's conclusion)
R3 credit fades in long games (N10): decisions 80+ from the end of walls-era games carry little of an option's effect, so early tempo decisions barely learn
design: Code facts: qprobe and tsearch skip decisions with an open prompt (env/remote_worker.js:276, 355); psearch plays prompts greedily (env/agents.js:354); Game.clone throws on an open prompt (env/game.js:290), so prompts are probed from the state before the Trainer. (1) Census: share of asked decisions that are prompts, by type and card, in human-vs-human and population games. (2) Line-scored puzzles: re-score puzzles whose winning first move opens a prompt, playing the whole turn, against prompt-free-led ones (PlusPower's target sits in the main-phase option, env/legal.js isTargetedTrainer). (3) Prompt Q-probe: extend qprobe with key sequences (Runner jobs take 'first'; add a sequence, as puzzles.js replays option paths into prompts); at main-phase decisions where a prompt-opening Trainer is legal, play it, then each first-step answer (up to 8, the pilot's included), 16 re-dealt lines each to the end of the game (greedy, #80's protocol, then sampled); split-half gap max_a Q - Q(pilot's answer) and agreement with the Q-best answer, per card and prompt type, vs main-phase decisions in the same games. Pilots scr-resetcap 499 and pilot-v2; decks the 24 lists (evaluation) and the 499 population. The sampled walls-vs-list run also gives the credit-share table by decisions to the end (R3). (4) Only if the prompt gap is >= 0.5 points: trainer_value.py panel (8 lists x 4 groups x 64 games, identical deals) under greedy, prompt-only lookahead (one-turn rollouts from the pre-Trainer state, main phase greedy) and main-only psearch.

predictions.predicted: line scoring drops prompt-led solves >= 15 points below first-move rates vs <= 5 for prompt-free-led; prompt gap >= 1.0 point for Gust, Energy Removal, Super Energy Removal, Computer Search and Item Finder (the order of their whole greedy timing gains, +0.6 to +2.1, #80); Q-best agreement <= 50% on prompts with >= 3 answers; prompt-only lookahead lifts search, disrupt and tempo groups >= 0.06 each, draw group within +/-0.02
both puzzle kinds lose <= 5 points; prompt gaps <= 0.3 with agreement >= 75%; prompt-only lookahead moves the panel <= 0.02 while main-only psearch carries the gains
credit share at lambda 0.95 <= 0.3 in the 80+ decisions-to-end bin of walls-vs-list games (A4-era games gave 0.56-0.75 overall, #75); otherwise >= 0.5 in every bin

readout: Prompt share of decisions; first-move vs line-scored solves by class; gap and Q-best agreement at prompt vs main-phase decisions per card; Trainer-panel groups under three agents; credit share and alignment by decisions to the end.
noise_and_power: Line scoring is paired; on the current suite (perhaps 40-60 prompt-led puzzles) only >= 20-point drops are detectable, on C10's expanded suite SE about 0.02. About 1,500 prompt probes per card group with 16 lines per answer: gap 95% CI about +/-0.3-0.5 points (#79-80: +/-0.3-0.9), agreement SE 0.013. Panel: 512 games per group per agent, group-difference SE about 0.02 (0.06 at about 80% power).
kill_rule: Stop after steps 1-2 if prompts are < 5% of asked decisions in human-vs-human games or line scoring costs prompt-led puzzles <= 5 points more than prompt-free ones. Stop step 3 after 500 probes if the gap is < 0.3 with a CI excluding 1.0, and skip step 4.
cost: Census and line scoring 2-3 h with code; key sequences and answer enumeration about half a day; probe runs about 35-40 min each (#79-80) x 2 pilots x 2 line modes, about 2.5 h; step 4 about 1.5-2 h GPU-served. No screen slot.
distinct_from: H08's verifier lists probing prompt and setup decisions that qprobe skips, and the credit probe on a walls-era pilot over walls-vs-list games, as untested; H06's lists psearch on the Trainer-value panel (#92 Next) as never run. Not #79-80 (main-phase only, base it79/pilot-v2 on archived lists: H08/H09 do-not-repeat) nor #92's greedy panel (H07). The never-varied factor is the decision class: prompt vs main phase.
rules_check: Diagnosis only: lists are evaluation decks; prompt-only lookahead is play-time evaluation over legal options and clones (game-agnostic); nothing enters training.
value: Locates the Trainer deficit drafting follows (drafts cut what the pilot cannot use, #92): R1 -> search over prompt answers in the judge and C37's targets, prompt-heavy branch starts (C36), a pointer over prompt cards; R2 keeps main-phase sequencing as the target; R3 puts horizon levers (C35, C36) before representation work.
merged_from: pilot: Prompt decisions: is the pilot's Trainer devaluation decided inside the Trainer's prompt (Gust target, Energy Removal target, Computer Search fetch)? No probe or search has ever looked there.

reviews.reasons:
C11 is distinct because it measures a decision class no earlier probe has scored: answers given inside a Trainer's prompt rather than main-phase choices. I read the whole ledger digest and grepped the progress log for "prompt", "line scoring", "first move" and "qprobe".

**Never-varied factor: decision class (prompt vs main phase)**
- qprobe has only ever sampled main-phase decisions with no prompt open (log, #75 Done text).
- #92's puzzles score the first move only. #92's Trainer panel and #96's psearch run never look at prompt answers.
- ledger_meta records this as a coverage gap. It says choices inside Oak, Computer Search, Item Finder and Energy Removal "have never been measured".
- The verifier lists it in H08's untested variants: "probing prompt and setup decisions ... The current qprobe skips ...".
- The only prompt-related figure in the log is #-era distillation imitation accuracy on prompts (75.0%, log line ~405). That is agreement with a teacher, not Q-value or competence, so it is not a repeat.

**Other steps match listed untested variants, not do-not-repeat entries**
- Step 3's R3 credit table uses a walls-era pilot (scr-resetcap 499) on walls-vs-list games, binned by decisions to the end. This is H08's other untested variant and ledger_meta's top-untested item.
- Step 4, main-only psearch on the trainer_value panel, is #92's Next. H06's verifier lists it as never run. The prompt-only lookahead arm is new.
- Step 2 re-scores the puzzles over the whole turn instead of the first move. That is a new scoring rule, not the H06 do-not-repeat "re-scoring A2 puzzles ... on measured checkpoints" with the old protocol. It also does not repeat #96's psearch on the puzzles.

**No do-not-repeat configuration is rerun**
- H08/H09: qprobe on base it79 / pilot-v2 over the archived lists, main phase only, sampled and greedy (#79-80).
- H07: card_ablation and the greedy trainer_value group panel (#92).
- H05/H06: psearch on the 408 puzzles at 220 (#96).
- H11: expert-iteration targets.

**Rules**
- Diagnosis only. The lists are evaluation decks, lookahead is play-time over legal options, and nothing enters training.

**Minor overlap, not blocking**
- Step 3's within-game main-phase control on pilot-v2 over the 24 lists overlaps #79-80. The new information is the prompt arm. The main-phase arm is justified only as a same-games paired control and should not be reported as a new main-phase result. Reusing or citing #79-80's numbers is the alternative.
- On scr-resetcap 499, both arms are new.

The core of C11 is diagnostic, and the readout fits the node. It is a pilot-level question (N2, N10) measured with pilot-level readouts: Q-probe gaps at prompt vs main-phase decisions, and the Trainer panel under three agents. No training is involved, so short-horizon bias does not apply. I checked the code facts against the repo and they hold: qprobe and tsearch skip `d.prompt` (env/remote_worker.js:276, 355), psearch plays prompts greedily (env/agents.js:354), `Game.clone` throws on an open prompt (env/game.js:290), and `isTargetedTrainer` is in env/legal.js. Per H08's verifier, nothing has probed this decision class before, so it does not repeat H06-H09.

Diagnosticity and statistics problems:

(a) Q-best agreement is not diagnostic as specified. With 16 lines per answer (8 per split half) and up to 8 answers, the noisy argmax and near-tied answers keep agreement low even for a perfect pilot. Computer Search fetches between interchangeable cards are the clearest case. So "<= 50% agreement" is also predicted under R2. The metric needs a noise ceiling and a tie rule.

(b) Absolute gap thresholds are fragile. The gap depends on the rollout policy (#80: +1.32 greedy vs +0.35 sampled) and on the number of options. The design already measures main-phase decisions in the same games, so the predictions should be stated as a paired, option-count-matched contrast (prompt gap minus main gap). As written, a measured gap of 0.3-1.0 falls between the R1 and R2 predictions. At about +/-0.5 CI that is a likely outcome, and it gives no verdict. Step 4's gate (0.5) also does not match R1's threshold (1.0).

(c) The R1 prediction is per card for five cards, but 1,500 probes is a per-group figure. Gust, Energy Removal, Super Energy Removal and Item Finder plays per game may be too rare to reach +/-0.5 per card. No per-card n is given from the census.

(d) Line-scored puzzles are confounded by line length. A prompt-led win (Gust, then an attack) needs more follow-up decisions than many prompt-free ones, and the follow-up decisions are main-phase play. R2 therefore also predicts a larger drop for prompt-led lines, and its "<= 5 points" is unjustified. With 40-60 puzzles, the design says only >= 20-point drops are detectable, yet R1 predicts >= 15. So step 2 is underpowered for its own prediction, and it should not be allowed to kill step 3. Win-this-turn puzzles allow exact scoring instead: force the winning Trainer, label each prompt answer winning or losing by exhaustive search over the rest of the turn, and score the pilot's answer. That isolates the prompt step without noise.

(e) The census kill gate is miscalibrated. No rival predicts the share of all decisions that are prompts, and a Trainer's value can turn on a prompt that is a small share of decisions. The gate should be feasibility (enough non-trivial prompt probes per group), not that share.

(f) An unlisted live rival makes the readout ambiguous. analysis.md section 9 records that the attached-Energy count bug is live (rl/token_model.py:367, slot_bind off): an Energy token on slot 5 reads as 42. Energy Removal, Super Energy Removal and many Gust targets depend on the opponent's attached Energy. A large gap there could come from the input bug rather than from learning (R1). Read that way, R1 would point the follow-up at the wrong levers (search over prompt answers, a pointer over prompt cards).

(g) Probing only the first prompt step misses the Computer Search fetch named in the title. The first step there is the discard of two cards, and Energy Removal also has two steps (target, then which Energy).

(h) R3 is orthogonal rather than a rival on the prompt readouts. Its prediction leaves 0.3-0.5 unassigned, and no per-bin n is given.

These are fixable within the stated cost, hence revise.
required_changes: State the step-3 predictions as a paired contrast: prompt gap minus main-phase gap, in the same games and matched on option count (or a k-matched subsample). Set rules with no gap between them, e.g. R1 if the contrast is >= +0.5 with a CI excluding 0; R2 if the contrast is <= 0, or its upper CI bound is < 0.5. Align step 4's gate and the kill rule with these thresholds; at present the gate is 0.5 against R1's 1.0, and 0.3-1.0 is unassigned.

Give Q-best agreement a noise ceiling: report split-half self-agreement of the Q-best answer. Count the pilot as agreeing when its answer is within the split-half CI of the best, or collapse answers that are interchangeable (same card name or same effect). Otherwise drop agreement as a discriminating readout, since R2 also predicts <= 50% on noisy, many-answer prompts.

Size the runs per card group from the census. Give the expected prompt-Trainer plays per game for Gust, Energy Removal, Super Energy Removal, Computer Search and Item Finder, and either collect >= ~1,000 probes per card or pre-register pooled groups (target prompts: Gust, ER, SER; search prompts: CS, IF) with a stated n and CI per group.

Fix the confound in step 2. Replace or augment line scoring with exact prompt scoring on win-this-turn puzzles: force the winning Trainer, label each prompt answer winning or losing by exhaustive search over the rest of the turn, and score whether the pilot's answer wins. Or match prompt-free puzzles to prompt-led ones on decisions remaining in the turn. Remove R2's unjustified '<= 5 points' line-scoring prediction.

Do not let the underpowered step 2 (40-60 puzzles, only >= 20-point drops detectable vs R1's predicted 15) or the prompt-share census (which no rival predicts differently) kill step 3. Make the step 1-2 gate feasibility only: enough prompt decisions with >= 2 non-equivalent answers to reach the stated n within budget.

Add the live attached-Energy count bug (rl/token_model.py:367, slot_bind off) as a rival R4. It predicts that the gap concentrates in prompts whose correct answer depends on the opponent's attached Energy (ER, SER, many Gust targets), varies with the target's slot index, and shrinks under a slot_bind checkpoint (#116). Stratify the gap by the target's slot and by whether the target choice depends on Energy, and add a slot_bind pilot if one exists, so that R1's follow-ups are not built on a representation bug.

Probe every step of multi-step prompts, conditioning on the pilot's earlier answers: Computer Search's discard and then its fetch; Energy Removal's target and then the Energy. Probing the first step only would not measure the Computer Search fetch named in the title.

Make R3 its own sub-readout with a contrast. Compare credit share by decisions-to-end bin for the walls-era pilot (scr-resetcap 499, walls-vs-list games) against the A4-era bins of #75/#77, give the n per bin, and close the 0.3-0.5 zone (e.g. R3 if the 80+ bin is below the A4-era bin by more than its CI).

reviews.reasons:
Rules: the candidate passes. It is diagnosis only. The 24 human lists are used only as evaluation decks, the prompt-only lookahead in step 4 is a play-time evaluation agent over legal options and clones, and nothing enters training. Prompts are a generic engine concept, so the method carries to MTG.

Code facts I checked, all accurate:
- qprobe and tsearch skip decisions with an open prompt (remote_worker.js, the `d.prompt` return).
- psearch plays prompts greedily (agents.js act).
- Game.clone throws on an open prompt (game.js:290).
- Runner jobs take a single `first` key (runner.js:56). Turning that into a key sequence is about 10 lines.
- puzzles.js already replays option paths into prompts.

Feasibility is real, but the design has a gap. Many of the target cards have multi-step prompts:
- Computer Search (ryuu-play set-base/computer-search.js) first opens a ChooseCardsPrompt to discard 2 of the other hand cards, with min 2, max 2 and allowCancel. The fetch from the deck is a second prompt. Item Finder works the same way. So "each first-step answer" probes the discard choice plus a cancel option, not the fetch the title names.
- The fetch prompt picks cards by fullName from the deck (chooseCardsSpace). With redeal on, which is #79-80's protocol, the deck and prizes are reshuffled in every line. The pilot's fetch key can then be missing from a copy, and the runner returns "not on offer" errors that thin the line samples unevenly.
- Energy Removal and Super Energy Removal are also two-step: the Pokemon first, then the Energy.

Cost is underestimated. #79-80 got about 4,400 probes over all Trainers in 1,000 games: up to 6 options, 16 lines each, about 360k lines in 31-37 min. C11 asks for about 1,500 probes per card group with up to 8 answers. That is up to about 190k lines per group, roughly 600-750k lines a run over 4-5 cards. Walls-era games from scr-resetcap 499 are longer (80+ decisions), so each line costs more than in the A4 era. Prompt-opening Trainers are offered at only a fraction of decisions, so more games or a higher probe rate are needed. A realistic figure is about 1-1.5 h a run, x 2 pilots x 2 line modes, so about 4-6 h of probe runs, not 2.5 h.

"No screen slot" holds only for screen accounting. The probes need a GPU-served pilot (RemoteAgent) and a 64-way concurrent CPU runner. With 3 screens at about 3.5 GB GPU each, on 16 threads, the probes will slow the screens or be slowed by them.

The kill rules and predictions are well formed. The step-2 kill (prompt share and line scoring) is cheap and comes first, which is good.
required_changes: Define the probed prompt step per card instead of 'first-step answer'. Computer Search and Item Finder: hold the pilot's discard pair (or enumerate a few discard pairs) and enumerate the fetch, which is the decision the title asks about. Energy Removal and Super Energy Removal: probe the target Pokemon, then the Energy. Gust: the bench target. Exclude cancel from the answers, or report it separately as the decision not to play the card.

Handle redeal for fetches from the deck. Either run the fetch probes with own-side redeal off (opponent's hidden cards still re-dealt), or report per probe the share of lines with the answer not on offer and drop probes where that share is above zero. Report line errors per card.

Revise the cost to about 4-6 h of probe runs (up to 8 answers x 16 lines x about 1,500 probes per group, longer walls-era games, and more games or a higher probe rate to reach the per-group counts), or cut to 1 pilot x greedy lines first and add the sampled-line run only if the greedy gap passes 0.3.

State the machine plan: the probe's GPU-served pilot and 64-way CPU runner share the GPU and 16 threads with up to 3 screens. Run it at reduced concurrency alongside the screens, or in place of one screen.
Extend Runner's job.first to an array of keys, with the 'not on offer' check at each step, and add a unit check that the replayed sequence reaches the intended prompt state for each probed card.

title: A leaf value for the policy that actually plays judged games: is the searched judge's leftover wall preference the critic's sampled-play bias?
rivals: R1 leaf bias: the PPO critic is fit to sampled play, under which Trainer payoffs vanish (+0.35 vs +1.32 per decision under greedy follow-through, #79-80) and the walls fare better (0.75-0.83 in sampled-play probes vs 0.70-0.72 greedy, unpaired, H21); searched lines score leaves with this critic, so search keeps a wall preference (0.57-0.59)
R2 not the leaf: the critic is calibrated across continuation policies and deck clusters; the leftover preference is in-turn rollout play or the clockless game
design: Step 1, no training: on identical deals play population decks (human-free) and the 3 walls vs the 24 lists (evaluation) sampled, greedy and with one-turn search on both seats (includes H21's untested paired greedy-vs-sampled walls run); record the critic's value at each player's first decision each turn; reliability and mean error (outcome - V) by continuation policy, deck cluster (walls, Trainer-rich, human lists) and turn bucket. Step 2, only if Step 1 shows a policy-dependent gap: V_eval, an MLP on the frozen trunk's pooled features with Monte Carlo targets from about 4 positions per greedy judge game on human-free decks (20k games); then #139's 576 walls-vs-list deals with both seats searched, critic leaves vs V_eval leaves (paired, via C03), and C10's searched human-vs-human rung with V_eval leaves.

predictions.predicted: under greedy play mean error >= +0.05 on human-list and Trainer-rich positions and <= -0.03 on walls, near 0 under sampled play; V_eval cuts held-out greedy-outcome Brier >= 5%; V_eval leaves lower the walls' searched score >= 0.04 (paired) and cut searched human-vs-human deck-outs
every policy and cluster calibration gap < 0.02; the paired searched verdict moves < 0.02

readout: Calibration by continuation policy x cluster x turn; V_eval's held-out Brier; the paired searched verdict; searched human-vs-human pace.
noise_and_power: Step 1: about 20k positions per policy, mean-error SE about 0.005. Step 2: 576 paired deals x 2 leaf arms give a paired-difference SE of about 0.02 if the arms correlate about 0.6, so 0.04 is detected at about 80% power.
kill_rule: Stop after Step 1 if every policy- and cluster-specific gap is < 0.02; stop Step 2 if V_eval's held-out gain is < 5%.
cost: Step 1 about 1-2 h (sampled and greedy runs in minutes, the searched run about 30 min GPU-served); Step 2 about 3 h (20k greedy games about 20 min, head training minutes, 1,152 searched games 30-40 min). No screen slot.
distinct_from: H47 refit the value on fixed sampled self-play data and judged it by value EV (do-not-repeat avoided by greedy and searched judge-game targets); H50 changed PPO's targets to Monte Carlo; H48 added auxiliary heads. Never varied: the continuation policy behind the value targets and its use at search leaves (H22's untested 'search whose leaf value does not come from the population pilot').
