reviews.reasons:
C12 does not repeat earlier work. Each family it could overlap was checked against the ledger and the progress log.

- H47 (value refit): its do-not-repeat list bans an MLP refit on the frozen trunk with fixed self-play data (#77, value_refit.py --head-only, about 5k sampled games). C12 keeps that architecture but changes two things that were never varied:
  - the continuation policy behind the targets: Monte Carlo results of greedy judge-style games on human-free decks, where #77 used sampled PPO self-play;
  - what the head is for: it only scores search leaves in evaluation. It never trains the pilot and is not judged by value fit alone.
  It also uses about 4x more data (about 80k positions from 20k games). H47's verifier lists "more data rather than more capacity" as untested.
- H50 and H49: those changed PPO's own value or advantage targets in training (--lam-value 1, --lam 1). C12 trains nothing in the pilot, so it is a different mechanism.
- H48: auxiliary heads trained with the trunk. Not overlapping.
- H22: C12's Step 2 is exactly the variant the H22 verifier listed as missing and distinct: "search whose leaf value does not come from the population pilot... in a paired design". env/agents.js:325-411 confirms that PolicySearchAgent scores each line by the pilot's own value, so this is the untested lever. C12 does not rerun any banned item, such as psearch k4 dets4 h1/h2 with the pilot's own value, or deeper or wider search.
- H21: Step 1 includes the H21 verifier's untested "paired greedy-vs-sampled walls vs the 24 lists, same deals, one pilot". It is not one of the banned items (--judge-explore 0 screens, the within-type block probe, greedy plus --max-turns 60).
- H18, H19, H20: the banned items there are judge sweeps over pilots and the pilot-v2 judge. C12 keeps the pilot fixed and varies only the leaf value.
- #79-80 measured Trainer timing gains with greedy vs sampled lines. A grep of the progress log finds no calibration of the critic (outcome - V, reliability or Brier) by continuation policy, deck cluster or turn. So Step 1's diagnostic is new.
- H67-H69: those use the value as a deck scorer. C12 uses it as a search-leaf evaluator inside the judge, which is a different node and role.

What is distinct, by axis:
- Node: N10 x N4 (the value as the judge's leaf).
- Mechanism: off-policy bias of the critic at search leaves.
- Never-varied factors: the continuation policy behind the value targets, and the source of the search leaf value.

Rules check: V_eval trains only on human-free games, and the walls and human lists appear only in evaluation games. That passes the self-discovery and game-agnostic rules.

Notes for the executor, not required for approval:
- #77 overfit from epoch 1 on 5k games. Keep the held-out Brier kill rule exactly as written. Hold out by game, not by position.
- Report Step 1 per wall set and per list, because only resetcap499's 3 walls have ever been used (an H22 gap).

The question is worth asking. H22 lists "search whose leaf value does not come from the population pilot" as untested, scr-jsearch479 left search-strength judging untested at adequate power, and the experiment uses no screen slot. The readout also sits on the right nodes, N10 (the critic) and N4 (the judge's verdict). As designed, though, it is weakly diagnostic in four ways.

(1) Step 1's readout does not match the mechanism. One-turn search ranks sibling leaves that come from the same root state, in the same matchup and on the same deal. A bias that shifts the whole walls cluster, or a whole continuation policy, by a constant (the proposed "mean error <= -0.03 on walls") is the same for every candidate line, so it cancels in the argmax. Such a bias cannot produce a wall preference in searched play. R1's actual claim is about differences between actions: Trainer lines are undervalued relative to non-Trainer lines from the same state, which is the #79-80 +0.35 vs +1.32 effect. Step 1 measures absolute calibration by cluster, so it can pass (or kill) on gaps that do not matter for search, and it can miss the gaps that do.

(2) Step 1 is close to a foregone conclusion. Walls score 0.75-0.83 under sampled play and 0.70-0.72 under greedy, a shift of 0.05-0.1, and the critic is fit to sampled play. So "every policy and cluster gap < 0.02" (R2) is almost surely false whatever causes the searched preference. Step 1 then works as a gate, not as a test between the rivals. All of the discrimination rests on Step 2.

(3) Step 2 has no matched control. V_eval differs from the critic in three ways at once: continuation policy (greedy targets), a fresh MLP head with new data, and 20k games of human-free decks, which are mostly Chansey/Snorlax population decks. Any change in the searched verdict could come from refitting a head at all, from more data, or from distribution shift. H47 already showed that frozen-trunk refits behave oddly (they overfit, with a head gain of +0.006). Only a sampled-target head with the same architecture, decks, game count and training is a control in which the continuation policy is the only difference.

(4) The noise and power assumptions are unverified. The 0.6 correlation between the two leaf arms on paired deals is assumed. Search adds its own randomness (determinizations, and search changed 51-54% of decisions in scr-jsearch479), and once the two arms diverge, outcomes on the same deal may correlate much less. At a correlation of 0.2 the SE is about 0.026 and power for 0.04 falls to about 50%. There is no A/A for the searched verdict: the same leaf run twice with different search seeds. R2's prediction of "moves < 0.02" cannot be tested at SE 0.02 and needs an equivalence margin.

Two smaller issues. Greedy targets stand in for searched continuation, but the judged games continue under search, so Step 1's searched arm should decide whether greedy-target V_eval is an adequate proxy. And a third rival is missing. The live attached-Energy count bug (token_model.py:367; with slot_bind off, aux slot*8+copies is read as a count) corrupts the trunk features. That gives a leaf bias that is specific to the deck cluster, does not depend on the continuation policy, and is aimed squarely at Energy-heavy walls. A frozen-trunk V_eval inherits the bug, so a null in Step 2 would not clear the leaf.

The rules check passes: V_eval trains only on human-free decks, and the lists appear only in evaluation games. The kill rules have no short-horizon training bias because this is offline, but Step 1's kill criterion is computed on the wrong statistic (see 1).
required_changes: Replace or augment Step 1's cluster-mean calibration with a readout of value differences between actions. At sampled root decisions (Trainer vs non-Trainer, and wall-side vs list-side), score the k candidate end-of-turn leaves with the critic. Get each leaf's re-dealt Monte Carlo outcome under greedy, sampled and searched continuation. Report, by continuation policy and cluster, the slope or rank correlation of V-differences against outcome-differences, plus the mean signed error on Trainer-minus-alternative pairs. Base Step 1's kill rule on this statistic, not on cluster-level mean error, which cancels in the search's argmax.

Add a matched control head to Step 2: V_samp, with the same MLP, frozen trunk, decks, game count (20k), position sampling and training as V_eval, but with targets from sampled-continuation games. Run three leaf arms (critic, V_samp, V_eval) on the same 576 deals. Attribute an effect to R1 only if V_eval differs from V_samp by >= 0.04 on the walls' searched score. A shift that V_samp shows as well is a refit or data effect, not a continuation-policy effect.

Add an A/A for the searched verdict: run the critic-leaf arm twice on the 576 deals with different search seeds. Estimate the noise band and the actual correlation between arms on paired deals from this, and recompute power before running Step 2. If the measured correlation gives an SE above 0.022, increase the deal count (e.g. all 24 lists x 3 walls x 16+ a pair) or use more determinizations.

Restate the decision rules as interval tests. R1: the V_eval - V_samp difference in the walls' searched score is <= -0.04 and its 95% CI excludes 0. R2: the 90% CI of that difference lies within +/-0.04. Anything else is inconclusive and must not be treated as support for either rival. Drop the untestable '< 0.02' prediction.

Name R3 (a cluster-specific feature bias, i.e. the live attached-Energy count bug at rl/token_model.py:367) as a rival. In Step 1, report the critic's error and the sibling-leaf errors split by the number of Energy attached and the slot index (or rerun Step 1 on a slot_bind pilot if one exists). Say explicitly that a null for a frozen-trunk V_eval does not clear the leaf while the trunk reads the corrupted count.

Use Step 1's searched-continuation arm to check the proxy. Proceed with greedy-target V_eval only if greedy-continuation and searched-continuation errors agree within about 0.02 on the sibling-leaf statistic. Otherwise generate V_eval targets from searched games (or a mix), even though this costs more.

Report V_eval's held-out Brier separately on walls, Trainer-rich population decks and human-list evaluation games, all on new deals. The training decks are mostly Chansey/Snorlax, so a gain in pooled Brier can hide worse calibration off-distribution. The 5% gate must hold on the human-list and Trainer-rich clusters, not only overall.

Specify the pilot, checkpoint and deck sets: which critic (e.g. scr-resetcap 499), which population snapshot supplies the human-free training decks and Trainer-rich cluster, and which 3 walls. For the human-vs-human deck-out readout, give the baseline: the searched rung's deck-out rate with critic leaves from C10, with its own A/A. Without it, 'cuts deck-outs' has no reference against the 27-35% greedy rate.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: this passes. V_eval is trained only on human-free greedy self-play, with results-only Monte Carlo targets. The walls and the 24 lists appear only in evaluation games. Nothing in it is game-specific, and it is a diagnostic, with V_eval one small head on a frozen trunk. It is distinct from H47 (refit on sampled self-play data, judged by value EV) and H50 (MC targets inside PPO). It fills H22's untested variant: a leaf value that does not come from the population pilot.

Mechanism: the premise holds in the code. env/agents.js PolicySearchAgent.searchAll (line 411) scores each line that reaches the end of the turn with the pilot's own `value` output. A swapped leaf is therefore an ONNX or model-slot change, with no change to the search. rl/token_model.py forward has return_pooled, and the value head is an MLP on the pooled token (line 305). V_eval can be grafted as the value output of a combined model whose policy is unchanged, so neither arm needs new search code.

Cost: underestimated in four places.
(1) Searched games. The only fixed-deal driver, notes/scripts/walls_vs_humans.js, runs on CPU and is capped at 4 workers. runs/probe/wvh_psearch_both_g0-7.summary.json shows 192 both-seat searched games took 73 min, about 23 s a game. At that rate Step 1's searched run on 576 deals takes about 3.7 h, not 30 min, and Step 2's 1,152 searched games take about 7 h. The GPU-served search path exists only inside rl/metagame.py's training loop (env/remote_worker.js judgeSearch with RemotePilot via rl/remote.py). In scr-jsearch479 it played 200 games in 320-460 s, but those were capped at 60 turns with a 37-turn mean; uncapped walls games run to a median of 61 turns. A standalone GPU-served driver over fixed deals, with seeds matching gpu_matrix jobs_for, is new work of about 1-2 h. With it, 1,152 uncapped games take an estimated 60-90 min under contention with 3 screens. The GPU has 16.3 GB, so the 80% cap is about 13 GB; 3 screens at 3.5 GB plus one served model at 1-2 GB fits, but tightly.
(2) Engineering. Step 1 needs a per-decision value logger: walls_vs_humans.js writes one row per game with no values, though Runner has an onDecision hook. Step 2 needs trajectory recording on human-free decks, pooled-feature extraction, the head fit, the graft and an ONNX export. That is about 3-4 h of building, which the stated cost leaves out.
(3) The 20k greedy games. At walls_vs_humans' CPU rate (576 games in 4.6 min) 20k games take about 2.7 h; GPU-served alongside screens, about 40-60 min. The stated 20 min is optimistic.
(4) C10's human-vs-human searched rung has no cost at all.

Power: overstated. The roughly 20k positions per policy come from about 400 games, and the positions within a game share one outcome. The mean-error SE should be clustered by game, giving about 0.02-0.04, not 0.005, and worse per cluster x turn-bucket cell. The +0.05 / -0.03 / <0.02 thresholds cannot be resolved at that size. Greedy and sampled games are cheap, so raise them to about 3-5k games per policy and cluster. The searched policy cannot reach that, so it needs a coarser readout.

Repeat risk: the critic-leaf arm on #139's deals overlaps the done-and-do-not-repeat both-seat psearch k4 dets4 run (192 deals, 8 lists, resetcap499.onnx). Those deals use the same seed and stride, so reuse that file and play only the other 384 deals for the critic arm.

Confound: V_eval sits on a trunk carrying the live attached-Energy count bug (analysis section 9). Both arms share it, so it does not bias the paired comparison, but it caps how far V_eval can improve on the critic.
required_changes: Recost the searched runs. title: Condition-matched ground truth on the representative field: three wall sets against all 24 lists under the exact STS rule over a fixed turn grid, across a strength ladder with seat-decomposed, CRN and nested search
rivals: E: the missing clock is first-order; the walls' edge lies past any plausible round length
ExP: the clock matters only with search-strength play (#139/#147's reading)
P: play strength alone flips the clockless verdict; once both seats search, the clock adds little
Plateau / W: no affordable strength or clock flips it; the walls are strong in the event's game in our engine (outside research or fidelity needed)
Subset artifact: the #139/#147 flip came from an unrepresentative 8-list subset
Imbalance: search helps only the tempo side; the walls' plan is search-saturated
design: New fact (recomputed from the probe files): every searched probe (#139, #145-147) used one list per archetype, and the Wigglytuff stand-in (Lieu) is an outlier: greedy walls score 0.396 against Lieu but 0.706 against the 10 Wigglytuff lists (range 0.396-1.000), 42% of the field; the subset's field-weighted greedy STS share is 0.533-0.582 vs 0.641-0.675 on all 24 (its unweighted 0.706 matched the full field's 0.702 by coincidence). Needs C01 (trace, rule) and C03 (GPU-served searched probe, CRN). Wall sets, each the 3 best decks of a population by its own judged score (never by distance): A = scr-resetcap 499 (#829/#796/#809), B = scr-gate479 499 (near-human shape, 23-27 Trainers), C = main seg_0460 (Energy-heavy). Opponents: all 24 lists, seats alternated, identical seeded deals in every cell (#139's 576 for A). Cells: J0 pilot-v2 greedy and J1 the resetcap499 pilot greedy (16 a pair for A, B, C: 3,456 each); J2 both seats one-turn k4 d4 (CRN if C03 adopts it) for A and B over all 24 (1,152) and C over the 8-archetype subset (192); seat cells for A: human-side k4 d4 and walls-only k4 d4 (576 each); J3 both seats CRN k8 (d4 on A's 576; d8 on the subset); level 2 nested within-turn search on both seats (192 deals; nest only where level 1 departs from greedy or the top two options are within 0.1). Every game scored untimed, with plain draws and under the exact STS rule at each T in G = {20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 60, 70, 80}. Pre-registered: W(J, T) = the walls' share of STS points, sets A and B pooled; W(J, Pi) = its mean over Pi = uniform over 20-45 engine turns (about 18 min of play at 25-55 s a player-turn), replaced by C02's interval only if it arrives before results are opened; the whole curve always reported; no T chosen by its result. Invasion readout: the walls' expected points against the share-weighted field vs the residents' points against themselves under the same judge and rule (resident baseline from C16's greedy 24x24; searched: 200 share-weighted resident pairs x 2 games); per-archetype edges get adaptive extra games (up to 64) for a Condorcet test.

predictions.predicted: W(J1, Pi) <= 0.55 and W(J2, Pi) <= 0.45 while W(J1, untimed) >= 0.65; under J2 the lists earn more points per game than the walls at every T <= 45

W(J1, Pi) >= 0.58 at every T in Pi but W(J2, Pi) <= 0.45 (the end-count proxy gives about 0.65 for J1 and 0.42 for J2 at T 20-45); clockless J2/J3/level 2 plateau >= 0.55 with >= 70% of wall wins by deck-out

field-weighted clockless score falls with each level, below 0.50 at J3 or level 2, with >= 2 archetypes beating the walls on resolved edges and the deck-out share of wall wins falling; |W(J2, Pi) - W(J2, untimed)| <= 0.04
level 2 within 0.02 of level 1; W(J2, Pi) >= 0.52 and W(J3, Pi) >= 0.50 for set A or B; every STS cell >= 0.50 field-weighted
on all 24 lists both-seats k4 d4 with STS or draws at T 50-60 stays >= 0.52 field-weighted (the subset gave 0.38-0.45 field-weighted, carried by Lieu)
walls-only search moves the walls' score <= 0.02 from greedy (0.702) while human-side search moves it >= 0.10

readout: W(J, T) curves per judge and wall set with 95% intervals, unweighted and field-weighted; points per game per side (a tie is 1/3); W(J, Pi); seat gains; invasion fitness and Condorcet status on resolved edges; deck-out share and median length of wall wins; an Energy axis (set C vs B at Pi: does the clock punish or reward the Energy-heavy deviation, cf. C15's SW); the lists' Prize-win turns and share finished by T (now a median 46-47 engine turns greedy against the walls), reported for C02, not decided on.
noise_and_power: Greedy 1,152 games SE about 0.013, 3,456 about 0.008; 576 searched about 0.019 unweighted, 0.02-0.03 field-weighted (Wigglytuff n = 240, Haymaker n = 168); J2 at 1,152 about 0.015. Rule comparisons re-score the same games (difference SE about 0.01); judge comparisons are paired on identical deals (#139: -0.128 +/- 0.044 at 192; about 0.018 at 1,152), so thresholds 0.05 apart are >= 3 SE. Level 2 on 192 deals SE about 0.035, paired vs level 1 about 0.03. Resident baseline about 0.03. Re-scoring untimed games is exact for clock-unaware play (all judges here); clock-aware play is C34's question. Sets B and C answer the critic's point that only resetcap 499's walls were ever probed.
kill_rule: Stop after J2 if field-weighted both-seats k4 d4 clockless is < 0.48 (P confirmed at level 1). Stop J3 after 96 games if within 0.03 of J2 on the same deals with no trend; stop level 2 if after 48 paired games it differs from level 1 by < 0.02; drop the walls-only cell after 192 games if its gain is < 0.02. If J2 over all 24 reproduces untimed 0.57 +/- 0.04 and the curve stays within 0.03 of it at every T in G, the clock is inert under search: drop C34.
cost: Greedy cells about 30 min each on CPU (576 games took 4.6 min) or minutes on GPU; searched cells about 1-2 h GPU-served for A's 576-deal cells and J2 on A and B (vs about 11 h CPU via ONNX; 192 both-seat games took 73 min); J3 about 1 h GPU; level 2 3-8 CPU hours. Runs beside screens within the thread cap; no screen slot.
distinct_from: H03/H05/H22/H23: #139 used human-side search on one list per archetype and the end-count proxy at cuts 30-60; #145-147 both-seat k4 d4 on the 8-list subset with plain draws at 40-100 (do-not-repeat as configured; subset deals are replayed only to carry the trace, and J1 is one pilot, not another population sweep, H18/H22). New: all 576 deals because the subset is shown unrepresentative, the exact count at the cut, cuts 20-35, wall sets B and C, the walls-only seat (H22's missing decomposition), CRN k8 and 8-16 determinizations (H22 untested), nested minimisation instead of longer rollouts (Bertsekas), a pre-registered prior-averaged statistic, points per game, and invasion/Condorcet against the field mixture.
rules_check: Evaluation only: the lists are probes; no training. The STS rule is the event's own, decided by the game's end score, used only for scoring; T comes from a stated prior or outside evidence, never from the answer key (Hernandez et al.'s warning against autobalancing).
value: Decides which upstream fix the in-loop work should build: P alone (search judging or distillation in the clockless game: C38, C37), E plus P (the 2000 clock with search judging: Evan's decision C33 with C02's evidence, then C34), or neither (stronger judges, fidelity C06 or the game definition: outside research). Checks whether the 0.44-0.46 flip that motivated scr-jsearch479 survives on the representative field before more searched-judging screens are spent, and whether the specification moves the verdict more than internal levers (analysis section 7's trigger).

reviews.reasons:
The readout matches the nodes. These are judge-level game results on fixed decks, which is right for N1, N2 and N4. But the pre-registration is stale against data already on disk, and several rivals are already split by it.

I scored the existing exact traces (Prize lead at the last entry with turn <= T; 3 / 2 / 1 / 0 points) with my script C:/Users/evanc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-evanc-Desktop-333/01b3993d-15d8-42fb-afe1-4932bce95de8/scratchpad/c13_sts.js.
- Greedy J1 on set A over all 24 lists gives W(T) = 0.479, 0.509, 0.540, 0.541, 0.549, 0.583 at T = 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, so W(J1, Pi) is about 0.53. This meets E's prediction (<= 0.55) and already refutes ExP's (>= 0.58 at every T in Pi). The candidate's figure of 0.65 for J1 comes from the old end-count proxy.
- Both-seat k4 d4 on the subset (166 games) gives 0.33-0.44 unweighted at T 20-45, against 0.648 untimed. P's clause |W(J2, Pi) - W(J2, untimed)| <= 0.04 is therefore already off by about 0.25.
- Plateau's W(J2, Pi) >= 0.52 already fails on the subset by about 0.13.
A rerun of 576 more games on set A cannot be a blind pre-registered test.

The Subset-artifact rival is weak a priori. Greedy unweighted subset and all-24 shares differ by only 0.02-0.03 at every T (0.449-0.554 against 0.479-0.583 at 20-45), and the headline 0.44-0.46 was unweighted. The Lieu distortion affects only archetype-weighted subset numbers. On all 24 lists, field-weighted with one weight per entrant is just the per-list mean.

W(J, Pi) is close to monotone in T: greedy rises from 0.48 to 0.70 and search from 0.33 to 0.65. The verdict is therefore mostly fixed by the assumed Pi, not by the data.

The kill rules are badly calibrated:
- J3 is stopped if it is within 0.03 of J2 after 96 games, but the paired SE at 96 games is about 0.06 (#139: 0.044 at 192).
- Level 2 is stopped if it differs by < 0.02 after 48 paired games, where the SE is about 0.06-0.09.
Both rules would usually stop a real 0.05-0.10 gain. The SEs for searched cells also assume CRN pairing, which is not validated. Without CRN, two runs of both-seat k4 d4 on identical deals gave 0.573 and 0.648, and two human-side runs gave 0.578 and 0.536.

Six overlapping rivals with about 12 cells and many thresholds invite multiple-comparison readings. E and ExP were separated only by the J1 cell, which is already measured.

The genuinely open questions are:
- whether stronger clockless search (J2 on all 24, J3, level 2) brings the walls below 0.5 without a clock;
- the walls-only seat (Imbalance);
- blind replication on sets B and C.
required_changes: Re-register the predictions against the existing exact-rule results: set A J1 W(T) at 20-45 is 0.48-0.58 (mean about 0.53); the subset both-seat W(T) at 20-45 is 0.33-0.44 against 0.648 untimed. Mark ExP's J1 clause and P's 0.04 clause as already decided on set A, and make sets B and C the blind confirmatory cells for E vs ExP.

Add an assumption-free primary readout: the break-even turn T50 at which each judge's W(J, T) curve crosses 0.5, with a bootstrap interval, for each wall set. Compare it with C02's interval later, instead of letting the prior Pi decide the verdict.

Make the clockless strength ladder (J2 on all 24, J3, level 2) and the walls-only seat the primary open tests, each with a stated minimum detectable effect. Drop the Subset-artifact rival, or restate it with the greedy subset gap (<= 0.03) as its prior.

Recalibrate the kill rules as interval-based futility rules. For example: stop a strength rung only when the upper 90% bound of its paired gain over the rung below is < 0.05, with at least 192 paired games. Use SEs from the observed search-rerun variance (0.573 against 0.648 on identical deals) unless C03's CRN is validated first.
Define 'field-weighted' once: per-list equal weight over all 24 entrants. Drop the archetype-weighted subset numbers that use a single Wigglytuff stand-in.

reviews.reasons:
The rules are respected. This is evaluation and diagnosis only: the human lists are probes, nothing is trained, and wall sets are chosen by their own judged score. The STS rule is the event's own end-score rule and is used only for scoring.

Cheaper than stated:
- C01's trace dependency is mostly done. walls_vs_humans.js already logs prizeTrace, and the replay matched 576/576 stored games.
- Exact STS scoring is about 20 lines; I wrote it to review this candidate.
- The walls-only cell needs no code: --a-agent psearch --b-agent greedy.

Underestimated or missing costs:
(1) Level-2 nested search is not in env/agents.js. PolicySearchAgent has only k, dets and horizon, so nesting is new code (about 2-4 h plus tests), and the '3-8 CPU hours' is a guess.
(2) J0 needs pilot-v2 either exported to ONNX for walls_vs_humans.js or a trace added to the GPU probe path. #147 judged it through probe_matchups.py, which logs no per-turn trace.
(3) The invasion readout's resident baseline under the STS rule needs a traced 24x24. The JF2 matrices (gpu_matrix.py) have no prizeTrace.
(4) Extracting wall sets B and C from the checkpoints is small, about 30 min.
(5) The searched cells depend on C03's GPU-served probe, which is unbuilt (3-4 h of code). Without it, the CPU ONNX rate is about 2.6-3.4 both-seat games a minute (192 in 73 min; 163 in 49 min in the 10-21 chain). The searched cells (J2 for A and B, J2 for C, two seat cells, J3, level 2) come to roughly 5,000-7,000 k4-d4-equivalent games, or about 25-35 CPU hours.
(6) 'No screen slot' is optimistic for the GPU-served route. It is a fourth GPU and Python process beside up to 3 screens, each about 3.5 GB GPU and 2.7 GB RAM. VRAM and RAM fit, but it contends for GPU compute and for the 16-thread cap with 4 node workers. Run it with at most 2 screens, or count it as a slot.

Staging the cheap cells first makes the candidate affordable. The full design as written is more than a day of machine time unless C03 lands.
required_changes: Restate the dependencies: the trace and greedy validation are done (sts_greedy_all24.jsonl). Finish the 26 missing games of sts_search_both_sub.jsonl first, which takes minutes.

Add code-cost lines for nested within-turn search in PolicySearchAgent, a traced pilot-v2 path (ONNX export or trace in probe_matchups/gpu_matrix), a traced resident 24x24 for the STS invasion baseline, and wall-set extraction for B and C.

Stage the work by cost. First, the CPU-only cells that need no new code: greedy exact-rule curves for sets B and C, and walls-only k4 d4 on A's 576 deals (about 2.5-3.5 h of CPU). Gate J2 on all 24, J3 and level 2 on C03 being built and validated, with a CPU-fallback estimate of about 25-35 h stated explicitly.

title: Draw-seeking check of Evan's turn-limit runs: pilot learning to reach the draw, selection of draw-prone decks, or shared drift? A deck x pilot replay plus a trace of capped games
rivals: D0 shared drift: games lengthen in every 479 fork (no-Pokemon endings fell from 58% to 13% over 480-499 in the untimed control) and the limit only reveals it
D1 pilot draw-seeking: the pilot learned to reach the limit when behind, since a plain draw pays it 0 against -1 for a loss
D2 deck draw-seeking: selection under a 0.5 draw kept decks that cannot lose before the limit (scr-turns40 went from 10/29/21 to 17/26/16 by 489)
D3 cycles and caps: losing pilots burn decisions in no-progress cycles toward the 5,000-decision or 250-decision turn cap
design: (a) 2x2 replays under each run's own limit, random pairs of population decks as they stand, 2,000 games a cell, same seeds in every cell, sampled play as in training: decks {scr-turns40 population_it0489, scr-ctl479 population_it0489} x pilot {each snapshot's pilot} at limit 40 (scr-turns40 reached 94% limit endings at 489); the same at limit 70 (scr-turns70 vs scr-ctl479 at 494); the 60-turn pair (scr-t60gate479 vs scr-gate479 at 494) reported apart since those recipes also differ in greedy judging. Needs a --max-turns pass-through in rl/gpu_matrix.py. (b) With C01's trace, in cells sharing decks: per turn, the rate of attacking when an attack was available and of playing draw Trainers, by Prize difference (behind, even, ahead) and turns left (1-3, 4-8, > 10), limit-trained vs control pilot. (c) Trace a sample of capped games (ending none: 0.3-1.4% in scr-ctl479, 28 at 499; anomaly A6's 62-69 an iteration in the aux branch) and scr-jsearch479's capped search lines (640-3,827 an iteration at 491-497) with notes/scripts/trace_loop.js --greedy on an ONNX export (notes/scripts/export_pilot_onnx.py): repeated decision sequences and which side was behind.

predictions.predicted: the control's decks with the control's pilot reach the 40 limit in >= 80% of games; deck and pilot effects each < 5 points

on the same decks the limit-trained pilot reaches the limit >= 10 points more often; when behind with 1-3 turns left its attack and draw-Trainer rates are >= 0.10 lower than the control pilot's, and not when ahead
scr-turns40's decks reach the limit >= 15 points more often than the control's under either pilot, tracking their Pokemon count
>= 70% of traced capped games show a repeated no-progress sequence by the side behind on Prizes

readout: Share of games ending at the limit per cell; deck effect, pilot effect and interaction in points; behaviour rates by Prize state and turns left; capped-game traces classified as cycle or long genuine turn, by which side was behind.
noise_and_power: 2,000 games a cell: share SE about 0.011, so 5-point effects are 4-5 SE; the rises to explain are 51 points at limit 40 (43% to 94%) and 19 at 70 (6% to 25%). Behaviour rates pool thousands of turns (SE < 0.01) but are board-confounded, so compared only within matched bins. One fork per run: this splits the fork's rise, not its spread across forks.
kill_rule: Stop after (a) if no cell reproduces at least half of the run's rise (iteration noise or a confound; skip (b)). Stop (c) after 50 traced capped games if no sequence repeats >= 3 times.
cost: (a) 12 cells of 2,000 games, 3-5 min each on GPU, about 1 h in one slot plus a small flag; (b) CPU analysis once C01 exists; (c) about 1 h CPU.
distinct_from: H04 refuted plain-draw limits as a lever (#142-143) without decomposing the rise in limit endings; its verifier says a Prize-decided or loss-paid limit would separate draw-seeking from #142's deck-shift explanation; H01's verifier bars any draw that pays the pilot more than a loss without logging the time share by the losing side and tracing a sample, which no run did; H01's untested 'trace post-fix capped games' and A6 are covered by (c). No new limit is screened (H04 do-not-repeat).
rules_check: Diagnostic on existing snapshots; no human lists; no training. Completes the analysis of Evan's own turn-limit idea (requests 24-25), as rule 4 asks.
value: Decides whether H04's refutation is confounded by an exploit of the plain draw's payoff. D1/D2: the plain draw made the limit a haven for the side behind (Pardo et al.; sports-league evidence), so the event's rule (time loss = loss, tie 1/3) is a distinct untested mechanism and C01's and C34's seat rewards are right. D3: cap adjudication or a progress invariant precedes any clocked run. D0: the limit's failure points at selection-driven drift toward long games (N5, N6).
merged_from: game: Draw-seeking check of Evan's turn-limit runs: pilot learning to reach the draw, selection of draw-prone decks, or shared drift? A deck x pilot replay, plus a trace of capped games

reviews.reasons:
I checked the candidate against H01, H03, H04, H23, H51, H53 and H66, anomaly A6 and the critic's coverage gaps in ledger_meta.json. I grepped notes/progress-log.md for #139-#147, the trace_loop.js uses (lines 1260 and 1353, the league-3 era, before the fixes) and draw-seeking terms.

It is not a repeat, for three reasons.

(1) It screens no new turn limit and trains nothing. H04's do-not-repeat list bars only further training runs at --max-turns 40/70/120 or 60+gate, and offline re-scoring of greedy games with draws at T (#139, #147). Part (a) plays new sampled games under each run's own limit. It crosses decks from the limit run and the control with the pilots from each, which no entry did.

(2) The factor never varied is the deck x pilot decomposition of the rise in limit endings. #142 Found (1) put the 43% to 94% rise down to decks shifting toward more Pokemon and less Energy, but it only asserted this (rival D2), and #143 did not decompose the 70-turn rise either. Draw-seeking by the pilot (D1) appears in no test.

(3) Parts (b) and (c) cover diagnostics the ledger itself lists as missing:
- H01's verifier untested item: "trace a sample of post-fix capped games ... with trace_loop.js --greedy. Cheap, and never done".
- H01's do-not-repeat clause, which bars draw outcomes paid above a loss when the time share by the losing side is not logged and no sample is traced. (b) supplies that logging.
- Anomaly A6 (the aux branch's 62-69 capped games an iteration, never investigated).
- The critic's coverage gap "Draw-seeking under capped or turn-limited games ... untraced", including scr-jsearch479's 640-3,827 capped search lines.

By node and mechanism: N1, N10 and N5. The mechanism is that the pilot learns to stall to a draw, which pays 0 against -1 for a loss. This is H01's incentive applied to the turn limit, never measured there. H04's mechanism (removing the walls' deck-out payoff) is a different one.

The design respects the H04 caveat about confounded controls. It reports the 60-turn pair apart because scr-t60gate479 and scr-gate479 also differ in greedy judging. It is a diagnostic on existing snapshots, so it is consistent with the rules, and it finishes Evan's own turn-limit request.

Minor non-repetition notes, which do not block approval:
- Part (c)'s capped search lines in scr-jsearch479 are searched rollouts, not games. trace_loop.js --greedy on an ONNX export may not reproduce them directly, so the trace sample should be drawn from capped games first.
- The 70-turn cell needs scr-turns70's population_it0494 snapshot to exist (the run was stopped at 496). This should be confirmed before the GPU slot is spent.

This diagnostic is worth running. The rivals predict different outcomes on the 2x2 readout: D1 predicts a pilot main effect, D2 a deck main effect, and D0 a high control-by-control cell with small contrasts. The readout matches the targeted nodes, since the deck contrast tests selection (N5) and the pilot contrast tests the pilot (N1/N10). The inputs exist: population_it0489.pt for scr-turns40 and scr-ctl479, and 0489/0494 for scr-turns70, scr-t60gate479 and scr-gate479, each carrying net, population and agents. The pilot sees the turn number (env/tokens.js g[0] = turn/48), so a learned "stall when behind near the limit" policy is mechanistically possible. At 2,000 games a cell, 5-point main effects sit at about 4-5 binomial SE. With pair clustering, use a pair-clustered bootstrap and the same pair list in every cell. The interaction SE is about 2.2 points, so it is only resolvable at 9 points or more. There is no training horizon, so short-horizon bias does not apply.

Problems:
(1) No common starting point. The design has no replay of the fork's starting state, the 479 decks with the 479 pilot. Without it D0, "shared drift", has no estimate under the same protocol. The 43% figure is the training-schedule share at iteration 480, not a random-pair replay, so neither D0's ">= 80%" nor the kill rule's "half the run's rise" is measured on a matched baseline.
(2) The wrong limit-70 snapshot. Per runs/screens/scr-turns70/log.jsonl, time endings peaked at 491-503 of 2,000 at 488-489 (about 25%), then fell to 301 at 494 (15%) and 241 at 496 (12%). At 494 the rise to explain is about 9 points, not 19. The reversal is itself evidence: D1 (a learned pilot policy) predicts the time share stays up, while deck turnover or drift allows it to fall. The proposal ignores this.
(3) The D1 test depends on C01's trace, which does not exist yet. On its own, a pilot main effect in (a) cannot separate draw-seeking from plain competence loss: a limit-trained pilot may close games worse on decks it was not trained with. The decisive signature is the behind-versus-ahead asymmetry, and the replay itself can log it.
(4) D3 is not a rival on the main readout. Capped games end 'none', not 'time', and they make up only 0.3-1.4% of games, so they cannot explain a 51-point rise in limit endings. Its result does not bear on D0-D2. Tracing with trace_loop.js --greedy on seeds from sampled games will not reproduce those games, and greedy play changes how often cycles occur. scr-jsearch479's in-turn search-line truncations are a different mechanism from game caps.
(5) There is no decision rule for mixed outcomes, and the expected result is a split of the rise.

Smaller problems:
- The turns-left bins skip 9-10.
- The limit counts both players' turns, so 40 game turns is 20 per player. The bins must use the same game-turn units.
- The 60-turn pair differs in greedy judging and in the gate, so it adds little. Run it last or drop it.
required_changes: Add an anchor cell under each limit, scr-ctl479's starting snapshot (the shared 479 decks and pilot), replayed with the same random pairs and seeds. Define the components against it: shared drift = control-by-control minus anchor, deck effect = mean deck contrast, pilot effect = mean pilot contrast, plus the interaction. State the kill rule as the own-by-own cell reproducing at least half of (own-by-own minus anchor) in this protocol.

For the limit-70 pair, use the 489 snapshots, where scr-turns70 peaked at about 25% time endings (scr-ctl479 has 0489), or run both 489 and 494. Record the fall from 25% to 12% over 489-496 as a pre-stated observation: D1 predicts the time share stays high, while D0/D2 allow it to fall.

Take the D1 discriminator out of C01's critical path. In the (a) replays, log per game the Prize difference when the limit is reached and which side was behind. Log per side and per turn whether an attack was available and taken, plus draw-Trainer plays, binned by Prize state and turns left (in game turns, matching g[0]). Pre-register: a pilot effect with no behind/ahead asymmetry (behind minus ahead below 0.05) counts as competence loss, not draw-seeking.

Pre-register a rule for mixed outcomes. A rival is supported if its component is at least 1/3 of the anchor-to-own rise and above 3 SE under a pair-clustered bootstrap. Use the identical pair list in all cells.

Recast (c) as a separate diagnostic of the cap and anomaly A6, not a rival for the limit rise. Trace capped games from sampled play by recording action sequences or the RNG stream in the worker, not by --greedy reruns of their seeds. Report scr-jsearch479's truncated search lines apart from game caps.
Fix the turns-left bins to cover every turn (1-3, 4-8, 9+). Run the 60-turn pair last or drop it, since it is confounded by greedy judging and the gate.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: clean. It only replays existing snapshots and traces games: no training, no human lists, nothing card-specific fed back into a learner. Classifying "draw Trainers" in (b) is a diagnostic label, which Evan's rules allow. It finishes the analysis of Evan's own turn-limit idea (requests 24-25).

(a) is feasible and the cost is about right. The snapshots exist:
- runs/screens/scr-turns40 has population_it0489.pt. Its log runs to iteration 492, where 1,856 of 2,000 games ended on time.
- scr-ctl479 has 0489, 0494 and 0499. scr-turns70, scr-t60gate479 and scr-gate479 each have 0494.
- Each snapshot holds 'net' (the pilot), the config and 99 population decks.
- n_agents is 0, so any pilot can play any run's decks.

rl/gpu_matrix.load_policy already reads the 'net' key. GpuMatrix.play already accepts pairs and pair_keys (same deals across cells), and --sample gives sampled play. It already counts endings ('time', and null for capped games).

env/remote_worker.js already honours cmd.maxTurns. The gap is that GpuMatrix.play never sends maxTurns, and there is no CLI flag for it. Also needed: a short driver that pulls the decks out of a snapshot, draws random pairs once with fixed pair_keys, and loops over the 12 cells. That is about 1 hour of code, not "a small flag".

Throughput checks out. Training spends about 200 s on 2,000 recorded games per iteration, so a cell takes 3-4 min and 12 cells take about 45-60 min in one GPU slot (about 2.7 GB RAM and 3.5 GB GPU).

One confound is not stated. The training configs have search_p 0.1, so some decisions in training games are searched. Replays through gpu_matrix use plain sampling, so they are not exactly "as in training". Say so, or check that the replayed control cell reproduces each run's logged share of limit endings at its iteration.

Underestimated or flawed parts:
- (b) needs a per-decision recorder, run through the existing onDecision hook in remote_worker.js. It has to log whether an attack was legal, the option chosen, the Trainer played, the Prize difference, the turn and turns left. It depends on C01, which is not built. On its own it is 2-4 h of engineering, not "CPU analysis".
- (c) as written does not work. notes/scripts/trace_loop.js reads a league export directory (strategies.json, agentN.onnx) and passes no maxTurns to env.reset. It looks for games over --long decisions rather than games with ending null.
- (c) also uses --greedy. That changes the cap rate relative to the sampled play where the 0.3-1.4% capped share was measured, and it biases the trace toward deterministic loops. That is exactly D3's prediction.
- At a cap rate of 0.3-1.4%, 50 capped games need about 3,500-15,000 single-process ONNX games on the CPU. That is several CPU-hours, or a parallel harness, not about 1 h.
- The cheaper route is to log option keys inside the (a) GPU replays through onDecision and keep only the games whose ending is null. That reuses the same games with no ONNX export.
- "scr-jsearch479's capped search lines" are PolicySearchAgent rollouts cut at maxSteps 40 inside the search. They are not game caps, and trace_loop cannot see them. That run was also stopped as untestable by design (analysis section 9). Drop this part, or cost it separately as instrumenting PolicySearchAgent.
required_changes: Restate (a)'s engineering: add max_turns to GpuMatrix.play (passed as maxTurns in the 'games' message) plus a --max-turns CLI flag, and write a driver that pulls decks from population_it*.pt, draws one fixed set of random pairs with shared pair_keys, and runs the 12 cells. About 1 h of code plus 45-60 min of GPU in one slot.

Add a calibration check to (a): in each run's own cell (its own decks and its own pilot), the replay must match that run's logged share of limit endings (about 93% at limit 40) within 5 points before deck and pilot effects are read. Training used search_p 0.1, so plain sampled replay can differ from training.

Cost (b) honestly: it needs a per-decision recorder through remote_worker.js onDecision (whether an attack was legal, the option chosen, any Trainer played, the Prize difference, turns left), about 2-4 h if C01 has not built it. Gate (b) on (a) passing its kill rule.

Replace (c)'s trace_loop.js --greedy ONNX route with key logging inside the (a) GPU replays: record option keys only for games ending null (capped) in sampled play, so the cap rate matches training. If trace_loop.js is kept, it needs maxTurns and a filter on ending null, plus a CPU budget of several hours to reach 50 capped games at a 0.3-1.4% cap rate.

Drop the scr-jsearch479 search-line trace from (c), or cost it as a separate PolicySearchAgent instrumentation job. Those are rollouts cut at 40 steps inside the search, not capped games, and the run was stopped as untestable by design.

title: Does the round rule change what the loop selects, and in which direction? Re-score one live iteration's judged games under the rule (human-free, no training)
rivals: SI inert: under the population's own judge the rule flips no more --select decisions than redraw noise and has no compositional direction
SR toward the human shape: the rule lowers the scores of walls and of moves that add Pokemon and cut Trainers
SW toward Energy-heavy aggro: the rule rewards early Prize leads, which our pilot gets from more Energy and basic attackers: a new Energy attractor
design: From scr-gate479 population_it0489 (gated, sampled judging) and scr-ctl479 population_it0489 (ungated), run one iteration of rl/metagame.py with each run's flags plus --freeze-pilot, C01's trace, and every judged game saved with its deck or candidate id. Offline, recompute every --select decision (and the --select-z gate where set), every deck's judged score and the draft head's per-card REINFORCE advantages under: untimed (must reproduce the logged decisions exactly), STS at each T in C13's grid G, and plain draws at each T. Noise null: redraw each candidate's games at its untimed rate 20 times (#148's null_searched) and count flips. Direction: regress each deck's or candidate's score change (rule minus untimed) on its Pokemon, Trainer and Energy counts and a wall flag (holds Chansey BS and Snorlax JU); compare the composition of moves accepted under the rule with those accepted untimed (acc row). Repeat with a second deal seed.

predictions.predicted: flips at T in Pi inside the null's 95% band; slopes < 0.005 per card with intervals spanning 0; accepted moves' Trainer change within 0.3 of untimed
flips above the null band; score change rises with Trainers and falls with the wall flag (coefficient <= -0.03); accepted moves add >= 0.5 more Trainers each than untimed
flips above the null; score change rises with Energy or basic Pokemon (interval excluding 0) and accepted moves add Energy

readout: Flipped decisions per iteration against the null band; regression coefficients on Pokemon, Trainers, Energy and the wall flag; acc rows per rule; the head's per-card advantage sums for Energy, Trainers and Pokemon per rule. No human list involved.
noise_and_power: About 400 decks and candidates an iteration (99 decks, 1-3 candidates, 10-20 games each); two checkpoints x two seeds give about 1,600, slopes to about +/-0.003 a card. Flips are compared with redraws of the same games; rule-vs-untimed changes are paired on identical games.
kill_rule: If the untimed recomputation does not reproduce the logged decisions exactly, stop and fix the bookkeeping. If SI holds at every T in G for both checkpoints, do not run C34's stage 2 under the greedy or sampled population judge.
cost: Two one-iteration runs per seed (6-7 min each in one slot) plus about 2 h of analysis code; needs C01's trace in the metagame path.
distinct_from: H04 and H23 ran limits inside training screens and read deck-shape trajectories; #147 re-scored only walls-vs-list games. H04's untested 'limit on judging games only' is the in-training version (its verifier's 'largely predicted by #147' concerns walls vs lists, not the population's choices). scr-jsearch479's flip count measured search, not a rule. C20 reads the Prize rule on designed paired variants at the 60-turn state; this re-scores the loop's own decisions and draft credit at every T.
rules_check: Human-free (population decks only), so it can be the decision of record without the answer key; no training.
value: The cheapest prediction of what a clocked loop would do before spending screens: SR justifies C34's stage 2; SI says a clock acts only through a changed pilot or a search judge; SW warns the clock alone could trade the wall attractor for an Energy-heavy one, the very deviation Evan's ground truth flags.
merged_from: game: Does the round rule change what the loop selects, and in which direction? Re-score one live iteration's judged games under the rule (human-free, no training)

reviews.reasons:
I keep the earlier repetition review's approve. I checked it against the full ledger and the log and found no concrete error. The do-not-repeat items that mention re-scoring under the STS rule or as draws at T (H03, H04, H19, H22) all cover the resetcap499 walls against the 24 human lists (#139, #147). None of them covers population-vs-population or candidate games. In-loop clocks (H04: scr-turns40/70/120, scr-t60gate479; H23: scr-jsearch479) were read from deck-shape trajectories. scr-jsearch479's flips and select_flips_null (#148-149) measured search under the min rule, not a game rule.

C15 is distinct on two counts:
- **Node and mechanism:** it recomputes the --select / --select-z decisions and the draft head's rloo advantages (N5, N6) from the loop's own judged games under a changed scoring rule. Grep finds no such recompute.
- **Never-varied factor:** the Prize tiebreak (1 / 2/3 / 1/3 / 0) has never been applied to anything but walls-vs-list games. H03, H04, H23, H29, H44, H51 and H53 all list 'STS round rule in training' as untested, and there is no tiebreak code in env/ (C01 builds it).

The plain-draw-at-T arm overlaps H04's in-loop nulls. It counts as a positive control only, as the earlier review required. The earlier review's other required changes still apply: use the per-turn Prizes from C01's trace, not #139's end-count proxy; launch from each run's config.json; and state that play is held fixed.
required_changes: Keep the earlier review's four changes: score STS from per-turn Prizes at T (C01 trace), not #139's end-of-game proxy; frame the plain-draw arm as a positive control against H04's in-loop nulls; launch from each run's saved config.json; state that fixed play rules out only the scoring channel.

reviews.reasons:
The rivals do predict different signs on a node-matched readout. This is a selection and draft-credit question, and it is read on selection flips, move composition and per-card REINFORCE credit, which is the right match. Paired rule-vs-untimed scoring on identical games removes deal noise. Several statistical defects would still blur or bias the verdict.

**(1) The regression is collinear.** Pokemon + Trainers + Energy = 60 for every deck, so regressing the score change on all three plus an intercept is not identified. SR's 'rises with Trainers' and SW's 'rises with Energy' are both contrasts against Pokemon, so they can hold at once. 'Basic Pokemon' is in SW's prediction but not among the regressors.

**(2) The noise null is mis-scaled.** 'Redraw each candidate's games at its untimed rate' redraws all of a candidate's games, but the rule can change only games that pass T. #148's null_searched redrew only the changed subset. A null over all games inflates the band and favours SI.

**(3) The deck-level regression mixes in opponents.** Each deck faces a different random field. Selection and the rloo credit are both within-deck comparisons, so the matched readout is per-move and paired: candidate minus parent of Δ(rule − untimed), regressed on the move's ΔTrainers and ΔEnergy, over all proposals, not only accepted ones.

**(4) The accepted-move criterion is underpowered under the gate.** scr-gate479 accepts 13-28 moves an iteration, and only the flipped ones differ between rules. 'Accepted moves add >= 0.5 more Trainers' rests on a handful of moves: with a move ΔTrainers SD of about 2 and ~10 flips, the SE is about 0.6.

**(5) The sample size is overstated.** In code, gate479 has candidates 1, so held = [deck, 1 candidate]: 198 entities at about 20 games each. ctl479 has 396 at about 10. That is about 1,200 entities over 2 checkpoints x 2 seeds, not 1,600. The two seeds re-judge the same decks, and a candidate shares five-sixths of its parent's cards, so the effective units are about 200 distinct decks per checkpoint. Slope SEs are still well under 0.005 a card, but they should be computed with deck-clustered errors.

**(6) Multiple T values invite forking paths.** Ten T values x two rules is a garden of forking paths. Pi (20-45) must be pre-registered as the pooled primary readout, with the whole curve reported as secondary.

**(7) The kill rule is miscalibrated.** It blocks C34 stage 2 under SI. But SI on fixed, clock-unaware play says nothing about a pilot that adapts to the clock, which is what C34 stage 1 tests. C34's own design gates stage 2 on CA and on the absence of SW, not on SI. The bookkeeping half of the kill rule is sound.

Short-horizon bias does not apply, since nothing is trained.
required_changes: Regress on two composition terms with Pokemon as the stated reference (e.g. Trainers and Energy, plus the wall flag, and basic-Pokemon share if SW names it). Restate SR and SW as signed contrasts (SR: Trainer coefficient > 0 and Energy <= 0; SW: Energy or basic-Pokemon coefficient > 0 and Trainer <= 0) so that they cannot both pass.

Match the noise null to the perturbation: redraw only the games that last past T (count matched per candidate) at the candidate's untimed rate, 20 redraws, as null_searched did for the searched subset.

Make the primary direction readout paired at the move level: for every proposal (accepted or not), (candidate − parent) of Δ(rule − untimed), regressed on the move's ΔTrainers and ΔEnergy with deck-clustered errors. Keep the deck-level regression and the acc-row comparison as secondary; drop the >= 0.5-Trainer accepted-move threshold for the gated run, or compute its power first.
Correct the sample size to about 198 (gate, ~20 games each) and 396 (ctl, ~10 games each) entities an iteration. Treat the two seeds as re-judging the same decks, not as independent units.
Pre-register W over Pi = turns 20-45 (pooled) as the primary T, before results are opened, and report the full grid as secondary.

Change the second kill branch: SI does not block C34 stage 2. It makes stage 2 conditional on stage 1 showing CA, the pilot channel. SW blocks stage 2, as in C34's own gate. Report the per-card advantage sums both raw and after the batch-SD scaling that draft.update applies.

reviews.reasons:
The design is feasible and within Evan's rules. It is human-free, involves no training, and is game-agnostic: a timed round with a score tiebreak exists in MTG too. The card-specific wall flag is used for diagnosis only.

**Code checked (rl/metagame.py):**
- --freeze-pilot sets rec_share to 0 and skips practice games.
- Both checkpoints use sampled judging (judge_explore null), so all 2,000 games judge decks with or without freezing, and the judged sample matches the regime.
- Selection with season 1 counts every iteration, and pick() and rloo(z, zeros) are deterministic given the per-candidate sums. The untimed reproduction check is therefore realistic.

title: Empirical-game audit and premise test: walls, self-discovered types, wide decks and the human field under a judge ladder, untimed and under the STS rule (Condorcet, sinks, Nash mass, invasion of the human equilibrium)
rivals: R-judge-bound / PR4: under every affordable judge, the searched one with the event's cut included, the walls are a resolved Condorcet winner (or the only sink) and invade the human field: no selection, estimator or diversity method can keep another type; the premise fails in our engine

R-selection-bound: under the searched judge with the cut (J3) a self-discovered non-wall deck beats the walls on a resolved edge; the judge's game holds a non-wall equilibrium the greedy loop never keeps
R-discovery-bound / PR1: under J3 the walls beat every self-discovered deck but cannot invade the human field (two or more archetypes beat them); the judge is adequate, the loop never found a counter
PR2 clock alone: the walls fail to invade under the STS rule even with the greedy population judge
PR3 strength alone: the walls fail to invade under search whatever the rule, and the rule leaves the human field's own equilibrium unchanged
design: Panel: walls = C13's sets A and B plus the 3 best of scr-t60gate479's last population; 12 self-discovered non-wall decks = the best deck of each k-means cluster (card counts) other than the incumbent's over main 290 and 360, scr-resetent 496, the 018 fresh-exploiter branch's last checkpoint, scr-v2 / scr-scratch and scr-t60gate479, plus the best of each of the 3 largest non-wall types of scr-gate479 499 (notes/scripts/screen_types.py); 4 wide decks; the 24 lists (evaluation-only rows). Judges on shared deals, seats swapped, with C01's trace: J0 pilot-v2 greedy and J1 resetcap499 greedy over the full panel; J2 one-turn search on both seats, CRN k4 d4 (C03), on the walls' edges, the top-12 human-free submatrix and a 12-deck core (one list per archetype, 2 walls, 2 non-walls); J5 = C07's best wall-naive judge (evaluation only). Every matrix scored untimed, with plain draws at 50 and 60 (J1', J3) and under the exact STS rule at each T in C13's grid. Sampling (ResponseGraphUCB): a pair plays until its Clopper-Pearson interval excludes 0.5 or reaches its cap (64 greedy, 48 searched), walls' edges first; the human 24x24 at 32 a pair for the logit equilibrium. Analysis (hodge_audit.py extended): the walls' Condorcet status on resolved edges, max-entropy Nash and maximal-lottery mass, sink components, Hodge cyclic share, Kendall tau across judges; sigma_H = logit equilibrium of the 24x24 (lambda 20 fixed now; 10 and 40 reported) and its bootstrap Nash, its TV to the real field; each wall's and non-wall's invasion fitness against sigma_H (points minus 0.5, bootstrap interval) and its mass in the full panel's equilibrium. Two decision statistics fixed now: the human-free submatrix (walls, self-discovered, wide; rule-compliant judges only) is the decision of record for methods; invasion of sigma_H at C13's prior Pi answers the premise.

predictions.predicted: under J3 the walls beat all self-discovered and wide decks and >= 6 of 8 human archetypes on resolved edges, max-entropy Nash mass on walls >= 0.9; under J2 at Pi their invasion fitness against sigma_H > 0 with the interval excluding 0, or they hold > 0.2 of the full panel's equilibrium
under J3 >= 1 self-discovered non-wall deck beats the walls with an interval excluding 0.5 and the walls' Nash mass in the human-free submatrix < 0.5, while under J1 they win every edge

under J3 the walls are Condorcet winners in the human-free submatrix while >= 2 archetypes beat them on resolved edges (Wigglytuff first: 0.25 under human-side search, #139); J2 at Pi: invasion fitness < 0 with the interval excluding 0, equilibrium mass < 0.05, sigma_H's TV at Pi no worse than untimed with Wigglytuff and Haymaker on top
J1 at Pi: walls' invasion fitness < 0 as well, while untimed J1 gives > +0.10
J2 untimed already gives invasion fitness < 0; from untimed to Pi the walls' fitness moves < 0.05 and TV < 0.03

readout: Per judge and rule: each edge's status, the walls' Condorcet status and equilibrium mass, sink components (human-free first); invasion fitness of each wall and non-wall against sigma_H with intervals; sigma_H's TV to the real field; changes from untimed to STS at each T; whether any non-wall population type earns equilibrium mass in the event's game.
noise_and_power: Edges within +/-0.125 of 0.5 never resolve at 64 games; at 32 a pair an edge has SE about 0.088 and only 99-108 of the human field's 276 edges resolved (JF2). Under J1 the walls' edges sit near 0.72 and resolve in 16-32 games; under J3 they averaged 0.44-0.46 (#147), so many fall near the zone: decisions read resolved edges, invasion fitness (24 opponents, SE about 0.02 a deck) and the logit equilibrium (Nash is unstable at 32 a pair: JF2's bootstrap TV [0.25, 0.71]); rule comparisons re-score the same games (SE about 0.01); TV changes < 0.05 count as noise.
kill_rule: Stop a pair once it resolves or reaches its cap; stop a judge once every walls edge is resolved or capped. Skip J2 beyond the walls' edges if J1 or J1' already shows a non-wall deck beating the walls, or if every walls edge under J3 resolves for the walls. Drop the J2 core if J0 and J1 already put the walls' invasion fitness below -0.10 at every T in Pi.
cost: Greedy judges about 20-40 GPU-min each (adaptive; a 36x36 at 32 a pair is about 20,000 games, about 26 min at JF2's rate). J2: about 3,500 games on the walls' edges, 2,600 in the top-12 submatrix and 2,100 in the core, about 3-4 h with C03's probe (about 40 h on CPU ONNX). Rule readings cost nothing extra. reviews.reasons:
I keep the earlier dedicated review's verdict (revise, 6). Its main points check out.

(1) Peeking at a per-game Clopper-Pearson interval inflates the false-resolution rate. Over a family of about 9 walls x 16 non-wall or wide decks (more than 80 edges, more than 140 with the 9 walls actually in the panel), 'at least one non-wall deck beats the walls' fires by chance. R-selection-bound's trigger is therefore not calibrated.
(2) Power at the decisive edges is low. A true 0.40 against 0.5 at n = 48 has SE 0.071, so z is about 1.4 and power about 0.3 at 2 SE. Under J3 the walls averaged 0.44-0.46 (#147), so 'mostly unresolved' is the likeliest outcome, and no rival maps it to a decision.
(3) J1', J3 and the base pilot of the searched judges are undefined. The verdict follows the walls' pilot (0.72 vs 0.24), so this is decisive.
(4) Invasion fitness has problems: optional stopping on adaptively capped edges, n_eff under a concentrated sigma_H, and a cross-judge mix if a greedy sigma_H is used with searched fitness.
(5) PR3's TV < 0.03 sits inside the stated 0.05 noise band.
(6) The skip-J2 kill rule keys on the biased judge.

I found no concrete error in that review. Three further points:
(a) The panel has 9 walls (sets A and B plus 3 from t60gate479), not 5. The multiplicity is larger than the earlier review assumed, which strengthens point 1.
(b) R-selection-bound and R-discovery-bound both take J3 as the right yardstick, and J3 pays plain draws at 50-60 turns. J3 is not the event's rule, and H04 shows plain draws reshape payoffs. The human-free decision of record should be read under the exact STS rule at Pi (C01) as well as J3, with agreement required. Otherwise an outcome that only J3's draw payoff produces would be credited to selection or discovery.
(c) Every non-wall deck was discovered under walls-biased judges. 'J3: the walls beat every self-discovered deck' therefore does not separate discovery-bound from 'the discovery judge hid the counters'. That is a limit on interpretation, not a fatal flaw, and the outcome table should state it.
