H-exposure / slow accumulation / reset-viable: judge-decoupling remedies (C39 with measured P0 and F, frozen or min-over judges) can remove the walls, and P1's 10-iteration reading says how fast a fresh judge acquires the preference. H-payoff or H-familiarity: the walls are strong for any competent payoff-1 pilot in the clockless game, no rule-compliant judge swap removes them, only the clock or strength can (C13, C16, C20, C38, C33), and pilot-v2's 0.264 stops being evidence that the walls are weak. H-fast-learner closes C39 before any screen.
merged_from: chain: Delta-debug pilot-v2's low verdict on the walls: matched fine-tunes crossing deck-out payoff with training field, card familiarity equalised; judge: Controlled-adaptation judge curves from one wall-naive start: deck-out payoff x wall exposure (2x2), then an equal-cluster reset-and-fine-tune curve

reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews to keep. I checked C17 against every family it could overlap: H14, H15, H18, H19, H20, H43, H51 and H52. The do-not-repeat lists for H03, H51 and H52 ban '--deckout-win 0' in training as game-specific shaping (#51), and they cover #33's deckout-w0/w1 card ablations. Those ablations were fine-tunes of a4-tok, which was trained on the human lists. They were judged by card ablation, never on the walls, and they had no exposure factor. C17 uses deck-out 0 only in quarantined diagnostic arms, so it does not rerun a banned training configuration. Two factors were never varied: (1) deck-out payoff crossed with training field (wall exposure) from one wall-naive start (pilot-v2 it349), read on fixed deals; (2) an equal-games-per-cluster fine-tune curve, the Mertan / Strgar-Kriegman equal-adaptation counterfactual. The ledger marks both as genuinely untested: H43 'Mertan-style equal-adaptation counterfactual', H19 'two-sided equal-budget fine-tune', H52 'matched deck-out 0/1 judge pair', H15 '#73 deckout0 arm never reported', H20 'independent judge with deck-out 1'. The critic ranks it top-untested #2. Grep of progress-log.md: the #70/#73 deckout0 arm was launched in pilot_ablation_run.sh and has no reported result. The #137 pairings, the #147 sweep and scr-judge2/scr-v2 compare whole pilots or put a frozen pilot-v2 in the loop, which is a different mechanism. The critic's version is from-scratch pilots. C17's fine-tune version is cheaper and adds the exposure and familiarity factors, so it is distinct and not a rerun. Small overlap: P1 regrows a population pilot from pilot-v2, which is close to how the main line itself began (#69). It is justified only as a positive control and should not be read as new evidence about population pilots (#147 do-not-repeat). H1 (pilot-v2 practising the human lists) is near #131 diag-human-practice, but it differs in start pilot and payoff.
required_changes: Label P1 explicitly as a positive control, not a new judge-sweep data point. #147's do-not-repeat covers static comparisons of more population pilots.

reviews.reasons: The readout matches the node. These are judge hypotheses (N4/N10), and the readout is the judge's verdict on fixed deals: walls vs the 24 lists on #137/#147 deals, 1,152 games, pair-clustered SE about 0.03. A human-free twin and a forgetting check sit beside it. The noise budget is adequate for the 0.25 main effects it targets (about 5 SE), and P1 plus the extension to 80 iterations guards against short-horizon bias. The P1 vs P0 contrast on identical deals cleanly separates payoff-given-exposure from exposure alone. Weaknesses: (1) W0 is the only cell that separates H-payoff from H-familiarity when W1 rises, yet the kill rule allows skipping it 'if W1/P1/P0 settle it'. They cannot settle that split. (2) The W arms see few stall chances: 74% of pilot-v2's random-deck games end by no Pokémon, and almost no wide deck holds both Chansey and Snorlax. A low W1 is then predicted by H-exposure, H-interaction, H-slow-accumulation and a low-dose H-payoff alike, so W1 low is not diagnostic. H-payoff's 'W1 >= 0.50' prediction should be conditional, with the decision resting on P1-P0 and on W1-W0. (3) H-familiarity's prediction omits P0. If familiarity is the cause, P0 also rises, which separates it from H-payoff (P0 <= 0.35). Familiarity is also not truly equalised between the W arms (each wall card in about 8 of 512 decks) and the P arms (in nearly every game), so exposure and familiarity stay partly confounded. (4) H-incumbency and H-exposure both predict a low H1. They differ only on H1 < W arms, which is a small margin. (5) The 'not a cause' bar of moving < 0.04 from 0.264 is about 1.3 pair-clustered SE of a paired difference. Set it at >= 2 SE (about 0.06-0.08), or decide by CI. (6) 40-iteration seed noise is unmeasured. Replicating only arms that end at 0.40-0.55 leaves the decisive P1/P0 cells single-seed. (7) The 0.264 baseline was measured under the old ending label, which also shaped pilot-v2's own training. Re-measure iteration 0 after the label fix. (8) bal-1's k-means (k 4 on card counts) may split the walls into several clusters, since 53 of 99 decks hold both Chansey and Snorlax at 479. If so, 'equal per cluster' still overweights walls and does not test equal adaptation.
required_changes: Run W0 whenever W1 rises by >= 0.10. Make W1 vs W0 the payoff test in the no-wall field, and P1 vs P0 the decisive payoff-given-exposure test. Make H-payoff's W1 prediction conditional on stall opportunity, and report W1's deck-out share.
Add P0 >= 0.45 to H-familiarity's predictions, and state that familiarity is only partly equalised between the W and P arms.

Replace the 0.04 'not a cause' bar with a paired-difference CI on identical deals, or a bar of >= 2 pair-clustered SE (about 0.07). Pre-register the decisive contrasts (P1-P0, W1-W0, P1-W1) as paired differences with CIs.
Run a seed-2 replicate of P1 and P0 regardless of where they end, because they carry the decisive contrast.
Re-measure pilot-v2's iteration-0 verdict and ending mix after the env label fix, and use that as the baseline instead of 0.264.

For bal-1, check that the Chansey/Snorlax walls fall in one cluster, or define clusters so they do (for example k chosen by silhouette, with the wall cluster checked by card presence). Check that at least 3 non-wall clusters with enough decks exist before running.

reviews.reasons: The code supports the design. rl/train.py has --matchups-file (names or {name, cards} lists), --init-from, --deckout-win, --d/--tok-layers/--heads/--count-features and seed, and its defaults differ from the adopted settings (lr 3e-4, epochs 3), so writing them out, as planned, is correct. rl/decks.py wide_deck already draws Trainers and special Energy over the whole pool, so the coverage floor is a small resampling wrapper. The label fix is a reorder of two lines in env/game.js `ending`, with the reward applied in runner.js/remote_worker.js. The claim of 2-3 h of code is plausible. Rules: deck-out 0 arms and H1 (trained on the human lists) are quarantined diagnostics, the same use as #131 diag-human-practice and allowed under rule 1 (evaluation and diagnosis). k-means clusters, coverage floors and the payoff are game-agnostic, and W1's lineage needs Evan's approval as stated. No rule violation. The compute cost is underestimated, and 'no screen slot' is wrong. Each train.py job uses 14 workers by default and about 3.5 GB of GPU. Three concurrent fine-tunes would oversubscribe the 16-20 CPU threads, so the measured 1-1.5 min an iteration when run alone becomes about 2-3 min, and each 40-iteration wave takes 1.5-2 h rather than 1-1.5 h. The jobs use the same GPU and RAM budget as the 3 metagame screens, so they cannot run beside 3 live screens within the 80% cap. The full plan is W1, P1, P0, W0, H1, bal-1, seed-2 replicates, a possible P1 extension to 80, and 6 readouts an arm of 1,152 games plus the twin and h2h. That is about 7-9 arm-runs, closer to two evenings than one. Editing env/game.js while screens run changes the ending labels and deck-out statistics for any worker that reloads the engine, and would pay any deck-out-0 job differently mid-run. Put it behind a flag, or apply it when no screens are live.
required_changes: Re-cost the plan: about 2-3 min an iteration with three concurrent fine-tunes (or cap workers, for example 6 each), 7-9 arm-runs including W0, H1, bal-1, replicates and the P1 extension, so about two evenings. State that the fine-tunes occupy the screen slots, or run them only when fewer screens are live.
Implement the ending-label fix as an opt-in flag (or apply it only when no screens are running), and re-measure pilot-v2's baseline under the fixed label.
Set --workers explicitly per arm so three jobs together stay within the 80% CPU/RAM cap, and write out every adopted PPO setting, since the train.py defaults differ (lr 3e-4, epochs 3).

title: Separate best-response pilot against frozen walls: can learnable counter-play beat the walls when their pilot cannot adapt?
rivals: R-exploitable: the walls win because their opponents' pilot never specialises against them; a separate network trained only on the challenger seat against the frozen walls' pilot beats them (F2; in #55 separate-network exploiters went 0.00/0.06 -> 0.94/0.81 against the leader)
R-robust-clockless: the walls beat any learnable counter-play in the clockless game; a dedicated pilot still loses by deck-out after about 60 turns
R-human-specific: only the human lists hold a counter structure; self-discovered decks stay losers with the same dedicated pilot (a discovery gap)
design: Code: rl/train.py --opponent-pilot P puts a frozen checkpoint, built from its own config, into model slot 1 at weight 1 through the league's slot path; only the learner's seat is recorded; matchups [challenger, wall]. Frozen side: resetcap499's pilot plays the 3 walls of #137 plus 9 more of its best walls (sampled in training, greedy in readouts). Two slots, 30 iterations, each from pilot-v2 it349 with its shape flags, adopted PPO settings, deck-out wins 1: arm H (diagnosis) the 24 lists as challengers; arm S 24 self-discovered non-wall decks (best of each non-wall cluster across snapshots) plus 24 wide decks. Readouts every 5 iterations: challengers vs the 3 #137 walls and 3 held-out walls, each side under its own pilot, greedy, 8 a pair on #137's deals; endings and win turns; per archetype (Wigglytuff, Haymaker: anomaly A2, Haymaker's Fighting attackers hit both walls for Weakness yet score only 0.35).

predictions.predicted: H rises from about 0.24 (#137's own/v2 gave the walls 0.761) to >= 0.55 by 30, mostly through Prize wins before turn 45, held-out walls within 0.05 of trained ones; S >= 0.45
H <= 0.40 at 30 with >= 50% of its losses by deck-out after turn 55: the levers are the cut and search (C20, C38, C33)
H >= 0.55 while S <= 0.35: counters exist only in human-built decks; send effort to exploration

readout: The challengers' score against the frozen walls' pilot on held-out deals as a learning curve, with endings and per-archetype splits.
noise_and_power: 576 games a readout (24 x 3 x 8): pair-clustered SE about 0.025; the start is about 0.24 and the shared pilot's practice gained only 0.06 in 20 iterations (#131), so 0.55 is about 12 SE up; an effect like #55's would be unmistakable. One seed per arm; rerun H with seed 2 if it ends 0.40-0.55.
kill_rule: Stop an arm at 15 iterations if the challenger score rose < 0.05 (as the wide challengers' 0.0 in #141's smoke), else at 30; stop if > 2% of games hit the decision cap and trace them (a frozen-pilot loop is itself a finding).
cost: About 3-4 h of code (frozen slot from its own config, one-sided recording, panels, readout hook); 2 slots x 30 iterations at 1-1.5 min, under an hour of wall time, plus 576-game readouts under a minute each.
distinct_from: #131/#133 put the lists on one side of 30% of games while the shared pilot trained both seats, so the walls' pilot adapted too (H17/H19 do-not-repeat 'diag-human-practice'); scr-vs479 and scr-gatevs479 trained the shared network from the challenger side; #55-57 used separate networks in the old swap-operator league. H17's verifier lists 'a separate best-response pilot trained against the walls' as untested; this replaces H19's two-sided counterfactual with a one-sided best response.
rules_check: Arm H trains on the human lists: diagnosis only, never a method (as #131). Arm S uses self-discovered and wide decks with a separate network and the true reward: rule-compliant as a candidate exploiter-pilot component, though its pilot-v2 start is diagnostic-grade (a real component starts from the population pilot or a human-free P0).
value: Decides among a separate exploiter pilot in the ecosystem (R-exploitable), the cut and search (R-robust-clockless), or discovery (R-human-specific); explains A2 per archetype.
merged_from: judge: Separate best-response pilot against frozen walls: can learnable counter-play beat the walls when the walls' pilot cannot adapt?

reviews.reasons: No earlier dedicated reviews, so all three angles are new. I checked every family that could overlap. H17 (challenger practice): scr-vs479 and scr-gatevs479 trained the one shared network from the challenger side, and the wide-challenger smoke scored 0.0 (#141). H17's verifier lists 'separate best-response pilot trained against the walls' as genuinely untested, and a grep after #59 finds no separate or exploiter pilot run against the walls. H19 (human-side misplay): #131 diag-human-practice put the lists on one side of 30% of games with the shared pilot training both seats, so the walls' pilot adapted too; #137 swapped pilots without training. H36 and H38 (deck-owning agents, exploiters): #55-57 used separate networks only in the old swap-operator league, against a drafting leader, with no frozen wall pilot. H20 (a frozen independent pilot as judge or drafter) froze the judge, not the opponent. H14, H15 and H16 changed the shared pilot. What makes C18 distinct comes from two factors the record never varied together: (a) a dedicated network that learns only the challenger seat; (b) a frozen opponent pilot (resetcap499) on the current walls. Together they give a one-sided best response, not the shared, two-sided adaptation of #131 or the swap-operator league of #55. No do-not-repeat entry matches: arm H uses the human lists as fixed decks, as diag-human-practice did, but with a separate network and a frozen walls' pilot, which that run lacked. Minor overlap: arm S's wide decks repeat #141's 0.0 smoke condition, but here a dedicated learner trains on them, so that is a new factor, not a rerun.

The design is diagnostic in principle. A frozen opponent with a dedicated learner is the cleanest test of F2 (the judge co-adapts to the walls), and n=576 a readout (SE about 0.025) is enough for the 0.24 -> 0.55 contrast. But five problems weaken the inference. (1) A confound sits in the R-exploitable reading. A dedicated network trained against one frozen policy can learn that policy's quirks (a fixed greedy wall pilot is easy to exploit, as #55's 0 -> 0.94 suggests), not counter-play against the wall decks. The held-out walls use the same frozen pilot, so they cannot separate 'the decks are beatable' from 'this pilot is exploitable'. Every live hypothesis predicts some rise against a frozen opponent, so the R-exploitable outcome is not unique. (2) A live rival is missing, R-incompetent: the learner cannot pick up prize-race tactics in 30 iterations. Trainer competence has been flat at 0.43-0.48, #131 gained 0.06 in 20 iterations, and #141 shows the human lists lose slow prize races, not deck-outs. This rival predicts H <= 0.40 with losses mainly by Prizes. The candidate leaves that outcome unassigned, or misreads it as R-robust-clockless, whose deck-out-after-55 signature #141 already argues against. (3) H vs S compares levels, and the starting levels differ: wide challengers start near 0.0 (#141), the lists near 0.24. R-human-specific vs R-exploitable must be read on the gain from each arm's own iteration-0 score, not on S >= 0.45 vs <= 0.35. (4) The 0.24 baseline comes from #137's probe at 32 games a pair, possibly sampled play, while the readouts are greedy at 8 a pair on #139's deals. An iteration-0 readout under the exact readout conditions is needed. (5) The kill rule is miscalibrated. A rise below 0.05 at 15 iterations is about 1.4 SE of a difference of two readouts (SE about 0.035), so a real but slow learner (the #131 rate) is killed about half the time. That would produce a false R-robust or R-incompetent verdict, the short-horizon bias the analysis warns about. train.py already logs win_vs per opponent every iteration on about 600 learner games, which gives a much better-powered learning curve to gate on. Per-archetype splits (Sponge 2 lists, about 48 games, SE about 0.07) are descriptive only. The readout does match the nodes (a pilot-level score for an N2/N3/N4 question).
required_changes: Add a held-out-pilot readout to separate exploiting the deck from exploiting the pilot: challengers (learner) vs the walls piloted by another population pilot never trained against (e.g. scr-resetent 496 or the scr-gate479 pilot, both rating the walls 0.68-0.75). Optionally also add a re-adaptation check: fine-tune a copy of the walls' pilot for 5 iterations against the final learner, then re-read. R-exploitable should hold within 0.10 on the unseen pilot. If the gain appears only against resetcap499, call that a new outcome: the gain exploits a frozen pilot's quirks.

Add a rival R-incompetent (the learner cannot learn the prize-race tactics): H <= 0.40 with most losses by Prizes (not deck-out), and the learner's training-time win_vs plateauing. State what each rival predicts for the ending mix, using #141's Prize-race finding.

Restate the H vs S predictions as gains from each arm's own measured iteration-0 score (not absolute levels), and run the iteration-0 readout under the exact readout conditions: greedy, 8 a pair, #139's deals, both pilots.

Recalibrate the kill rule. Gate on the per-iteration training win_vs trend (about 600 games an iteration) plus readouts at 0/5/10/15: stop at 15 only if the readout gain is below 2 SE of a difference (about 0.07) and the training win_vs slope over iterations 5-15 is within noise of 0. Otherwise run to 30.
Mark per-archetype splits as descriptive (no decisions on archetypes with fewer than 7 lists), and pre-register what the 0.40-0.55 zone means beyond 'rerun with seed 2'.

reviews.reasons: The code supports most of this. In rl/train.py's GPU path, opponents given as 'slot:k' are served from a models dict, and env/remote_worker.js (lines 125-152) records only the 'learner' seat, randomises the learner's seat, and always gives the learner deck A of each matchup pair. So one-sided recording and matchups [challenger, wall] already work, and --matchups-file takes {name, cards} decklists. The work left is about what the candidate says: snapshot models are built with build_model(args, info), that is, with the learner's own config. A frozen opponent with a different architecture (resetcap499 in deck_mode cross, d 256) beside a pilot-v2 learner needs its own model built from its checkpoint config. rl/metagame.py already does this for --judge-pilot (frozen(), line 389), so it can be reused. Also needed: an --opponent-pilot flag at weight 1, and a readout hook. probe_matchups.py already runs two-pilot pairings, so readouts are cheap. Total 2-4 h. Watch two things. (a) train.py's argparse defaults are not the adopted recipe (lr 3e-4 vs 2e-4, epochs 3 vs 2, shaping 0, d 192, tok-layers 3). Pass every setting explicitly, along with pilot-v2's shape flags, or the run silently uses pre-adoption settings (the analysis section 9 clutter item). (b) The iteration time is likely underestimated. 14 workers x 4,096 transitions, recording only the learner seat, in long wall games (60+ turns), is about 600-700 games an iteration, plus serving the frozen model. Expect about 2-3 min an iteration, so 30 iterations take about 1-1.5 h an arm, plus readouts (576 games x up to 3 pilot conditions). Still cheap, within 2 of the 3 screen slots (about 2.7 GB RAM and 3.5 GB GPU each with two models loaded), and within the 16-thread cap through rl/limits.py. It fits the user's 'cheaper spend' choice. Rules: arm H trains a pilot on the human lists, the same diagnostic use as #131, which Evan allowed for diagnosis. It must stay a diagnostic, never a component. Arm S is human-free: pilot-v2 start, self-discovered and wide decks, the true end reward. It is game-agnostic: a frozen opponent slot plus a separate learner is a generic league mechanism that carries to MTG, and nothing card-specific is added.
required_changes: Pass the adopted PPO settings and pilot-v2's architecture flags explicitly to rl/train.py (--lr 2e-4 --epochs 2, the shaping as intended, --d/--tok-layers/--deck-mode matching pilot-v2, --inference gpu): its defaults are pre-adoption.
Build the frozen opponent from its own checkpoint config by reusing rl/metagame.py's frozen() helper, not build_model(args, info), and assert that both models consume the same token encoding.
Budget about 2-3 min an iteration (about 1-1.5 h an arm) plus readout time for the extra held-out-pilot condition, and check nvidia-smi against the 80% cap with two models loaded per process.

title: Core-transplant probe: does a fresh wide field pull toward the walls' core under each pilot?
rivals: H1 co-adapted gradient: only the walls' own pilot rewards the walls' core inside generic decks
H2 stall is strong: every competent plain-result pilot rewards the core anywhere in the clockless game
H-valley: the core pays only inside an assembled wall shell; walls are a coordinated basin reachable only from wall-like states
design: Evaluation only. (1) Core: the 8-16 cards most over-represented in the resetcap-499 population relative to 99 wide decks (ratio of mean copies), computed by script. (2) In each of 99 wide decks (rl/decks.py wide_deck, fixed seed) remove the same kind-matched set and add: FULL (the core), HALF (the core's Pokemon only), CTRL (a kind-matched random package of the same size); composition identical across variants. Optional diagnosis-only contrast: the Haymaker core (over-represented cards of the 7 Haymaker lists). (3) Each variant plays 16 games vs the wide field on common deals (same opponent, seat, seed across variants). Pilots: resetcap-499, pilot-v2, base-cont it39 (plain result, C07's panel), W (C30) when available, random init as floor. Positive control: the 3 walls with their core replaced by CTRL, vs the same field under the 499 pilot.

predictions.predicted: FULL-CTRL >= +0.12 under the 499 pilot; <= +0.04 under pilot-v2, base-cont and W
FULL-CTRL >= +0.08 under every competent plain-result pilot (499, base-cont, W), lower under pilot-v2 (deck-out-0 trained)
FULL-CTRL <= +0.03 and HALF-CTRL near 0 under all pilots including 499, while the positive control shows the core is worth >= +0.10 inside the wall shell

readout: FULL-CTRL and HALF-CTRL with paired SE per pilot; the positive control; the Haymaker-core contrast if run.
noise_and_power: 99 decks x 16 paired games = 1,584 pairs per variant per pilot: paired SE about 0.012-0.018, bands 4+ SE apart. Kind matching removes the composition confound that C23 measures.
kill_rule: If the positive control moves the walls' win rate < 0.05 under the 499 pilot, the core definition is wrong: recompute once, else stop.
cost: About 1.5 h of code on top of probe_matchups.py and about 30 min of GPU (5 pilots x 3 variants x 1,584 games plus controls, greedy).
distinct_from: #147 (H18, H22) judged whole walls against the lists; #127's two hand-made variants moved walls toward human types; H07 swapped Trainers for Energy inside existing decks. None transplanted the walls' core into rules-generated decks with kind-matched controls and a half-core dose; no H18 do-not-repeat probe is rerun.
rules_check: Evaluation only; the core comes from the population's own decks; the Haymaker contrast uses human lists for diagnosis only.
value: Predicts whether prevention starts (C41, Stage 3) get pulled back into walls by their pilot: H1 keep the judge fresh and prevention works; H2 the game definition must change first (C33); H-valley fresh populations are protected and walls form only when proposals assemble a shell (group changes, mutants), which sets the readout window and makes the X link concrete (C28).
merged_from: scratch: Core-transplant probe: does a fresh wide field pull toward the walls' core under each pilot?

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for this candidate. I checked it against H03, H07, H15-H23, H39-H46 in the ledger and grepped the progress log for transplant, graft, valley, core, kind-matched, over-represented and the #127 probe variants. Nothing matches its configuration. The nearest do-not-repeat items are H18's 'probe_matchups.py on resetcap 499 walls under the #147 pilots' and H18/H19's four-pilot pairing of the 499 walls against the 24 lists (#137). C19 uses the same script, but on new host decks: the 99 rules-generated wide decks plus a population-derived core. It also plays against a new opponent set, the wide field rather than the human lists. #127's two hand-made variants replaced the walls' Pokemon with human-type Pokemon, the opposite direction, and judged them against the lists. H07 (#68, #69, trainer_value.py) swapped Energy and Trainers inside existing decks. None of these varied the host deck context (wall-free, rules-generated), the dose (FULL / HALF) or a kind-matched random control. The distinct factors are those three, plus the judge panel applied to the same transplant. It is also distinct in node: it gives the first direct test of the X link (N7/N9: whether walls are reachable from a fresh state), which the analysis lists as 'not yet tested directly'. Its overlap with other candidates, not with the ledger: the H-valley rival overlaps C28 (fitness along edit paths from the walls to human archetypes), and the pilot panel overlaps C07's judge zoo. C19 goes in the opposite direction from C28 (core into wide hosts, not walls towards human lists), so the two complement each other. They should still share the core definition and the pilot set so the results can be compared, not be built twice.

Good: the readout matches the node. FULL-CTRL measured under each judge is a judge-dependence readout (N4), and the positive control checks that the core is real. The three rivals predict different signs and patterns across pilots, so 'relapses like the control' is not the only possible outcome. A one-shot evaluation has no short-horizon bias, so the kill rule (positive control < 0.05: recompute the core once, else stop) is calibrated as a validity check. Problems: (1) The control has a confound. CTRL is a random kind-matched package, but the core holds population-selected cards that are also human staples (Oak, Gambler, Energy Removal, DCE, Bill; #127 per-deck means). Under any competent pilot, cards that selection picked should beat random cards. So a 'generic selected-card quality' rival predicts FULL-CTRL > 0 under every competent pilot, and that is H2's signature. H2 cannot be told apart from 'good cards beat random cards'. (2) HALF is not defined. It adds only the core's Pokemon, yet 'composition identical across variants' needs the Trainer and Energy slots filled with something; it should be core Pokemon plus CTRL's non-Pokemon part. Only H-valley predicts HALF; H1 and H2 have no HALF prediction. HALF is the wall-specific part (Chansey, Snorlax), and the split between that part and the staples is the comparison that separates H2 from card quality. (3) Power is thin where H1 and H2 differ. They part under base-cont and W at <= +0.04 versus >= +0.08, a gap of 0.04. The stated SE of 0.012-0.018 treats the 1,584 games as independent pairs. The effect will vary across the 99 host decks, so the SE must be clustered by host deck (likely 0.02-0.025), which puts the gap at about 2 SE. The 0.04-0.08 band is left unassigned. (4) The positive control's sample size and SE are not stated: only 3 walls, so its error is dominated by between-deck variation. (5) The pilot that decides between H1 and H2 is W (C30), and W does not exist yet. Without it, the test rests on base-cont, which trained on meta-99 decks with Snorlax in 143 of 477, so it is not wall-naive, and on pilot-v2, which carries the deck-out-0 confound H18 already flags. The random-init floor helps (it measures raw card strength such as HP) but needs a stated prediction. (6) Kind-matching holds the Energy count fixed. The probe therefore says nothing about the Energy axis of the ground truth, and the write-up should say so.
required_changes: Make the Haymaker-core contrast mandatory as a selection-matched control: the over-represented cards of the 7 Haymaker lists, diagnosis only, kind-matched and the same size. Alternatively, split FULL into a wall-specific block (Chansey, Snorlax, healing special Energy) and a shared-staple block (Oak, Gambler, ER, DCE, Bill). Under H2 the wall-specific block must carry the gain; under 'generic card quality' the staples or the Haymaker core gain as much.
Define HALF as the core's Pokemon plus CTRL's Trainer and Energy part, and write H1 and H2 predictions for HALF-CTRL and for the random-init floor.

Report deck-clustered SEs (bootstrap over the 99 host decks) and assign the 0.04-0.08 band in advance. For the deciding pilots (499, base-cont, W), raise the games per host deck to 32, or use more host decks, so the H1/H2 gap is at least 3 clustered SE.

State the positive control's games (for example, 3 walls x 99 wide opponents x 4 games for each of the two variants) and its SE. Use at least 2 wall sets (resetcap 499 plus main 460) so it does not rest on 3 decks.
Treat W as required for the H1-vs-H2 verdict: report the H1/H2 split as provisional until W exists, and note that base-cont is not wall-naive.
