title: Acceptance audit: would a powered searched verdict, a clone-invariant panel or a Prize-decided cut reverse what selection accepts? (paired, offline)
rivals: R-strength: greedy play over-rates Pokemon-adding and under-rates Trainer-adding edits; at adequate power one-turn search reverses the preference (simulation-balancing bias)
R-redundancy: scoring against a field about 80% walls rewards mirror-winning edits; equal weights over behaviourally distinct opponents reverse it (clone sensitivity)

R-draw-haven: the plain 60-turn draw pays survival (in scr-jsearch479's searched games over 480-498, no-Pokemon endings fell from 105 to 23-45 of 200 and limit draws rose from 37 to 93); Pokemon-adding edits turn losses into 0.5 draws and lose that edge under the event's Prize decision
R-invariant: the Pokemon-up, Trainers-down preference is what this game pays under every affordable judge, weighting and reading of the cut
design: Frozen state: scr-t60gate479's last checkpoint (pilot, head, population; 80 of 99 decks hold Chansey and Snorlax; in matched scr-jsearch479 rows accepted moves from 488 added 1.2-3.1 Pokemon and cut 0.6-2.9 Trainers each). Per deck, the parent plus three variants built by in-place substitution (unchanged cards keep their list positions so shuffles align; builder shared with C26): (h) one draw of the run's head, as the loop draws it; (t) Trainers +4 / Pokemon -4 (copies of Trainers the deck runs replace its least-copied Pokemon, legal); (p) Pokemon +4 / Trainers -4, the drift itself, positive control. Opponents: U = 16 population decks drawn as the loop draws them; P = a clone-invariant equal-weight panel (best deck of each of 6 k-means clusters plus the best of main 290 and scr-resetent 496). Parent and variant share opponent, seat and seed. Judges with the regime's 60-turn limit: G greedy; S one-turn search on both seats, CRN k4 d4 (C03). Greedy: every variant x (16 U + 8 P) deals; searched: (t), (p), (h) and parent x 8 U deals; the parent's deals also played greedy for the control-variate rho and beta. Every game scored twice from its row: as the loop scores it (draw at the cut 0.5) and under the event's rule (more Prizes at the cut 2/3, equal 1/3 each); per-opponent results kept for later weightings (max-entropy Nash, cluster-balanced).

predictions.predicted: over the 99 decks: Delta(t) under S minus G >= +0.05 and Delta(p) under S minus G <= -0.05; the head draws' slope of Delta on Delta-Trainers higher under S by >= 0.01 a card; S - G similar on U and P
Delta(t) P minus U >= +0.04 and Delta(p) P minus U <= -0.04 while S about equals G; wall opponents carry all of (p)'s gain
under the Prize reading Delta(p) <= 0 and Delta(t) >= 0.04 above its plain-draw value, concentrated in games reaching the cut: the fix is a judging rule (C33)
Delta(p) > 0 and Delta(t) < 0 under every condition and reading, all differences within +/-0.03: do not run C38; escalate to the game definition, a stronger judge or the learner

readout: Mean paired Delta (variant minus parent) per variant, judge, opponent set and reading; the head draws' composition slopes; the share of z 1.0 gate decisions that would differ from today's greedy uniform-field judge, against the null redraw rate; endings each variant shifts; rho and beta between greedy and searched outcomes on the same deal.
noise_and_power: A deck's Delta from 16 paired deals has SE about 0.15 (rho 0.2-0.3, like #50's phi 0.23-0.28); the mean over 99 decks about 0.016 greedy (24 deals) and 0.022 searched (8 deals), so S - G (SE about 0.027) resolves 0.05-0.06 at about 2 SE and P - U (about 0.02) resolves 0.04; the two readings differ only by games reaching the cut. If parent-variant rho < 0.15, double the deals.
kill_rule: After the greedy half (about 15 min): if P - U and plain-vs-Prize differences are within +/-0.02 for (t) and (p), and searched S - G on the first 30 decks is within +/-0.02, stop and record R-invariant (provisional). If parent-variant rho < 0.1, stop and fix the substitution code.
cost: About half a day of code (variant builder, panel builder, paired dispatch through C03, second scoring). About 9,500 greedy games (15 GPU-min) and 4,000 searched (about 1.8 h at 1.6 s a game with 4 workers) on one GPU share.
distinct_from: #68 swapped about 4 Energy for Bill, Oak or Computer Search in meta-99 decks under greedy and SimpleBot judges (H07 do-not-repeat; its verifier lists the swap on the walls under search on both seats as untested). scr-jsearch479 gave about 2 unpaired searched games a candidate under a min rule that cannot raise a score (analysis section 9; H23); H24/H25 measured gate noise, not judge preference; no family varied who a deck is scored against (critic gap). #139/#147 read the Prize rule only for walls vs lists with the end-count proxy. C15 re-scores the loop's natural decisions in untimed states; this tests designed edits at full power, paired, under three judging factors.
rules_check: Human-free. The designed variants only probe the judge and are never drafting moves (Evan, 10-06: no forced card-specific swaps); search, CRN and card-count clustering are game-agnostic; the Prize reading evaluates the game's own end score.
value: Gates every in-loop judge screen before a 6-minute iteration is spent: R-strength runs C38's searched arms, R-redundancy its panel arm, R-draw-haven turns C33's judging-only question into a concrete request, R-invariant closes the estimator and weighting family; the measured rho and beta size C38's control-variate estimator.
merged_from: judge: Acceptance audit: would a powered searched verdict, a clone-invariant panel or a Prize-decided cut reverse what selection accepts? (paired, offline)

reviews.reasons:
No earlier reviews exist for C20. I read the full ledger digest and grepped progress-log #148-#149. C20 is distinct from the ledger on three factors that were never varied.

(1) Who a deck is scored against. Every family scores a deck against the population mean. The critic's N4/N5 coverage gap says no current-loop family varies the opponent mix, so the U-vs-P (clone-invariant panel) contrast is new.

(2) A searched verdict at adequate power on paired, designed edits. H23's verifier records that scr-jsearch479's min rule made search inert: 2.02 searched games a candidate, 6 flips against 15.5 from noise. The critic's top-untested item 1 is 'powered search judge'. H07's verifier lists swaps on the walls under search on both seats as untested.

(3) A Prize reading of population-vs-population games. The do-not-repeat lists of H03, H04 and H19 cover re-scoring only the 3 resetcap499 walls against the human lists (#139, #147), a different object.

No do-not-repeat item matches:
- H07's 'swaps on meta-99 decks' were Energy-to-Bill/Oak/CS swaps on a different state, under greedy and SimpleBot judges. C20's swaps are Pokemon-for-Trainer, on t60gate decks, under S and P.
- H22's 'search k4d4 as the only change, without a limit' does not apply: C20 keeps the 60-turn limit.
- H23's '--judge-search 200 min rule' is in-loop. C20 is offline and paired.

Overlaps inside the slate, which are not ledger repeats:
- C20's (h)-greedy-U arm measures the same thing as C26: head draws paired against fixed opponents under the greedy judge with the 60-turn limit, regressed on dP/dT/dE. Merge them, or reuse C26's games for (h) greedy, rather than run it twice.
- C15 re-scores the loop's natural decisions under the round rule. C20's Prize reading of designed edits is a different object, so both can stand.

The distinct_from field is accurate. I checked the scr-jsearch479 searched endings in the log: no-Pokemon endings fell 105 to 23-45 and time endings rose 37 to 93. The accepted-move ranges for 488-498 are P +1.22 to +3.06 and T -0.59 to -2.87.
required_changes: Merge the (h)-variant greedy-U arm with C26, or take C26's paired head-draw games as that cell, so the same measurement is not run twice in this slate.

reviews.reasons:
The readout matches the nodes: paired deck-level Delta under alternative judges is a judge/selection readout, and the design is offline, so short-horizon bias does not apply. The factorial (judge x opponent set x reading) separates R-strength, R-redundancy and R-draw-haven in principle, and pairing parent and variant on opponent, seat and seed is the right design. Seven problems remain, and they decide whether the experiment can separate the rivals.

(a) A rival the logs favour is missing. In both relevant screens the composition of accepted moves is close to the composition of proposals. scr-t60gate479 (the frozen state) at 487-498: acc minus prop averages about +0.10 Pokemon and -0.05 Trainers a move, against about +1.2 Pokemon proposed. At this state its accepted moves cut Energy, not Trainers (e.g. 490: acc [+2.59, +0.24, -2.82]). scr-jsearch479 gives about +0.05 P and -0.26 T. So the drift is mostly the proposals passing through a nearly neutral judge. This rival, R-neutral/proposal-driven, predicts Delta(p) and Delta(t) near 0 under G. None of the four listed rivals predicts that, so a likely outcome has no reading.

(b) The power figures are optimistic.
- P - U compares 16 U deals with 8 P deals on different opponents, so it is unpaired. Its SE is about 0.027, not 0.02, so a 0.04 effect sits at about 1.5 SE.
- S - G at SE 0.027 resolves 0.05 at under 2 SE.
- The predicted slope difference of 0.01 a card on the head draws has SE about 0.017 (8 searched deals, Delta-Trainers SD about 1.5), which is under 1 SE.

(c) R-invariant's '+/-0.03' is about 1 SE, so a null cannot confirm it. Confirming equivalence (TOST) at that bound needs an SE of about 0.015.

(d) The kill rule is miscalibrated. S - G on the first 30 decks has SE about 0.05, so a +/-0.02 window says nothing and the rule can stop a real 0.05 effect about 20% of the time. The searched half costs only a few hours, so the early stop on R-invariant saves little and risks a false close.

(e) R-draw-haven's threshold is near its ceiling. The Prize reading moves a game by only +/-1/6, and only for games at the cut (about 28% under greedy at 498, about 45% of searched games late in jsearch479). Delta(t) rising 0.04 above its plain value would need nearly every cut game to break the variant's way. Restate the threshold as the share of cut games that change direction; it is paired on the same games, so its SE is small.

(f) The panel P may not be clone-invariant in practice. K-means on card counts over a field that is 80% walls will put most of the 6 clusters inside the wall type, and the two hall-of-fame decks are also wall-era. P - U then has no lever.

(g) Searched-line capping contaminates S at this state. Capped lines rose to 640-3,827 an iteration at 491-497 in scr-jsearch479, and those lines are scored 0.
required_changes: Add rival R-neutral (the drift comes from proposals; the judge is nearly indifferent). Prediction: |Delta(p)|, |Delta(t)| <= 0.03 under G on U. As a free pre-check, report acc minus prop per kind (P/T/E) over every gated screen's log.

Pair S against G on the same deals: play every variant greedily on the 8 searched U deals and use the per-deal S-G difference with the measured rho. Raise P to 16 deals per deck so P-U has SE <= 0.02. State the SE each prediction is read at.
Restate R-invariant as an equivalence test (TOST) at a bound the design can reach (SE <= 0.015, or widen the bound to +/-0.05), or call it 'not separable' when the CIs straddle.
Drop the R-invariant early stop on the first 30 decks. Keep only the rho < 0.1 code-bug stop.

Recast R-draw-haven's threshold as the share of games reaching the cut whose Prize reading favours the variant over the parent (the counterfactual is exact on those games), and state the maximum possible Delta shift given the observed cut rates (about 28% G, about 45% S).

Build the panel so that at most 2 of the 8 decks are walls (e.g. cluster on a descriptor that separates Chansey+Snorlax decks, or stratify by the wall flag), and report the panel's wall share beside P-U.
Log capped search lines per arm, and report S both with and without games that had capped lines.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: passes. The designed (t)/(p) variants only probe the judge and are never drafting moves, which agrees with Evan's ruling against forced card-specific swaps. Kind-level substitution, k-means on card counts, and search with CRN are all game-agnostic. The Prize reading uses the game's own end score (rule 2) for diagnosis only, and using it in judging stays with C33. No human list or bot enters training.

State and data: runs/screens/scr-t60gate479 holds checkpoint.pt (498) and population_it0494.pt.

Code against the repo:
- rl/gpu_matrix.py play() already takes decks as {name, cards} lists, so order is kept, and pair_keys gives shared deals.
- It keeps per-game results, and env/runner.js rows carry prizesLeft at the game's end.
- Under --max-turns 60 the game ends at the cut, so the Prize reading needs no new trace (C01 is not needed).
- gpu_matrix.py today has no maxTurns or judgeSearch pass-through (grep), so the searched arm depends on C03's dispatch code (about 3-4 h) and on C26's builder. 'Half a day' holds only if C03 and C26 land first; standalone it is about one day.
- The builder needs explicit rules for two cases:
  - (t) adds copies of Trainers the deck already runs, but walls run many 4-ofs, so a fallback is needed.
  - Removing the 'least-copied Pokemon' can strand evolutions, so the variant would then measure line-breaking rather than Trainer value.

Compute is underestimated. The 1.6 s a searched game comes from 480. Late scr-jsearch479 iterations took 347-665 s per 200 searched games (1.7-3.3 s a game), with capped-line bursts. So about 3,200-4,000 searched games run 2-3.5 h, and 4-7 h if deals are doubled for power. The greedy part (about 9,500 games, 12-18 min at 9-13 games/s) is fine.

Machine: 4 search workers beside 3 screens reaches the 16-thread budget, so run it with at most 2 screens, or overnight. GPU memory is a small share.
required_changes: State the dependency explicitly: the searched arm needs C03's judgeSearch and maxTurns pass-through in rl/gpu_matrix.py (absent today) and C26's position-aligned builder. Cost C20 at about 1 day if they are not built first.

Revise the searched compute to 1.7-3.3 s a game, as measured in scr-jsearch479 at 485-498: about 2-3.5 h at the stated deals, 4-7 h with the doubled deals the power fix needs. Schedule it with at most 2 concurrent screens, or overnight.

Specify the builder's fallbacks: when the deck's Trainers are at the copy limit, use another rule-generic choice (e.g. Trainers drawn uniformly from the pool's Trainer kind, logged); never remove a card that another card in the deck requires (no stranded evolutions); log every variant's realised dP/dT/dE.
Confirm with one smoke game that searched rows from env/remote_worker.js carry prizesLeft and ending, so the Prize reading works for S as well as G.

title: Judge-variance audit: does the spread of a deck's score across judges single out the walls, and does a spread penalty rank decks differently from the searched verdict?
rivals: R-A8: pilot dependence marks degenerate stall decks (walls 0.72 under their own pilot, 0.24 under pilot-v2, while in result #2 the deck explained about 70% of cross-play strength); a mean-minus-spread score over rule-compliant judges ranks non-wall decks above the walls
R-generic: every type's score swings as much across judges; a spread penalty is noise
R-collinear: over judges the loop could use, the spread is just |searched - greedy| and ranks decks as the searched verdict does
design: No new games beyond C07, C16 and C17; at most 1,000 greedy games fill missing deck x judge cells. For each panel deck (walls, self-discovered non-walls, wide decks; human lists for evaluation) take its panel score under J1, J1', J2, J3 (C16), pilot-v2, C07's wall-naive judges and C17's arm pilots (W1, P1, bal-1) as reset-judge stand-ins. Compute the mean and SD across (a) all judges and (b) rule-compliant judges only; the variance split into deck, judge and deck x judge (A8's 70% deck share as reference); rankings by mean - lambda x SD for lambda 0.5, 1, 2; Kendall tau between the penalised ranking and J2's.

predictions.predicted: the walls' SD across rule-compliant judges >= 2x the median SD of self-discovered non-walls and of the human lists; at lambda 1 >= 1 self-discovered non-wall ranks above every wall; deck x judge share >= 30%, concentrated on walls
walls-to-others SD ratio < 1.5 (bootstrap interval includes 1.5); interaction spread over every type: drop the penalty
tau between the penalised ranking and J2's >= 0.9: use the searched verdict directly (C38)

readout: Cross-judge spread of deck verdicts on a fixed panel and its ranking consequence. No population run.
noise_and_power: A deck's panel score under one judge rests on 200-400 games (SE about 0.03); an SD over 3-7 judges is biased up by about 0.03 with wide intervals, so the test uses bootstrap ratios across decks (6 walls vs >= 13 non-walls), not single decks.
kill_rule: Drop the idea if the SD ratio's bootstrap interval includes 1.5 or tau with J2 >= 0.9; no screen is built otherwise.
cost: About 1-2 h of analysis plus at most 1,000 greedy games (minutes).
distinct_from: #148's min rule and scr-judge2's pooled pilot-v2 share combine judges by a minimum or pooling, never by their disagreement (H18, H20, H23); the critic lists a judge-variance penalty as an uncovered gap (A8); degenerate-env idea 6 uses only the trend across two strengths of one judge.
rules_check: Evaluation only; an in-loop penalty would use only rule-compliant judges (the population pilot greedy and searched, a human-free reset judge); pilot-v2, the a4-tok family and the lists stay evaluation-only.
value: At almost no cost, decides whether a multi-judge spread penalty is a distinct selection lever worth a screen or redundant with using the searched verdict.
merged_from: judge: Judge-variance audit: does the spread of a deck's score across judges single out the walls, and does a spread penalty rank decks differently from the searched verdict?

reviews.reasons: No dedicated earlier reviews to inherit. The candidate does not rerun any do-not-repeat configuration. The ledger has measured that judges rank decks differently (H18: #85/#86/#89 panels, #115's 0.81/0.67/0.28, #127/#132/#137/#147). It has combined judges by pooling (scr-judge2, H20) and by the shrunk-search minimum (scr-jsearch479, H23/#148). It has also split deck from pilot once, in result #2 (#63: deck about 70%, pilot about 30%, line 1388 of the log). No run decomposes deck x judge variance per deck type, and none uses the cross-judge spread as a score. The critic lists this as an open gap (coverage gap on A8, 'Judge-variance penalty'). The parts that are new are three: the analysis runs offline over 3 or more judges, the variance is split per type, and the penalty weight lambda is varied. One concrete error in 'distinct_from' needs fixing. With the two judges a loop can actually use (population pilot greedy g and searched s), mean - lambda*SD is just a fixed linear blend of g and s. At lambda = 1 with the population SD it equals min(g, s) exactly, which is the #148 min rule. scr-jsearch479 failed because of the shrinkage prior (analysis section 9), not because of how the two judges were combined. So any in-loop follow-up with two judges is the min-rule family, and lambda is its only new factor. It becomes a distinct mechanism only with 3 or more rule-compliant judges, such as C17's W1/P1/bal-1 reset-judge stand-ins.
required_changes: Correct 'distinct_from': with two in-loop judges, mean - 1*SD_pop = min(greedy, searched), which is the #148 min rule. State that the never-varied factors are lambda != 1 and a third or later rule-compliant judge (a reset or arm pilot). The disagreement statistic itself is not new.

reviews.reasons: The readout matches the nodes: deck verdicts are used for judge and selection questions, and there is no population run, so no short-horizon bias. But the rivals are not cleanly separated. (1) R-A8 and R-collinear can both be true: the walls can have a large spread while the penalised ranking still has tau >= 0.9 with J2. (2) R-A8's ranking prediction ('at lambda 1 at least one self-discovered non-wall above every wall') is also what C16's R-selection-bound predicts under J2 alone, so it does not show that the penalty adds anything. (3) Over the rule-compliant set made only from the population pilot (J1, J1', J2, J3: one network at different strengths and rules), the spread is essentially |g - s| plus the clock effect. R-collinear is then near-certain by construction, and the walls' first prediction is largely known in advance: 0.72 / 0.57 / 0.44-0.46 gives an SD of about 0.12, against a noise floor of about 0.03 per cell. Only C17's arm pilots, independent networks, can tell R-A8 from R-collinear. (4) The SD is confounded with the opponent set. C07's and C17's judges play only walls vs the 24 lists (plus a small human-free twin), so a list's 'panel score' under them is roughly 1 minus the walls' score, mirrored. Comparing the walls' SD with the lists' SD then measures that mirroring, not judge dependence. Each judge needs one common opponent panel. (5) Statistics: the 6 walls come from 2-3 source populations and are near-duplicates. A deck-level bootstrap overstates the effective n, so it should be a cluster bootstrap by source population. (6) Global Kendall tau over about 43 decks, 24 of them human lists, is dominated by the lists' order and can stay >= 0.9 while the top decks swap. Selection acts on pairwise candidate-vs-incumbent decisions near the top. The kill rule should use tau on the human-free submatrix, or the share of selection-relevant pairwise orders that flip relative to J2 (the null-redraw logic of #148). Flips should be compared against a redraw null at the cell SE of about 0.03.
required_changes: Make R-A8's ranking prediction differential: a non-wall ranks above the walls under mean - lambda*SD where it does not under J2 alone, or the spread predicts wall membership after controlling for |greedy - searched| (partial correlation or logistic fit).

Score every judge against one common opponent panel (the human-free submatrix as the decision of record, the lists as evaluation rows), so the SD does not mix judge with opponent set. Drop the walls-vs-lists SD comparison under judges that play only walls vs lists.
Require at least one independent-network, rule-compliant judge (C17's W1, P1 or bal-1) in set (b). Otherwise say in advance that R-collinear holds by construction, and do not run.
Cluster-bootstrap the SD ratio by source population (C13 set A, set B, t60gate), not by deck.
Replace the global tau kill threshold with tau on the human-free submatrix plus the share of top-quartile pairwise orders flipped versus J2, compared against a redraw null at the per-cell SE.

reviews.reasons: Rules are satisfied. The audit is evaluation and diagnosis only. The proposed in-loop penalty would use only rule-compliant judges (pilot-v2, the a4-tok family and the lists are kept out of it). It is game-agnostic: any judges and a variance. It is simple: one selection statistic. The cost is badly underestimated, though, and it rests on three expensive upstream experiments. (1) It needs C07 (zero-training zoo, about 3,500 games plus checkpoint-compatibility work), C16 (searched matrices with ResponseGraphUCB over a panel of about 40 decks under several rules) and C17 (40-iteration rl/train.py fine-tunes in 3-5 arms, plus the env/game.js ending reorder). The '1-2 h' is marginal cost only if all three have run. Without them the judges W1, P1 and bal-1 do not exist. (2) The missing cells are most of the table, not a fill. C07's and C17's judges score only the 3 walls vs the 24 lists (plus walls vs 12 wide and 3 cluster decks). The 13 or more non-walls, the wide decks and the lists have no cells under them. At the design's own 200-400 games a deck-judge cell, about 19 human-free decks x 7 rule-compliant judges is about 27k-53k games, and more with the lists or C07's checkpoints. That is far above 1,000. (3) The searched judges' cells (J2/J3) exist in C16 only for the walls' edges, the top-12 submatrix and a 12-deck core. Greedy games cannot fill searched cells. One-turn search on both seats at k4 d4 runs at the scr-jsearch479 rate (200 games an iteration as a large share of a 6-minute iteration), so filling searched cells for the panel takes hours of CPU. (4) Greedy cells are affordable on 16 CPU threads beside 3 screens (a few hours via notes/scripts/probe_matchups.py, which already takes --pilot and --pilot-b). C07's older checkpoints (the 278-card table, max_tok 128) need the per-checkpoint token-bound check C07 already plans. Overall feasible, but only as a post-processing step scheduled after C16 and C17, with a game budget an order of magnitude larger, or with the panel cut down.
required_changes: State the dependency explicitly: run only after C16 (J1/J1'/J2/J3 matrices) and at least C17 wave 1 (W1, P1) finish. Otherwise the reset-judge stand-ins do not exist.

Re-cost the fill. Give the number of deck x judge cells, games per cell and wall-clock time on the CPU budget. Either budget about 30k-50k greedy games (several CPU hours beside the screens), or restrict the panel to the human-free 12-deck core x 4-5 rule-compliant judges at 64-128 games a cell.
Do not claim greedy games can fill searched-judge cells. Either take J2/J3 only on the submatrix C16 already covers, or budget the searched games separately (one-turn k4 d4, on the order of hours).
Name the script: extend probe_matchups.py or hodge_audit.py to emit a deck x judge x opponent table on shared deals, so all judges use the same opponents and deals (common random numbers).

title: Plasticity probe: does the pilot, after about 800 iterations, learn new decks more slowly than the same policy in fresh weights (anomaly A4)?
rivals: R1 lost plasticity: about 800 iterations of shifting data (pilot-v2's 349 on wide decks, then a population narrowing to walls from 160) left the weights slow to learn, explaining A4 (20 iterations of human-list practice left the pilot 44 Elo behind pilot-v2, #131/#134) and the competence plateau since 160
R2 plastic, signal-limited: old and fresh weights learn new decks equally; the slowness is in data and training signal
R3 data, not initialisation: a student distilled on a broad deck mix learns faster whether fresh or grown
design: Two students of scr-resetcap 499 via rl/warmstart.py on the same 4,000 teacher games over a broad human-free mix (40% current population, 40% past populations from main seg_0160-0460 and screen snapshots, 20% wide decks): one fresh-initialised (no load_grown), one grown, each distilled to held-out KL <= 0.15. Probe A: teacher, fresh, grown and pilot-v2 it349 (reference) each train 15 iterations (rl/train.py --matchups-file, both directions, lr 2e-4, 2 epochs, identical deals and budget) on 12 held-out coherent human-free decks (best decks of other screens' largest non-wall types plus 6 pre-160 main-line decks). Probe B: 2,000 fresh-Adam steps per arm fitting soft CRN-search targets (C03) on 20k held-out states. Probe C (diagnosis only, as #131): probe A on the 24 lists, pilots never seed training. Supporting audit: dormant GELU units, feature rank and QKV norms across main seg_0160-0460 and pilot-v2 it24-349.

predictions.predicted: the fresh student's 15-iteration gain >= 1.5x both the teacher's and the grown student's (CIs separated by 15); lower probe-B cross-entropy; in probe C it reaches pilot-v2's level on the lists, which old weights did not (#131/#134); dormancy rises or rank falls along 160 -> 460 but not along pilot-v2's run
all three slopes within a factor 0.8-1.25; equal probe-B cross-entropies
fresh and grown students learn about equally, both faster than the teacher

readout: Learning slope (win rate vs the frozen teacher on fixed deals at 0/5/10/15); probe-B held-out cross-entropy; probe C pace (C10 metrics) and h2h vs pilot-v2; audit metrics as support.
noise_and_power: 800 paired games a checkpoint: win-rate SE about 0.018, a 0.05 gain difference at about 80% power. #131 gained only 0.06 in 20 iterations, so if every arm gains < 0.04, extend to 30 before concluding.
kill_rule: Drop the fresh arm if it cannot reach held-out KL <= 0.3 within 10 epochs; end at 15 once slope CIs separate, else at 30.
cost: About 2-3 h of distillation for two students, 4 arms x 15 iterations at about 1 min, 1-2 h of evaluation, about 30 min for probe B: about half a day on one GPU process beside screens.
distinct_from: The log has no plasticity metric and no fresh-vs-old control; warm starts (#98, #105, #113) grew students only to give new architectures a fair start (H60); H15/H16 changed what the pilot sees, not its parameters; H56 capacity never cleanly tested; ITER untried.
rules_check: Probes A and B are human-free; probe C is diagnosis only and its pilots never seed a training line; distillation uses self-play states.
value: Decides whether ITER (periodic fresh-init distillation on a broad mix) and regenerative pulls toward the initialisation get slots and whether C37 should train a fresh network; explains or rules out A4. R2 sends pilot effort to the training signal (C11, C35, C36, C37).
merged_from: pilot: Plasticity probe: does the pilot, after about 800 iterations, learn new decks more slowly than the same policy in fresh weights (anomaly A4)?

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for C22. I read the full ledger digest and grepped notes/progress-log.md for plasticity, dormant, fresh-init, primacy, re-init and pilot reset: there are no hits. The plasticity research note's fact-check (claim 242) also found no earlier attempt. The closest families are different. H60/H55 (#98, #105, #113) used grown warm starts only to give a new architecture a fair start, not to compare fresh and old weights. #25 distilled a fresh token student from the A4.1 teacher, but to compare architectures, not learning speed. H15/H16/H17 change the pilot's data (wide practice, KL anchor, challengers) and leave its parameters alone. H56 (capacity) is about size, not initialisation. H34 resets the draft head (node N6), not the pilot. H59/H58 are input or architecture changes. The idea that is new in node N3/N11 is to hold the policy fixed and vary only the weights (fresh vs old), with a learning-speed readout. Iterated relearning (ITER) and regenerative pulls are listed as untested in the research index. Probe C repeats #131's protocol (practising the human lists), but it is a diagnostic sub-arm whose new factor is the initialisation, so it is not a forbidden repeat. Nothing in any do-not-repeat list is rerun.
required_changes: Name the new factor in distinct_from: the weights' initialisation (fresh vs old) with the policy held fixed, a factor never varied in H15/H16/H55/H56/H60. Cite #25 as the only earlier fresh-init distillation and say it was an architecture comparison.

reviews.reasons: Readouts fit the node: a pilot change is read by pilot measures (learning slope against a frozen reference on fixed deals, supervised cross-entropy on held-out states, head-to-head), not deck shape. R1 and R2 do predict different outcomes. Four concrete problems remain. (1) The 'grown student' cannot test R3. rl/warmstart.py calls load_grown(student, teacher net). With the student's architecture equal to the teacher's, that copies every weight, so the grown student starts at KL 0 and distillation leaves it equal to the teacher, apart from a new Adam state. R3's prediction (grown faster than the teacher) can then only come from the optimizer reset, not from the broad mix. (2) Teacher mismatch with A4. The A4 pilot is the main line at 450-469 (pilot-v2 ahead by 40-44 Elo, #134). The chosen teacher, scr-resetcap 499, is the pilot that already recovered: pilot-v2 is 22.7 Elo behind it [-41.9, -3.6] (#138). The same 460-era weights thus gained about 60 Elo of generality in about 40 varied-field iterations. That is existing evidence against strong plasticity loss (it leans toward R2, with a data dose of 30%-of-games one-sided practice in #131), and the candidate does not cite it. (3) Starting strength is confounded. A fresh student at KL 0.15 starts below the teacher, and lower starts gain more ('headroom'), so a steeper fresh slope is expected under R2 too. Gain alone does not separate R1 from R2. The level reached by a fixed horizon does: R1 predicts fresh ends above the teacher arm, R2 predicts at or below. (4) Power is overstated. Each gain is the difference of two checkpoints at SE about 0.018, so SE(gain) is about 0.025 and SE(difference of two arms' gains) about 0.035. A fitted slope over 0/5/10/15 gives about the same. A 0.05 difference is then about 1.4 SE, roughly 30% power, not 80%. The 1.5x criterion on #131's base gain (about 0.045 at 15 iterations) is a difference of about 0.02, which cannot be detected. The variance between training seeds (A/A Elo sigma about 8.8, about 0.013 in win rate) is not measured at all with one seed per arm. (5) The stopping rule is biased toward a short horizon. Warm-started nets usually learn faster at first, and the fresh-init advantage in the cited literature (Ash & Adams, Igl) shows at equal training fit, late. Stopping 'at 15 once CIs separate' therefore favours R2. Probe B (2,000 supervised steps on 20k held-out states) is the best-powered readout, and seeds are cheap there, but it is not made primary. The dormancy and rank audit crosses the 290 architecture change and pilot-v2's different (joint) encoder, so comparisons across that line are confounded. The research fact-check said to split at 290.
required_changes: Replace the grown-student arm with two controls: (a) a fresh student distilled on the teacher's own narrow population (#98-style data), to the same KL as the broad-mix fresh student, which separates data (R3) from initialisation (R1); (b) the teacher with a reset Adam state, so the optimizer state is matched across arms.

Make the main line seg_0460 (A4's pilot) the primary teacher; keep scr-resetcap 499 as a second teacher if budget allows. State that #134 to #138 already show the 460-era weights regaining about 60 Elo under a varied field, and lower R1's prior accordingly.

Decide on level, not only slope: R1 predicts the fresh student reaches a higher win rate than the reset-Adam teacher by a fixed horizon (30 iterations) on the 12 held-out decks; R2 predicts at or below. Report gain normalised by headroom as secondary.

Fix the power: at least 2 training seeds per probe-A arm (or an A/A replicate of the teacher arm) and about 2,500-3,000 paired games per checkpoint, or drop the 1.5x criterion for an effect size actually detectable at the stated n.
Make probe B primary, with 3 seeds per arm and written CE thresholds per rival; probe A secondary.
Replace 'end at 15 once slope CIs separate' with a fixed 30-iteration horizon (no early stop on separation); keep the fresh-arm KL kill.
Split the audit at 290, compare only within one architecture, and treat pilot-v2 as a reference only.

reviews.reasons: Rules: compliant. Probes A and B are human-free, use self-play states and process-generated decks, and are game-agnostic: weight initialisation and distillation carry over to MTG unchanged. Probe C trains a throwaway pilot on the 24 lists for diagnosis only, as #131 did, and it never seeds a training line; that is allowed under rule 1. The engineering is larger than 'about half a day', which assumes the tools exist. (1) rl/warmstart.py samples games only from the teacher checkpoint's own st['population']. A broad mix (past populations from main seg_0160-0460, screen snapshots, 20% wide decks) needs a deck-source option. A fresh-init flag that skips load_grown is also needed (trivial). (2) warmstart keeps every state and token tensor in RAM. 4,000 games (~600k decisions, both seats) is likely several GB, above a screen's 2.7 GB, though the machine has room. (3) Fresh-init distillation to KL 0.15 is uncertain: #25's fresh token student reached only 69.6% top-1 against its teacher. Up to 10 epochs over ~600k states with teacher and student forwards each batch is more like 3-6 h, not 2-3 h, for the fresh arms. (4) rl/train.py --init-from loads checkpoint['model'], but metagame and warmstart checkpoints store 'net' and 'config', so an adapter is needed. Its argparse defaults (lr 3e-4, epochs 3, shaping 0) differ from the adopted recipe, so every flag (deck_mode cross, lr 2e-4, epochs 2, shaping 0.1 fading, deckout-win) must be set explicitly (clutter list, analysis section 9). (5) rl.lab h2h supports only --panel drafted or archived, so the 12 held-out decks need a --panel-file option. (6) Probe B needs soft one-turn-search targets. tsearch in env/remote_worker.js gives per-option mean scores (used in #103-106), but the CRN variant (C03) and a supervised fitting script with held-out cross-entropy are not built. (7) The dormancy, rank and QKV audit script is new, though small. Compute: with the revised design (2 seeds, 30 iterations, 5-6 probe-A arms, about 2,500 games per checkpoint, 3-seed probe B) it is about 1 day of engineering and 1-1.5 days of GPU. GPU: each extra process is about 3 GB, and three screens use about 10.5 GB of the 12.8 GB cap. The probe cannot run beside three screens; it needs a screen slot, or two screens at most while it runs.
required_changes: Revise the cost to about 1 day of engineering (warmstart deck-source and --fresh options, checkpoint adapter for train.py --init-from, h2h --panel-file, probe-B target generation and fitting script, audit script) plus about 1-1.5 days of GPU for the powered design.
Book the run as one of the 3 screen slots (or cap screens at 2 while it runs): 3 screens plus this process exceed the 80% GPU-memory cap.
Pass every PPO flag explicitly in train.py (lr 2e-4, epochs 2, deck_mode cross, adopted shaping and deck-out reward), not the argparse defaults, and give the games per iteration.
Budget warmstart RAM for 4,000 games, or stream or shard the states; call limits.apply and limits.cap_workers in any new entry point (probe B, audit).

Say what happens if the fresh arm stalls above KL 0.3: the experiment then fails its core arm, so record that outcome (a capacity or data limit of distillation, as #25) rather than dropping the arm silently.

title: Null-drift accounting: how much of every from-scratch and fresh-head composition drift is the proposal base rate?
rivals: R-arrival (H27): a near-uniform head draws by card identity from a pool that is 81% Pokemon (225/42/6/4) and selection is near composition-neutral, so decks drift at the proposal rate whatever the pilot
R-results: selection itself adds Pokemon early (a non-attacking pilot pays deck-out piles, H45; or wide decks lose to bench-outs and gain from more Basics)
R-resist: selection opposes the pull and loses only by volume (about 70% of decks move an iteration under ungated --select)
design: Offline, no games. (a) Proposal-only expectation: rl/draft.py Drafter.sample 1,000 times per deck with each run's own settings (6 swaps, group_p 0.3, 3-nat floor, legality masks) for every run or phase with a near-uniform head: scr-v2 it0-6, scr-scratch 0-5, 016-scratch-recipe-m 0-39, the fresh heads of 017-meta-league3-m and 018 exploiters, the first 10 iterations of scr-reset, scr-resetcap, scr-resetent, scr-gamma and scr-judge2 (a fresh head's logits are 0, so no pilot reading; initial wide/random decks regenerated from each run's seed and checked against logged iteration-0 shapes; later iterations use saved checkpoints or shape-matched surrogates). (b) Observed: log.jsonl's per-iteration shapes, ids and moved counts give mean change = moved share x E[change | moved]. (c) rho_k = observed / (moved share x proposal mean) for Pokemon, Trainers, Energy, with deck-level bootstrap intervals. (d) Validate the simulator on the 479 forks, which log prop, and tabulate their acc-prop (selection's own pull at the wall state). (e) Transfer: the composition a uniform head drives toward for the 2005 pool (card-type counts only, from notes/data/eval/legal_pool_2005.json) and optionally one MTG format.

predictions.predicted: rho within [0.75, 1.25] on every kind in the uniform-head select runs (scr-v2, scr-scratch, first reset iterations); 016 (forced moves) near 1 until its head entropy leaves about 5.5 nats; a selection pull appears only at the wall state (e.g. ctl479's acc-prop +0.18 Energy a move)
rho_P >= 1.5 in the select runs; larger under the random pilot (scr-scratch) than under pilot-v2 (scr-v2) if the no-attack equilibrium is the source, about equal if bench-out avoidance is
rho_P <= 0.6: the observed rises (scr-v2 15 -> 29, scr-scratch 12 -> 27.5 median Pokemon) are arrival despite selection

readout: rho per kind and run with 95% intervals; the share of scr-v2's and scr-scratch's Pokemon rises explained by proposals; the uniform head's null composition for the 2000 and 2005 pools (and optionally MTG).
noise_and_power: 31-77 moved decks an iteration with a per-deck Pokemon change SD of 2-3 cards: SE 0.3-0.5 an iteration, 0.15-0.2 pooled over 5-6, against means of +2.5 to +4 per moved deck, so rho has SE about 0.06 and the bands are 4+ SE apart; simulator error is bounded by the prop validation; forced-move runs only calibrate the null.
kill_rule: Analysis only. If the simulated proposal mean misses the 479 forks' logged prop by > 0.3 cards a draw after 2 h of fixes, report only the forks' acc-prop.
cost: About 2-3 h of agent time and a few CPU minutes; no GPU, no screen slot.
distinct_from: H27 is descriptive (its verifier: drift 'always mixed with what the games accept'; no class-balanced ablation). No run decomposed observed drift into proposal and selection, and the acc/prop logging added at #138 was never read across runs; generators idea 1 audits proposals at the 479 head only; generators idea 2 (null-reward head) tests head-update drift (C24, C25); H45's verifier argues qualitatively from scr-v2.
rules_check: Log analysis with card types from the rules; no training change, no human lists; the 2005 pool is read for type counts only, never its decklists, so the Phase B holdout stays sealed.
value: Go/no-go and expected effect size for C41's base-measure factor (and whether its pilot factor is needed); a calibrated proposal-drift model so later screens can read acc-prop; how the identity-uniform bias changes across pools, which decides whether a kind-aware base measure is a Stage 3 requirement or a 2000-pool patch (C40).
merged_from: scratch: Null-drift accounting: how much of every from-scratch and fresh-head composition drift is the proposal base rate

reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews to keep. The candidate is distinct in mechanism. Nothing in the ledger splits the observed composition drift of the near-uniform phases into what the proposals bring and what selection adds. H27 (N6) is descriptive only: its tests are #63, #124, #121-125 and the entropy U-shape, and its untested list names kind-stratified proposals, whole-line adds and orphan-evolution rates, not this decomposition. H45 and H46 argue qualitatively from scr-v2, scr-scratch and 016, and their do-not-repeat lists cover training runs, not offline analyses. A grep of notes/progress-log.md for 'base rate', 'arrival', 'proposal mean', 'uniform head' and 'null drift' finds only #63's operator base rate (line 1391) and #140's remark that acc is close to prop (line 3694). No entry computes the expected proposal drift for scr-v2, scr-scratch, 016 or the first reset iterations. C24 and C25 test drift from head updates at the 479 head, and generators idea 1 audits proposals at the 479 snapshot only, so the never-done part is (a)-(c): the uniform-head expectation for the pre-#138 runs, which never logged prop, compared with the logged per-deck shapes. One part overlaps. Part (d)'s acc-prop tabulation at the 479 forks has largely been done already. The generators fact-check gives OLS slopes of acc on prop (0.98/0.99/1.17 in ctl479, 0.81/0.78/0.50 in gate479) and ctl479's selected +0.18 Energy / -0.18 Pokemon per move after 486. C25's design computes the selection differential for gate479, t60gate479, jsearch479 and gatevs479. That table should be reused and cited, not derived again. The forks should serve only to validate the simulator. Part (e), the null composition for the 2005 pool, is new.
required_changes: In (d), cite the generators fact-check slopes and C25's acc-prop figures for the 479 forks rather than deriving them again; use the forks only to validate the simulator, and add any forks those sources lack (ctl479 before 486, league479, lamv479, vs479).

In distinct_from, state that the never-done part is the proposal/selection decomposition for runs before #138 (scr-v2, scr-scratch, 016, the reset runs at 460-463), so the analysis is not later counted as a repeat of the acc-prop work.

reviews.reasons: The readout matches the nodes. A drafting and selection question gets a deck-composition readout (rho per kind), and no pilot claim depends on it. The three rivals predict different rho_P bands (0.75-1.25, >=1.5 and <=0.6), and the scr-v2 vs scr-scratch contrast inside R-results separates its two sub-mechanisms. A rho near 1 is not an outcome all rivals predict. The logs support the observed side: scr-v2 (7 iterations) and scr-scratch (6) log per-deck shapes and ids each iteration, and neither had a turnover. In both, h_in stays at 5.603-5.616 nats, so the uniform-head surrogate is accurate there. Four problems remain. (1) The reset-run window is wrong. In scr-reset, scr-resetcap, scr-gamma and scr-judge2, h_in falls from 5.60 to 4.9-5.2 by 464-466 and to 3.3-3.8 by 467-468, so 'the first 10 iterations' mixes learned-head bias into a uniform-head null. No head snapshot exists between 460 and 469. These runs must be cut to the iterations with h_in >= 5.5 (460-463; scr-resetent to about 468), or the learned-head share must be reported separately. (2) The proposed validation is close to circular. At the 479 forks the snapshots hold the real decks and head, and the simulator is the real Drafter.sample, so matching the logged prop only checks sampling noise. The real error source is the shape-matched surrogate decks for iterations where only P/T/E shapes are logged. With group_p 0.3, a group change moves every remaining copy of the cut card (up to 9 basic Energy into up to 4 copies of a Pokemon), so the expected drift depends on the copy structure, not the shape alone. The surrogate needs its own check on real decks: at 460, at scr-v2's final checkpoint, and at 479-499 snapshot decks against shape-matched surrogates of the same decks. 016 and 017 had no group changes and 016's moves are random among the held decks (composition-neutral by construction), so 016 calibrates the null without group changes, not the group-change regime. (3) The rival bands leave gaps (0.6-0.75 and 1.25-1.5) with no stated reading. A rough expectation is that 6 uniform swaps from a 15-Pokemon deck give about +3.4 Pokemon, and group changes add about 1-2 more. scr-v2's observed rise is about +3.3 per moved deck, so rho_P could land near 0.7. The bands need to cover the whole range, or a gap outcome needs a reading such as 'weak selection against, then rerun with real-deck surrogates'. (4) The SE is optimistic. Group changes widen per-deck change, to an SD of maybe 4-6 rather than 2-3. Decks repeat across iterations, so the deck-level bootstrap must resample decks across all iterations, not deck-iterations. Even so, pooled over 5-6 iterations, the SE of rho should stay near 0.1, enough to separate 1.0 from 0.6 and 1.5. The kill rule is suitable for an analysis.
required_changes: Cut the reset-run windows to iterations with logged h_in >= 5.5 (460-463 for scr-reset, scr-resetcap, scr-gamma and scr-judge2), or report the learned-head contribution separately using the 469 snapshot.

Replace or extend validation (d) with a check of the shape-matched surrogate under group changes: on real snapshot decks (460, scr-v2's final checkpoint, 479-499), compare the uniform-head proposal mean from the real decks with that from shape-matched surrogates; and use 016 (random moves, no groups) as the null calibration without group changes.
Make the rival bands cover the whole range, or state how a rho_P in 0.6-0.75 or 1.25-1.5 is read and what follows from it.
Recompute the noise estimate with the group-change per-deck SD and a bootstrap that resamples decks across iterations; report the expected SE of rho before running.

reviews.reasons: The rules are met. The work is log analysis, card kinds come from the rules, and nothing changes in training. legal_pool_2005.json is a format definition (sets and the engine-legal card names), not a human decklist, so reading type counts from it leaves the Phase B holdout sealed. The code supports the plan. Drafter.sample (rl/draft.py 196-241) needs only vw.deck, ids, counts, vw.s and vw.logits. For a fresh head (W, b_in and the out layer initialised to zero), the logits are 0 over the legal cards and s is 0, so a DeckView can be built without the pilot encoder: CPU only, seconds. Initial wide decks can be regenerated: rng = default_rng(args.seed) at metagame.py:367, then wide_deck or random_deck at 461. The candidate already plans to check them against the logged iteration-0 shapes. End-of-run decks are in checkpoint.pt, the reset-family runs have population_it0469/0479 snapshots, and the 479 forks have 484/489/494/499. The 479-fork validation needs real views, meaning pilot.encode over 99 decks x 4 opponents x about 277 candidates per snapshot: a few seconds on the GPU or minutes on CPU. That is negligible beside 3 screens, but it contradicts the stated 'no GPU' and should be noted. The cost is underestimated. The plan covers about 15 runs or phases: regenerating seeds, building and validating surrogate decks under group changes, per-kind rho with bootstraps, and type counts for the 2005 pool (resolved through engine card data, not the json alone). 017 and 018 fresh heads need their per-head rows extracted, since 017-m's top-level h_in of 3.75 is not the fresh heads' value. That is 4-6 h of agent time, not 2-3 h. The optional MTG null has no data in the repo and should be dropped or left to C40.
required_changes: Restate the cost as about 4-6 h of agent time, with a few CPU minutes and a few seconds of GPU for the views at the 479-fork validation snapshots.
Drop the optional MTG null composition (no card data in the repo), or defer it to C40.
Read the 017-meta-league3-m and 018 fresh heads' per-head entropy and decks from the per-head log rows, not the aggregate h_in, before including them.

title: Draft-head bench: replay the exact head on frozen 479 views with null and planted rewards (drift or signal, for the incoming and the cut choice)
rivals: H-drift: REINFORCE with Adam on unit-SD advantages collapses the incoming choice and tilts the cut choice with no information in the results (EDA genetic drift: frequencies hit the boundary at a rate set by step size against sample size, Doerr & Zheng 2020)
H-signal: the head collapses only on consistent advantages, passing on the judge's real per-card preferences (S12) at the rate their size implies

H-overreact: the head commits on evidence far below one iteration's noise (planted 0.005 per copy suffices), so its step rule, not the judge, sets collapse speed and evidence-scaled updates would fix it
design: Offline, no games. Load runs/screens/scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt (pilot, the 479 head at h_in 2.745, 99 decks); compute each deck's view once with Drafter.view (fixed field of 4); replay step 4 for 20 steps with the exact Drafter code (6 swaps, 3-nat floor, group 0.3, draft-lr 3e-4, entropy 0.01, Adam restarted as at a fork). Each step every deck holds its incumbent plus K candidates (K=3 at 10 games, as scr-ctl479; K=1 at 20, as the gate); Bernoulli results, leave-one-out advantages, Drafter.update. Arms, 5 seeds each: N null (p = 0.5); P_card(delta) +delta per added copy of one card (the 479 favourite; separately an unfavoured Trainer), delta in {0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05}; P_kind(delta) +delta per Energy added and -delta per Trainer cut (S12's preference); P_in(delta) value on the incoming card only (does a Trainer over-cut appear through the shared advantage?). Decks fixed, plus one null arm moving decks at the null rate with recomputed views. Stage 2: plain SGD; Adam eps 1e-3 or beta2 0.9; updates pooled over 3 steps; sig-gated updates (a card's event counts only above 2 SE of its pooled history); a KL trust region; a frozen copy-uniform cut choice under P_kind; winner-only credit (C42) as a safety check under N. Calibration already run this session (scratchpad meta_lens/op_audit.py, 26 s a snapshot): sampling saved heads reproduces logged proposals (ctl479 head at 489 +0.44/-0.76/+0.32 P/T/E per draw vs logged +0.50/-0.94/+0.44 at 490; gate479 at 489 +1.71/-0.60/-1.11 vs +1.84/-0.66/-1.18); the learned cut over-cuts Trainers at 1.08x their copy share at 479 and 1.17-1.36x at 489-499 in ctl, gate and t60gate; at T=1 the head adds Energy in ctl479 (+0.72 to +1.72 a draw) and Pokemon in gate479 (+1.2 to +1.8).

predictions.predicted: null arm with K=3: h_in <= 1.5 by step 12 in >= 4 of 5 seeds (>= 60% of scr-ctl479's fall from 2.745 to 1.25 at 492); the favourite incoming card changes >= 3 times; the cut's Trainer share rises to >= 1.15x the copy share with no signal

null arm: h_in >= 2.5 through step 20 in >= 4 of 5 seeds and cut ratio 1.08 +/- 0.03; reproducing the 20-step collapse needs planted delta* of 0.005-0.03 per copy (the size of #92's single-card effects, 0.006-0.03); P_kind at delta* reproduces the 1.2-1.35x over-cut

planted delta 0.005 per copy (below a card's per-iteration advantage SE of about 0.06) brings h_in below 1.0 within 20 steps; in Stage 2 pooled or sig-gated updates keep h_in >= 2.0 under 0.005 and still learn 0.05 within 20 steps

readout: N6 only: h_in and h_out per step against scr-ctl479's logged path (2.745; 2.50 at 483; 2.09 at 488; 1.25 at 492; 0.97 at 494; 0.50 at 499); the cut's Trainer share over copy share; steps to h_in < 1.0 vs delta; KL per update against the batch's per-card signal-to-noise. No deck-shape readout.
noise_and_power: Only Bernoulli results and sampling vary; 5 seeds an arm. Expected seed SD of h_in at step 12 is 0.1-0.2 nats against a 1-nat gap between bands, so one 5-seed arm decides; comparison with the control uses the in-loop A/A RMS of h_in, 0.38 (ctl479 vs resetcap); the 4-point dose-response locates delta* within a factor of 2.
kill_rule: Fixed diagnostic: stop after the planned arms. If the null arm ends step 12 between 1.5 and 2.5 nats, settle it in the loop with C25's null-reward fork and nothing more. Skip Stage 2 if H-signal holds with delta* >= 0.01 (the head is a faithful conduit; fixes belong to the judge).
cost: About 2-3 h of code (a replay loop around Drafter.view/sample/update; the audit script already loads snapshots and samples heads); 30-60 GPU-min for 6 arms x 5 seeds x 20 steps; Stage 2 about 1 h more. No screen slot.
distinct_from: H30-H34 (collapse, entropy bonus, floor, slower lr, reset) varied entropy amount or step size inside system screens and never controlled the information in the reward; the optimizer swap is untested (verifier); generators idea 2 never run. No do-not-repeat item rerun (no dual ascent, floor 2/3 card, x5/x10 bonus, lr 3e-4 vs 1e-3 screen, reset from 460). First test of the cut choice (critic gap: no family covers the outgoing choice). C25 tests the same question in the live loop; this is the offline synthetic bench.
rules_check: Evaluation bench with synthetic rewards; planted 'kind' rewards only probe the head. Any fix it picks (optimizer, pooled or sig-gated updates, credit rule, frozen cut) is a game-agnostic change to the one learned head, still trained on results (rule 3).
value: Splits the head's collapse and growing Trainer over-cut into optimizer artifact (evidence-scaled updates fix a process fault behind about 20 ledger rows) or faithful transmission of the judge (head-entropy work stops, effort moves to the judge); measures delta* for C32; makes head fixes screenable in minutes.

reviews.reasons: I read the whole ledger digest for H24-H35 and grepped the progress log for bandit, null and permuted rewards. The candidate is distinct on a factor that was never varied: how much information the draft head's reward carries. Every N6 family (H30 collapse, H31 entropy bonus, H32 floor, H33 lr 3e-4, H34 reset) changed the entropy amount or the step size inside system screens, always with real game results, so none can tell drift from signal. The closest earlier object is #109's check_draft bandit (rl/tests.py:348). It was a unit test on a tiny CPU head at lr 1e-3 with 3 swaps and a planted 8-card target (target mass 0.029 to 0.95 in 200 steps). It never used a null reward, never ran on the real 479 head, and never touched the optimizer or the cut choice. This candidate reruns no do-not-repeat item: no dual ascent, no floor 2/3 lab card, no x5/x10 bonus, no lr 3e-4 vs 1e-3 screen, no reset from 460. The optimizer swap and the trust region are listed as untested in the verifier notes for H30 and H33. The outgoing (cut) choice is a named coverage gap with no family (ledger_meta gap: 'No family covers the outgoing (cut) choice'). Research index item 52 (null-reward drift test, then evidence-scaled updates) was never run. C25's N0 asks the same question inside the live loop. That is a sibling, not a repeat, and the kill rule correctly sends a mid-band result there instead of running both by default.

The core split works. On the null arm, H-drift predicts h_in <= 1.5 by step 12 and a cut ratio >= 1.15x, while H-signal predicts h_in >= 2.5 and a cut ratio of 1.08 +/- 0.03. Those are about 1 nat apart against an expected seed SD of 0.1-0.2, so 5 seeds can decide, and the 1.5-2.5 band goes to C25. The readout (h_in, h_out, cut Trainer share against copy share, steps to h_in < 1 by delta) fits the N6 node, and the 20-step horizon matches ctl479's 480-499 window. I checked the logged path (2.745, 2.50 at 483, 2.09 at 488, 1.25 at 492, 0.97 at 494, 0.50 at 499) against scr-ctl479/log.jsonl and it matches. The kill rule is a fixed plan, which is right for an offline diagnostic. Three problems remain. (1) The comparison target is confounded. ctl479's logged h_in is the head's entropy on that iteration's decks, and those decks moved about 75% an iteration toward walls. Part of the logged fall can come from the decks changing rather than the parameters (an untested rival, H-view). A bench on fixed 479 views measures only the parameter path, so 'null reproduces 60% of ctl479's fall' compares two different quantities. The saved heads in scr-ctl479/population_it0484/0489/0494/0499.pt allow a matched readout. (2) H-signal (delta* 0.005-0.03) and H-overreact (0.005 suffices) overlap at 0.005, so the lowest dose cannot separate them. The kill rule's 'delta* >= 0.01' cut implies a boundary that the predictions do not state. Also, if real per-card effects are 0.006-0.03 (#92), collapse at 0.005 is consistent with the head faithfully passing on real signal, so H-overreact needs a prediction only it makes, such as collapse onto a planted card while a null card shows equal movement, or a KL per update independent of SNR. (3) The seed SD is assumed rather than planned as a measurement.
required_changes: Add an H-view arm. Evaluate the frozen 479 head on the views of scr-ctl479's 484/489/494/499 populations, and evaluate ctl479's saved heads from those snapshots on the fixed 479 views. This splits the logged fall into a deck-distribution part and a parameter part. Compare the bench's null and planted paths with the parameter part, not with the logged h_in.

Make the dose predictions disjoint and match the kill rule: H-overreact means collapse (h_in < 1.0 within 20 steps) at delta = 0.005 with KL per update unchanged between 0.005 and 0.05; H-signal means no collapse at 0.005 and collapse first at delta in [0.01, 0.03]. State what a collapse at 0.005 means given #92's real effect sizes before running.
Report the measured seed SD of h_in at step 12 in the null arm. If it exceeds 0.3, treat any null result within 0.5 nats of a band edge as unresolved (go to C25) rather than as a verdict.

reviews.reasons: Cheap and within the rules. The run needs no games and no screen slot: one pass of Drafter.view over 99 decks (field 4 x about 277 candidate rows each) through the pilot encoder, then head-only forward and backward passes per step. This fits beside 3 screens (about 1-2 GB of GPU). Only the moving-decks null arm recomputes views each step, about 100 recomputes in total. Drafter.sample/log_prob/update and rloo (rl/draft.py) can be called as they are, and the loop in rl/metagame.py (about lines 484-669) shows exactly what has to be copied: one sample per game, z per game, RLOO over all of a deck's games including the incumbent's zero-gradient ones, unit-SD scaling over the batch, grad clip 1.0, floor temperatures recorded in ev_T. The rules are fine: planted Energy/Trainer rewards only probe the head offline, and any fix it selects (optimizer, pooled or significance-gated per-card updates, trust region, credit rule) is a game-agnostic change to the one learned head, still trained on results. Two concrete problems. (1) 'Adam restarted as at a fork' is wrong for the draft head. population_it0479.pt carries 'drafter': {'head', 'opt'} (I checked: lr 3e-4, 22 tensors, step 20), and Drafter.load restores the optimizer at a fork. Only the pilot's Adam starts fresh (metagame.py docstring line 35). A restarted Adam takes sign-like early steps of size lr, which would inflate drift on the null arm and bias the test toward H-drift. (2) The cited calibration script is not at the stated path. It lives in another session's scratchpad (.../9afecfab-fdea-4a82-8aad-02daab001fd1/scratchpad/meta_lens/op_audit.py, with audit_*.json), so it has to be copied or re-pointed. Stage 2's 'about 1 h' is low: significance-gated per-card updates need a running per-card event history, the KL trust region needs a line search or penalty around Drafter.update, and the frozen cut and winner-only credit each touch log_prob or rloo. Plan about 2-3 h.
required_changes: Load the snapshot's draft optimizer state (Drafter.load restores opt; Adam step 20) for the main arms, matching how scr-ctl479 actually forked. If wanted, add a fresh-Adam arm as a separate factor.
Point the calibration and loading code at the actual op_audit.py location (9afecfab... scratchpad meta_lens) or copy it into this session's scratchpad first.
Re-estimate Stage 2 at about 2-3 h of code (significance-gated per-card history, KL trust region, frozen cut, winner-only credit), and keep the plan to skip it if H-signal holds.

title: Does the draft head's learning amplify a weak judge preference? Frozen-head and null-reward-head forks from 479
rivals: H-amplifier: the judge prefers Pokemon-adding, Trainer-cutting moves only weakly; REINFORCE turns that into a strong proposal stream that carries the drift
H-judge-alone: acceptance alone moves the population; the head's learning is incidental
H-S-intrinsic: the head drifts or collapses with no signal at all (genetic drift; the pool's 81% Pokemon base rate)
design: Logs already point at the split (computed from select rows): in scr-gate479, scr-t60gate479, scr-jsearch479 and scr-gatevs479 the head's proposals (prop, mean change per candidate) went from -0.09 Pokemon / +0.58 Trainers / -0.49 Energy at 480 to +1.3..+2.7 Pokemon and +0.1..-1.3 Trainers by 489-491, while the selection differential (acc - prop) over 480-489 averaged only +0.02..+0.34 Pokemon and -0.03..-0.35 Trainers a move; afterwards acc tracked prop. Two forks from scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt with scr-gate479's flags and --reseed 2 (control: scr-gate479, identical deals at the fork): F0 = --draft-lr 0 (479 head frozen); N0 = the head learns from its rewards permuted across its draws within each iteration (new --draft-null flag, about 20 lines) while selection uses the real games. 20 iterations each. N0 is also C24's in-loop settle step.

predictions.predicted: F0 and N0 keep prop near its 480 value (|prop Pokemon| < 0.3); Chansey+Snorlax decks <= 60 at 499 (control 73) and median Trainers >= 27 (control 25)
F0 tracks the control (Chansey+Snorlax >= 70, median Trainers <= 25) through a growing selection differential (acc - prop >= +0.8 Pokemon and <= -0.8 Trainers a move)
N0's prop drifts directionally (Pokemon >= +1 by 490) and its incoming entropy falls below 1 nat despite null rewards

readout: prop, acc and their difference per iteration; h_in; Chansey+Snorlax decks (screen_types.py) at 484/489/494/499; median Pokemon/Trainers/Energy; largest type.
noise_and_power: 479 forks replicate type trajectories (S03: 33/19, 48/44, 74/72, 74/76 for the A/A pair); the control's Chansey+Snorlax count went 54 -> 63 -> 66 -> 73; prop averages about 99 candidates x 6 changes an iteration (jitter about 0.3), so its drift is 5-8x noise; contrasts of 10+ decks and 2+ median Trainers at 499 lie outside the 479-fork spread; distance alone (A/A RMS 2.6) is not used.
kill_rule: Stop a fork at 489 if its Chansey+Snorlax count is >= the control's 63 and its median Trainers <= 27 (H-judge-alone settled); else run to 499.
cost: About 30 min of code and a smoke for --draft-null; two screens x 20 iterations, about 2 h in two slots.
distinct_from: H33 varied the draft learning rate (3e-4 vs 1e-3), never to zero, with no null-reward control; H30-H32 and H34 change exploration, not whether the head's learning carries the judge's signal; H26's verifier lists acc/prop analysis as missing; no run separated proposal from acceptance causally. C24 answers drift vs signal offline; the frozen-head counterfactual exists only here.
rules_check: Diagnostic: a frozen or null-reward head is not a method; rule 3's learned head stays; no human data.
value: H-amplifier: S fixes (evidence-scaled or trust-region head updates, best-of-K credit C42) must accompany any judge or clock fix, since even a mildly biased judge collapses the population through the head. H-judge-alone: S is secondary, and the judge's raw selection differential is the quantity any J/E fix must reverse.
