reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews to keep. I read the full ledger and grepped the progress log for draft-lr 0, frozen head, null reward, permut and selection differential. The only hit was an unrelated ONNX candidate-permutation test (#400), so neither arm has been run. The nearest families are H33 (draft lr 3e-4 vs 1e-3, never 0; its verifier lists only 1e-4 and trust-region variants), H30 (head collapse; its untested list names optimizer and trust-region swaps, and entries.json calls Adam amplification an unproven contributor), H24/H25/H26 (gate and selection noise; H26's verifier lists the acc-vs-prop analysis as never done), H27 (proposal base rates) and H34 (head reset). None of them cuts the head's learning while selection still uses real games, so none separates transmission from selection by intervention. The never-varied factor is the draft head's learning signal: lr 0 (F0) and a null permuted reward (N0) on N6, against the N5 selection differential. The 479 fork, scr-gate479's flags and --reseed 2 all match a do-not-repeat control, but here they are the control, which is correct. N0 overlaps C24's settle step by design (it is a merged chain). C24 is offline and this run is causal in the loop, so the overlap is acceptable. It is not a rerun.

The design is good. Freezing the head and nulling its reward against real selection is the right split between transmission and selection, and the readouts (prop, acc, acc-prop, Chansey+Snorlax decks, median Trainers) fit an N6/N5 question. I checked the stated numbers against runs/screens/scr-gate479 and scr-t60gate479 log.jsonl: prop is -0.09/+0.58/-0.49 at 480 and rises to about +1.3 to +2.1 Pokémon by 488-490; acc-prop over 480-489 averages about +0.2 Pokémon. Four problems remain. (1) F0 does not freeze the proposal distribution. Drafter.view() (rl/draft.py:145-188, called from rl/metagame.py:484 with the live `net`) reads every deck and candidate through the PPO pilot as it trains, against a field sampled from the population as it is now. With lr 0, prop can still drift through encoder drift and field context. That outcome (F0 prop drifts, acc-prop stays flat, Chansey+Snorlax tracks the control) has no rival assigned, and the current table could misread it as H-judge-alone or as a failed H-amplifier test. (2) The H-S-intrinsic entropy threshold is miscalibrated. The real-signal control's h_in stays at 2.1-3.4 nats over 480-499 (t60gate reaches 1.59 at 498), so 'below 1 nat' is not predicted even by the hypotheses it is meant to beat. (3) The 61-69 band of Chansey+Snorlax at 499 is unassigned, and the A/A spread for this exact count is not given (S03's pairs look like type sizes). Control-like arms ended at 73-80 (gate 73, jsearch 76 at 494, t60gate 80). (4) The kill rule has a short-horizon bias against H-amplifier. In the control, the head's prop only turned Pokémon-ward around 486-490. A frozen fork can therefore sit at or above the control's 63 at 489 and diverge only by 494-499, yet the rule would stop it at 489 as 'H-judge-alone settled'. The full run costs only about 2 h, so the kill rule saves little and risks a false verdict.
required_changes: Add a fixed-reference proposal readout. Each iteration (or offline from the saved population_it*.pt files), score a frozen panel (the 479 population's decks and a fixed 479 field sample) with the current head and the current encoder, and log prop on it. Do the same with the current head and a frozen 479 encoder. This splits prop drift into head learning, encoder drift and deck-state drift.

Either add an arm F0r (lr 0, with the head reading through a frozen copy of the 479 pilot while PPO still trains the playing pilot) or add an explicit fourth rival, H-encoder (proposals drift through the pilot's representation or the field context), with a prediction: F0's prop drifts to >= +1 Pokémon while F0r's prop stays below 0.3.

Recalibrate H-S-intrinsic against the control's own h_in path. For example: N0's h_in falls at least as fast as the control's (about 1 nat over 20 iterations), with prop on the fixed panel drifting >= +1 Pokémon. Do not use an absolute <1 nat bar.
State what a 61-69 Chansey+Snorlax count at 499 means (partial amplification), and compare against the control-like spread of 73-80 rather than one control value.

Replace the 489 kill rule. Either run both forks to 499 unconditionally, or kill only on a mechanism readout, for example stop F0 at 489 if its fixed-panel prop already matches the control's drift (the freeze is not effective). Never kill on Chansey+Snorlax >= the control at 489.

reviews.reasons: The rules check passes: this is a diagnostic only, with no human data, nothing game-specific, and the learned head stays the method. F0 is free. Drafter builds Adam from --draft-lr (rl/draft.py:141), so lr 0 makes opt.step a no-op, and scr-gate479's config.json (draft_lr 3e-4, draft_ent 0.01, floor 3, group 0.3, candidates 1, select_z 1, type_cap 0.5, reseed 2, fork scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt) can be copied with one flag changed. Pass the flags from the config explicitly, because argparse and the screen.py defaults differ from the recipe (draft-lr default 1e-3). N0 is small. Shuffle z across all (deck, draw) pairs in the batch_d loop (rl/metagame.py:654-661) before rloo, while per[d] and draws[...]['sum'/'n'] keep the real results for selection. That is about 10-20 lines plus a smoke, as stated. Note that the draft-ent 0.01 entropy term still acts in N0, which is the system as it really runs. Two screens x 20 iterations is about 2 h and fits the 3-screen cap. The cost is underestimated only for what makes F0 a real freeze: a frozen 479 reader for Drafter.view() (deepcopy the pilot at the fork, eval, no grad; about 10 lines, a few tens of MB of GPU) or the offline fixed-panel scoring script over the saved checkpoints (about 1 h). If F0r runs as a third arm it takes the third screen slot for 2 h and blocks other screens.
required_changes: Budget about 1 h more for the fixed-panel prop scorer (offline over population_it0484/89/94/99.pt and checkpoint.pt) and/or about 30 min for a --draft-reader-frozen option used in Drafter.view(). If F0r runs, schedule it as the third concurrent screen (about 2 h) or run it after the first two.

Launch from scr-gate479's config.json values passed explicitly (draft_lr, draft_ent 0.01, draft_h_in_floor 3, draft_group_p 0.3, practice_games 250, lr 2e-4, epochs 2, shaping 0.1, swaps 6), not from argparse or the screen.py defaults.

title: Paired common-random-number re-test of the head's proposals: their true effects, the gate's precision, and whether pairing pays
rivals: H-noise-walk: almost every proposal's true effect is within +/-0.05, so accepted moves are mostly noise and the population follows proposals (logs lean this way, scratchpad meta_lens/price.py: the gate moves 20.5% of decks an iteration vs a 15.9% null at z 1; its logged gains 0.21-0.26 equal the null's expected conditional gain 0.24 at 20.2 games a side; in scr-ctl479 transmitted proposals carry -0.40 of the -0.43 Trainers lost per iteration, the selection differential only -0.04 Trainers and +0.11 Energy)
H-real-selection: a sizeable share of proposals have true effects beyond +/-0.05, accepted moves are enriched for real gains, and the judge selects the Energy-for-Trainer edits
H-pairable: incumbent and candidate results on shared deals correlate (rho >= 0.3), so pairing cuts the SE of a difference >= 16% at no extra games
H-divergent: games diverge once a changed card is drawn (about 79% of deals put one in the first 13 cards), so rho < 0.15 and no design resolves a 6-card edit at 15-30 games
design: Offline, evaluation only. State runs/screens/scr-t60gate479/population_it0494.pt (gate, greedy judge, 60-turn draws). 60 decks: 30 inside and 30 outside the wall cluster (copy-weighted overlap on copy-limited cards >= 0.5 to a founder; 55 of 99 inside at 494). One candidate per deck from the 494 head with the recipe's sampler (6 swaps, floor 3, group 0.3), written position-aligned with its incumbent (each removed copy's slot takes the added card, so shared seeds deal unchanged cards to the same places since env/game.js shuffles with one seeded RNG; builder shared with C20). 10 fixed opponent incumbents per deck x 2 seats x 10 seeds = 200 greedy games for the incumbent and the same 200 for the candidate (rl/gpu_matrix.py pair_keys; a one-line maxTurns 60 pass-through). Sanity: the incumbent against itself on shared seeds gives rho = 1; a one-card change outside the first 13 gives identical openings. Per deck: paired difference delta_i and rho, split by whether a changed card falls in the first 13; resample the gate's real budget (20.2 unpaired games a side, z 1.0) 1,000 times per deck for its acceptance probability vs delta_i; regress delta_i on the candidate's dP/dT/dE (the judge's selection gradient on the head's proposals).

predictions.predicted: SD of true effects (sampling error removed) <= 0.05, >= 70% of delta_i within +/-0.05, gate precision P(delta > 0 | accepted) <= 0.65, slopes on dT and dE within +/-0.01 a card with CIs including 0
SD of true effects >= 0.08, >= 30% beyond +/-0.05, precision >= 0.8, delta rising with dE and falling with dT (|r| >= 0.3)
pooled rho >= 0.3 (>= 0.5 with no changed card in the first 13); paired variance <= 0.7 of unpaired
pooled rho < 0.15; paired/unpaired variance ratio > 0.85

readout: Per walls and non-walls: distribution of true candidate-minus-incumbent effects; the gate's precision and recall against the 200-game truth; paired correlation and variance ratio; the selection gradient on composition.
noise_and_power: 24,000 games; rho from 12,000 pairs SE about 0.01; each delta_i SE 0.035-0.045 (rho 0.2-0.4), so 60 candidates estimate the SD of true effects to about +/-0.01 and classify |delta| > 0.1 reliably; gate precision CI about +/-0.12. The only earlier paired datum (#50) gave phi 0.23-0.28.
kill_rule: After 20 decks, stop if rho < 0.1 and the SD of delta_i <= 0.04 (both questions answered). Build no paired gate if the variance ratio exceeds 0.85; stop a paired-gate screen if its accepted moves' re-test precision is not above the unpaired gate's after 10 iterations.
cost: About 3 h of code (aligned lists, pair keys, maxTurns pass-through, resampling); about 24,000 greedy games, 30-45 min at 9-13 games/s (resetcap499_own_vs_own ran 2,304 in 254 s). One GPU job, no screen slot.
distinct_from: H24 covered selection noise (score SD #43, sample size #64, the league's fresh re-test #56, --common-deals in the value builder #43/#46); H25 is the unpaired z gate. Neither paired a candidate with its incumbent on shared real deals, and no one re-tested the head's own proposals against ground truth (verifier: paired CRN estimates and pooled acceptance untested); #83's forks-are-not-CRN concerns another object. C20 tests designed variants under three judging factors; this measures the true effects of the loop's own proposals under the live judge.
rules_check: Evaluation only, human-free (population decks under their own pilot); a paired gate uses only seeds and results.
value: Decides how to fix selection: tiny true effects mean the gate is a slow random filter (its 'shape holding' is a lower move rate) and the head's REINFORCE is the only optimiser, so invest in head credit and the judge, judge fewer larger edits or pool evidence; real effects with rho >= 0.3 mean build the paired gate (half a day). The gradient says whether the Energy-for-Trainer drift is selected or only transmitted. The games train C32's payoff model.
merged_from: meta: Paired common-random-number re-test of the head's proposals: their true effects, the gate's precision, and whether pairing pays

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for this angle. I checked every ledger family it could overlap. H24 (selection noise): #43 measured score SD under the start-of-game value scorer, not real games. #56 re-tested league finalists on 16 fresh games in the obsolete deck-owning league. #64 was a sample-size calculation. #138 was a move-rate count. H25 (z gate): only z 1.0 was ever run, and it was read only by deck-shape and type trajectories. H26 untested list: logging accepted vs rejected composition. The scratchpad price.py analysis already did a log-based version of that, so C26's composition gradient is the powered, ground-truth version of it, not a rerun. H68/H24 do-not-repeat '--common-deals' is common random numbers inside the value-scorer builder used as a fix (#43/#46). C26 pairs real games as a measurement, which is a different object. #50's phi 0.23-0.28 compared two policies on the same deck by opening deal, not a deck edit against its incumbent. #83's forks-are-not-CRN point concerns training forks. The grep of progress-log for paired/CRN/common deals/re-test finds no run that re-tested the head's own proposals against a high-power truth, and none that paired candidate and incumbent on shared deals. Two factors were never varied: (a) CRN pairing of candidate and incumbent in real games under the live greedy 60-turn judge, and (b) a 200-game ground truth per proposal, split walls vs non-walls, that gives the gate's precision. It is diagnostic and touches no do-not-repeat configuration. One overlap is not in the ledger but sits between candidates: C20's (h) arm also plays a head draw against its parent, paired, under the greedy judge, and also measures parent-variant rho. The two should share the aligned builder and the games of that arm so the same measurement is not paid for twice.
required_changes: Coordinate with C20: run C20's (h) head-draw arm and C26 on one shared set of aligned candidates and paired games (or have C20 reuse C26's 60 decks), and report rho once.

reviews.reasons: The node and readout match. N5/N6 are selection and drafting, and the readout is per-proposal effects, gate precision and the composition gradient under the live judge, with no deck-shape trajectory over a short horizon. The rivals predict different outcomes on the SD of true effects (<=0.05 vs >=0.08 with about +/-0.01 precision from 60 candidates), on rho (<0.15 vs >=0.3, SE about 0.01) and on the dT/dE slopes. So the core question discriminates, and it splits a standing claim (H25: drift follows the judge) from the price.py reading (drift transmitted by proposals). Being offline, the kill rule has no short-horizon bias. Several criteria are mis-specified, though. (1) '>=70% of delta_i within +/-0.05' and '>=30% beyond' apply to raw per-deck estimates whose sampling SE is 0.035-0.045. Under a pure null about 73% fall within +/-0.05 and about 27% beyond, so these thresholds barely separate H-noise-walk from H-real-selection. They must use the deconvolved distribution of true effects. (2) Gate precision P(delta>0 | accepted) computed by resampling 20.2 games from the same 200 games that define delta_i is circular. Acceptance and the truth estimate share data, which inflates precision. Scoring the sign against a noisy delta_i also attenuates it toward 0.5 when true effects are small. (3) Ten fixed opponents a deck put opponent-sampling error into the 'truth'. The live gate faces random population opponents, so the true effect against the field is the target. (4) The divergence mechanism is confounded. The pilot reads its own decklist (MY_UNSEEN) and the opponent's (OPP_DECKLIST), so greedy play can differ from the first decision even when no changed card is drawn. A low rho in the 'no changed card in first 13' stratum would then be misread. (5) dP+dT+dE=0 for swaps, so the three-way regression is collinear. The 30/30 wall split halves power for the per-stratum SD (about +/-0.015). That is acceptable but should be stated. The sanity checks (self-pair rho=1) are good and catch GPU nondeterminism.
required_changes: Estimate the distribution of true effects by deconvolution or empirical Bayes (observed variance minus mean sampling variance; a normal-mixture or NPMLE prior). State the 70%/30% and SD criteria on the deconvolved quantities, not on raw delta_i, and pre-register what the 0.05-0.08 zone means.

Make gate precision non-circular. Simulate acceptance on games held out from the truth estimate (e.g. 40 of the 200 per side for the gate, 160 for truth), or compute it analytically from binomial noise at 20.2 games a side against the deconvolved effects. Report precision as posterior P(delta>0 | accepted), not agreement with sign(delta_i).

Sample opponents as the loop does: many distinct population incumbents, e.g. 100 opponents x 2 seats, one deal each, or at least 25 opponents. Pair each candidate game with its incumbent's game by (opponent, seat, seed), so delta_i estimates the effect against the field the gate sees.

Log the first decision step at which incumbent and candidate trajectories diverge, and whether it comes before any changed card is seen. Read H-divergent from that, not only from the first-13 split, because the pilot conditions on both decklists.
Regress delta on two of dP/dT/dE (e.g. dT and dE, or dE and dT+dP), and report the slope SE achieved given the spread of the head's proposals before reading 'CI includes 0'.

reviews.reasons: The code supports it. population_it0494.pt saves net and drafter (rl/metagame.py:846). Drafter.view(pilot, deck, field) and Drafter.sample(vw, rng) (rl/draft.py:145, 196) reproduce the recipe's draws with h_in_floor 3 and group_p 0.3. GpuMatrix.play already takes pair_keys (rl/gpu_matrix.py:59-70, keyed shards). The remote 'games' command reads cmd.maxTurns (env/remote_worker.js:365), so the pass-through is one key in play()'s msgs. env/game.js shuffles with one seeded RNG and rng.permutation over list positions, so aligned lists share deals until play diverges. Engineering notes: pool.names() expands decks sorted by card id (rl/decks.py:49). The aligned builder must bypass it and map removed copies to added cards from the vector diff, which group changes make a little fiddly. The resampling, deconvolution and stratification analysis adds time, so 4-5 h is more realistic than 3 h. 24,000 greedy 60-turn games at 9-13 g/s is 30-45 min with the default 14 workers, but that only holds when no screens run. Alongside up to 3 screens on 16 CPU threads, use fewer workers (about 6) or run between screens, which means about 1-1.5 h. GPU memory is small. Rules: evaluation-only and human-free (population decks under their own pilot). CRN pairing uses only seeds and results, so it is game-agnostic and carries to MTG. A follow-on paired gate is a simple selection-statistics change with no human prior.
required_changes: Budget 4-5 h of code (aligned builder bypassing pool.names, group-change mapping, deconvolution and held-out gate simulation) rather than 3 h.
Run with about 6 workers when screens are live (or schedule between screens), and budget about 1-1.5 h of games accordingly.

title: Solution-concept dynamics on measured matrices: which population rule keeps a cyclic field, under the population pilot and under pilot-v2
rivals: H-judge-bound: under the population pilot (J1) a wall is a Condorcet winner over the human field (runs/probe/resetcap499_own_vs_own.json: #829 beats all 24 lists at 32 a pair, minimum 0.531, 20 of 24 resolved at 2 SE, none lost), so every rule ends on walls and no selection-layer change helps under J1

H-truncation-collapse: under pilot-v2 (J4), where 15 of 24 lists beat all three walls and the logit equilibrium is within TV 0.10-0.14 of the field at lambda 5-10 (#149), the loop's mean-vs-field truncation still collapses the field to its Nash support (Haymaker/Sponge), while a QRE allocation or a torus keeps >= 3 archetypes

H-noise-holds: at the loop's noise (10-20 games a deck), truncation already behaves like a logit response and keeps an effective number >= 2.5 under J4; no solution-concept change is needed once the judge is fixed
design: CPU simulation on matrices on disk: J1 runs/probe/jf2_human24_resetcap499.json (24x24) and resetcap499_own_vs_own.json (3 walls x 24); J4 jf2_human24_v2.json and resetcap499_v2_vs_v2.json. Completion per judge (walls x walls; 6 population non-wall elites = best deck of each copy-weighted cluster outside the wall cluster in scr-gate479 499 and scr-t60gate479 498; 4 wide decks as the weak entrant row) comes from C16's panel games, or about 10,500 greedy games per judge if run first. Simulator (numpy): 99 decks over the 37 strategies; each iteration every deck plays about 20 games vs uniformly drawn decks, binomial from a per-seed bootstrap draw of the matrix. Rules: R0 the loop's (5-iteration window means; every 5 iterations the worst 15% replaced, 1 in 4 by a copy of a best-quarter deck, 3 in 4 by a wide entrant; soft cap 0.5); R1 QRE allocation (targets proportional to exp(lambda x payoff vs the current field), lambda 5/10/20, floor 1); R2 max-entropy Nash allocation, floor 3; R3 a 9x11 torus with neighbourhood games and Mitchell's local turnover; R4 epsilon-lexicase turnover on per-opponent scores; R5 replicator dynamics with stochastic universal sampling. Starts: the real field (24 x 4, the 3 walls as single invaders) and uniform; 20 seeds x 300 iterations per rule and judge. Human lists are evaluation-only rows; the decision of record for a rule is the human-free sub-matrix (walls, population types, wide decks). Add C16's searched matrix when it exists.

predictions.predicted: under J1 every rule ends with walls >= 85% of the population in >= 18 of 20 seeds (R2 at 100%), except QRE at lambda 5, which holds walls near 40-70% by noise alone

under J4, R0 reaches effective number <= 1.6 within 100 iterations in >= 15 of 20 seeds, led by its Nash support (one Haymaker list >= 60%); R1 at lambda 5-10 holds >= 3 with TV to the field <= 0.2; R3 keeps >= 3 archetype domains of 10+ sites
under J4, R0 keeps effective number >= 2.5 for 300 iterations in >= 15 of 20 seeds, within 0.5 of R1

readout: Per rule and judge with seed and bootstrap bands: effective number of strategies and archetypes over time, time to effective number < 1.5, the walls' share, TV to the real field (evaluation only).
noise_and_power: Matrix uncertainty dominates (at 32 a pair only 99-108 of 276 human edges resolve, #149), so every seed draws a bootstrap matrix; 20 seeds per cell resolve 0.5 in effective number (seed SD 0.3-0.5); J1's #829 edges are already resolved.
kill_rule: Fixed diagnostic. Skip the completion games if the existing 27x27 matrices (plus walls x walls) already separate the rivals under both judges. A rule that fails to keep >= 2 archetypes under J4 gets no system screen.
cost: About half a day of CPU code; 30-40 min of greedy completion games (two judges) unless C16 supplies them; simulations take minutes. No screen slot.
distinct_from: Never run: the first review's rank 8 (max-entropy Nash scoring over types), game-theory idea 4, coevolution idea 9. Nash-PSRO (#26-#40) collapsed under a deck-out pilot; #149's JF2 computed only static equilibria of the human 24x24, never with walls or the loop's own selection and turnover rules. Takes the judge's matrix as given (C16 audits the judge) and shares C16's completion games.
rules_check: CPU simulation; human lists only as evaluation rows; decision of record on the human-free sub-matrix. A QRE or Nash allocation is a non-learned population rule needing Evan's approval under rule 3 before any system screen.
value: At near-zero cost: a written stop rule for every selection-layer diversity screen under the current judge (torus, islands C43, caps C44, lexicase, Nash allocation), and whether the loop's solution concept would still collapse a cyclic field once the judge is fixed; if only QRE or a torus holds the field under J4, that is the decision for Evan before the first screen under a judge that passes fidelity.
merged_from: meta: Solution-concept dynamics on measured matrices: which population rule keeps a cyclic field, under the population pilot and under pilot-v2

reviews.reasons: C27 is distinct in node and mechanism. It is the ledger's own coverage gap for N7/N5, 'Best-response climbing converges to a monoculture by construction', which the ledger marks as never tested: no family compares the loop's per-deck climbing against the population mean with a mixed-equilibrium or spatial rule. The nearest ledger material is different in kind. The PSRO runs (#26-#40, H44/H67) were closed loops with value search and pilot fine-tuning, so they collapsed through the deck-out pilot, not through a choice of solution concept. #149 (JF2) computed only static Nash and logit equilibria of the human 24x24, with no walls, no turnover and no selection dynamics. H39's untested list names rectified-Nash niches and payoff-row DPP, but it does not name replicator, QRE allocation, a torus or lexicase. Grep of notes/progress-log.md (3,947 lines) finds no replicator, torus, lexicase or quantal entry, and no simulation of selection rules on a measured matrix. Nothing in a do-not-repeat list is rerun: the candidate trains nothing and screens no flag. The factor never varied is the population's solution concept, held on fixed measured payoffs under two judges. One overlap is with sibling candidates, not the ledger. C32 (surrogate testbed) screens the same rules (QRE allocation, epsilon-lexicase, torus) on a fitted payoff model with the real draft and select logic, and C16 supplies the completion games. C27 should be logged as C32's cheap first stage on measured matrices so the same rule comparison is not counted twice.
required_changes: State in the entry that C27 is the measured-matrix first stage of C32's rule screen (same rules R1/R3/R4), so the two are not logged as separate tests of one mechanism.

reviews.reasons: The J4 arm discriminates. H-truncation-collapse predicts an effective number of 1.6 or less within 100 iterations, with one Haymaker list at 60% or more. H-noise-holds predicts 2.5 or more for 300 iterations, within 0.5 of R1. These are far apart compared with a claimed seed SD of 0.3-0.5. The claims behind the arms check out on disk: under J1, pop829 beats all 24 lists (minimum 0.531, mean 0.804, none lost); under v2/v2, 15 of 24 lists beat all three walls. The readout (effective number, wall share, time to collapse) matches the target nodes N5/N7. Four problems remain. (1) The J1 arm tests nothing. pop829 is a Condorcet winner over the human field, so it is a pure Nash, and every payoff-responsive rule must converge to it. No rival predicts otherwise; H-truncation-collapse and H-noise-holds both speak only about J4. As written, the 'judge-bound' prediction is every rival's outcome. The only open J1 questions are how often bootstrap draws break the Condorcet status (4 of 24 edges are unresolved at 2 SE) and the walls-vs-population-elite edges. (2) R0 is not the loop. In rl/metagame.py the main force is the per-iteration --select move: one candidate draw of 6 changes, accepted at z 1.0, which moved 13-28 decks an iteration in scr-gate479. In turnover, the 1 in 4 is a best-quarter deck with 10 cards replaced at random (a mutant), not a copy. A fixed-strategy simulator with copy-only replication understates R0's spread rate, so a 'noise-holds' result could be an artifact of the missing move kernel. (3) The decision of record is the human-free sub-matrix (3 walls, 6 elites, 4 wide decks), but every prediction is written on human rows (Haymaker share, TV to the field). Under J4 that 13-strategy set may have no cyclic structure, which would make 'keeps 3 or more archetypes' unattainable for any rule. (4) There is no neutral-drift control. Drift from 99 decks with replication and 3-in-4 wide entrants lowers the effective number with no selection at all, and the seed SD is asserted, not measured. Simulations take minutes, so 20 seeds is needlessly few. The kill rule is fine for a fixed diagnostic; short-horizon bias does not apply at 300 simulated iterations.
required_changes: Reframe the J1 arm as a positive control, not a rival test. Report the share of bootstrap draws in which pop829 stays a Condorcet winner over the human-free panel. Use J1 to calibrate the simulator's timescale: R0 must reproduce the logged rise of the wall cluster (scr-gate479: 53 to 73 decks with both walls over about 20 iterations).

Add the --select move to R0. Each iteration, each deck proposes one other strategy, weighted by card distance between decklists (for example exp(-d/6)), and moves when the candidate's sampled score beats its own at z 1.0. Model turnover's 1-in-4 as a 10-card-distance mutant of a best-quarter deck, not a copy. Check the move rate against the logs (13-28 moves an iteration under the gate).

Write predictions for the decision-of-record sub-matrix (human-free) under each rival. First compute its cyclic (Hodge) share and say in advance that if it has no cycle, the human-free decision cannot separate the rules.
Add a neutral-drift control (all off-diagonal payoffs 0.5) for every rule. Measure the seed SD instead of asserting it, and run 100 seeds per cell, since a cell costs seconds.

reviews.reasons: The cost is roughly right. All four matrices exist in runs/probe/: jf2_human24_resetcap499.json, jf2_human24_v2.json, resetcap499_own_vs_own.json and resetcap499_v2_vs_v2.json, each 2,304 or 8,832 games. Much of the solver code exists: notes/scripts/judge_fidelity.py has qre() and the matrix loader, and rl/nash.py has solve(). rl/gpu_matrix.py can play only the pairs that involve the last `new` decks, so completion runs without replaying old pairs. #149 played 8,832 games in 490-690 s, so about 10,500 games per judge is 10-14 minutes on a free GPU. With 3 screens sharing the GPU, plan on up to twice that. The numpy simulation (about 8 rule settings x 2 judges x 2 starts x seeds x 300 iterations x about 2,000 binomial draws) takes minutes on CPU. Half a day of code is plausible, plus about 2 hours if the --select move kernel requested in the diagnosticity review is added. Rules: training is untouched. The human lists serve as evaluation rows and as a diagnostic seed start, which the brief and analysis section 2 allow. The decision of record is human-free. Every rule is game-agnostic. The candidate correctly flags QRE and Nash allocation as non-learned population rules that need Evan's approval under rule 3, but the torus (R3) and lexicase (R4) are also hand-designed population rules and need the same flag. Small engineering errors: scr-t60gate479 has no population_it0498.pt (the last saved file is population_it0494.pt; the run crashed at 498), so use 494 or its checkpoint.pt. The 'copy-weighted cluster' needs a stated descriptor; deck_kinds and pokemon_overlap understate the walls (H39), so use k-means on card counts or Chansey+Snorlax co-occurrence. The J1 human matrix used scr-resetcap's population_it0499.pt, but the walls file used checkpoint.pt. Confirm the two hold the same weights before joining them into one judge's matrix.
required_changes: Take the scr-t60gate479 elites from population_it0494.pt (or checkpoint.pt), not from 498, which was never saved.
State the clustering descriptor for the 'non-wall elites' (k-means on card counts, or a Chansey+Snorlax marker), not the Pokemon-overlap descriptor.
Confirm that scr-resetcap's checkpoint.pt and population_it0499.pt hold the same pilot weights before merging the J1 matrices.
Flag the torus (R3) and lexicase (R4) for Evan's rule-3 approval, as QRE and Nash allocation already are.

title: X-link valley test: fitness along block-wise edit paths from the walls to human archetypes, under judges that disagree
rivals: H-valley (X barrier): intermediate decks are worse than both ends, so 6-card moves cannot cross even under a judge that prefers the target
H-open: a monotone path exists under that judge; fixing J (and E) suffices for local drafting
H-judge-blocks: under the live judge the target sits below the walls, so every path descends
design: Endpoints: the 3 walls to the 3 lists they beat least greedily (Graham Haymaker 0.375, Lieu Wigglytuff 0.396, Knight Clefable 0.583). Decompose each wall/target difference into blocks (each evolution line with all copies; each special Energy; each Trainer's copies; basic Energy by type in chunks of 4); pair removal and addition blocks into steps of <= 6 cards that keep 60 cards and whole lines; 3 orders per path (random, Pokemon-first, Trainers-first): about 9 decks a path, 27 paths. Score every deck against (a) the current field, the 12 best decks of scr-resetcap 499, and (b) the 24 lists, field-weighted. Judges: J1 the 499 population pilot, greedy; J4 C17's W1 (payoff 1, full-pool familiar, wall-naive) or pilot-v2; J3 both-seats k4 d4 search with the STS rule at C13's T, on a subset (1 wall -> Lieu and Graham, 2 orders), through C03's GPU-served search.

predictions.predicted: under every judge with f(target) > f(wall), each order dips >= 0.06 below both ends (2+ SE pooled over paths)
>= 1 order rises monotonically within noise (dip < 0.03) under J3 and/or J4
under J1, f(target) < f(wall) on both fields for all three targets, and the profile descends

readout: f(k) along each path; valley depth = min(f(0), f(K)) - min over k of f(k); the sign of Spearman(f, k); per judge and field.
noise_and_power: Greedy: about 288 games a deck (192 vs the field, 96 vs the lists), SE about 0.03; valley depth SE about 0.04 a path, pooled over 9 paths per target. Searched subset: 96 games a deck, SE about 0.05, so a 0.1 valley is 2 SE per path.
kill_rule: Skip J3 if neither J4 nor C13 shows any target above the walls on field (a). Stop evaluating a path once its first three points rise monotonically by > 2 SE (open).
cost: Path builder 2-3 h; greedy evaluation about 70k games, about 1.5 h GPU per judge (J1, J4); searched subset about 3,500 games, 1.5-3 h GPU-served.
distinct_from: No family covers fitness valleys or edit paths (analysis section 1: X 'not yet tested directly'); group changes (H28, --draft-group-p) are a proposal operator, not a landscape measurement; C31 tests reachability only at the endpoints.
rules_check: Evaluation only: human lists are measurement endpoints; nothing trains on them.
value: Tells whether a corrected judge alone lets 6-card drafting climb from the walls to human archetypes (H-open) or whether any J/E fix must come with archetype-scale moves (whole-line blocks, niching, self-generated seeds) (H-valley), so an expensive in-loop judge fix (C38, C39) does not fail for a reason it cannot address.
merged_from: chain: X-link valley test: fitness along block-wise edit paths from the walls to human archetypes, under judges that disagree

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for C28. I read the ledger digest and grepped the ledger meta, the research index and progress-log.md for valley, hybrid, landscape, interpolation and edit path. No family H01-H69 measures fitness along edit paths. The critic's effort map and coverage gaps do not either, and analysis section 1 says the X link is 'not yet tested directly'. H28 (changes per draw, --draft-group-p) and H27 (whole-line adds) change the proposal operator; they do not measure the landscape. C31 tests stability at the endpoints only. The configuration is in no do-not-repeat list. The candidate is distinct in mechanism: a landscape measurement along block-wise paths with several orders under judges that disagree. The never-varied factors are the intermediate decks themselves and the order of blocks. One precedent goes uncited. Log #127 hand-built two hybrids of the main walls at 450: probe-hitmonchan (8 cards changed) and probe-chan-buzz (16 cards). Both were scored against the 24 lists and the main decks, under the main pilot and under pilot-v2. Under the main pilot the scores fell monotonically, 0.80 -> 0.553 -> 0.355 against the lists. Under pilot-v2 the 8-card hybrid rose above the walls, 0.26 -> 0.452 against the lists and 0.72-0.91 against the main decks. So that was a 2-point, 1-order path toward a non-human type, not toward a human list. It is a partial precedent, not a repeat. C28 should cite it and use it as a sanity check: J4 = pilot-v2 should reproduce a rise at the first Pokemon-swap step on field (a). The run must also not re-spend games on those two decks.
required_changes: Cite log #127's probe-hitmonchan / probe-chan-buzz result as the only prior landscape points (no valley at 8 cards under pilot-v2; monotone decline under the population pilot), and state what C28 adds: paths to actual human lists, block orders, more judges, field (a).

reviews.reasons: The readout matches the target node. N6/N7 exploration is measured by deck fitness on fixed fields, and decks are the right objects. The rival structure is sound in principle, but the statistics and the rival mapping have concrete flaws. (1) The valley statistic is biased by its own minimum. Depth = min(f(0), f(K)) - min_k f(k) over about 9 noisy points at SE 0.03 has an expected value of roughly 0.03-0.045 on a perfectly flat path. The expected minimum of 9 iid normals is about -1.5 sigma. So H-open's 'dip < 0.03' fails often even on a truly monotone path, and H-valley's 0.06 sits barely above the noise floor. The searched subset is worse: SE 0.05 gives a min-bias near 0.075 against a 0.1 valley. Pooling over paths reduces variance, not this bias. A fix: re-play the argmin deck and both endpoints on fresh deals (at least 576 games), or test the interior mean against the chord between the endpoints. Calibrate both thresholds against a simulated null with the measured per-deck SE. (2) 'Monotone within noise' does not mean climbable by the loop. The gate accepts a step only at z 1.0 with about 20 games a candidate, which is a minimum detectable gain of about 0.11-0.16. H-open must require each step's gain to clear that gate threshold, or report the expected number of gate passes along the path. Otherwise a gently rising path counts as 'open' when the loop cannot climb it. (3) H-judge-blocks is largely decided already. Under J1 the walls score 0.375 against Graham and 0.396 against Lieu, so those targets already beat the walls on a walls-heavy field (a). The walls' 0.70 against the 24 lists already makes f(target) < f(wall) near-certain on field (b). So 'f(target) < f(wall) on both fields for all three targets' is pre-refuted on (a) and pre-confirmed on (b). J1 on field (a) is in fact the decisive in-loop test of H-valley vs H-open (the live judge, the live fitness). It should be the primary cell, not the H-judge-blocks cell. (4) Three orders out of about 9! cannot establish 'every path dips'. State H-valley as 'all three orders, including the best-of-orders, dip'. Add a greedy best-next-block order (at each step take the block with the highest f) as the strongest test of H-open. That costs about K^2/2 decks a path at the greedy tier. (5) The kill rule truncates the readout. 'Stop once the first three points rise' cuts paths whose valley lies mid-path, for example after Chansey/Snorlax leave and before the attackers' Energy arrives. That is the H-valley signature. Greedy cells are cheap, so evaluate every path in full and apply early stopping only to J3. (6) There is no common-random-number pairing. Use identical deal seeds per opponent across all decks of a path, so that step differences f(k) - f(k-1) have much lower variance than 0.03 * sqrt(2). (7) Endpoint selection by the minimum of 24 lists brings a winner's curse. The 288 fresh games per endpoint handle it, but say so, and do not reuse the selection games.
required_changes: Replace raw min-based valley depth with a bias-corrected statistic: either fresh-deal re-evaluation (>= 576 games) of the argmin deck and both endpoints, or interior-mean-vs-chord; set H-valley and H-open thresholds from a simulated noise-only null at the measured SE

Define H-open as climbable under the loop's actual acceptance rule: each step's gain must exceed the gate's minimum detectable gain (z 1.0 at ~20 games/candidate, ~0.11-0.16), or report expected gate passes along the path

Re-map rivals: make J1 on field (a) the primary H-valley vs H-open cell (Graham and Lieu already beat the walls under J1); drop or restate H-judge-blocks, whose prediction is already settled by existing data on both fields
Add a greedy best-next-block order per path (strongest monotone-path search) alongside the 3 fixed orders
Remove the 'first three points rise' early stop for greedy judges; evaluate full paths; keep early stopping only for the searched J3 subset
Use common deal seeds per opponent across all decks of a path, and analyse paired step differences

reviews.reasons: Rules: compliant. The human lists serve only as measurement endpoints in a diagnostic, as with #127's hand-made variants and C31's seeding. Nothing trains on them. The path builder can use only rules data (rl/decks.py already reads 'stage' and 'evolvesFrom'). One caveat: 'whole evolution lines' is a Pokemon-specific block. If H-valley wins and the follow-up is an archetype-scale move operator, that operator must be defined game-agnostically, for example by co-occurrence clusters or a rules-derived dependency, to carry over to MTG. The candidate should say so now. Code: J1 and pilot-v2-as-J4 run on the existing notes/scripts/probe_matchups.py. It takes --a as a JSON of {name, cards}, --b 'best:<ckpt>:12' or 'archived', a GpuMatrix and 4 workers. That cell is cheap: path builder plus field weighting is about 2-3 h, as stated. Underestimated: (1) Greedy throughput. JF2's human-vs-human cells ran 12.8-18 games/s at 4 workers (runs/probe/jf2_human24_*.log). Wall-containing games run longer (deck-outs at about 60 turns) and will be slower, maybe 8-12 games/s. About 70k games is then about 1.6-2.5 h per judge, not 1.5 h, and more with full paths and a best-next-block order. Still no screen slot, but it shares the 16-thread cap with up to 3 screens. (2) J4 = C17's W1 does not exist yet: C17 is about one evening of code plus training. Only the pilot-v2 fallback is available now. (3) J3 needs C03 (GPU-served searched probe, about 3-4 h of code; probe_matchups has no search or turn-limit option) and C01/C13 (the STS round rule and T, not built). The candidate counts none of that. Without C03, 3,500 searched games on the CPU path cost about 22 h (192 both-seat games took 73 min). (4) A design inconsistency: 'steps of <= 6 cards that keep whole lines' cannot hold for 2-card lines of 4+4 (Jigglypuff/Wigglytuff: 8 changes) or 4+3 Clefairy/Clefable (7). Either allow 7-8-card steps for those blocks, which exceeds the loop's 6-swap operator and weakens the H-open inference, or split lines basic-first, which creates orphan-free but non-'whole' steps. Choose one explicitly.
required_changes: Re-estimate greedy cost at 8-12 games/s for wall-containing games (about 2-2.5 h per judge, more with full paths and a best-next-block order) and schedule it beside the screens within the 16-thread cap

State dependencies explicitly: J4 runs as pilot-v2 now (C17's W1 only after C17); J3 runs only after C03 (and C01/C13 for the STS rule), or else uses a plain draw at 60 turns as a stated stand-in. Do not budget J3 on the CPU path (about 22 h)
Resolve the whole-line vs 6-card conflict for 7-8-card lines (Wigglytuff, Clefable): either allow oversize steps and flag them as beyond the operator, or split lines basic-first
Note that any operator that follows from H-valley must define blocks game-agnostically (for MTG), not as Pokemon evolution lines

title: Three-reseed A/A of the gate recipe at 479: noise floor for the escape regime and replication of the one positive lever
rivals: H-noise: run-to-run spread from one state is large enough that single-run 479 arm differences of 2-6 cards or 10-15 decks are unresolved
H-attractor: the 479 relapse is near-deterministic; the arm nulls stand, and drafting or selection levers cannot escape the wall state within 20 iterations
H-gate-real vs H-gate-luck: the gate's type effect (largest type 23 vs 74 at 499) replicates or not, and whether it only splits the walls (wall-core decks 73 vs 79)
design: Two new reseeds (--reseed 3 and 4) of scr-gate479's exact command (from C04's registry) from scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt, iterations 480-499, same worker and share settings; with scr-gate479 (reseed 2) that is 3 gated runs, and scr-ctl479 and scr-resetcap 480-499 give 2 ungated. Pre-written metrics: window-mean top-12 distance 490-499 (smoothed); largest type and wall-core decks at 484/489/494/499 (checkpoint, after turnover); deck-out share; moves; acc-prop; final-pilot walls verdict. Then re-read the 479 arms (vs479, league479, turns70, turns120, lamv479 vs ctl479; gatevs, t60gate vs gate479; jsearch479 vs t60gate479) against the measured bars.

predictions.predicted: SD across the 3 gated runs >= 3 cards on window distance or >= 10 wall-core decks at 499; gatevs (9.7 vs 9.5), t60gate and league479 (14.0 vs 15.7) are then unresolved and their refutations drop to inconclusive
SD <= 1.5 cards and <= 5 decks, type trajectories within +/-5 decks at every checkpoint: the nulls stand, drafting/selection tests move to fresh starts, and 479 is kept for judge experiments

real: all 3 gated runs end with largest type <= 40 at 499, >= 30 below both ungated runs (74/76), while the wall-core gap stays within its interval (the gate slows the type split, not necessarily the walls); luck: any gated run ends above 50

readout: Run-level SD per metric (3 gated, 2 ungated); the gate's effect with a Welch interval on largest type and wall-core decks; the re-read table of the nine 479 arms.
noise_and_power: 3 vs 2 runs: an SD from 2 degrees of freedom has a 95% upper bound about 4.4x its estimate, so only coarse bars (<= 1.5 vs >= 3 cards) decide; the gate's type effect (about 51 decks) is large enough to replicate or fail clearly.
kill_rule: None as an A/A; a crashed reseed is resumed, not replaced or read early.
cost: 2 runs x 20 iterations x about 5.3 min, about 3.5 slot-hours (about 1.8 h wall-clock in two slots).
distinct_from: H42's verifier and the critic's top untested: a matched A/A of >= 3 reseeds of one state was never run; the lab A/A cards (#86, #102) calibrated Elo and shape at iteration 160, before four adoptions. It repeats scr-gate479's configuration (H25 do-not-repeat) but varies only the never-run seeds 3 and 4 (H25's verifier lists 'a second reseed' as untested).
rules_check: No method change.
value: Gives every 479-fork readout, including judge experiments built on gate479 (C25, C38, C39, C42-C44), a measured noise floor; replicates the incumbent's only positive lever before it stays in every recipe; decides whether to stop testing drafting and selection levers from the wall state (escape) in favour of fresh starts (prevention: C41).
merged_from: scratch: Three-reseed A/A of the gate recipe at 479: noise floor for the escape regime and replication of the one positive lever

reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews to carry over. The ledger has no matched multi-seed A/A of one state under one recipe. H42's verifier lists 'a matched multi-seed A/A (3 or more --reseed forks of one state with identical settings)' as untested. H25's verifier lists 'a second reseed' of the gate as untested. H62 lists 'k = 3-5 replicate forks per card' as untested. The critic's top-untested list has 'A/A of the screen recipe with 3 or more reseeds'. The progress log confirms that every 479 fork (gate479, ctl479, turns40/70/120, vs479, league479, lamv479, t60gate479, gatevs479, jsearch479) used --reseed 2, so seeds 3 and 4 were never run. The candidate does repeat a configuration on H25's do-not-repeat list ('--candidates 1 --select-z 1.0 from 479'), but the factor it varies, the seed, was never varied, and the purpose is replication and noise measurement, not another test of the lever. It also avoids two H42 do-not-repeat items. It is not the ungated --candidates 3 relapse replicate (scr-ctl479, already done). It does not use forks that differ in a setting (gatevs, t60gate) as a stand-in for an A/A. The existing same-state A/A (scr-ctl479 vs scr-resetcap 480-499) covers only the ungated recipe and gives 1 df, so a gated three-seed set is distinct. It is distinct in node and in the never-varied factor: N12/N5 measurement, gate recipe, seeds 3 and 4. It covers only part of the critic's item, which asked for 40 iterations of the screen recipe after the 4 adoptions, not 20 iterations of the gate recipe from a wall state.

The readout matches the node: an N12/N5 measurement read on deck and selection metrics, with no kill rule, which is right for an A/A. The gate-replication question is the strongest part. The ungated pair already sits at 74/76 decks in the largest type, the gate's claimed effect is about 51 decks, and a Welch interval on 3 vs 2 runs resolves an effect that size. The noise-floor half is weaker, for four reasons. (1) With 2 df, an observed SD of 1.5 has a one-sided 95% upper bound of about 6.6 (the candidate's own 4.4x). So the 'H-attractor' outcome (SD <= 1.5) cannot establish that the nulls stand. And SD >= 3 has a lower bound near 1.6, so it barely establishes H-noise. (2) The bands leave gaps that no hypothesis claims: SD 1.5-3 cards or 5-10 decks, and a largest type of 41-50 (t60gate479 ended at 41, so that zone is likely). (3) The new metric, run-level SD of window means, cannot be compared with the existing bars, which are RMS of per-iteration differences between paired runs: A/A 2.0-4.8, ungated same-state pair 2.6, gatevs/t60gate near-A/A 2.0/2.3. The existing data already predict a per-run SD of about 1-2. (4) Largest type uses the Pokémon-overlap descriptor, which H64 says understates walls and must not decide a card by itself. Wall-core (Chansey+Snorlax) decks should lead. The 20-iteration horizon matches the nine arms it recalibrates, but it cannot tell whether the gate slows the type split or holds it (gatevs went 21 to 36 and t60gate 13 to 41, both rising). The step 'low variance, so move drafting tests to fresh starts' does not follow: variance tells whether the nulls are real, not whether escape is impossible.
required_changes: Report pairwise per-iteration trajectory RMS across the 3 gated pairs (distance, wall-core, largest type, moves), in the same form as the existing A/A bars. Also pool with the ungated same-state pair (ctl479 vs resetcap) to get a 3-df within-recipe SD, and re-read each 479 arm against that pooled SD's upper confidence bound, not against the point estimate.

Close the gaps: label SD 1.5-3 cards or 5-10 decks 'inconclusive, keep the 2.0-4.8 band'. Replace the fixed 40/50 type thresholds with the Welch-interval rule, for example: the gate is real if the 95% interval of gated minus ungated excludes 0 and its bound nearer zero is at least 20 decks below.
Make wall-core (Chansey+Snorlax) decks at the 484-499 checkpoints the primary type readout, with Pokémon-overlap largest type secondary (H64).
Drop the claim that H-attractor decides 'escape is impossible' or 'move to fresh starts'. State that it only decides whether the 479-arm nulls are real nulls.

Optional, only if the budget allows: extend the two new gated runs to 509 so that 'slows' can be told from 'holds'. No ungated control exists past 499, so read only whether wall-core passes the ungated 499 level.

reviews.reasons: Cheap and buildable as stated. --reseed is a supported int flag (rl/metagame.py:301, 454-456: it seeds the pairing/deal RNG and torch). scr-gate479's exact command is recorded at the top of runs/screens/scr-gate479/stdout.log (workers capped 4 to 2; --turnover-every is passed twice and the last value, 5, applies, as config.json shows). save_every 5 gives the checkpoints at 484/489/494/499 the readout needs. That is within 3 screens and about 2.7 GB RAM and 3.5 GB GPU each, and the GPU is idle now (1.6 GB used, 0%). It is the cheaper option the user chose. Code drift since gate479 (which finished 10-21 10:50) looks harmless. The env/env.js, game.js and runner.js changes add maxTurns (default 0, no effect). The #148 judge-search code in rl/metagame.py and env/agents.js/remote_worker.js runs only behind args.judge_search, and null_searched uses its own nrng, so the main RNG is drawn in the same order when the flag is off.
