It is small, but it is not in the estimate. Rules: no method change; human lists appear only in the evaluation readout (walls verdict, distance to medians), so self-discovery, game-agnostic and Occam all hold.
required_changes: Launch from the exact command in scr-gate479/stdout.log, changing only --run and --reseed. Before reading anything, diff each new run's config.json against scr-gate479/config.json (only run, reseed and stop_file may differ), because argparse defaults are not the adopted recipe.
Add the two final-pilot walls-verdict evals (about 15-30 min GPU each) to the cost, or drop that metric.

title: Pilot-first warm-up W: plain-result PPO on rules-generated wide decks until games end by the game's own win condition
rivals: H-bootstrap-ok: the plain result suffices for the attack bootstrap on rules-generated decks, as #71 found on drafted decks, so pilot-first is a rule-compliant bootstrap

H-bootstrap-stall: on incoherent wide decks the plain result settles into stalling (deck-out wins pay 1), so the bootstrap needs another device such as the Prize margin in the pilot's reward (#124 b, C35)
By-product judge rivals: H5 (any competent plain-result pilot rates the walls high) vs H1 (only co-adapted pilots do)
design: Write 512 wide decks over the full 277-card pool (wide_deck) and 2,048 random pairs; train with rl.train from random init in the population pilot's shape (tokens, d 256, 4 layers, 8 heads, --deck-mode cross, so rl.metagame can --init-from it) with count features off (the live bug, C08) or fixed if C08 fixes it first. Adopted PPO settings (lr 2e-4, 2 epochs, entropy 0.01, lambda 0.95, gamma 1, prize shaping 0.1 fading over 100), self-play, plain result (deck-out wins 1), two seeds W1/W2. Stop at a game-agnostic criterion: >= 70% of games end by the primary win condition (Prizes or no Pokemon in play) and <= 25% by deck-out for 3 consecutive iterations, then 10 more; cap 60. Evaluation only at it20, it40 and the end: win-this-turn puzzles (C10), JF1 (3 walls x 24 lists, 16 a pair, #147 deals) and JF2 (24x24 logit-equilibrium archetype shares vs the real field, analysis 3a). Fallback arm only if W fails by 60: the same with the Prize margin in the terminal reward.

predictions.predicted: criterion met by iteration <= 40 in both seeds (#71's base went from 92% to 7% deck-outs by it24 on drafted decks); attack-only puzzles >= 0.80
deck-outs >= 50% and prize endings <= 30% at iteration 40; puzzles near random
JF1(W) <= 0.35 and JF2 TV <= 0.25 vs the real field (W judges like pilot-v2 within the human field, without its deck-out-0 shaping)

readout: Endings by iteration (time to criterion) for both seeds; puzzles; JF1 and JF2 of W1/W2.
noise_and_power: About 600-700 games an rl.train iteration: ending shares SE about 2%, and the 3-iteration window makes a false pass unlikely; two seeds give the spread of time to criterion. JF1 SE about 0.013; JF2 as in analysis 3a. A 40-60 iteration pilot is weaker than pilot-v2 (349 iterations), so JF1 in 0.40-0.55 is unresolved, not support.
kill_rule: Stop a seed at 60 iterations if deck-outs are still >= 50% (bootstrap fails: record it and start the margin fallback); otherwise stop at criterion + 10.
cost: About 1-1.5 h of code (deck and matchup writer; check that rl.train builds the cross-mode pilot rl.metagame loads); about 1-1.5 min an iteration (deck-cross took 65 s in #73), roughly 1 h per seed beside two screens with fewer workers; probes about 20 min.
distinct_from: H45's untested 'pilot first on wide random decks with the plain result' and #124 remedy (a). #70/#71's base trained on meta-99 drafted decks in joint mode (shaped under pilot-v2, which learned on the human lists' 56-card pool); #42/#48 used deck-out wins 0 on that pool. H45's do-not-repeat ('plain-result PPO on fixed undrafted decks run only to see whether it attacks') is respected: attacking is only a gate; the products are C41's bootstrap pilot and a never-co-adapted judge (C07's H-payoff question for a fresh pilot, C19, C31). C17's W1 is a pilot-v2 fine-tune; this starts from random init (the deck-out-1 arm of the matched 0/1 pair without its deck-out-0 arm).
rules_check: Plain game result, rules-generated decks, no human data or bots in training; lists and puzzles are evaluation only. wide_deck reads Pokemon-line structure from rules fields (stages, evolves-from, types), whose MTG analogue needs Evan's ruling (C40); the margin fallback uses the game's own end score (rule 2).
value: Produces the rule-compliant bootstrap pilot Stage 3 needs (no pilot-v2, no deck-out-0 shaping) and C41's pilot factor; settles whether pilot-first suffices to attack from scratch on the full pool; gives a fresh judge's JF1/JF2 at no extra cost and a candidate human-free P0 for C39.
merged_from: scratch: Pilot-first warm-up W: plain-result PPO on rules-generated wide decks until games end by the game's own win condition

reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews to keep. Overlaps checked against H45, H14, H20, H46, H51, H52 and H54, and the log entries #42, #48, #69-#73 and #124. What makes it distinct: it varies a factor nobody has varied. That factor is the training-deck distribution: rules-generated wide_deck lists (rl/decks.py:118) over the full 277-card pool, never drafted, for a plain-result (deck-out wins 1) pilot trained from random init in cross mode. #42 and #48 (pilot-scratch, pilot-v2) used the 56-card field pool with deck-out wins 0. #70-#73 (base, base-s2, deck-cross) trained from scratch with deck-out wins 1, but on meta-99's drafted decks, which came from a loop started from pilot-v2 and include its slow, Energy-heavy stall types (#69: 22/5/32 at 149). #124 drafted from iteration 0. The idea is H45's own listed untested variant ('Pilot first on wide random decks with the plain result') and #124's remedy (a). Its judge by-product is the deck-out-1 arm of H52's untested matched 0/1 ablation, and also H20's untested 'frozen independent judge trained on wide random decks with deck-out wins 1'. H45's do-not-repeat list is respected, because the attack gate is not the product. Repetition risk that remains: the bootstrap half is close to #70-#73. deck-cross from scratch at deck-out 1 already reached 5-12% deck-outs by it39, and the log confirms #71's 92%->7% by it24. So the only new thing in the gate is the deck generator. The genuinely new content is the judge (JF1 of a never-co-adapted deck-out-1 pilot trained on wide decks) and the rule-compliant P0. One thing is unexploited, but it is not a repeat: the #147 judge sweep never probed the existing #70-#73 from-scratch deck-out-1 checkpoints (runs/abl/base it79, base-s2, deck-cross it39, no-deck). That is a cheap near-neighbour of the W judge question and is taken up under diagnosticity.
required_changes: In distinct_from, name the never-varied factor exactly: the training-deck distribution (full-pool wide_deck vs meta-99's drafted decks in #70-#73, and vs the 56-card wide decks at deck-out 0 in #42/#48). Also say that the attack gate itself mostly replicates #70-#73 and is kept only as a stopping rule.

reviews.reasons: The readouts fit the node: endings, puzzles and JF1 are pilot and judge readouts for a pilot and initialisation change. The ending-share noise (SE about 2%, a 3-iteration window) and JF1 SE 0.013 are adequate. The kill rule at 60 iterations is generous: #71 reached 7% deck-outs by it24. Five problems remain. (1) The bootstrap rivals predict different outcomes, but the prior almost settles the question in advance. A from-scratch plain-result cross-mode pilot attacked on fixed full-pool decks (#73 deck-cross, 5-12% deck-outs by it39), and pilot-v2 and pilot-scratch attacked on 56-card wide decks. H-bootstrap-stall has little support, so this half is mainly an engineering gate, not a crucial experiment. (2) JF2 does not separate H5 from H1. Analysis 3a already gives logit-equilibrium TV 0.10-0.25 for both pilot-v2 (not co-adapted) and the scr-resetcap population pilot (co-adapted), so the clause 'JF2 TV <= 0.25' under H1 is predicted by every live hypothesis. JF2 should be a sanity check, not a discriminator. (3) JF1 lacks a competence covariate. A weak 40-60 iteration pilot can rate the simple stall plan high because of low skill (the P link), not because of H5. A high JF1 then fits both 'any competent plain-result pilot' and 'weak pilot'. A head-to-head against pilot-v2 on the 24 human lists (and on held-out wide decks) is needed so that JF1 is read only when W is within a pre-set Elo margin of pilot-v2. The it20, it40 and end JF1 points should get a pre-registered reading: JF1 rising with competence points to stall learned under deck-out 1 (H51 and H5); JF1 falling points to skill. (4) A cheap pre-probe that partly answers H5 vs H1 at once is missing: JF1 on the existing never-co-adapted deck-out-1 from-scratch pilots (runs/abl/base it79, base-s2 it79, deck-cross it39, no-deck), the 3 walls x 24 lists at 16 a pair as in #147, about 20 min each. This gives W a prior, and the contrast between W (wide decks) and those pilots (stall-rich meta-99 decks) isolates the training-deck effect on the judge. (5) The kill rule does not cover the middle zone: deck-outs between 25% and 50% at iteration 60 is neither pass nor fail. With two seeds, a JF1 in the stated unresolved band 0.40-0.55 is a likely outcome, so a resolving step should be planned, such as continuing the better seed to about 120 iterations or adding a third seed.
required_changes: Remove JF2 TV <= 0.25 from the H1 prediction (analysis 3a: both co-adapted and independent pilots already give 0.10-0.25), and report JF2 as a sanity check only.

Add a competence covariate measured at each JF1 point: head-to-head Elo against pilot-v2 on the 24 human lists (evaluation only) and on held-out wide decks. Pre-register that JF1 is read as H5 or H1 evidence only when W is within about 30 Elo of pilot-v2, and how the trajectory reads: JF1 rising with competence means stall learned (H5/H51), JF1 falling means low skill.

Before training, run JF1 (3 walls x 24 lists, 16 a pair, #147 deals) on the existing from-scratch deck-out-1 checkpoints in runs/abl (base it79, base-s2 it79, deck-cross it39, no-deck) as a cheap prior on H5 vs H1 and a training-deck contrast.

Add a middle-zone rule (deck-outs 25-50% at 60: continue to 90 or start the margin fallback, pre-chosen) and a resolving step for JF1 in 0.40-0.55 (a third seed, or the better seed continued to about 120 iterations).

reviews.reasons: The rules check passes. Training uses only self-play results with the plain game result, plus potential-based prize shaping. That shaping uses the game's own end score and is already in the adopted recipe. The decks come from rl/decks.py wide_deck, which reads only rules fields (stages, evolvesFrom, types, Energy provided); it already feeds turnover and practice in the adopted loop. The human lists, puzzles and the pilot-v2 head-to-head are used only for evaluation. The MTG analogue of 'Pokemon lines' is correctly flagged for Evan's ruling (C40). The code cost is overestimated. notes/scripts/pilot_decks.py already writes 512 decks and 2,048 pairs as {name, cards} for rl.train --matchups-file; switching it to the full pool and wide_deck is about 10 lines. rl.train already has --deck-mode cross, --d/--tok-layers/--heads, --shaping/--shaping-iters, --deckout-win and --lr/--epochs, and count features are off by default. rl.metagame --init-from builds the net from the checkpoint's own config (metagame.py:377-381), so a cross-mode rl.train checkpoint loads. The criterion-based stop is not in rl.train, so it needs an external monitor or a small patch. The time cost is underestimated. The 65 s an iteration from #73 was measured on an otherwise idle machine with 14 workers. Beside two metagame screens with fewer workers, collection and PPO slow by roughly 2-3x: about 2-3 min an iteration, so 2-3 h per seed to 60 iterations. Running two seeds at once takes 2 of the 3 screen slots. The 'probes about 20 min' also does not cover the evaluation as designed. JF1 is 1,152 games for each pilot and point (2 seeds x 3 points), and JF2 is 24x24x32, about 18,400 games for each pilot. JF2 at every evaluation point costs several hours of CPU, so it should run at the end only. Clutter trap: the rl.train argparse defaults differ from the adopted recipe (lr 3e-4, epochs 3, shaping 0, d 192, tok-layers 3, heads 4, deck-mode joint), so every adopted setting must be passed explicitly. With count features off, W's shape also differs from PILOT (count_features True); C41's pilot factor is then confounded with that flag unless C08's fix is applied to both.
required_changes: Revise the run-time estimate to about 2-3 h per seed beside two screens (or about 1-1.2 h only when the machine is otherwise idle), and state whether the two seeds run in parallel (2 of 3 slots) or one after the other.

Run JF2 at the end only, and budget JF1 plus the head-to-head at it20 and it40 per seed (about 1,152 + ~800 games each). Revise the 'probes about 20 min' to the real total, about 1.5-2 h of CPU over both seeds.

Write the full command with every adopted setting given explicitly (--model tokens --d 256 --tok-layers 4 --heads 8 --deck-mode cross --lr 2e-4 --epochs 2 --ent 0.01 --lam 0.95 --gamma 1 --shaping 0.1 --shaping-iters 100 --deckout-win 1), because the rl.train defaults differ, and implement the ending-share stop as a monitor or a small rl.train patch.

Reduce the code estimate to about 30-45 min (pilot_decks.py switched to the full pool and rl.decks.wide_deck, plus the stop monitor). Say whether count features stay off in Stage 3's population too, so that C41's comparison is not confounded with that flag.

title: Is the human field a fixed point of the loop? Seeded 24 lists plus wall invaders under frozen, learning, clocked, fresh and walls-trained pilots (diagnostic only)
rivals: H-reach / H-meta-OK / R-fixed: the human field is a stable state of the loop; the failure is that random or wall starts cannot reach it (S/X)

H-wrong-fixed-point / R-environment: even a pilot adapted to the human field lets the walls invade and drift toward stall (more Energy, fewer Trainers, wall cores) in the clockless game; the attractor is the walls (E/P/J)
R-judge: stable under a fresh pilot, invaded under the walls-adapted pilot
H-clock: the field is stable only when games end under the 2000 round rule

H-arrival-drift / H-S-bias: drafting and selection drift away from any field even under a fixed judge (one uniform-head draw on population decks adds +5.6 to +6.1 Pokemon, -1.8 to -2.8 Trainers, -3.0 to -4.2 Energy; scr-v2 went 15 -> 23 Pokemon in 4 iterations under frozen pilot-v2)
H-judge-shape-bias: even a judge rating the walls low pulls shapes toward Energy and away from non-draw Trainers, since every pilot values only draw Trainers above basic Energy (S12)

H-convergent-collapse: shapes hold but the shared head drafts every deck toward a few favourites and archetypes merge (in scr-t60gate479, 11 of 25 non-walls at 479 and 8 wide entrants joined the wall cluster by 498 through accepted moves; meta_lens/lineage.py)
R-co-adaptation: the field holds while a fresh pilot is fresh, then relaxes as the pilot specialises on it
design: Snapshot (about 50 lines, scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt format): 99 decks = the 24 lists x 4 plus the 3 walls (#829/#796/#809) as single invaders; fresh draft head; per-deck lineage logging (id, parent, founding list, overlap with it, cluster). Recipe: the gate (--select --candidates 1 --select-z 1.0 --judge-explore 0), 6 swaps, floor 3, group 0.3, draft-lr 3e-4, entropy 0.01, margin 0, turnover every 5 (wide entrants and mutants, protect 20), soft type cap 0.5, --reseed 2, no turn limit (JF2's matrices are untimed). Wave 1, frozen judges (--freeze-pilot, no PPO): F = pilot-v2 it349 (the field is near its logit equilibrium, JF2); Fq = F with C41's composition-neutral head (its seeded-field cell); C = arm A's starting pilot frozen (= F when A starts from pilot-v2). Wave 2, learning pilots: A = C17's H1 checkpoint (a human-field specialist knowing the full pool) or pilot-v2 plus a 10-iteration burn-in with decks frozen (--select-z 99, turnover off) and 250 wide practice games an iteration; B = A under C01's STS round rule, T from C02, else 60 as a stated assumption; W = C30's warm-up pilot (never saw walls or lists), head with C41's base measure if Evan allows (C40), else uniform; R = the scr-resetcap 479 pilot. 20 iterations (A, B, C to 30). Run after C17 (whose H1 reading predicts A) and C30. Each arm's pilot gets C07's walls probe at start (static prediction, with W's JF1/JF2), then every 10 iterations.

predictions.predicted: frozen and learning arms hold: Chansey+Snorlax decks <= 6, accepted moves <= 10% of decks an iteration (below the gate's 15.9% null), acc-prop near 0 or pointing back to the seed (< 0.3 cards a move), >= 70-80% of decks keep overlap >= 0.5 with their founding list, >= 6 of 8 archetypes keep >= 3 decks, median P/T/E within +/-2/+/-3/+/-2 of 13.5/28/18, the walls leave at the first turnover; the start pilot rates the walls <= 0.45

the start pilot rates the walls >= 0.55; in A, C and W the walls spread through turnover mutants and convergent drafting (Chansey+Snorlax >= 25 by 30; >= 10 wall-core decks by 20), accepted moves add Pokemon or Energy and cut Trainers by >= 0.5 a move, deck-out endings up >= 10 points
W holds as in H-reach while R accepts >= 20% of decks an iteration with acc-prop >= +0.5 Energy a move and >= 15 wall-core decks by 20
A is invaded as above while B holds (Chansey+Snorlax <= 6, archetypes survive)

F's prop starts near +5 to +6 Pokemon a draw; by 20 median Pokemon +4 or more (>= 17.5), Trainers -3 or more, acc following prop (slope >= 0.8), < 70% of decks keeping their archetype; F still drifts with a static judge while Fq stays within +/-2 of 13.5 Pokemon
by 20 median Energy +3 or more and Trainers -3 or more with Pokemon within +/-2; acc - prop >= +0.3 Energy a move; the head's top_in turns to basic Energy
shape within the H-reach bands, but >= 60 decks in one or two clusters (effective number < 2.5) and most top_in sharing 2-3 cards; lineages show conversions by accepted moves, not turnover copies
W as in H-reach to iteration 10, then acceptance above 15% while W's own walls verdict rises across checkpoints

readout: Per arm: acc and prop drift vectors per 5-iteration window and their difference; acceptance rate against the gate's null; Chansey+Snorlax decks and the invaders' descendants (screen_types.py); archetype retention and survival; clusters and effective number; median shape; endings and length; lineages (conversion vs replacement); the arm pilot's walls verdict. Evaluation only: the best decks against the 24 lists under pilot-v2.
noise_and_power: About 20 accepted moves an iteration under the gate, about 100 a window; a per-move Trainer SD of 1.5-2 cards gives a window SE of about 0.2, so the wall-era drift (+1 to +2.5 Pokemon, -0.5 to -2 Trainers a move at 486-499 in scr-gate479) is 5-10 SE; invasion from 3 decks to 25+ is unambiguous. Retention over 99 decks SE about 0.05 near 0.7; acceptance SE about 0.035 an iteration, 0.01 pooled over 20. Frozen arms sit below the screens' A/A (median RMS P 1.3, T 1.4, E 0.8), every band >= 3x it; shape distance (A/A RMS 2.0-4.8) is secondary. One run an arm with shared deals; replicate an arm whose median Pokemon or Energy change lands between +2 and +4.
kill_rule: Stop an arm once Chansey+Snorlax decks reach 40, or retention is < 30% at iteration 10 (the direction of drift is the result). Frozen arms stop at 10 if median Pokemon rose >= 6, Energy >= 5, or the wall cluster holds >= 10 decks. Stop B if time-ties exceed 60% for 3 iterations. Stop any arm after iteration 20 if the gate moves < 5 decks for 5 iterations with no drift (stable state settled).
cost: Snapshot and lineage scripts 1-2 h; the STS rule from C01. Frozen arms about 4-5 min an iteration (1.5-2 h each); learning arms 2-4 h each. Two waves in the three slots, about 1-1.5 days in all.
distinct_from: No run ever seeded the population with the human field (analysis section 2; grep). diag-human-practice (#127/#131) and --fixed-decks put fixed lists on one side of games, never drafted, selected or invaded (H17/H19 do-not-repeat, not rerun); scr-v2 (H20/H46) froze pilot-v2 drafting from wide decks, ungated, 3 candidates, 7 iterations; the turn-limit sweep used plain draws from the walls; JF2 measured the 24x24 offline with no drafting or co-adaptation; the STS Prize decision was never trained (H03, H04, H29, H44, H51 untested). Every 460/479 screen changed the judge and the meta dynamics together; the frozen arms isolate N5-N7. C16 is the offline version.
rules_check: Diagnostic only: human lists seed a quarantined run; no pilot, head, deck or statistic from it seeds any later run (as diag-human-practice). pilot-v2 and H1 carry human or field-card priors and deck-out-0 training (S06, S29), acceptable for diagnostic judges. Arm B evaluates the E hypothesis; adopting the rule in training is Evan's decision (C33).
value: The top-level split of the hypothesis space. H-reach: stop judge and pilot work and invest in reachability (C28, C41, C43). H-wrong-fixed-point: no exploration or selection fix can work; effort goes to E, P and J (C13, C17, C08, C38). R-judge: keep the judge fresh (C39) and Stage 3 prevention works. H-clock: the clock is necessary, which with C02 is the evidence for Evan's decision (C33). Arrival drift: C41's base measure is a precondition for any judge fix to show. Judge-shape bias: the Energy-heavy minimum is a per-card valuation bias shared by every pilot, for the pilot and judge work. Convergent collapse: change head credit (C24, C42) or allocation (C27).
merged_from: chain: Is the human field a fixed point of the loop? Seeded 24 lists plus wall invaders, with learning, frozen and clocked arms (diagnostic only); meta: Fixed-point test of the meta algorithm: seed the human field (diagnostic only) under a frozen judge that supports it; scratch: Is the human field a fixed point of the Stage 3 method? A human-seeded population under a fresh pilot and under the walls pilot

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for this candidate. I read the full ledger and grepped the progress log for seeded, invasion, fixed point, --fixed-decks and diag-human-practice. No run has ever started the drafted, selected population from the 24 human lists, so the starting population (node N9) is a factor that was never varied, and the fixed-point/invasion test is a new mechanism. The nearest families are all different. (a) diag-human-practice / --fixed-decks (H15, H17, H19 do-not-repeat): the lists sat on one side of 30% of games and were never drafted, selected or invaded. (b) scr-v2 (H20, H27, H46 do-not-repeat: --freeze-pilot pilot-v2 --init-wide --select --candidates 3, ungated, 7 iterations): arm F changes both the starting decks (human field instead of wide decks) and the selection rule (gate z=1 with 1 candidate). (c) scr-gate479 and scr-t60gate479 (H25, H23 do-not-repeat): arm R uses the same recipe and pilot but starts from a different population, which tests prevention rather than escape. That is the coverage gap the critic named (25 of 27 screens forked from wall states). (d) JF2 / C16 measured the 24x24 matrix offline, with no drafting or co-adaptation. Arm B's STS round rule in training is untested (H03, H04, H29, H51 untested lists). There are two internal overlaps with other candidates, not with the ledger: Fq is C41's seeded-field cell, and A depends on C17's H1 checkpoint. Run the shared cell once and cite it in both, so it is not counted twice. Nothing in this design reruns a do-not-repeat configuration.
required_changes: Mark Fq as the same run as C41's seeded-field cell (run once, report in both) so the slot budget does not count it twice.
If arm C collapses to F (A starts from pilot-v2), drop C rather than run a duplicate frozen pilot-v2 arm.

reviews.reasons:
The top-level split is well posed: H-reach predicts the seeded field holds, and H-wrong-fixed-point predicts the 3 wall invaders spread. F against Fq separates arrival drift from judge bias under a static judge. W against R separates judge freshness from the attractor. The kill rules treat the direction of drift as the result, which suits a diagnostic, and invasion from 3 decks to 25+ is far outside the A/A noise. But the code makes several of the stated predictions mechanical rather than diagnostic.

(1) Turnover confound (rl/metagame.py lines 750-777). Turnover replaces round(0.15*99)=15 decks every 5 iterations, but only from decks older than --protect 20. Entrants are protected, so each turnover must remove seeded decks. 75% of replacements are wide_deck entrants (MUTANT_SHARE 0.25), which carry 1-4 Pokémon lines and 8-34 Energy. By iteration 20, about 60 seeded decks are gone and about 45 wide decks are in, under every hypothesis. That makes H-reach's '>= 70-80% keep overlap >= 0.5 with the founding list' impossible by construction. It also lets the wide generator's shape move the population median P/T/E and the cluster counts, so H-arrival-drift's 'median Pokémon >= 17.5' and H-judge-shape-bias's Energy band can come true from turnover alone. If the snapshot's 'born' is not set at least 20 below its iteration, the opposite happens: no turnover runs until iteration 20, and 'the walls leave at the first turnover' and invasion through turnover mutants cannot be tested at all.

(2) Two arms add little. R's and F's start verdicts are already measured (JF1: population pilots 0.68-0.75, pilot-v2 0.24-0.26), so the static walls probe at start has a known answer. R-judge is mostly settled by existing data. The open question is whether a judge verdict turns into invasion through the gate and the head.

(3) Horizon. The learning arms run 20-30 iterations. Short-horizon bias cuts against H-wrong-fixed-point: the main line took ~160 iterations to reach walls from scratch, and starting from 3 walls, spread through turnover depends on about 4 mutants per turnover. A hold at 20-30 in A or W therefore bounds the invasion rate; it does not refute the walls attractor. The 'stable state settled' kill rule (< 5 moves for 5 iterations) needs the same caveat.

(4) Eight rivals, 7 arms, one seed each and many thresholds invite post-hoc fitting. The replicate-if-borderline rule helps, but there is no stated decision table.

The noise statements are sound for the per-move drift vectors (window SE ~0.2 cards) and for acceptance against the gate's 15.9% null. The readouts are deck-level, which suits N5-N7, and A and W also get the pilot walls probe. Pilot competence is not the target here, so that is acceptable.
required_changes: Compute every shape, retention, archetype and cluster readout separately over seeded lineages: the 96 seeded ids, whose id persists through accepted moves, plus mutant descendants traced through 'parent'. Report wide entrants as their own stratum and never in the population median.

In wave 1 (frozen arms), either turn turnover off (--turnover-every 0) and keep a mutants-only variant for the invasion-through-mutants question, or set born so seeded decks are older than --protect, and state the mechanical removal count. Rewrite the H-reach retention band against that count (e.g. >= 70% of the surviving seeded-lineage decks keep overlap >= 0.5).

Define invasion as wall-core decks (Chansey+Snorlax) by origin: descendants of the 3 invaders, seeded decks converted by accepted moves, and wide entrants. Only the first two count toward H-wrong-fixed-point.

Write a decision table before running: for each combination of the F/Fq, A, W/R and B outcomes, the rival it supports. State that a hold in a learning arm at 20-30 iterations bounds the invasion rate only and does not refute H-wrong-fixed-point.
Demote R to a positive control, its invasion expected from JF1. The static walls probe at start for F and R needs no new games: cite #137/#147.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: allowed. Analysis section 2 explicitly permits seeding the human lists as a quarantined diagnostic, nothing from the run feeds later training, and the human lists stay a diagnostic input. pilot-v2 and the H1 checkpoint carry deck-out-0 and field-card priors, which is acceptable for a diagnostic judge. Arm B's round rule is the E hypothesis under test, and adopting it stays Evan's decision (C33). Fq and W's base measure are correctly gated on Evan (C40).

Engineering, checked against rl/metagame.py: --fork-from accepts a population snapshot with no optimizer state (it then needs --reseed). --freeze-pilot, --draft-reset, --select-z, --turnover-every 0, --protect and --type-cap all exist. The type cap will not fire on the seeded field: deck_kinds gives the 24 lists types of 9/7/4, so the largest is 36 of 99, under 49.5. pilot-v2's joint-mode config builds via the fork's config, and scr-v2 already drafted through it. The snapshot is about 50 lines as stated, with these gotchas. (a) It needs a 'drafter' key even with --draft-reset, because lines 434-435 index src['drafter']. (b) Each entry needs id, deck, born, parent, kind, sum, n, and born must be set to iter+1-20 or less, else turnover is inert until iteration 20 (line 754). (c) Populations are saved only every --save-every (default 25), so lineage needs --save-every 1-5 or a per-iteration dump. (d) The cited meta_lens/lineage.py is not in this scratchpad (find returned nothing), so the lineage and overlap script must be written: count it.

Cost is understated. The stated 1-1.5 days counts runs only. Wave 2 and Fq depend on C01 (3-4 h of code), C02 (about 4 h of research), C17 (one evening plus GPU), C30 (1-1.5 h of code plus about 1 h a seed), C41 (half a day of code) and C07 (about 1 h GPU). In practice that is 2-4 days of serial dependencies. Run budget: 6-7 arms at 20-30 iterations are about 15-18 slot-hours, 5-6 h wall-clock in 3 slots. That fits the machine: a frozen arm still plays 2,000 games an iteration but skips PPO, at about 4-5 min. The sound first wave needs only the snapshot and lineage scripts: F (frozen pilot-v2), A (pilot-v2 learning, with the 10-iteration burn-in via --select-z 99 --turnover-every 0) and R (resetcap 479 pilot, learning). The rest can follow conditionally.
required_changes: Restate the cost with prerequisites: the snapshot and lineage scripts at about 2-3 h (lineage.py must be written), plus C01, C17, C30 and C41 before wave 2 and Fq, so 2-4 days elapsed, not 1-1.5.
Make wave 1 dependency-free: F, A (pilot-v2 + burn-in) and R, launched as soon as the snapshot exists. Run B, W, Fq and A-from-H1 only once their prerequisite lands.

Snapshot spec: include 'drafter' (any head; --draft-reset discards it), iter, config and net (pilot-v2 it349, or the arm's pilot), and per-deck id/deck/born/parent=None/kind='seed:<list>'/sum=0/n=0, with born no later than iter+1-protect. Launch with --reseed and --save-every 1 (or a lineage dump each iteration).

Write every hand-set flag out in full (lr 2e-4, epochs 2, swaps 6, draft-lr 3e-4, draft-margin 0, shaping 0.1, h-in-floor 3, group 0.3) rather than relying on screen.py or argparse defaults, which are pre-adoption (analysis section 9 clutter).

title: Surrogate metagame testbed on top of the head bench: screen selection and population rules in seconds
rivals: H-static: the relapse is a property of the meta algorithm on a fixed payoff structure; a frozen matchup model with the real head and selection code reproduces the control's relapse, the gate's slower drift and acc about equal to prop, with no judge co-adaptation

H-coadapt: reproducing the relapse needs a judge that moves toward the incumbent (F2), i.e. an incumbent-bias term beta > 0 growing with a cluster's share; its fitted size measures the dynamic part of F2
design: Extend C24's bench (the real Drafter on pilot views) with (i) a payoff model fitted on self-play games: P(i beats j) = sigma(r(x_i) - r(x_j) + a(x_i)^T Omega a(x_j)) over card-count vectors (per-card ratings plus a low-rank intransitive term), trained on C26's 24,000 paired games (real 6-card edits around population decks) and C16/C27's completion games, never on human lists, plus a knob beta x the share of the deck's cluster; (ii) the real pick, --select-z, turnover and cap logic from rl/metagame.py, recomputing views for moved decks (10-20 s an iteration on GPU) or a frozen-feature CPU proxy. Validate against the logs: (a) from 479 with scr-ctl479's rules, 65-83 moves an iteration at 10 games and a wall cluster above 60 within 10-16 iterations; (b) with the gate, about 20 moves an iteration and a rising wall cluster; (c) slopes of acc on prop near 1 (ctl479: 0.98/0.99/1.17). Then screen at matched noise: paired acceptance (with C26's rho), pooled LCB acceptance, winner-only credit (C42), C41's base measure, islands and a torus (C43), the hard cap (C44), QRE allocation, epsilon-lexicase. A rule passes only if, at the fitted beta, it keeps 3+ clusters for 50 surrogate iterations and crosses a seeded valley in >= 10 of 20 seeds (target: a self-generated non-wall elite 8-10 cards from the walls).

predictions.predicted: with beta = 0 the surrogate reproduces (a)-(c): relapse timing within a factor of 2, move rates within 10 points, slopes within +/-0.2
with beta = 0 the wall cluster stays below 60 for 20+ surrogate iterations or acc departs from prop by > 0.3 cards; matching (a)-(b) needs beta >= 0.05 per unit of share

readout: Validation: relapse timing, move rates and acc-prop slopes against the logged screens. Screening: clusters kept, valley crossing and wall share per rule and beta.
noise_and_power: Bernoulli results at the system's budgets (10-30 games), 20 seeds per rule; the payoff model must beat per-deck Elo by >= 2% in held-out log-loss. The matchup models of #34-#37 predicted held-out pairs but not new decks, so validity is judged on dynamics, not deck predictions.
kill_rule: Abandon if held-out log-loss is not >= 2% better than per-deck Elo, or (a)-(c) still fail after one round of model fixes. A rule failing the surrogate gets no system screen; one that passes still needs one.
cost: 1-2 days of code on top of C24; no new games if C26 and C16/C27 have run (else about 1 h of greedy games); seconds to minutes per rule; no screen slot.
distinct_from: H68/H69 used learned surrogates to rank or search decks and were exploited (#34-#39); here the model never ranks or accepts a deck in the system, it only screens meta algorithms. Analysis section 5's testbed and selection-diversity idea 4 were proposed, never built; #138 had only a one-off null simulation of move rates.
rules_check: Fitted on self-play games among population decks and their edits (human-free); used only to choose methods, never as a training signal.
value: Turns 2-hour screens into seconds for every N5-N7 rule (C42-C44, QRE, lexicase); the fitted beta says how much of the relapse needs a co-adapting judge: if beta > 0 is required, every meta rule is screened under the fitted bias and the judge work becomes a precondition.
merged_from: meta: Surrogate metagame testbed on top of the head bench: screen selection and population rules in seconds

reviews.reasons: No earlier dedicated review exists for C32. I read the ledger digest's families and checked the closest ones in full: H24, H25, H26, H37, H39, H40, H41, H68, H69. None of them builds a meta-algorithm testbed. H68 and H69 (#34-#39) used learned matchup and strength models to rank or search decks inside the builder, and those models were exploited. C32 never lets the model rank or accept a deck; it only chooses which N5-N7 rules get a system screen. The H69 do-not-repeat items ('matchup model as decider', 'any surrogate fitted with archived human lists') are therefore not rerun, and the fit uses only self-play games. Grepping notes/progress-log.md for surrogate, simulat, testbed, payoff model and null rate finds no meta-level simulation. #138 reports observed move rates (65-83 of 99), not a simulation, and selection-diversity idea 4 and analysis section 5 were proposed but never built. One small inaccuracy: the 'one-off null simulation of move rates' credited to #138 is not in the log (the research fact-check says the same). It changes nothing. What makes C32 distinct: (1) it is the first testbed that runs the real learned draft operator (the 479 Drafter, its REINFORCE updates, 6-card draws) against a card-level payoff model that generalises to edits; (2) it varies a factor no run ever varied, an incumbent-bias term beta that grows with a cluster's share, which is the dynamic part of F2. Overlap is with a sibling candidate, not the ledger. C27 already screens R0, QRE allocation, a torus and epsilon-lexicase on measured matrices at the strategy level, with no draft operator. C32's added value is the draft operator, edit-level payoffs and valleys, and beta. It should not re-screen those rules as if new: it should take C27's strategy-level verdicts as given and focus on what only an edit-level model can show (valley crossing under the real head, and head-plus-rule interactions).
required_changes: State that C27's strategy-level results for R0, QRE, the torus and lexicase are taken as given. C32 should screen those rules only for what needs the real draft operator and edit-level payoffs (head-rule interaction, valley crossing), so the same rules are not counted as tested twice.
Correct the provenance line: #138 logged observed move rates, not a null simulation.

reviews.reasons:
The screening half (does a rule keep 3+ clusters and cross a seeded valley at matched noise) is matched to the right node: N5-N7 rules read on deck and population outcomes. The 20 seeds per rule and the >=10/20 pass bar are adequate for a binary pass. The H-static vs H-coadapt split, the candidate's main scientific claim, does not discriminate as designed.
(1) The fit data is post-co-adaptation. C26 plays at scr-t60gate479 494, and C16/C27 use the resetcap 499 pilot. A static payoff fitted there already contains whatever bias the judge gained over 479-494. So 'beta = 0 reproduces the relapse from 479' is also predicted by H-coadapt: the co-adaptation sits inside the fitted ratings.
(2) The judges do not match. The validation targets ctl479 and gate479 used sampled judging with no turn limit (config.json: judge_explore null, no max_turns). C26 uses greedy play with 60-turn draws (t60gate479: judge_explore 0, max_turns 60). Any misfit can come from the judge change, not from beta.
(3) A model-misspecification rival predicts exactly what H-coadapt predicts: beta = 0 fails and a positive beta absorbs the misfit. The kill rule's 'one round of model fixes' makes this worse. beta is one free parameter fitted to one or two logged seeds, so its CI must come from seed variance and be compared with A/A (distance RMS 2.0-4.8).
(4) The validation targets are weak. About 74 of 99 moves an iteration is the null rate (H24), so (a)'s move rates check the noise model, not the payoffs. 'Relapse timing within a factor of 2' allows 5-32 iterations, which almost any model with a wall advantage meets.
(5) Valley crossing is decided by extrapolation. Per-card ratings plus a low-rank term are smooth in card counts. No training data lies on the 8-10-card path between the walls and a non-wall elite, so whether a valley exists there is an artefact of the model.
(6) The log-loss gate is mis-specified. 'Per-deck Elo' cannot predict unseen decks at all. The relevant baseline is 'candidate = parent's rating', scored on held-out edits (split by edit or by deck, not by game). If the model cannot beat that baseline, the simulated selection runs on noise.
A more direct readout for the beta question exists and costs little: judge a fixed panel of decks (walls, edits, non-wall elites) under pilot snapshots 479/484/489/494/499 and regress each deck's rating on its cluster's share at that snapshot. This measures beta rather than inferring it from the fit to the dynamics.
required_changes: Fit the validation surrogate on games from the judge being validated: the 479 pilot, sampled, untimed (as ctl479/gate479), with C26-style edits around the 479 population. Add a second fit under a later snapshot (494/499) of the same lineage. Then H-static predicts unchanged ratings and beta about 0, and H-coadapt predicts a growth in wall advantage that tracks share.

Measure beta directly: rate a fixed deck panel under pilot snapshots 479-499 and regress on cluster share. Treat the fitted-dynamics beta only as a cross-check, with a seed-bootstrap CI that must exclude 0.

Add a misspecification arm to the predictions. Fit beta at the same time as an alternative misfit term (for example a higher-rank Omega, or separate per-cluster offsets) and require beta > 0 to survive it. Do not allow a 'model fixes' round after beta is fitted.
Replace the per-deck-Elo baseline with 'edit = parent's rating' on held-out edits (split by edit or by deck), and keep the >= 2% log-loss bar.

Anchor the valley: before valley crossing counts, play games along 2-3 interpolation paths (walls to self-generated non-wall elite, every 2 cards, against a fixed field) and require the surrogate to reproduce the measured path profile within its CI.

Drop move rates as evidence of model validity (they match the null rate). Tighten relapse timing to the observed ctl479 and resetcap replicates plus or minus the A/A spread, and require the gate's slower drift to be reproduced at the same beta.

reviews.reasons:
The rules check passes. The model is fitted only on self-play games among population decks and their edits, uses card-count vectors (game-agnostic, carries to MTG), and only chooses methods, never acting as a training signal or deck ranker inside the system. Human lists stay out. No screen slot is needed. The cost is underestimated in four places, checked against the code and logs.
(1) Selection logic. The pick/--select-z, turnover, protect and type-cap logic is not a reusable function: it sits inline in rl/metagame.py main() (pick() at ~683, turnover/cap at ~741-790, deck_kinds at 220). Extracting or re-implementing it with a parity test against logged rows is about a day on its own.
(2) Dependencies. C24 needs 3-4 h of code. C26 needs about 3 h of code plus 24,000 games. C16 needs C01, C03 and 3-4 GPU-h for J2. The '1 h of greedy games' fallback covers only part of this, and the 479-pilot refit required above adds about 10-20k games (about 20-30 min).
(3) The simulator's compute. Drafter.view (rl/draft.py:145) encodes about F=4 x (C+1 ~ 277) rows per deck. The logged 'read' time for all 99 views is 4.7-11.3 s an iteration (scr-ctl479 log), and the field of 4 is resampled each iteration, so every view is recomputed, not only those of moved decks. At about 8 s an iteration, 20 seeds x 50 iterations is about 2-3 GPU-h per rule per beta, and roughly 8 rules x 2-3 beta values is about 40-70 GPU-h, not 'seconds to minutes per rule'. This shares the GPU with up to 3 screens (3.5 GB each).
(4) No proxy or log-based fit. The 'frozen-feature CPU proxy' freezes the deck embedding H of moved decks, which removes the head's response to its own moves (the mechanism being tested). log.jsonl keeps only per-deck mean z, ids and shapes, with decks in 5-iteration snapshots, so per-game results of the system's own judge games cannot be refitted from the logs.
Realistic cost: about 3-4 days of code and data, plus about 1-3 GPU-days of simulation unless it is staged.
required_changes: Restate the cost: about 3-4 days including extracting the selection, turnover and cap logic from rl/metagame.py main() into functions, with a parity test that replays a logged ctl479/gate479 iteration's decisions; C24/C26/C16 listed as hard prerequisites with their own costs; about 10-20k extra games for the 479-pilot fit.

Budget the simulation honestly (about 8 s an iteration from the logged view time; 2-3 GPU-h per rule-beta at 20 seeds x 50 iterations). Stage it: 5 seeds x 30 iterations for all rules, 20 seeds x 50 only for finalists. Batch seeds' views in one forward pass, or fix each deck's field to cut recomputation. Schedule it when fewer than 3 screens run, or cap its GPU memory.
Drop the frozen-feature CPU proxy as a validity-equivalent mode: it freezes H for moved decks. Keep it only for smoke tests.
Pin which head the bench runs: the 479 head with live REINFORCE updates under surrogate rewards (as C24), Adam restarted as at a fork, and say so.

title: Evan's decisions on the game's specification: is the event's round rule part of the game (training and judging, judging only, or evaluation), how T is fixed, the payoff at time, information sets, and committing engine fixes
rivals: Safety-net reading (request 24: 'some turn limit for draw if ... games are not terminating'; request 26 read as the process, not the rules): the game is untimed and a limit only guards against games that never end
Specification reading: the lists are optimal for the game they were built in, 20-minute rounds decided by Prizes at time, so that rule is part of the game like the card pool and the 60-card rule
R-draw-haven: the plain draw at the cut pays survival 0.5 and drives the Pokemon-up drift (C20); deciding unfinished judged games by Prizes removes the haven
R-rule-irrelevant: the Prize decision changes neither edit preferences nor the walls' verdict (greedy walls kept 0.625-0.658 of the event's points, #139)
R-search-needed: the Prize decision matters only with searched play (#139: 0.40-0.49 with search on the human side)
design: One message to Evan with the evidence attached (C13's curves, C16's invasion test, C14's draw-seeking result, C02's facts, C15's direction, C20's plain vs Prize readings), or now with the current evidence (#139/#147's proxy numbers, the verified STS page, #142's 94% draws). D1: is the reference event's round rule part of the game (Phase A: one game per Swiss round; an unfinished game goes to the side with more Prizes taken for 2 points; a Prize tie 1 point each)? Options: (a) training and judging (C34); (a') judging only: only the games that score decks for --select, turnover, the best quarter and the draft reward end at T and are scored 1 / 2/3 / 1/3 / 0, while PPO's recorded and practice games and the pilot's objective stay as they are (an in-loop arm of C38 once approved); (b) evaluation only, beside the untimed verdict; (c) neither. And should Phases B and C use their own events' rules (Worlds 2005; the Magic Tournament Rules), fixed before any run? D2: how T is fixed: (a) outside evidence (C02), frozen before any training run; (b) the game's own self-play length, human-free (e.g. the 75th percentile of the population's game length, as AlphaZero set its caps); (c) drawn per game from a stated prior with the time left visible; (d) not fixed, curves only; never by its effect on distance to the human lists (#147 chose 50-60 after seeing the flip). D3: the clock's unit: game turns or decisions, and whether the 5,000-decision cap is then decided as time. D4: the pilot's payoff at time: per-seat points (+1 / +1/3 / -1/3 / -1, a time loss pays like a loss; recommended, as the event scored) or the zero-sum difference (a time loss -2/3, a haven for the side behind). D5: if the rule is not adopted, replace the plain-draw --max-turns safety net (a draw pays the pilot 0, better than a loss: H01's incentive) with bootstrapping the value at the cut (Pardo et al.). D6: information sets: the pilot sees the opponent's full list (OPP_DECKLIST), which a 2000 player did not; keep it or remove it for the next pilot (C09 measures what it does to the verdict first). D7: commit, behind flags, the engine fixes found by #139 and C06 (2000 Confusion, Maintenance order, Thick Skinned cure, ending label, Sudden Death) in the submodule and the uncommitted work since #127 (15 modified files, +1,361 lines; every flag since #128 exists only in the working tree) before the registry and factorial runs. D8: if the age divisions played under different rules (C02 Q7): all 24 lists as the answer key, or per-division readouts. Engine part for (a'): a judging-only maxTurns with time-win / time-tie endings and per-seat scores (C01), about half a day. D1(a') is asked only if C20 returns R-draw-haven, or R-search-needed while C38's searched arms run.

predictions.predicted: C13, C15 and C16 still run as evaluation (no approval needed); plain draws give way to bootstrapping at the cut (D5); the untimed verdict stands, so the walls' edge must be removed by pilot strength or a search judge alone, which today leaves them at about 0.57 against the lists (#147)

C34 runs with T fixed by D2 and per-seat points; if C13 shows E or ExP the loop's target becomes the event's game, the untimed results since #127 read as a misspecified environment, and Phases B and C inherit their events' rules

in C20, under the Prize reading Delta(p) <= 0 and Delta(t) >= 0.04 above its plain-draw value; in the approved (a') arm acc Delta-Pokemon <= 0 and draws at the cut stop rising (scr-jsearch479: 37 -> 93 of 200)
C20's two readings differ by <= 0.02 for every variant: no (a') request; the plain draw stays
the readings differ only under search: (a') is requested together with a searched judge (C38 arm A or B), never alone

readout: Evan's answers to D1-D8, quoted in notes/evan-requests.md with what was done about each; after an (a') approval, the in-loop arm's acc composition, share of judged games reaching the cut and decks holding both walls' core cards.
noise_and_power: Not a measurement; each decision carries the intervals of the evidence attached. C20's two readings score the same games, so their difference carries only the noise of games reaching the cut (19-47% of searched games ended at the limit in scr-jsearch479) and resolves 0.04 at about 2 SE. Evan can wait for C13's search arms and C02, or decide now on #139/#147 (8 games a pair, end-count proxy: underpowered).
kill_rule: If D1 is (b) or (c), drop C34 and keep the rule as an evaluation readout; D5 still needs an answer before any further limit run. Do not ask D1(a') unless C20 shows a reading difference >= 2 SE; after approval stop the (a') arm at 489 by C38's rule or if > 60% of judged games end at the cut for 3 iterations (the signal flattens, as at 40 turns in #142).
cost: About 1 h to write the summary and one message of Evan's time; no compute for the evidence (re-scoring). After approval: about half a day of engine and scoring code and one screen slot (about 2.5 h) for the (a') arm.
distinct_from: #139's Next asked D1 and the turn count once; Evan answered with a plain-draw limit (request 24) and 'Refer back to Claude.MD' (request 26), and the sweep ran as his requested variety (#140-143, H04/H23 do-not-repeat). Never asked: judging-only scoring (a'), how to fix T without the answer key (D2), the unit (D3), the payoff mapping (D4), the safety-net alternative (D5), information sets (D6), the answer key's scope (D8). The critic's top-untested STS item covered training or judging without separating the two.
rules_check: Rule 4: these choices are Evan's, and no workflow message stands in for his consent. Rules 1-2: the rule uses results, turns and the game's own end score; T is never fitted to the human lists; no human data; information-set fidelity is a rule-2 question.
value: Resolves the ambiguity that has kept the best-supported lever in the record (the event's rule with search-strength play, #139/#147) out of training, offers the cheapest fix if the draw haven drives the drift (a judging rule only Evan can approve), fixes the specification for Phases B and C before results can tempt a choice, and protects provenance before more runs stack on uncommitted code.

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for this angle. The candidate overlaps H03, H04, H23, H51 and H53, plus Evan's requests 24-26. It reruns no configuration on any do-not-repeat list: it re-scores no #139/#147 games at new cuts, adds no plain-draw limit at 40/70/120 and no greedy-plus-60 limit, and re-runs no psearch judge sweep. Grep backs its claim that a Prize decision at time has never run in the loop. #140 built only a plain-draw maxTurns (env/game.js:10-12, 112-132: winner 0, ending 'time'). The untested lists of H03, H04 ('limit on judging games only'; 'a Prize-tiebreak limit in training'), H23, H51 and H53 all name it. What is distinct: (1) at the judge node N4, a judging-only time rule (a') decided by Prizes, a mechanism never varied, since every limit so far applied to all games and paid a plain draw; (2) at N1/N12, how T is fixed without the answer key (D2) and the pilot's payoff at time (D4), never asked; (3) D6 information sets, touched only by the 40-iteration no-deck screens #73-74. The one part that repeats is D1 options (a)/(c), which re-ask the question Evan already answered in request 24 ('Maybe have some turn limit for draw...') and then request 26 ('Refer back to Claude.MD'). The candidate admits this and gates (a') behind C20, so the overlap is in the wording, not the mechanism. The message should read as a follow-up to his answer, not a re-ask. reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for this angle. As a decision request, Evan's answer does separate the first two rivals (safety-net vs specification reading) by definition. The other three (R-draw-haven, R-rule-irrelevant, R-search-needed) are settled by C20, not by this candidate, and the gating rule (ask (a') only if C20's two readings differ by >= 2 SE) sends the question only when the evidence supports it. That is good design. The power claim is conservative. A paired re-score on the same games changes only games unfinished at the cut, by +-1/6 each (0.5 -> 2/3 or 1/3). At 192 games with 19-47% reaching the cut, the SE of the mean difference is about 0.005-0.008, so 0.04 sits at about 5 SE, not 2. Three gaps remain. (1) The 'no compute, re-scoring' evidence is exact only for runs that carry prizeTrace (notes/scripts/walls_vs_humans.js:146-166, added in #150). #139 used the Prize count at the game's end as a stand-in for the count at the cut. That stand-in favours whoever led at the end (the walls led at 109 of 148 deck-out wins, #141), so evidence from before #150 is biased, not just underpowered. (2) The (a') in-loop arm names no matched control. It should be the plain draw at the same T, fork, recipe and seeds (scr-t60gate479 is the nearest existing one, ideally re-run with common random numbers), so the only factor that varies is plain draw vs Prize decision. (3) The arm's readouts (acc Delta-Pokemon, share of games at the cut, decks holding both Chansey and Snorlax) are deck and selection readouts. They match an N4 judging change, but the arm should also report JF1 (walls vs the 24 lists) under the new judge, to show the judge changed before reading the decks. The acc prediction (<= 0, against the +0.7 to +2.5 Pokemon per accepted move the gate showed over 486-499 in #140) lies well outside that band and is a sound discriminator. The 10-iteration stop at 489 is enough for acc composition, which reacts within an iteration. It is not enough for type composition, since relapse takes 10-15 iterations, so a null type readout at 489 must not count as a refutation. The >60%-at-cut kill is calibrated to #142.
required_changes: State that C20 and the evidence sent to Evan use only runs with exact prizeTrace (log #150 or later), and that #139's end-of-game Prize count is biased toward the walls, not just noisy.
Name the (a') arm's matched control: a plain draw at the same T, same fork, recipe and seeds (common random numbers where possible), so plain draw vs Prize decision is the only factor that varies.
Add JF1 (walls vs the 24 human lists under the arm's judge, scored with the arm's rule) at the arm's start and end, as the check that the judge changed.

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for this angle. No rule is violated. The rule uses only results, turns and the game's own end score, which rule 2 permits. T is never fitted to the human lists, and D2 forbids that outright. Every game has its own tournament time rule, so the mechanism carries to MTG, where the time rule is itself close to a plain draw after extra turns. D2(a) uses outside facts about round length, not human decklists, so it is a game specification, not shaping. The cost of (a') is roughly right but somewhat underestimated. maxTurns is set per Runner (env/runner.js:23-25, 63), while metagame.py sends one maxTurns per shard message (rl/metagame.py:549). So (a') needs: a per-job override; a Prize-decided time ending in env/game.js (today it returns winner 0); fractional per-seat scores (1, 2/3, 1/3, 0) carried through judged()/judged_mean, the draft reward, turnover, the best quarter and the judge_search clone path, all of which assume win/draw/loss today; and engine tests. That is about half a day to a day. The split between recorded and judged games is clean under the current recipe, because with --judge-explore set the recorded games judge no deck (metagame.py:525-527). Without that flag, recorded games also score decks, and the candidate's 'PPO's recorded games stay as they are' would mix two scoring rules. The bigger problem is the request's size. Eight decisions in one message conflict with how request 26 was read ('iterate on those without handing decisions back') and with Evan's terse past answers, so most of D1-D8 may go unanswered. Several are not his to make. D3 (turns or decisions as the clock's unit) is engineering. D5 (bootstrapping the value at the cut under the existing safety net) is a learning-method choice the loop may make itself. D8 (the answer key's scope) is an evaluation choice. D6 waits on C09 by the candidate's own design. Only D1(a/a'), D2 and D7 (the commit go-ahead, which #139 already flagged as needing him) need Evan. The '1 h, no compute' figure holds only for re-scoring runs that have prizeTrace. The arm's one screen slot (about 2.5 h, 10 iterations) fits within 3 screens.

Re-estimate (a') at half a day to one day: a per-job maxTurns override in env/runner.js, a Prize-decided time ending in env/game.js, and fractional scores carried through judged()/judged_mean, the draft reward, turnover and the judge_search path, with engine tests.

title: Training-side test of the round rule (needs Evan's go-ahead): the pilot on frozen decks under the STS rule against a plain draw and no clock, then, only if it passes, system screens including a from-scratch prevention arm
rivals: CA clock-aware racing: under the event's payoff the pilot learns to close games before time (Pardo et al.'s 'photo finish') and its verdict on the walls falls
TC competence-bound: the incentive alone does not make the pilot faster; the verdict moves only with search (ExP)
TU turtle: the pilot learns lead-then-stall, and the walls, which heal and hold leads, gain from time wins
DS plain-draw draw-seeking at the pilot level: on frozen decks the plain-draw arm's limit endings rise although decks cannot drift
design: Stage 1, decks frozen so drafting cannot confound: fork the scr-resetcap 479 pilot, --reseed 2, the 479 population's 99 decks frozen (a small --freeze-decks flag: no draws, select or turnover), the recipe's 250 wide practice games, 500 recorded games an iteration, no judge games. Three arms, three slots, 25 iterations: A_sts the round rule with per-seat points (+1 / +1/3 / -1/3 / -1, C01); A_draw the same clock with today's plain draw (0 to the pilot); A_none untimed. T as Evan decides (C33 D2): T* from C02 if known, otherwise T drawn per game from C13's prior Pi with the time left as a global feature ((T - turn)/48, zero-initialised weights), the same draws in A_draw. Readouts at 489, 494, 504: each arm's pilot judges wall sets A and B against the 24 lists under the same rule (greedy, 1,152 games a set); the lists' Prize-win turns and share finished by T; the share of training games ending at time per iteration (in A_none, the share longer than T from traces); a turtle detector (time wins as a share of each deck type's wins; the leader's turns without attacking while an attack was available); puzzles (C10). Stage 2, only if CA holds and C15 does not show SW: the gate recipe with the rule from 479 (escape; control the same recipe without it) and #124's recipe from scratch with the rule for 40 iterations (prevention of F5; control 016-scratch-recipe-m); add search-strength judging if C13 says ExP.

predictions.predicted: at 504 A_sts's pilot gives the walls an STS share >= 0.08 below A_none's under the same rule, the lists' Prize-win median >= 4 turns shorter, A_draw's change at most half of A_sts's; in stage 2 from scratch, Prize endings > 20% by iteration 20 (#124: 8 of 2,000) and median Energy > 8
A_sts and A_none within 0.03 on the walls' share at 494 and 504; tempo unchanged; puzzles within the 0.06 bar
in A_sts time wins exceed 30% of the walls' wins and rise, the leader's no-attack turns lengthen near T, and A_sts's pilot rates the walls >= 0.03 higher than A_none's
A_draw's time endings rise >= 10 points over 25 iterations on frozen decks while A_none's share of games longer than T stays within 3 points

readout: Stage 1 (pilot readouts): the trained pilot's verdict on the walls under the rule, its tempo with the lists, turtle and time-share trajectories, puzzles. Deck-shape stall rules apply only in stage 2.
noise_and_power: Judge probes SE about 0.013 per 1,152-game set, two sets; ten population pilots of different recipes spread 0.676-0.746 on the walls (#147, SD about 0.022), so 0.08 is about 3.5 SD; if CA appears, a second seed of A_sts and A_none confirms it before stage 2. Time shares: 750 games an iteration, SE about 0.018, so a 10-point rise over 25 iterations is clear. Stage 2 is read against the screen A/A bands (distance RMS 2.0-4.8; relapse timing reproducible, S03; C29).
kill_rule: Stage 1: stop an arm if its value loss doubles and does not recover within 5 iterations or time endings exceed 60% for 3 iterations; all arms stop at 25; skip stage 2 under TC or TU. Stage 2: stop at 15 if the largest type is >= the control's and >= 70 decks hold Chansey and Snorlax, or time ties exceed 60% for 3 iterations, or the walls' time-win share rises for 3 iterations while their points against the lists do not fall; stop the from-scratch arm at 25 if Prize endings stay < 5%.
cost: About 3 h of code beyond C01 (freeze-decks flag, time-left feature, seat rewards). Stage 1: three slots for 1.5-2.5 h (no judge games), plus about 10 min a probe. Stage 2: two or three slots for 3-4 h.
distinct_from: H04 trained plain draws in the full loop from 479 (decks moving, the draw paying 0 to the pilot and 0.5 to each deck): never the Prize decision, per-seat points, frozen decks or a randomised clock. H51-H53 changed the deck-out payoff or discount, which the rule leaves alone; H23's scr-jsearch479 paired search judging with a plain draw; H46's from-scratch recipe never had a clock. A_draw is the matched control, not a new limit screen: its never-varied factor is frozen decks (removing the deck drift behind H04's 'no --max-turns 40 in any configuration'); a fixed T* of exactly 40 is avoided unless C02 gives it. C31's arm B tests the rule on a seeded human field; this tests the clock-to-pilot link on the population's own decks.
rules_check: The rule uses results, turns and the game's own end score (rule 2), the time left is part of any clocked game's state, and it carries to MTG with that event's rule. Evan chose a plain draw (request 24) and request 26 was read as 'the process, not the rules', so this runs only with his explicit go-ahead (C33 D1a). It logs the time share by the losing side and traces samples, as H01's verifier requires for any outcome paying more than a loss (a tie pays -1/3).
value: The only test of the clock-to-pilot link that offline re-scoring cannot reach: whether a pilot trained under the event's payoff plays the human lists' game faster and stops rating the walls first. CA opens the system screens and the from-scratch prevention arm; TC says adopt the rule only with search-strength judging; TU warns of a new attractor; DS confirms the plain draw's failure was an artifact of its payoff (C14).
