reviews.reasons: This is new at both the mechanism and node level. The STS round rule (Prize tiebreak at time, per-seat +1 / +1/3 / -1/3 / -1) has never been trained on. Every family that touches the clock lists it as untested: H01's missing variant, H03 'STS round rule in training: genuinely untested', H04 'Prize-tiebreak limit in training', H23, H51 and H53. The ledger critic says the same ('The only payoff ever trained is a plain draw'). In the progress log the rule appears only in #139/#140 as an offline re-score plus Evan's plain-draw choice, and there is no tiebreak code (env/game.js maxTurns gives a plain draw only). A second factor was also never varied: frozen decks with pilot-level readouts. Every earlier limit screen (#142-143, scr-t60gate479, scr-jsearch479) let the decks drift and read deck shape. Checks against the do-not-repeat lists: (a) H04's '--max-turns 40 in any configuration'. A_draw comes close if C13's prior Pi puts heavy weight near 40. Freezing the decks is a real new factor, since the decks' shift is the stated reason for that entry, and A_draw serves as a matched control rather than a lever. Still, Pi's mass near 40 should be reported. (b) H01 forbids a draw payoff above a loss unless it is logged. The candidate logs the time share by the losing side and traces samples, so it complies. (c) H51/H52 '--deckout-win 0' and H53 '--gamma 0.995' are not used. (d) H46 'recipe from scratch' becomes distinct in stage 2 only through the rule, which is a never-varied factor, so it is fine. C15 and C31 overlap in theme but use other nodes and designs: offline re-scoring, and a seeded human field.

The readout matches the node: stage 1 changes the pilot's payoff and reads the pilot's verdict, tempo, time share, turtle stats and puzzles on frozen decks, with deck-shape rules saved for stage 2. That is the right pairing, as analysis section 4 asks. Judging every arm under the same rule isolates what the pilot learned from what the rule itself does. A_draw separates the payoff at time from the clock. The rivals are mostly separated. Five problems remain. (1) Power. Using the 10-pilot spread (SD about 0.022), the difference between two single-seed pilots has SD about 0.031, so the 0.08 CA bar is about 2.6 SD, not 3.5. TC's 'within 0.03' is about 1 SD, so TC would be confirmed only about two thirds of the time even when it is true. Results between -0.03 and -0.08 belong to no rival. A second seed is planned only if CA shows up, which is asymmetric: a TC or TU verdict from one seed then closes stage 2. (2) An unlisted rival makes a null ambiguous. The frozen 479 field is about 75% walls (73-76 of 99 decks hold both Chansey and Snorlax), so the pilot hardly ever plays tempo decks under the rule. A null cannot tell TC ('the incentive does not make it faster') from 'the field never asked it to race'. Standing fact: competence has been flat since iteration 160, so TC is the a priori favourite either way. (3) The probe T is not set. With T drawn per game, the judging T or grid, and common deals across arms, must be fixed in advance. (4) The kill rule is miscalibrated against the effects it is meant to measure. The critic's data show the time share rose within about 10 iterations wherever the limit bit (40 turns: 43 to 94%, 60: 13 to 33-38%). 'Time endings > 60% for 3 iterations' would therefore stop A_draw and A_sts just as the DS or TU signal appears. Changing the reward scale and adding a feature can double the value loss in the first iterations by itself. (5) Stage 2's from-scratch control, 016-scratch-recipe-m, is historical (#117-124). It ran on older code and on argparse defaults that differ from the adopted recipe, so it cannot be read against the screen A/A bands.
required_changes: Run 2 seeds of A_sts and A_none from the start (or before any TC/TU verdict is read). Base the bars on the SD of a difference between pilots (about 0.031). Pre-register the 0.03-0.08 zone as inconclusive and test TC as an equivalence (TOST) at a stated margin.

Add the field-exposure rival and a readout that separates it. Either freeze a second, varied deck set from the population's own decks (for example scr-gate479's near-human-shape population or a type-capped field) as an extra A_sts/A_none pair, or report the pilot's Prize-win turns and time share on the 250 wide practice games and on the non-wall population decks for each arm.
Fix the judging condition in advance: one T, or C13's grid, the same seeded deals for every arm and checkpoint (common random numbers), and both wall sets.
In stage 1, make the time-endings > 60% condition a logged flag, not a kill: it is the TU and DS signal. Exempt the first 3 iterations after the reward switch from the value-loss-doubling kill.
Use a concurrent from-scratch control on the current code with the adopted recipe's flags written out, not the historical 016-scratch-recipe-m.

reviews.reasons: Rules: the change uses results, the game's own Prize score and the turn, and it uses no human lists, bots or card-specific moves. It counts as part of the game's definition, not shaping, under rule 2. The candidate rightly gates itself on Evan's explicit go-ahead. Evan's request 24 chose a plain draw, and request 26 was read as 'the process, not the rules'. The relayed 'let's do the cheaper spend' does not approve this. One more point is Evan's to decide (C33 D2): T taken from research on human turns per 20-minute round is a parameter derived from human play. Its MTG carry-over is 'the event's own rule', not the Prize tiebreak itself. Machine budget: three stage-1 slots are fine, since 750 games an iteration with no judge games is lighter than a 6-minute iteration. The 18 probes (3 arms x 3 checkpoints x 2 sets x 1,152 games) at about 9 min each on 4 CPU workers fit alongside. The cost is underestimated, though. (a) The time-left feature changes GLOB_F (env/tokens.js, 82 bytes) and so the shape of nn.Linear(glob_f, d) in rl/token_model.py:195. That is a shape change, not a missing module, so load_grown and ZERO_AT_GROWTH (rl/train.py:448-478) do not cover it. It also needs new ONNX exports for every walls_vs_humans probe. (b) A per-game T needs per-job maxTurns: Runner takes one maxTurns at construction (env/runner.js:23, 63), and the same holds for remote_worker's runner and the tsearch clones. (c) Per-seat time rewards have to replace the win/draw/loss z in env/runner.js:76 and env/remote_worker.js:413, and in search scoring. (d) The freeze-decks flag is cheap: a bypass of drafter.sample at rl/metagame.py:508, plus turning off select, turnover and the draft step. Altogether that is about 5-7 h beyond C01's own 3-4 h, plus the inputs from C13 (prior Pi, wall set B, grid) and C10 (puzzles, about 4 h). With a fixed T*, the feature can be dropped, because the turn is already in glob[0]. Stage 2 needs a concurrent from-scratch control: 4 runs of 25-40 iterations, about 8 h across 3 slots, not 3-4 h. Hand-launched runs must also state the adopted recipe's flags, because the argparse defaults differ (swaps, lr, epochs, shaping).
required_changes: Re-estimate the code at about 5-7 h beyond C01. List the glob-shape migration (custom loading that pads the glob Linear with zero columns), the ONNX re-exports for the probes, per-job T in env/runner.js and env/remote_worker.js (including tsearch clones), and the seat rewards at env/runner.js:76 and env/remote_worker.js:413. Or use a fixed T* and drop the time-left feature.
List the dependencies on C01, C10, C13 (prior Pi, wall set B, grid) and C33 (D1a, D2) as hard prerequisites of stage 1.

Re-cost stage 2 with a concurrent from-scratch control (4 runs, about 8 h of slot time) and write out every adopted-recipe flag instead of relying on argparse defaults or notes/scripts/screen.py's pre-#127 main_args.
Do not launch until Evan explicitly approves the round rule for training (C33 D1a) and the source of T (C33 D2). The relayed 'cheaper spend' message is not that approval.

title: Prize margin as the pilot's terminal reward: is the human field slow because a slow win pays like a fast one?
rivals: R1 objective: a win pays 1 however it comes, so slow play costs nothing; the reward is known to move pace (deck-out wins paid 0 cut deck-outs 39% -> 27%, #33; pilot-v2, trained that way, decks out in fewer human-vs-human games, 27% vs 35%, and rates the walls 0.26); the game's own end score is the rule-2-compliant form of that lever
R2 competence: the pilot already wants to win fast but cannot; a margin reward leaves pace unchanged
R3 margin pays the walls: they lead on Prizes in 109 of their 148 deck-out wins (#141), so a margin speeds human-vs-human games without lowering the walls' verdict
design: env/runner.js terminal reward = (1 - w) x result + w x (Prizes taken - Prizes conceded)/6 from prizesLeft at the game's end, for every ending (deck-out, no-Pokemon, draws); --margin-reward w in rl/train.py and rl/metagame.py. Testbed: C08's shared human-free pilot testbed; fork scr-resetcap 499's pilot and train 20 iterations with identical seeds: control (w = 0) and w = 0.5, plus w = 1 if a slot is free. The control arm and a second control seed (the testbed A/A) are shared with C36, C37 and C08's step 2. Evaluate on C10's human-vs-human 8x8 tempo panel, the walls verdict (#147 protocol) with #137's 2x2 seat decomposition, Elo by win rate against the control, and the puzzles.

predictions.predicted: human-vs-human deck-outs fall >= 5 points (35% -> <= 30%), median prize-win turn >= 3, pace up >= 0.3 Prizes by turn 20; walls verdict down >= 0.04, mostly through the margin pilot on the lists' seat; win-rate Elo >= -15
deck-outs and pace within the A/A band; walls verdict within +/-0.02; puzzles flat
pace rises but the walls verdict is flat or higher, and the walls' deck-out wins keep their Prize leads

readout: Human-vs-human tempo metrics; walls verdict with seat decomposition; win-rate Elo vs control; ending mix of training games.
noise_and_power: Deck-outs SE about 1.4 points on 1,024 games (about 0.5 on the full 24x24x16 matrix); walls verdict SE 0.013 (1,152); fork noise from the shared second control seed.
kill_rule: Stop at 10 iterations if deck-outs and pace are within the control's A/A band; stop at once if win-rate Elo falls below -40 (trading wins for margin).
cost: About 10-20 lines; two arms x 20 iterations at about 1 min (#73: 49-65 s an iteration) on one GPU process plus about 1 h of evaluation; the control is shared.
distinct_from: H29 put the margin only into the draft reward (0.5, refuted once in an obsolete setup); H52 paid deck-out wins 0 (game-specific, #51); H53 discounted with gamma; H54's potential-based shaping telescopes at gamma 1 (shape_rewards zeroes the terminal potential), so it never changed the objective; H04 tested draws. H29, H51, H52 and H54's verifiers all list margin in the pilot's reward as never built. C34's round rule decides only at a cut; this pays the margin in every game.
rules_check: Rule 2 names the game's own end score as allowed; no human input; carries to MTG as the life difference; one scalar change to the existing result reward.
value: R1: a one-line rule-compliant objective change that makes the pilot, and so the judge, play the prize race, adopted before more judge work (also C30's fallback). R2: pace is a competence problem (C11, C36, C37). R3: the objective is fine for human-vs-human play and the walls' edge needs the clock or search (C13, C33).
merged_from: pilot: Prize margin as the pilot's terminal reward: is the human field slow because a slow win pays like a fast one?

reviews.reasons: No earlier dedicated reviews to keep. I checked every family that could overlap. H29 (N6) put the margin only into the draft head's REINFORCE reward (rl/metagame.py:660, --draft-margin), and its do-not-repeat list covers only draft-margin settings. H51 and H52 cover --deckout-win 0, which pays by ending type and was ruled game-specific in #51; the margin instead pays by the game's own end score in every ending, prize wins included. H53 is gamma 0.995. H54 is potential-based prize shaping: rl/train.py shape_rewards gives the last decision -Phi, so with gamma 1 it telescopes and leaves the objective unchanged. In effect C35 is that same potential with the terminal value kept, which is a change of objective, not of credit timing. H04 and H24 are plain turn-limit draws, and C34 (the round rule) acts only at a clock cut. The verifiers of H29, H51, H52 and H54 all list 'prize margin in the pilot's PPO reward (#124 remedy b)' as never built. Grep agrees: the progress log has it only as a proposal at line 3227, and env/runner.js finish() writes rewards from the result and deckoutWin alone. The distinct, never-varied factor: the pilot's terminal reward as a function of the final Prize difference (node N10, objective rather than credit timing), on a pilot testbed with frozen decks. Small caveat: it shares H52's direction of incentive (it devalues deck-out wins while level or behind), so a positive result should be read against #33's effect size, not as new in kind.

The readouts fit the node: a pilot-objective change is read on pilot and judge measures (the human-vs-human tempo panel, the walls verdict with seat decomposition, win-rate Elo against the control, puzzles), not on deck shape. R1 and R3 predict clearly different outcomes on the walls verdict and on its seat decomposition. Several weaknesses remain. (1) R2's prediction (pace inside the A/A band) is also what you get if w=0.5 over 20 iterations is too weak or too short to change behaviour. A minimum win still pays 0.5 or more, so this incentive is weaker than #33's deck-out-win 0. With only one dosed arm, a null cannot separate 'the pilot cannot win faster' (R2) from 'the incentive never took effect'. That makes the w=1 arm necessary, not optional, and the design also needs a manipulation check. (2) The stated SEs are binomial and within-pilot: 1,024 games give about 1.5 points on deck-outs, and 1,152 give 0.013 on the walls verdict. A difference between two arms has SE about 2.1 points and about 0.018, before fork noise. The fork noise rests on a single A/A pair, which is one draw. R2's walls band of +/-0.02 is about 1 SE of a difference, too tight to tell apart from a small R1 effect. R1's 0.04 threshold is about 2.2 SE before fork noise, which is borderline. (3) The 10-iteration kill is keyed to evaluation deck-outs measured against a one-seed A/A band. In #33 a stronger reward moved sampled training deck-outs by about 20 points within 15 iterations, and greedy evaluation lagged. A weaker reward judged at 10 iterations on evaluation games risks a short-horizon false null. The kill should key to the training-game ending mix, which reacts first. (4) Separating R3 needs the walls' deck-out wins' Prize-lead share (109/148 at baseline, #141) measured in both arms. It is named in R3 but not in the readout. The Elo floor of -15 is about 1.7 sigma at sigma 8.8, which is acceptable.
required_changes: Make the w = 1 arm required (or run w = 0.25 and w = 1) so there is a dose-response. Read R2 only when the doses agree and the manipulation check passes.

Add a manipulation check from each arm's own sampled training games: mean final Prize margin of wins, the deck-out share of endings, and the value head's correlation with the final margin, per iteration. If these do not move, report 'not delivered', not R2.
Change the 10-iteration kill: stop only if the training-game ending mix and the training-game win margin are both inside the A/A arms' range. Otherwise run to 20 before reading the evaluation panels.

Evaluate the A/A pair and all arms on the same fixed seeds (common random numbers). Define the band as |A/A gap| + 2 x the SE of a difference (about 2.1 points on deck-outs, about 0.018 on the walls verdict). Widen R2's walls band to about +/-0.035, or double the walls-verdict games to about 2,300 per pairing so that R1's 0.04 clears the noise.
Add to the readout the walls' deck-out-win Prize-lead share (baseline 109/148) and the walls' prize-win share in the verdict games for each arm. These are what separate R3 from R1.

reviews.reasons: Rules: compliant. Brief rule 2 names the game's own end score (the Prize margin) as allowed. No human list enters training, since the testbed takes no run that saw the lists and the lists appear only in the evaluation panels. In MTG it becomes the life difference, normalised by starting life. It is one scalar change, so it is simple. Engineering is somewhat more than 10-20 lines. In env/runner.js finish(), left() is computed after the reward is written, so it must move before the reward loop. The margin weight has to be threaded through the Runner constructor and every remote_worker.js call site that builds a Runner (about 5: lines 151, 202, 231, 306, 365), plus qprobe's own z at line 412 if probes are used, plus rl/train.py and rl/metagame.py argparse and the message dicts (metagame.py:549, train.py:678). Also decide whether aux_targets' result target (the sum of unshaped rewards) should include the margin. That comes to about 30-40 lines plus a unit test. The compute estimate also omits several dependencies and pitfalls. (a) The 'shared C08 testbed and control' come from C08 step 2, which runs only if C08 step 1 finds R1. If it does not, C35 must build its own matchups file (the 499 population's decks, other types from snapshots, wide decks) and run its own control and A/A seeds, about 1-2 h of assembly plus 2 x 20 iterations. (b) C10's 8x8 tempo panel and #137's 2x2 seat decomposition are evaluation tooling that is not yet built (C10 is about 4 h). (c) rl/train.py's argparse defaults differ from the 499 pilot and the adopted recipe (deck-mode joint vs cross, d 192 vs 256, tok-layers 3 vs 4, lr 3e-4 vs 2e-4, epochs 3 vs 2). Every arm must pass them explicitly, or --init-from fails or silently trains with settings from before adoption (the clutter list). --shaping also restarts its fade from iteration 0 under --init-from, so set the same value in every arm (0 matches the 499 pilot). (d) train.py defaults to 14 workers, so two concurrent arms would exceed the 16-20 CPU threads. Run them one after another (about 20-25 min each at 49-65 s an iteration) or cut --workers to about 7 each. GPU and RAM fit easily, and no metagame screen slot is needed. A realistic total: 2-4 h of build if C08 and C10 are not done, about 1.5-2 h of training for 3-4 arms, and about 1-1.5 h of evaluation.

title: Branch starts from the pilot's own games: exploring starts and a reverse curriculum over decisive prize-race positions, in the component testbed
rivals: R1 coverage: the pilot rarely trains at decisive prize-race positions (exact lethals about once per 1,194 probes, #106); PPO from normal starts never learns them, as Dominion RL never learned engines from normal starts (Gerigk & Engels 2023)
R2 variance: such positions occur, but one game's signal is mostly luck (SNR 0.14-0.29, #75); paired continuations from one state supply the missing low-variance credit
R3 representation or learning rule: abundant low-variance data at decisive positions still leaves puzzles flat (research trigger T1)
design: A neutral re-deal clone (a Game.clone variant reshuffling each player's deck and Prizes together, hands kept) and a branch job (Runner fromGame jobs exist). Branch points: main-phase decisions at turn >= 8 from the previous iteration's recorded games where the pilot's value lies in [-0.8, 0.8] (win probability 0.1-0.9); start with each game's last 10 turns and move earlier once > 70% of branches end within 3 turns. C08's testbed, forked from scr-resetcap 499, equal recorded transitions, 15-20 iterations: A control (shared with C35); B 50% of games from branch states, K = 1 continuation; C the same states, K = 4 continuations with the first decision's advantage replaced by R_k minus the mean of the other three (a vine baseline); optional D Dominion engine starts: in practice games, 3 of the deck's least-played cards (by the pilot's own play rates) stacked into the opening hand.

predictions.predicted: B and C both beat A with C about equal to B: PlusPower-only +>= 0.10 and Trainer-first +>= 0.05 (line-scored), human-vs-human deck-outs down >= 3 points, pace up >= 0.3 Prizes by turn 20
C beats B on the same readouts while B is about equal to A
all arms within +/-0.03 of control on every puzzle class while the branch arms' value error on branch states falls

readout: Per-class line-scored puzzles (C10); tempo metrics; value Brier on natural games (covariate shift); Elo vs control on normal starts; branch-point turn and share decided within 3 turns; for D, play rates and panel values of search and disrupt Trainers.
noise_and_power: Puzzles paired across arms (about 160 PlusPower-only, SE_diff about 0.037; about 970 Trainer-first, about 0.015); Elo sigma about 8.8 an arm (lab A/A); deck-outs SE about 1.4 points; A/A from the shared second control seed.
kill_rule: Stop at 10 iterations if B and C are within +/-0.03 of control on every puzzle class, if Elo on normal starts is below -30, or if natural-game value Brier worsens by > 10%.
cost: 1-2 days of code (neutral re-deal clone, branch capture, branch jobs, vine advantage in rl/train.py); 15-20 iterations an arm, about 1-1.5 h on one GPU process; no extra games (branches come from the recorded budget); control shared.
distinct_from: Nothing in the log started PPO games mid-game: challenger practice (H17) changed the opponent, wide practice (H16) the decks, hard lethal targets (H11) supervised toward search; the 408 puzzles are evaluation-only. Arm C is H08's untested 'variance-reduced advantages (re-dealt paired baselines)'; arm D's start-state change is new.
rules_check: Start states come from the pilot's own human-free games; hidden zones are re-dealt from their posterior (no leak); branch points use the pilot's own value; game-agnostic wherever an engine can clone; the reward is still the result.
value: R1/R2: a cheap rule-compliant route to prize-race competence, adoptable before any distillation (C37). R3 stops data-side pilot work and sends the question to outside research on the learning rule.
merged_from: pilot: Branch starts from the pilot's own games: exploring starts and a reverse curriculum over decisive prize-race positions, tested in a component testbed

reviews.reasons:
No earlier reviews exist for C36, so all three angles are fresh. I read the whole ledger digest (H01-H69). I grepped notes/progress-log.md for reverse curriculum, exploring start, vine, mid-game start, branch state/point, start state and fromGame. The only hit is line 1775, which describes the Runner's fromGame/first feature built for qprobe. Every PPO game in the log starts from a fresh deal. Cloned mid-game states (Game.prototype.clone, env/game.js 285-309) have been used only for evaluation and targets: credit probes (#75-#80, H08), play-time search (H05, H22) and supervised distillation targets (H11 #103-#106). The research index fact-check says the same: 'Nothing in the log has started PPO episodes mid-game.'

The factor that was never varied is the start-state distribution of PPO episodes (node N2/N10, data side). It is distinct from these families:
- H11 (EI hard targets) distils one-turn search argmaxes as a supervised loss. C36 trains RL returns from full continuations. H11's untested 'lethal targets on late-game probes' is adjacent, but it is a target-selection variant of distillation, not a start-state change.
- H16/H17 change decks and opponents, not where games start.
- H09/H10 change sampling and entropy.
- H49/H50 change lambda and value targets.

Arm C, a leave-one-out baseline over K continuations from one re-dealt state, is exactly H08's listed untested variant ('variance-reduced advantages (re-dealt paired baselines)'), which the verifier confirms has no paired or common-random advantage estimator anywhere. It also covers H49's untested 'variance reduction ... per-decision baselines'.

Arm D (opening hands stacked with the deck's least-played cards) is research ccg idea 1, never run. It matches no do-not-repeat entry. No configuration in any do-not-repeat list is rerun. Small caution: the readout must not slide back into deciding a pilot change on one fork's deck shape (H60/H62 do-not-repeat). The candidate correctly uses pilot readouts.

The readouts match the node: line-scored puzzles, tempo on the human-vs-human panel, and Elo against control on normal starts are pilot readouts for a pilot-data change, not deck-shape stall rules. R1 and R2 predict different patterns across arms (B≈C>A versus C>B≈A). But several outcomes are not diagnostic as written.

(1) R3's distinguishing marker, 'value error on branch states falls', is predicted by every rival, because the branch arms train on those states. A flat puzzle result is also predicted by an unlisted rival: insufficient dose or coverage. The testbed is wall-heavy (scr-resetcap 499 decks), wall games seldom hold PlusPower or Gust lethals, and exact lethals occur once per 1,194 probes. So 'flat' cannot separate R3 from 'the branch arms never met the positions the puzzles test'. The design needs a dose readout and an on-distribution positive control. Without them, the R3 outcome is the 'relapses like control' kind that every live hypothesis allows.

(2) Under R1, 'C about equal to B' is not a sound prediction. At equal recorded transitions, K = 4 gives C about a quarter of B's distinct branch states, so under pure coverage C should fall below B. A C > B result is then confounded between variance (R2) and coverage. Either match the arms on distinct states, or change R1's prediction.

(3) No threshold for 'C beats B' is given, though R2 rests on it.

(4) Noise. Puzzle-sampling standard errors are given (PlusPower-only SE_diff 0.037, so +0.10 is about 2.7 SE; Trainer-first 0.015, so +0.05 is about 3.3 SE). But each arm is one training fork, and the 'shared second control seed' gives a single draw of the A/A difference, not a variance (the same flaw the C08 review found). Fork-to-fork competence drift (A/A RMS 0.025 on the composite, with the bar of 0.06 driven by the small PlusPower class) is of the same order as the predicted effects.

(5) Kill rule. '±0.03 on every class at 10 iterations' sits inside 1 SE on PlusPower-only, so it fires or fails mostly by chance. Ten iterations of a ~1-minute testbed is a very short dose for a pilot whose competence was flat for 300 iterations, which biases the rule toward a false null. The Elo < -30 rule (about 3.4 sigma) and the Brier rule are fine.

(6) Arm D is a separate mechanism (deck-usage exploring starts) with its own readouts. It dilutes the comparison and has no rival or prediction of its own.
required_changes: Add a dose and coverage readout per iteration: the share of branch states (and of control-arm states at turn >= 8) where a win-this-turn line exists or PlusPower, Gust or Energy Removal is in hand, measured with the existing tsearch/qprobe clone path. If the coverage of PlusPower lines is near zero in the testbed decks, put Trainer-rich wide decks in the branch pool, or drop the PlusPower prediction.

Add an on-distribution positive control: a held-out set of branch states (from games no arm trained on), played out with common random numbers by each arm's pilot against the control pilot. Outcomes: learned there and transferred (R1/R2); learned there but puzzles flat (no transfer, a new rival); not learned there (R3 or too low a dose). Replace R3's 'value error on branch states falls' with this readout.

Match B and C on the number of distinct branch states (give C four times the branch-game share, or add a K = 1 arm at C's state count), or restate R1's prediction for C given a quarter of the states. State a numeric threshold for 'C beats B'.

Run at least two seeds for B and C, plus the two control seeds, and set the bar from the spread across seeds, not from one A/A difference. Or pool B and C against control for the R1 test, and treat C versus B as secondary.

Recalibrate the kill rule. At 10 iterations, kill only if the branch arms fail the on-distribution held-out branch-state test (no gain beyond the seed spread), or on the Elo and Brier guards. Read the puzzles and tempo at 20 iterations, not 10.
Split arm D into its own candidate with its own rivals and predictions, or drop it from this run.

reviews.reasons:
Rules: no violation. Start states come from the pilot's own human-free games. Branch points are picked by the pilot's own value plus hindsight on game length, both self-generated. The reward is still the result. The human lists enter only through the C10 puzzles and tempo panel, which are evaluation only. Exploring starts and a re-dealt clone exist in any engine that can copy a game, so the idea carries to MTG.

The neutral re-deal (deck plus Prizes reshuffled together, hands kept) samples from both players' information sets. It does not leak. Its one inaccuracy is that a player who has searched their deck knows which cards are prized, and the re-deal forgets that. This is minor and acceptable. Arm D's opening-hand stacking is generic, uses the pilot's own play rates, and is not shaping.

What exists in code:
- Game.prototype.clone(rng, viewer) (env/game.js 289-309) needs a stable state, which holds at main-phase decisions. A 'hands kept' variant is about 10 lines: today's viewer clone also re-deals the opponent's hand.
- Runner jobs with fromGame/decklists (env/runner.js 34-60) already start games from a copy.
- rl/train.py's GAE (advantages(), lines 73-93) runs per trajectory and handles trajectories that start mid-game.
- Node workers are persistent Popen processes (rl/train.py:45, rl/remote.py:55), so each worker can keep a local branch pool across iterations without serialising Game objects.

The cost is underestimated, and C36 depends on unbuilt pieces:
(a) Branch capture: snapshot clones in a per-game ring buffer during collection (an onDecision hook or a Runner change). Pick points after the game ends (last 10 turns, value in [-0.8, 0.8]). Run the band and curriculum controller. Add branch jobs to the collect command of whichever worker rl/train.py uses (rollout_worker.js, not remote_worker.js) and to rl/metagame.py's games path if the testbed uses it.
(b) The vine advantage needs a branch-group id through the Runner rec, packRollout and rl/rollouts.py, then an override of the first decision's GAE advantage in rl/train.py. Both seats are recorded in self-play, so groups must be keyed per seat.
(c) Tests: the clone's re-deal invariants (extend env/tools/test_search.js) and the curriculum statistics.
Realistic total: 2-3 days, not 1-2.

C36 also presupposes two unbuilt pieces:
- C08's 'shared human-free pilot testbed'. C08's feasibility review found it does not exist: rl/train.py --init-from expects ckpt['model'], while metagame checkpoints hold 'net'/'config'. That is about half a day of glue, and the '~1 min an iteration' is unverified.
- C10's line-scored puzzle mode and the ~10x puzzle regeneration (about 4 h, plus 1-2 CPU-hours).

Machine budget is fine: one GPU process, a small branch pool (only selected states kept), 3-4 arms x 15-20 iterations, within the 3-screen, 2.7 GB and 3.5 GB limits. Asking for two seeds per branch arm (diagnosticity) doubles the GPU time, still within budget at about 1 min an iteration.
required_changes: Re-cost at about 2-3 days of code: the hands-kept clone variant, ring-buffer capture and post-game selection, a per-worker branch pool in the rollout worker that rl/train.py actually uses, branch-group ids through rec, packRollout and rollouts.py, the first-decision RLOO override in advantages(), and re-deal invariant tests.

List the dependencies and their costs: C08's human-free testbed (about half a day of glue, with the checkpoint format mismatch between rl/train.py --init-from and the metagame 'net'/'config') and C10's line-scored puzzles (about 4 h). Measure the testbed's per-iteration time before committing to the arm counts.
Define the branch-pool lifetime and size: keep it per worker, cap it (for example a few thousand states), replay a share of older starts against forgetting as Florensa does, and log pool statistics.
Key the vine groups per seat. In self-play both seats are recorded, and only the deciding seat's first decision gets the leave-one-out advantage.

title: Expert iteration v4 on a fixed deck panel: soft, gated, CRN-paired search targets with a frozen leaf value
rivals: R1 target quality: the three failed runs (-79/-56/-37 Elo) used hard one-hot targets over independent re-deals, a best-minus-worst gate keeping about 95% of probes, the live pilot's own value, and a loss over searched rows only; fixing all four transfers search's in-turn gains
R2 not transferable: this pointer policy cannot absorb one-turn search's conditional lines (a setup move that turns the attack into a Knock Out) through PPO-side distillation, whatever the targets
R3 style without strength: puzzles rise but human-vs-human pace and Elo do not, because one-turn tactics rarely decide those games
design: Gated on C03 (CRN self-agreement >= 0.80) and on C10 not finding R2. A testbed, not a screen: fork scr-resetcap 499's pilot on C08's testbed with the same seeds; control (shared with C35) and v4, 3 segments of 10 iterations. v4 probes 10% of recorded main-phase decisions (and prompts if C11 finds R1); each probe runs CRN tsearch over up to 8 options x 4 shared worlds at horizon 1; leaves scored by the fork-time frozen value or C12's V_eval, never pilot-v2 (its random decks drew on the human lists' cards, S29). Target pi_t proportional to pi x exp(clip(A/tau)) over the probed options (CMPO-style); a probe is kept only if the paired best-vs-chosen difference exceeds 2 SE; loss KL(pi_t || pi) at weight 0.05, averaged over all rows.

predictions.predicted: after 3 segments: Trainer-first +>= 0.05 and PlusPower-only +>= 0.10 (line-scored), deck-outs down >= 3 points and pace up >= 0.3 Prizes by turn 20, Elo vs control >= -10, policy entropy up <= 0.05
puzzles within +/-0.03, or Elo <= -20 (the #103-106 pattern): trigger outside research on distilling imperfect-information search (whole-turn policies, learned-model search)
puzzles rise but pace and Elo stay within noise

readout: Per-class line-scored puzzles; tempo metrics; Elo vs control; policy entropy; share of probes passing the gate; target-pilot agreement.
noise_and_power: Elo sigma about 8.8 an arm (lab A/A, #83-86); puzzle classes paired as in C10; deck-outs SE about 1.4 points at 1,024 games; the shared second control seed gives the testbed's own A/A.
kill_rule: After segment 1, stop if Elo < -20 or entropy rose 0.15; after segment 3, stop if puzzle classes are up < 0.03 over control.
cost: About a day of code (soft targets, paired gate, frozen leaf, loss normalisation); tsearch adds 30-40 s an iteration (#106); 30 iterations about 1.5-2 h an arm on one GPU process; control shared.
distinct_from: H11's do-not-repeat covers every tested form: --distill 1.0 and 0.3 with one-turn 2-4-line hard argmax targets; horizon 2 with margin 0.15; lethal-only targets; best-minus-worst gates; a live-pilot value. H11 and H14's verifiers name v4 (soft, clipped, gated, frozen leaf) as untested; CRN pairing of the targets is new.
rules_check: Targets come from the pilot's own search on its own human-free decks; the frozen leaf is its own snapshot or V_eval, not pilot-v2; legal options, clones and end results only (game-agnostic).
value: The only remaining route to a pilot stronger after training rather than only at play time: R1 adopts v4 (a judge with search-like Trainer play at greedy cost); R2 stops distillation and starts outside research; R3 redirects effort to multi-turn levers (C35, C36).
merged_from: pilot: Expert iteration v4 on a fixed deck panel: soft, gated, CRN-paired search targets with a frozen leaf value

required_changes: State that Gumbel top-k option sampling (part of #144's v4) is not included, so a null does not close the whole v4 family in the ledger.

reviews.reasons:
The readouts fit the node. C37 is a pilot change, read on pilot readouts (line-scored puzzles, tempo on fixed panels, Elo against the control, entropy) on a fixed deck testbed with a shared control and an A/A seed. That avoids the deck-shape stall readout that analysis section 4 criticises. Several problems weaken how well the rivals separate.

(a) The gate has a selection bias that can produce the old failure signature by itself. A probe is kept only when the best option beats the chosen one by 2 SE. So every kept target moves mass away from the sampled action, which is usually high-probability, and no target ever sharpens toward a chosen move that search confirms. That systematically raises entropy. The kill rule (entropy +0.15) and R2's Elo <= -20 could then fire because of the gate, not because the policy cannot absorb the targets.

(b) The gate's false-pass rate is uncontrolled. The SE comes from 4 paired worlds (df 3), and the comparison is the max over up to 7 alternatives against the chosen move. Under the null, the per-probe pass rate is plausibly 25-40%, which repeats the near-noise targets of #105 and #106 (60-70% disagreement).

(c) R2 versus a dose or absorption null is not separated. Puzzles within +/-0.03 are also what you would expect if a 0.05 all-rows weight (about 6x below anything tried) never moves the policy, or if few probes pass the gate. The readout lists target-pilot agreement, but no prediction uses it. Absorption (held-out probe KL falling) with flat puzzles means the targets are wrong. No absorption means R2 or too low a dose.

(d) R1 and R3 share the Elo band (>= -10 versus 'within noise', with sigma ~8.8 an arm, so an arm difference has SE ~12). They are therefore told apart only by tempo. Deck-outs at 1,024 games have SE ~1.4 an arm, about 2.0 for the difference, so -3 points is about 1.5 SE. Pace has no stated SE. R1 is a five-way conjunction, and mixed outcomes are not mapped.

(e) Puzzle power is adequate for Trainer-first (about 970 puzzles, paired SE about 0.015) and marginal for PlusPower-only (about 160 puzzles, +0.10 at roughly 2-2.5 SE). The between-seed per-class noise is unknown until the testbed A/A runs. The +0.10 bar should be checked against that A/A once it exists.

(f) tau and the clip are unspecified, so R1's success is not pre-registered.

(g) R2's conclusion ('whatever the targets') overreaches for one configuration without Gumbel sampling.

The kill rules are reasonably calibrated: Elo < -20 at 10 iterations is about 1.6 SE of the difference, and the earlier failures sat at -37 to -79 with entropy +0.27-0.29. The 30-iteration puzzle check is acceptable.
required_changes: Make the gate symmetric: keep a probe when the spread between the best option and the runner-up (or any significant advantage) passes, including probes where search confirms the chosen move, so targets can sharpen as well as flatten.

Control the gate's false-pass rate under selection across options. Either split the worlds (pick the best option on 2 CRN worlds, confirm it against the chosen move on 2 fresh ones), or use a pooled per-probe-class variance with a Bonferroni correction over options. Report the pass rate on a null where two independent CRN evaluations of the same options are compared (C03's self-agreement data).

Add an absorption readout with written predictions. Track KL(pi_t || pi) and target agreement on held-out probes against the control. Define R2 as no absorption at a dose that measurably moves the policy, separate from 'absorbed but puzzles flat', which falsifies v4's targets rather than transferability. Consider a second dose arm (0.15) if a slot is free.
Pre-register tau and the clip, for example tau set to the median per-probe advantage SE.
Give pace an SE and map the outcome when puzzles rise and tempo is mixed. Use 2,048 tempo games, or pair them on the same deals, so a 3-point deck-out difference reaches about 2 SE.
Scope R2's conclusion to this target family.

reviews.reasons:
There is no rule violation. Targets come from the pilot's own engine search (Game.clone, legal options, end results, value) on human-free decks. The puzzles and human-vs-human tempo games are evaluation only, and nothing is card-specific. One point in the write-up is inconsistent: it excludes pilot-v2 as the leaf because of its human-field-card prior (S29), yet the fork-time snapshot (scr-resetcap 499) descends from the main line, which was initialised from pilot-v2 (H45). That prior is inherited by every current pilot and is not new here, but the rationale should be corrected.

The cost of 'about a day of code' is underestimated against the code. Five pieces are needed.
(1) The testbed does not exist. rl/metagame.py has no frozen-draft or pilot-only mode, and C08's reviewer costed it at about half a day. tsearch and --distill are wired only into rl/metagame.py (lines 546-590), so a testbed built on rl/train.py --matchups-file needs them ported.
(2) A frozen leaf needs a second served model inside tsearch lines. Today the lines are played and valued by RemoteAgent(0) (env/remote_worker.js tsearch), and r.stopped.value comes from slot 0. A separate slot is needed, and the design must say whether the lines are played by the frozen pilot or the live one. A live-pilot line scored by a frozen value is a growing mismatch.
(3) The paired SE needs per-line scores returned. Today only means and n come back.
(4) Soft targets replace the integer search_target and the CE over ce.sum()/S (rl/train.py 247, 343-347) with per-row distributions over options and a KL normalised over all rows. They need pi over all options at the probe and a rule for unprobed options when there are more than 8.
(5) CRN world seeds depend on C03's change.
With tests, that is realistically 1.5-2 days, plus lead time for the four gating candidates (C03, C10, C11, C12).

Compute: '10% of recorded main-phase decisions' with no per-game cap is several times #105's roughly 1,000 probes an iteration (maxProbes 2). At 8 x 4 = 32 lines a probe and about 600 lines/s (#106: 17,876 in 29 s; 24,704 in 38 s), 1,000 probes cost about 55 s, but an uncapped 10% could cost 3-5 min an iteration. The 30-40 s figure and the 1.5-2 h an arm hold only with a cap. The machine budget is fine: each arm is one GPU process within 3 screens.
required_changes: Re-cost the code at about 1.5-2 days. Include building the C08 testbed (or depend on it explicitly), porting tsearch and target handling to whatever drives the testbed, a second model slot for the frozen leaf, per-line score return, soft-target and KL storage in the batch, and tests (identity at weight 0, KL equal to CE for one-hot targets).
Cap probes per game (for example maxProbes 2, about 1,000 probes an iteration) or set a probe budget, and measure the per-iteration time in a 1-iteration smoke before committing to 3 x 10 iterations.
Say whether the search lines are played by the frozen snapshot or the live pilot, and make the leaf's player and value consistent.
Correct the rules rationale: the frozen snapshot inherits pilot-v2's initialisation like every current pilot, so state that this inherited prior is accepted rather than avoided.

title: In-loop powered judge screen, gated on C20: all-searched judge, paired pooled search correction, clone-invariant panel
rivals: R-strength-in-loop: a searched judge with real power (no min, no shrinkage toward greedy) stops accepting Pokemon-up / Trainers-down moves and holds the type
R-redundancy-in-loop: an equal-weight panel of distinct opponents does the same by removing the mirror match's weight
R-inert-in-loop: even with power the judge's verdict on within-population edits agrees with greedy over the iterations (or the pilot co-adapts), and the walls spread as in the control
R-pooling-misspecified: the pooled correction moves selection where the all-searched arm does not, or the reverse: the composition model, not search, drove it
design: Gate: C20's branch picks the arms (R-strength: A and B; R-redundancy: P; both: B, P and B+P). Fork scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt, --reseed 2, scr-t60gate479's flags written in full (argparse defaults differ; C04): --select --candidates 1 --select-z 1.0 --judge-explore 0 --max-turns 60 --type-cap 0.5, 250 practice games, the adopted lr, epochs, swaps and draft settings. Arm A, all-searched (no new code): --judge-search 1600 covers every unrecorded game, so judged() returns the searched mean (n = 0 greedy) and --select-z uses its own SE; CRN k4 d2 if C03 validates it. Arm B, pooled correction: 300 searched games an iteration, each deal also replayed greedily; ridge fit of y = searched minus greedy outcome on the two decks' difference in card-kind counts (basic Pokemon, evolutions, Trainers, basic Energy, special Energy) over the last 5 iterations' pairs; deck score = greedy mean + (x_deck - mean x of its opponents) . w, with the fit's SE added to --select-z's. Arm P, panel: judge games against the best decks of 6 k-means clusters plus 2 hall-of-fame decks from the run's own snapshots, refreshed every 5 iterations, equal weights; incumbent and candidate paired on opponent, seat and seed with in-place substitution (C20's builder); PPO's recorded games unchanged. Optional (a') arm after Evan approves judging-only Prize scoring (C33). Control: scr-t60gate479 (480-498) and scr-jsearch479 (480-497), the same snapshot, reseed and flags with search inert: a near-A/A pair.

predictions.predicted: arms A and B: over 485-499 mean acc Delta-Pokemon <= +0.5 and Delta-Trainers >= 0 per accepted move (control: +1.2 to +3.1 Pokemon, -0.6 to -2.9 Trainers a move from 488); decks holding both walls' core cards <= 58 at 494 (control 70 and 76); in B the correction changes >= 3x as many decisions as a permuted-feature null
P moves as above while A and B stay in the control band, and >= 3 panel clusters keep a deck with panel mean >= 0.5

reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews were on file. Arm A differs from H23's do-not-repeat config (scr-jsearch479: --judge-search 200, min rule, prior 4, z 1.5, about 2.02 searched games a candidate, 0-2 flips an iteration against 15.5 from noise, log #149) in two factors that were never varied. The first is power: all of the roughly 1,500 unrecorded games are searched, about 15 a candidate, the same n as the greedy control. The second is the estimator: with n = 0 greedy, judged() returns ssum/sn, so there is no min and no shrinkage. H23's verifier lists exactly this as untested ('a searched share that has power ... all judge games', and '--judge-score search'). It is not H22, which was offline walls against human lists only, and it is not H20/H21 (an independent or greedy judge). Arm P varies the opponent mix: a cluster-balanced, equal-weight panel plus hall-of-fame decks. ledger_meta's coverage critic says this was never varied ('No current-loop family varies the opponent mix'), and grep finds no hall-of-fame, k-means or opponent-panel run in progress-log.md. H39's untested k-means item is about a cap, not about judging opponents. Arm B partly overlaps H69's do-not-repeat ('deck-shape linear features (Energy/Trainer/Basic counts) as a ranker'). Its distinct factor is the regression target, a paired searched-minus-greedy residual refit each iteration and added to real greedy means. That target is new, and the candidate says so correctly. Gating on the offline C20 audit avoids the predictable-null pattern of section 6. The control pair (t60gate479 / jsearch479) is reused, not rerun.
required_changes: State in distinct_from that B's correction is a deck-shape linear model (H69's do-not-repeat class) and that only the paired search-minus-greedy residual target separates it, so that B is closed if w's out-of-sample fit is no better than its permuted null.

reviews.reasons: The core contrast works. The readout (accepted against proposed composition per accepted move, 5-iteration means, SE about 0.4 card) is a selection-level readout matched to the judge and selection nodes. Strength predicts <= +0.5 Pokemon a move against the control's +1.2 to +3.1, a gap of about 4-6 SE, and the decks-holding-both threshold (<= 58 at 494, 12 below the lower control) is about 2x the pair's spread. The kill rule needs both conditions and is lenient (control value at 489), and a judge change acts at every selection decision, so short-horizon bias is small. There are four problems. (1) The gate drops arms that the predictions need. R-redundancy's prediction says 'P moves while A and B stay in the control band', but the redundancy branch runs only P. R-pooling-misspecified compares A with B, but the 'both' branch runs B, P and B+P with no A. In those branches the rival cannot be told apart. (2) R-pooling's '>= 8 decks at 494' is inside A/A noise: the near-A/A control pair already differs by 6 at 494 and 9 at 498, so this outcome is predicted by noise alone. (3) In arm A every deck has n = 0 greedy games. pick()'s greedy comparison (metagame.py ~703) then never moves, and null_searched returns x unchanged when n = 0, so the 'decisions changed vs null' readout (flips / flips_null) is undefined there. A's evidence is composition alone unless a small greedy-paired subsample is kept. (4) B's correction is linear in the same Pokemon/Trainer/Energy counts the readout measures. Any nonzero w therefore shifts accepted composition partly by construction. The permuted-feature null tests whether w is real, but not whether the corrected score predicts held-out searched outcomes. Arms are also one seed each, and the A/A band comes from a single near pair (C29's reseeds would firm it up), so a positive arm is a screen result, not an adoption.
required_changes: Keep arm A in every gate branch (it needs no code and is the power reference), or rewrite each rival's prediction for the arms its branch actually runs; drop the R-pooling contrast in branches without both A and B.

Raise R-pooling's deck-count threshold to >= 12 at 494 (2x the pair's spread), or base it on selection-level disagreement (share of decisions where B's corrected choice differs from A's searched choice on comparable decks) rather than end counts.
In arm A, keep a small greedy replay of the same deals (e.g. 200 a iteration) so that flips against null_searched can be computed, or state that A's readout is composition-only.
For B, add a held-out check: the corrected score must predict the next iteration's searched outcomes better than the greedy mean (paired log-loss or Brier), beside the permuted-feature null.
Require a second reseed of any arm that passes before adoption, and use C29's A/A band once available.

reviews.reasons: I checked arm A's 'no new code' claim in rl/metagame.py and it holds. games 2000 with record 500 gives rec_share 0.25, about 1,500 unrecorded games, and --judge-search 1600 marks every one of them search (line ~520). Recorded games are unjudged under --judge-explore 0. judged() with n = 0 returns (ssum/sn, sn), and --select-z takes jcount, so it uses sn. CRN does not exist: grep finds no crn in env/*.js. 'CRN k4 d2' therefore depends on C03's build and is not free. A's cost is underestimated. Log #148 has 200 searched games at 319 s of searched Runner (4 workers), so 1,500 scale to about 2,400 s of play, about 42-48 min an iteration on its own. That is the top of the stated 25-42 min and on top of the 45-min kill, so A may be stopped for cost, not outcome. 20 iterations take about 15-16 h, and the 489 check comes after about 7.5 h. With 3 screens at once (about 12 node workers plus 3 learners on about 16 usable threads) it slows further. B's 300 searched games at about 480 s plus paired greedy duplicates give about 9-10 min alone, close to its 12-min kill under contention. B's code (duplicate jobs on the same seed, ridge with SE over 5 iterations kept in checkpoints, wired into jscore) is about 1 day. P depends on C20's in-place-substitution builder, which does not exist yet. Pairing incumbent and candidate on opponent, seat and seed, k-means refresh, hall-of-fame snapshot loading and checkpoint state are new scheduling code. The --fixed-decks path (fixed_share) can host panel opponents, but --select-z's unpaired binomial test throws away the pairing unless a paired-difference test is added. So P is closer to 1 day than half a day. On the rules, A and P comply (own pilot, own snapshots, no human data). B is borderline. Hand-chosen features in the ground truth's own axes, with a Pokemon-specific 'evolutions' split, are a hand-designed meta-level model with no MTG analog for evolution, and it needs Evan's sign-off before adoption, as the candidate admits. Given Evan's request for the cheaper spend, A's roughly 15 h slot is the main cost.
required_changes: Recompute A's iteration time from #148's 319 s / 200 searched games (about 42-48 min) and either run A at k4 d2 (CRN only if C03 has validated it) or more search workers, or raise A's time kill to about 60 min and measure the first iteration before committing the overnight slot.
Recalibrate B's time kill (about 9-10 min alone, more under contention) to about 15 min, or measure first.
Re-cost P at about 1 day plus C20's builder, and add a paired-difference --select-z test so the pairing is used.

Make B's features game-agnostic: use the engine's card supertype only (creature/Pokemon, non-creature spell/Trainer, land/Energy, with basic vs special if the engine marks it), drop the Pokemon-specific evolution split, and record that adoption needs Evan's approval as a meta-level hand-designed model.

title: Reset-and-fine-tune judge in the loop (Strgar & Kriegman's few-shot regime), with a zero-shot arm; gated on C17
rivals: R-accumulation: the walls' verdict is skill the continuously co-trained judge accumulates on the incumbent (first mover, Lamarckian); a judge reset to a broad P0 and fine-tuned briefly with equal games per cluster stops paying it and the population stays split
R-fast-learner: the reset judge relearns the walls within its short fine-tune and the population relapses at the control's pace
R-P0-bias: the zero-shot (frozen P0) and reset arms both drift toward what P0 plays best (Pokemon piles, as in scr-v2 and scr-judge2), not the human shape
design: Gate: C17 returns H-reset-viable (bal-1 <= 0.45 for k up to 5 while P1 >= 0.55) or H-slow-accumulation (P1 <= 0.40 at 40). P0: C17's W1 final weights if Evan accepts the pilot-v2 lineage; otherwise a from-scratch P0 on wide full-pool decks with the true reward (C30's W). Code: --judge-refresh P0 --judge-ft F --judge-every R: every R = 5 iterations load P0 into model slot 1 with a fresh Adam, play F = 1,000 games among the current population with equal games per k-means cluster, both seats under slot 1, deck-out wins 1, then 2 PPO epochs on slot 1 only; slot 1 then plays every unrecorded game (judge share 1.0, greedy) until the next refresh; the training pilot, head and reading path unchanged. Arms from scr-resetcap 479, --reseed 2, scr-t60gate479's flags: reset (R 5, F from C17's curve, default 1,000); zero-shot (the frozen P0 as judge, Strgar's second arm). Control: the scr-t60gate479 / scr-jsearch479 pair. After each refresh, probe the judge's own walls-vs-lists verdict (1,152 greedy games, evaluation).

predictions.predicted: reset arm: decks holding both walls' core cards (and the incumbent-cluster share) <= 55 at 494 (control 70-76); mean pairwise deck distance flat or rising while the control's falls; acc Delta-Pokemon <= +0.5; the judge's walls verdict <= 0.5 after each refresh
by 494 the reset arm is in the control band (>= 65 decks holding both) and its judge is back to >= 0.6 on the walls within one refresh
in both arms median Pokemon >= 20 or deck-outs >= 50% for 3 iterations (scr-v2 went 15 -> 23 Pokemon in 4 iterations)

readout: Selection (acc vs prop, moves) and the population: incumbent-cluster share, the legacy Chansey + Snorlax count, mean pairwise deck distance (Strgar's collapse metric); the judge's own verdict after each refresh.
noise_and_power: Control pair as in C38 (70 vs 76 decks holding both at 494; distance RMS about 2.3); per-refresh judge probe SE about 0.03. Strgar's evidence is 3 trials in one simulated domain, so the effect size is unknown and the kill rule follows the control's trajectory.
kill_rule: Stop an arm at 489 with >= 58 decks holding both (the control at 489), or median Pokemon >= 20 or deck-outs >= 50% for 3 iterations; stop the reset arm if its judge's walls verdict exceeds 0.65 after two refreshes.
cost: About 1 day of code (a trained slot-1 stream with its own optimizer and recording, cluster-balanced fine-tune games, the refresh schedule); +10-15% per iteration; 2 screens x 20 iterations, 2.5-3 h in parallel; P0 from C17 costs nothing more, a from-scratch P0 6-10 h of one slot (or C30's W).
distinct_from: scr-v2 and scr-judge2 ran Strgar's zero-shot arm with pilot-v2 (H20); the KL anchor (#135, H16) keeps the training pilot near pilot-v2 while the judge keeps accumulating; seasons (#93-101, H43, Evan's row 5) practised candidates inside the shared accumulating pilot; --draft-reset reset the head, not the pilot (H34). Resetting the judge's weights and fine-tuning it equally across types was never run (codesign-eval idea 1).
rules_check: Self-discovery and game-agnostic if P0 is human-free (a from-scratch wide-deck P0 is). W1 descends from pilot-v2 (field-card random decks, deck-out-0 training), so using it is Evan's decision (the whole main line shares that ancestry). Fine-tuning uses only the population's decks and the true reward; a second trained judge network is an Occam cost to name. Extends Evan's row 5 ('practise each deck before it counts') from the shared pilot to the judge.
value: The in-loop test of the one evaluation regime never tried: adopt it with C17's measured F, or close the evaluation-regime family with evidence.
merged_from: judge: Reset-and-fine-tune judge in the loop (Strgar & Kriegman's few-shot regime), with a zero-shot arm; gated on candidate 3

reviews.reasons: Distinct in mechanism. A judge reset to a broad P0 every R iterations with a fresh Adam, then fine-tuned briefly on cluster-balanced population games, has never run. Grep of progress-log.md finds no judge reset, judge refresh, cluster-balanced fine-tune, Strgar or few-shot entry. The research fact-check (codesign-eval idea 1) confirms that #130 reset the draft head, #131-134 froze pilot-v2 and #124/#132 started from scratch. Nearest families: H20 (frozen independent judge: scr-v2, scr-judge2), H43 (seasons: practice inside the shared pilot), H16 (KL anchor keeps the trained pilot near pilot-v2 but the judge still accumulates), H34 (--draft-reset resets the head, not the pilot) and H18/H14 (judge comparisons). The reset arm repeats no do-not-repeat configuration. The zero-shot arm is Strgar's frozen arm, which H20 ran with pilot-v2. Here three factors that were never varied make it distinct: P0 is not pilot-v2 (deck-out paid 1, full-pool wide decks: C17 W1 or C30 W, which is H20's verifier-listed untested 'frozen independent judge trained with deck-out wins paid 1'); judge share is 1.0, not 0.5; and it runs on the gate + type cap + t60 recipe (H20's untested 'frozen judge with --select-z 1.0 --candidates 1, type cap'). The control (scr-t60gate479 / scr-jsearch479) is reused, not rerun. One condition keeps it distinct: the zero-shot arm must not use pilot-v2 it349 itself, which would replay scr-judge2's mechanism (H20 do-not-repeat, --judge-pilot pilot-v2), changing only the share.
required_changes: State explicitly that neither arm uses pilot-v2 it349 as P0. With pilot-v2 the zero-shot arm becomes an H20 do-not-repeat variant that changes only the judge share.

reviews.reasons: The readout fits the node. N4 gets a judge readout (the judge's own walls-vs-lists verdict after each refresh, SE about 0.03) plus selection composition (acc vs prop) and the population (incumbent-cluster share, Chansey+Snorlax count, pairwise distance). For the reset arm the rivals predict clearly different outcomes: R-accumulation <= 55 decks with both at 494 and acc dPokemon <= +0.5; R-fast-learner >= 65 and a judge back to >= 0.6; R-P0-bias Pokemon >= 20 or deck-outs >= 50%. The effect looked for (>= 15 decks below a control pair 70/76) is about 2.5x the pair's spread, so one seed can detect a large effect. Gaps: (1) The zero-shot arm has predictions only under R-P0-bias. It exists to split 'reset+fine-tune' from 'any decoupled frozen judge', and R-accumulation (both hold?) and R-fast-learner (zero-shot holds while reset relapses) each predict something specific for it that is not written. Without those, a zero-shot outcome cannot discriminate. (2) The reset arm bundles reset with cluster balancing, and with decoupling the judge from the training pilot (judge share 1.0, which the zero-shot arm shares). If it holds, R-accumulation cannot be credited over 'equal games per cluster'. A third screen is free, since the control is reused, so a reset arm with a frequency-weighted (unbalanced) fine-tune would separate them. (3) Strgar fine-tunes on parents and offspring. Here the judge practises only population decks and stays frozen for 5 iterations, so candidate draws are always judged unpractised, which keeps an incumbent-familiarity edge at the edit level. A null would then not refute R-accumulation. Add the current candidate draws to the fine-tune games (about half), or test R=1/F=500. (4) The kill rule stops an arm at 489 with >= 58 decks holding both, which is exactly the control's value at a single seed whose A/A spread is about 6 decks. A truly effective arm starting at about 53 could cross it by noise (roughly 1 in 3). Use >= 64, or >= 58 combined with mean acc dPokemon >= +1.0 over 485-489 as in C38. With only 2 refreshes by 489 the kill should not be a pure trajectory match. (5) The 56-64 band at 494 fits no rival. Declare it inconclusive, triggering a --reseed replicate, rather than reading it as relapse. (6) N3 is listed as a node but has no pilot readout. Drop it, or add h2h of the refreshed judge vs P0 on wide decks (forgetting check).
required_changes: Write predictions for the zero-shot arm under R-accumulation and R-fast-learner (e.g. fast-learner: zero-shot holds <= 55 while reset relapses >= 65; accumulation: both hold unless P0-bias fires).
Include current candidate draws (offspring) in the refresh fine-tune games, or run R=1/F=500, so the judge practises what it judges, as in Strgar's design.
Recalibrate the kill: stop at 489 only if >= 64 decks hold both, or if >= 58 together with mean acc dPokemon >= +1.0 over 485-489.
Declare 56-64 decks holding both at 494 inconclusive (a --reseed replicate), not relapse.

Optionally use the free third screen for a reset arm with frequency-weighted (unbalanced) fine-tune games, to separate reset from cluster balancing; otherwise state that a positive result credits the reset and the balancing jointly.
Drop N3 from the nodes, or add a pilot readout (refreshed judge vs P0 h2h on wide decks).

reviews.reasons: The code supports it at about the stated cost. rl/metagame.py already serves a second model in slot 1 (jnet via frozen(), models={1: jnet}). It assigns slots [1,1] per job and judges --judge-share of the unrecorded games (share 1.0 = every judged game). remote_worker.js records the slot per transition (batch['slot']; subset by slot is already done for practice-vs). Greedy judging applies to unrecorded seats whatever their slot. ppo_update(model, opt, batch, args, device) in rl/train.py is generic. Missing pieces: a trainable jnet with its own Adam reset at each refresh, a separate rp.collect round of F recorded slot-1 games with cluster-balanced pairing (a small numpy k-means on pool.vector counts; no helper exists), a slot-1 PPO step without fading shaping, and checkpointing jnet and its Adam for resume. Half a day to a day is realistic. The zero-shot arm needs no new code: --judge-pilot P0 --judge-share 1.0 --judge-explore 0. Machine: 2 screens fit the 3-screen cap. A second d256 network and its Adam add little GPU memory; the 1,000-game PPO batch is about 1.3x the main one and micro-batching covers it. The per-iteration overhead is underestimated if the 1,152-game judge probe runs in-loop. Refresh plus PPO plus probe every 5 iterations is about 6-8 min on a 30-min block, roughly 20-25%, not 10-15%. Run the probe on the saved judge checkpoint as a CPU/side job. The from-scratch P0 cost (6-10 h) conflicts with C30's own estimate (about 1 h a seed, 40-60 iterations), and a 40-60-iteration W may be too weak to be a broad P0; reconcile this. Rules: training uses only population decks and the true reward; k-means on card counts and reset/fine-tune are game-agnostic; the human lists enter only the evaluation probe and the experimenter's kill rule, never selection or the head's reward. P0 = C17 W1 descends from pilot-v2, which per the fact-check learned on the human lists' 56 cards with deck-out 0. The candidate rightly defers that to Evan. Without his ruling, the default must be the human-free full-pool P0. The second trained network is an Occam cost to name before adoption. The arm is also gated on C17, whose cost is not counted here.
required_changes: Default P0 to the human-free full-pool pilot (C30's W) unless Evan explicitly accepts the pilot-v2 lineage (C17 W1); record the ruling in notes/evan-requests.md.
Run the per-refresh 1,152-game walls probe out of loop on a saved judge checkpoint, or raise the per-iteration overhead estimate to about 20-25%.
Reconcile the from-scratch P0 cost with C30's estimate, and check that W is strong enough (puzzles, JF1/JF2) before it serves as P0.
Write all flags in full (argparse defaults differ from the adopted recipe) and checkpoint jnet plus its Adam so a resume does not silently reset the judge.

title: Evan's ruling on the Stage 3 bootstrap components: a kind-aware proposal base measure, a pilot-first warm-up, and the random-deck generator
rivals: R-allowed: a kind-aware base measure, a criterion-based pilot-first warm-up on random legal decks and a rules-structured random-deck generator use only rules information and results, so they may be method components
R-prior: Evan reads one or more as hand-set game shaping, so they stay diagnostics and Stage 3 needs learned or more generic alternatives
design: Ask Evan three questions with the numbers from C23 and C30: (1) May the draft head's incoming draw start from a kind-aware base measure (same card type as the outgoing card with probability 0.8, type-balanced otherwise; Pokemon/Trainer/Energy here, land/creature/instant ... in MTG) instead of uniform over card identities, given that the pool is 81% Pokemon and a uniform head pulls decks toward the pool's composition? Every card can still change, drawn at random, as he asked on 10-12. (2) May Stage 3 train the pilot on random legal decks with the plain result until games mostly end by the game's own win condition before drafting starts (#124 remedy a, his plan's order)? (3) For initial and turnover decks, keep wide_deck (Pokemon lines and matching Energy, read from rules fields) or require the flat random_deck (a random split over card types) that carries to MTG unchanged? The commit go-ahead for the work since #127 is asked as C33 D7.

predictions.predicted: (1)-(3) yes: C41's kind-aware warm-pilot cells are method candidates, and a holding flat (or wide) cell starts the Stage 3 headline run directly

(1) no: kind-aware cells stay diagnostics and C41's pilot-feature base measure (or uniform over clusters of W's card embeddings, about a day of code) carries the Stage 3 method; (3) no: W retrains on flat decks (about 1 h) and the wide cells become diagnostics

readout: Evan's answers recorded in notes/evan-requests.md and as rule-status fields in C04's recipe registry.
noise_and_power: Not applicable (a decision); the evidence offered is C23's rho and C30's time to criterion.
kill_rule: If no answer within a day, run C41 as a diagnostic with the game-agnostic base-measure level, so Stage 3 does not wait on the ruling.
cost: About 10 min of Evan's time; no compute.
distinct_from: #51 and the 10-09 rule settled 'no human lists or bots in training' and ruled out the deck-out-0 reward; #124 asked to raise the bootstrap with Evan, and README Next item 4 still lists 'a general bootstrap for a pilot from scratch' as open with him; no ruling exists on kind-aware proposals or the deck generator.
rules_check: This is the rules question itself: it protects rule 1 (self-discovery) and rule 2 (game-agnostic) before Stage 3 spends compute, and keeps rule 4 by putting his plan's own bootstrap order first.
value: Unblocks Stage 3's design (which components may enter the method, and whether the wide generator survives the move to MTG).
merged_from: scratch: Evan's ruling on the Stage 3 bootstrap components and on committing the screen-era work (questions 1-3; question 4 is C33 D7)

reviews.reasons: No earlier review exists for C40. It is a rules ruling with no compute, and no earlier ruling covers any of its three questions. notes/evan-requests.md has the 10-06 ruling (no card-specific moves), the 10-09 ruling (#51: no human lists or bots in training, deck-out-0 ruled out) and the 10-12 ruling (every card may change, drawn at random). None of them says anything about a non-uniform base measure over card types, a pilot-first warm-up criterion, or which start-deck generator to use. #124's Next said 'Raise with Evan' about remedies (a) and (b), and README Next item 4 still lists 'With Evan: a general bootstrap for a pilot from scratch' as open. No row in evan-requests records an answer, so the question was never asked or never answered. In the ledger, H27 lists 'kind-stratified proposals' as untested and H45 lists 'pilot first on wide random decks with the plain result' as untested. C40 is the rules gate in front of both, not a rerun. wide_deck dates from #42 (10-06, before the 10-09 rule). Its standing as a method component was never ruled on: the 10-09 ruling removed pilot-v2's deck-out-0 reward, not its deck generator. C40 is also distinct from C33, which covers game specification D1-D6/D8 plus D7, the commit, and C40 leaves the commit to C33 D7. It reruns nothing and touches no do-not-repeat list. What makes it distinct: node N9/N6 at the level of rule status, a factor (rule status of the base measure, the warm-up criterion and the generator) that was never put to Evan. One efficiency note, not a repetition problem: send C40 and C33 to Evan as one message so he rules on the bootstrap and the game specification together.

For a decision, the readout (Evan's answers per question) is the right one: each answer sends Stage 3 down a different path (kind-aware cells as method or as diagnostics; W on wide or flat decks; C41's Nf level needed or not). Noise and power do not apply, and the one-day fallback stops Stage 3 from stalling. The weakness is how the evidence is presented: three questions are framed so they could bias the ruling, and his ruling is only as good as what he is shown. (1) Q3 calls wide_deck 'Pokemon lines and matching Energy, read from rules fields'. The rules fields are real, but the generator also has hand-set constants: Energy uniform over 8-34, 1-4 lines, a Stage 1 60% and a Stage 2 50% of the time, 75% of Energy matching the lines' types. Its 300-deck median is 8 Pokemon / 29 Trainers / 20+2 Energy (log #127), close to the human 13.5/28/18 on Trainers and Energy. That is a possible back door for a deck-shape prior, and Evan has to see it to rule. The flat random_deck is a Dirichlet(1,1,1) split, mean about 20/20/20, with one forced Basic. (2) Q2's criterion is called 'the game's own win condition', but deck-out is one of the game's own win conditions. Counting >=70% Prize or no-Pokemon endings and <=25% deck-outs as success is a game-specific judgment close to the deck-out-0 distinction ruled out on 10-09. The question should say so and offer a game-agnostic form, such as a positive end-score (Prize) margin, which rule 2 names. (3) Q1's 0.8 / type-balanced constants are hand-set. The 0.2 type-balanced share is also not composition-neutral: per swap the drift is 0.2*(1/3 - n_k/60), so about -0.16 Trainers and +0.13 Pokemon per 6-swap draw from the human median, with a fixed point at 20/20/20 under neutral selection. That is small against a uniform draw's +5.6 Pokemon, but it should be disclosed (C41's 'unchanged in expectation' is wrong for this component). It also has to say whether 'type' means the three supertypes or splits basic from special Energy. (4) The design cites 'numbers from C23 and C30', and neither has run. Either ask now with the evidence that exists (#124: a uniform draw is 81% Pokemon and 2% basic Energy; #63: 29.0 Pokemon; #71: deck-outs 92% -> 7% by it24; H27's entropy U-shape) and send the C23/C30 numbers later, or the one-day fallback fires before the evidence exists. (5) The two rivals are all-yes or no on (1) and (3). Partial answers are likely, such as 'allowed if the constants are learned or derived from the pool'. Pre-register the action for each answer to each question, including a conditional yes.
required_changes: Show Evan wide_deck's hand-set constants (Energy U[8,34], 1-4 lines, Stage 1 60%, Stage 2 50%, 75% matching Energy) and its median start of 8/29/20+2 beside the human 13.5/28/18 and random_deck's Dirichlet mean of about 20/20/20, so he can judge whether the generator carries a shape prior.

Rewrite Q2's criterion: deck-out is one of the game's own win conditions, so say that the 70% Prizes/no-Pokemon rule singles out some endings as the real ones, and offer a game-agnostic alternative (e.g. a share of games won with a positive end-score margin, or a fixed lead over a random-init pilot) for him to choose between.

In Q1, state that the 0.8/0.2 constants are hand-set, that the type-balanced share drifts composition toward equal thirds (about -0.16 Trainers and +0.13 Pokemon per 6-swap draw from the human median), and which type partition is meant.
Ask now with the evidence already in the log (#63, #71, #124, H27) instead of waiting for C23/C30, or line them up so the one-day fallback cannot fire before those numbers exist.
Pre-register the Stage 3 action for each answer to each question, including conditional yeses (e.g. 'yes if constants are learned/derived'), not only all-yes or no.
