title: Proposal base measure from scratch: a factorial of base measure (uniform, kind-aware, pilot-feature similarity) x pilot start (random vs W) x start decks (wide vs flat)
rivals: R1 arrival (H27): exploration flattens toward uniform over card identities (fresh and reset heads, the floor, the entropy bonus) from a pool where 225 of 277 cards are Pokemon; one uniform-head draw adds +5.6 to +6.1 Pokemon and on collapsed ctl479 heads the 3-nat floor adds +0.7 to +1.0 a draw; with selection at the null rate, scr-scratch's drift (median Pokemon 12 -> 27.5 in 5 iterations, about 70% of decks moving) matches proposals alone; a composition-neutral base measure stops it
R2 bootstrap (H45): without an attacking pilot, results pay deck-out piles; a warm pilot alone stops it
R1xR2: both are needed; only neutral, warm-pilot cells hold
R3 results-driven: selection adds Pokemon early under any pilot; neither fix holds composition
R-generator: neutral cells only keep the near-human composition wide decks start with (Energy 8-34, 1-4 lines) and do not find it from flat starts
design: rl/draft.py: a fixed offset b0 = log q0(c | j) on the head's incoming logits over legal cards c for the cut card j, so a fresh or reset head proposes q0, not uniform; the floor tempers toward q0 (softmax(b0 + (x - b0)/T)); --draft-ent becomes -KL(pi || q0); log-probs stay exact (rl.tests). Factor A: U uniform (now); Nk kind-aware (same type as the outgoing card w.p. 0.8, type-balanced w.p. 0.2; neutral selection leaves composition unchanged in expectation); Nf like-for-like q0(c | j) proportional to exp(cos(f_c, f_j)/tau) over the pilot's own card features (card plus text embedding), tau set once so q0's mean entropy is 3 nats, no type labels. Offline first, with scratchpad meta_lens/op_audit.py (seconds): Nk- and Nf-flattened and fresh-head draws change Pokemon by at most +/-0.5 a draw on the 479 decks. Factor B: R random init vs W (C30). Factor C: wide (--init-wide --turnover-wide) vs flat (rl/decks.py random_deck for init and turnover). Base: scr-scratch's scale (50 decks, 1,000 games, 300 recorded, 32k PPO transitions, about 3.8 min an iteration), adopted main_args plus --select --candidates 3 --draft-h-in-floor 3 --draft-group-p 0.3 --protect 20, deck_mode cross, gamma 1, count features off, --practice-games 0 (wide practice decks would leak into flat cells). Cells: Nk.R.wide; Nf.R.wide on scr-scratch's exact recipe (gamma 0.995, 150 practice games, seed 2) so scr-scratch is its control; U.W.wide; Nk.W.wide (two seeds); U.W.flat; Nk.W.flat; an anchor Nk.frozen-pilot-v2 on scr-v2's exact configuration, read against scr-v2; Nf.W cells if Evan rules out kind labels (C40); Nf on the seeded human field under frozen pilot-v2 runs as C31's arm Fq. U.R.wide is not rerun (H45/H46 do-not-repeat): scr-scratch and 016 stand in. 10 iterations a cell (Nf.R.wide 8, as scr-scratch); cells holding composition at 10 extend to 30. Launch the anchor and the R cells while W trains.

predictions.predicted: U cells gain >= +10 median Pokemon by iteration 10 from either start (scr-v2 gained 14 in 6 under an attacking pilot); neutral cells and the anchor stay within +/-3 of their starting medians with |acc - prop| <= 0.3 a move; Nf.R.wide rises <= 4 over 0-5 (control +15.5) and <= 6 by 8, with prop's Pokemon within +/-0.5 a draw (control about +6) and deck-outs < 70% (control 61% -> 87%); Nk.R.wide's deck-outs fall >= 20 points from peak by 30 as its pilot learns

Nk.R.wide reaches >= 80% deck-outs and <= 5% prize endings by iteration 6 and stays there to 30; every W cell keeps >= 50% prize or no-Pokemon endings, and U.W.wide holds composition (acc - prop Pokemon <= -0.5 a move)
only neutral W cells hold composition with >= 50% prize/no-Pokemon endings at 10 and 30; neutral R cells hold composition but stay >= 70% deck-outs at 30; U.W cells drift like scr-v2
acc - prop Pokemon >= +0.5 a move in every cell; neutral cells gain >= +5 Pokemon beyond their null by 10; Nf.R.wide still rises >= 8 by iteration 5

Nk.W.wide holds near its 13/25/20 start but Nk.W.flat's distance to 13.5/28/18 falls < 3 cards by 30 with acc - prop Trainers <= +0.1 a move (success instead: a fall of >= 6 cards through accepted moves, acc - prop Trainers >= +0.3, with >= 50% prize endings)

readout: Per iteration: median and quartiles of Pokemon/Trainers/Energy; endings (prizes, no Pokemon, deck-out, cap); acc and prop per kind; h_in/h_out; moves; the audit's incoming and outgoing kind shares. At 10 and 30: deck types (deck_kinds, matchup-matrix effective rank), evaluation-only distance to 13.5/28/18, and the cell pilot's walls verdict. A effect from neutral vs U at fixed pilot and start; B from R vs W on wide; C from wide vs flat; replicate spread from the two Nk.W.wide seeds.
noise_and_power: From-scratch drifts are large (+2 to +3 Pokemon an iteration in scr-v2 and scr-scratch; scr-scratch's +15.5 in 5 iterations is about 10x the per-component A/A RMS of 1.3). A 50-deck median has SE about 1 card and ending shares about 1.5% at 1,000 games, so +/-3 vs >= +10 is 4+ SE at 10 iterations; prop's composition comes from about 150 draws an iteration (SE 0.15-0.2 cards); acc - prop per kind SE about 0.15 a move an iteration, 0.05 pooled over 10. The from-scratch A/A is unknown: the two Nk.W.wide seeds estimate it and every band is >= 2x the 479 shape A/A RMS (2.6). A fraction of the full factorial (no U.R or R.flat), so A x B is read on wide decks only.
kill_rule: Never before iteration 4. Stop a cell when median Pokemon >= 35 or deck-outs >= 90% for 2 consecutive iterations (the collapse is its outcome); stop Nf.R.wide at 4 if median Pokemon rose > 8 (R3). Extensions stop if the largest type exceeds half the population at two checkpoints, median Energy >= 26, or deck-outs >= 60% for 3 iterations.
cost: About half a day of code (q0 per view for Nk and Nf, the prior, tempering, the KL term, exactness tests); the offline check takes seconds. About 7 cells x 10 iterations x 3.8 min = about 4.5 slot-hours plus the frozen anchor (about 0.4 h): about 2 h wall-clock in 3 slots after W; each 20-iteration extension about 1.3 slot-hours.
distinct_from: The critic's top-untested 2x2, H27's untested 'kind-stratified proposals' and H45's 'pilot first on wide decks'. H27 observed the bias and never acted; H31/H32 (entropy bonus, floor) varied the amount of flattening, never its target; H34 resets restart a near-uniform drift. U.R.wide is deliberately not rerun (H45/H46 do-not-repeat: joint from-scratch pilot and drafting under the near-uniform draw, the recipe from scratch, scr-scratch's config); scr-v2 (H20 do-not-repeat) is reused as the U anchor. Generators idea 1 proposed a one-factor neutral screen; this crosses the target of flattening with the bootstrap (#124 named both pulls, never separated) and the start generator, which no run has varied.
rules_check: Card types are a field every card game gives, and Nf uses only the pilot's card features (no type labels enter the change, only the readout); q0 is neutral about which card is better, every card can still change in a draw at random (Evan, 10-12), and the head learns on top of it; no human data. Nf's features include the frozen MiniLM text embedding, a language prior the pilot already reads (S29): flag it to Evan. W is plain-result; the pilot-v2 anchor is diagnosis only. Whether Nk and the wide generator may enter the method is Evan's ruling (C40); until then those cells are diagnostics.
value: Chooses the Stage 3 bootstrap: whether a neutral base measure, the pilot-first warm-up or both are necessary and sufficient to stop the from-scratch collapse (F5), and whether success depends on the wide generator. R1: a cheap fix and a precondition for from-scratch rediscovery and for every diversity method that pushes the head toward 'undecided'. A holding Nk.W.flat (or Nf.W) cell starts the Stage 3 headline run; R3 moves the problem to the pilot, judge and game definition before any Stage 3 compute.
merged_from: meta: Composition-neutral exploration: flatten toward a like-for-like base measure built from the pilot's card features, tested where arrival bias dominates; scratch: From-scratch factorial: proposal base measure (uniform over cards vs kind-aware) x pilot start (random vs W), with a flat-deck contrast

reviews.reasons: I read the full ledger digest and grepped the progress log for kind-balanced, kind-stratified, kind-aware, base measure, type-balanced, stratif, log base rate and like-for-like. Nothing matches, so no proposal base measure other than uniform over card identities has ever been built. Why C41 is distinct: (1) Node N6, mechanism the target of flattening. H31 and H32 varied how much the draw is flattened (entropy bonus x5/x10, floors of 2 and 3 nats). H34 resets only restart the uniform drift. None of them changed the reference distribution. This is H27's listed untested 'kind-stratified proposals' and H31's verifier variant (3), 'entropy toward a non-uniform reference / a prior balanced over card features'. The ledger critic notes H27's drift was 're-observed' in 6 runs because this control was never built. (2) Node N9, pilot start. A learning plain-result warm-up pilot W (C30) is H45's untested 'pilot first on wide random decks with the plain result'. No from-scratch drafting run started from such a pilot: scr-v2 used frozen pilot-v2, which pays deck-out wins 0. (3) Start generator, flat vs wide, never varied in any from-scratch run. The cells that come close to do-not-repeat configurations each differ by a factor never varied. Nf.R.wide is scr-scratch's config (H46/H53 do-not-repeat) with only the base measure changed. The anchor is scr-v2's config (H20/H45 do-not-repeat) with only the base measure changed. U.W.wide's pilot is not pilot-v2. The candidate correctly drops U.R.wide (H45/H46 do-not-repeat: joint from-scratch under the near-uniform draw) and reuses scr-scratch and scr-v2 as historical U controls. The design is the critic's top-untested 'from-scratch 2x2' (ledger_meta top_untested), extended. There are no earlier reviews to keep.

Strengths: the factorial gives the rivals clearly different predictions. R1 predicts U cells gain at least +10 Pokemon while neutral cells stay within +/-3. R2 predicts W cells hold composition and Nk.R.wide stays at 80% or more deck-outs. R3 predicts acc - prop of +0.5 a move or more everywhere. R-generator predicts flat cells do not converge. The readout matches the nodes: the acc vs prop per-kind decomposition (already logged at rl/metagame.py:724) separates proposal drift from selection, which suits an N6 operator change, and endings serve the N9 bootstrap. Effect sizes (+10 to +15 vs +/-3, 50-deck median SE about 1) clear the A/A band. Two Nk.W.wide seeds estimate the from-scratch A/A. Four concrete problems remain. (a) The kill rule has short-horizon bias against the R cells. A random-init pilot starts near 90% deck-outs even on fixed decks: #70/#71 went from 92% to 7% only by iteration 24, and scr-scratch went from 61% to 87% in 5 iterations. So 'deck-outs >= 90% for 2 consecutive iterations' and the extension stop 'deck-outs >= 60% for 3 iterations' will end Nk.R.wide and Nf.R.wide under every rival. Yet the one readout that separates R1 from R1xR2 and R2 on those cells is the deck-out fall by iteration 30. Also, 'extend only cells holding composition' makes reaching 30 conditional, when the prediction requires it. (b) Nk as specified is not composition-neutral. The type-balanced branch (w.p. 0.2, 1/3 per kind) gives a fixed point of 20/20/20. From the human shape (13.5/28/18) it pushes Pokemon up and Trainers down, which is the failure direction itself. That fixed point also equals the mean of flat random_deck (Dirichlet(1,1,1), rl/decks.py:168), which confounds the R-generator test. (c) The offline neutrality bar of +/-0.5 Pokemon a draw is too loose. With 10-15 accepted moves a deck over 30 iterations it allows +/-5-7 cards, more than the +/-3 hold band. (d) Controls. Nk.R.wide (gamma 1, practice 0) has no matched U control: scr-scratch and 016 differ in gamma, practice games, scale and code version. Nf.R.wide's 'exact recipe' historical control ran before code changes since #132, and the count-feature setting is ambiguous, so 'control +15.5 in 5' is not guaranteed reproducible.
required_changes: Exempt the R (random-init) cells from the deck-out kill criteria and from the extension stop on deck-outs. Run both R cells to 30 iterations unconditionally, since R1 vs R1xR2 vs R2 is read there. Keep only the composition kill (median Pokemon >= 35), or calibrate the deck-out kill to #71's curve (e.g. stop only if deck-outs at iteration 20+ exceed #71's matched-iteration value by more than 20 points).

Make Nk exactly neutral. Draw the 0.2 branch's kind in proportion to the deck's current kind shares, not uniformly over kinds, so that expected incoming kind shares equal outgoing ones under the copy-uniform cut. Alternatively, state the 20/20/20 fixed point and its predicted drift per cell.
Tighten the offline audit bar to about +/-0.1 Pokemon (and Trainers) a draw for Nk and about +/-0.15 for Nf, so cumulative null drift stays under about 2 cards over 30 iterations.

Give the R cells a valid control. Either put Nk.R.wide on the same scr-scratch config as Nf.R.wide, or run a short matched U control (about 5 iterations, about 20 min) as a control, not a test. In addition, replay scr-scratch's config for 2 iterations in the current code to confirm it reproduces its initial deck-out share and Pokemon rise, and state the count-feature setting for that cell.

reviews.reasons: Code. Adding an offset b0 = log q0(c|j) to DraftHead's incoming logits fits rl/draft.py. The head is zero-initialised (W, b_in and the out layer), so a fresh head proposes exactly q0. sample() and log_prob() already carry the per-event mask and temperature T, so b0 can be stored on DeckView and reused in log_prob for exact log-probs. The superType field gives the kinds for Nk (rl/decks.py:113). The pilot's card_resid embedding and its card_text projection of text_emb give Nf's features (token_model.py:183-184). --draft-ent (default 0.01, metagame.py:249) feeds beta*(h_out+h_in) in update(), so replacing h_in with -KL(pi||q0) is a few lines. Flat starts are already the default (random_deck when --init-wide and --turnover-wide are absent), as are --gamma, --practice-games, --freeze-pilot and --init-from. Items the half-day estimate omits: floor_temperature must be rewritten to bisect on the tempered form softmax(b0 + (x-b0)/T), not x/T. In R/W learning cells, Nf's q0 changes with the pilot, so it must be recomputed per view and frozen inside it. scratchpad meta_lens/op_audit.py does not exist yet and must be written. Budget: 50-deck, 1,000-game screens fit 3 slots, and the arithmetic (about 4.5 + 0.4 slot-hours) is right. But W cells wait on C30's warm-up (up to 60 rl.train iterations), and the R cells must run to 30 to be read (see diagnosticity), adding about 2.6 slot-hours. That makes about 7-10 slot-hours if a few cells extend, roughly 3-4 h wall-clock after W rather than 2 h. Rules: no human data enters training (the human shape is readout only). Nf uses only the pilot's own features, with the MiniLM text prior (S29) correctly flagged to Evan. Card types exist in MTG. The candidate itself defers whether Nk's hand-set 0.8/0.2 prior and the wide generator may enter the method to Evan's ruling (C40), and treats them as diagnostics until then. That respects the self-discovery and learned-and-simple rules. The pilot-v2 anchor is diagnosis only.
required_changes: Raise the cost line. Code: add rewriting floor_temperature for base-measure tempering, writing op_audit.py, and per-view caching of Nf's q0 under a learning pilot, about 0.75-1 day in all. Machine: make the R cells' 30-iteration runs part of the base budget (about +2.6 slot-hours), and state the C30 dependency for W cells.

title: Best-of-K credit: train the draft head for the selection it serves (winner-only credit, distinct starts)
rivals: H-objective-mismatch: the head is trained on mean results (leave-one-out over a deck's games) while --select keeps only the best of K, so it learns to propose the one best-on-average edit K times; crediting only the winner keeps the K proposals jointly useful and the head undecided (in PKPO, pass@k credit kept entropy where entropy bonuses did not)
H-preference: one edit class is genuinely best for most decks under this judge; winner-only credit collapses as fast or faster, all its weights positive and rewarding lucky winners
design: Gated on C24: run only if the collapse is signal-driven, not drift. In rl/metagame.py step 4 with --select --candidates 3 and no gate (scr-ctl479's recipe, the only one with K > 1): the winner among {incumbent, 3 candidates} gets advantage (s_win - s_second) / SE of that difference, capped at 3, on its games; every other draw gets 0 (Poppy's theorem 1; PKPO's k=2 estimator a second arm if a slot is free). The 3 candidates' first outgoing cards are drawn without replacement (Gumbel-top-k), that first choice left out of the log-prob (POMO's distinct starts). Fork 479, --reseed 2, 20 iterations; control scr-ctl479 (same fork and reseed). Before the screen, C24's bench checks that winner-only credit does not collapse faster than mean credit under null rewards.

predictions.predicted: h_in >= 2.0 at 492 and >= 1.5 at 499 (control 1.25 and 0.50); the best deck's top_in share <= 0.5 in most of 492-499 (control above 0.5 in 6 of 8); the share of triples sharing their first incoming card below the 0.27 measured now; the copy-weighted wall cluster <= 70 decks at 499 (control 80); mean gain of accepted moves at least the control's
h_in <= 1.0 by 494, like the control (0.97) or lower; wall cluster >= 75 at 499; prop's composition within 0.3 cards a draw of the control's

readout: N6: h_in; top_in share and its rotation; candidate uniqueness (how often a deck's three candidates share their first incoming card: 0.27 at 479, 489 and 499 under the current sampler, scratchpad meta_lens/dup.py); prop's composition; the wall cluster as a secondary N7 readout.
noise_and_power: A/A RMS of h_in between scr-ctl479 and scr-resetcap over 480-499 is 0.38; the predicted gap at 499 (>= 1.0 nat) is >= 2.5x that. Cluster sizes in the A/A pair differed by 2-14, so the type readout is secondary. One run against the logged control.
kill_rule: Stop if h_in is below the control's at the same iteration for 3 consecutive iterations, or the wall cluster reaches 75 decks by 494.
cost: 2-4 h of code (winner credit, Gumbel-top-k first cuts, log-prob exclusion, tests); one slot for about 2 h, or 12 iterations (about 1.2 h) if the head readout is already decided. C32 can pre-screen it in seconds.
distinct_from: H30-H34 (entropy bonus, floor, lr, reset) and H37/H38 (leagues, exploiters) never changed the head's objective, mean results against a leave-one-out baseline since #67; the gate (#138) changed acceptance, not credit; generators idea 3 (fact-checked: keep) was never built. No do-not-repeat item rerun.
rules_check: Results-only credit for the one learned head; game-agnostic (only the candidates' results); no human data.
value: Decides whether the collapse is an objective mismatch fixable in place (adopt: same games, same head, rule 3 kept) or the judge's preference (the head's objective is not the lever). If it works, the next arm is winner-takes-all credit over Evan's 3 heads (Poppy's population, every head proposing for every deck).
merged_from: meta: Best-of-K credit: train the draft head for the selection it serves (winner-only credit, distinct starts)

reviews.reasons: I read the ledger digest in full and grepped progress-log.md for winner, Poppy, PKPO, pass@k, Gumbel-top, without replacement, distinct start, POMO, best-of-K and leave-one-out. The head's credit rule has never been varied. rl/metagame.py:660 has applied rloo(z + margin*m) over all of a deck's games (incumbent and candidates, mean credit against a leave-one-out baseline) since #67. The seasons of #93 used the same baseline. Candidates have always been drawn i.i.d. by repeated Drafter.sample calls (metagame.py:492). The only log hit for 'without replacement' (line 792) is about the old value-search builder, not the head. The overlapping families all changed something else. H30-H34 changed entropy bonus, floor, lr and reset. H24, H25 and H26 changed acceptance (select, z-gate), not credit. H37 and H38 (leagues, exploiters) changed head count and reward targets. The research index lists this idea as unbuilt (generators, kept). None of the do-not-repeat items is rerun: the fork and recipe are scr-ctl479's, but scr-ctl479 sits only as the control, and the changed factor is new. Distinct in mechanism (credit and objective of N6) and in a never-varied factor (draft credit assignment, plus correlated proposal sampling). Small overlaps: C24's bench and C32 already plan winner-only credit as an offline check. That is a staged pre-screen of the same idea, not a repeat. The sibling idea 'gap baseline: credit each edit against its incumbent' is close in mechanism (both drop the mean-of-others baseline) and should be cross-referenced, so the two are not later run as separate novelties.

The node and readout match: an N6 change read by h_in, top_in share and proposal composition, with the wall cluster as a secondary N7 readout. The predictions are written per rival and differ on h_in (>= 2.0 at 492 vs <= 1.0 by 494). I checked the control trajectory in runs/screens/scr-ctl479/log.jsonl: 2.745 at 480, 1.25 at 492, 0.97 at 494, 0.50 at 499, about 74 of 99 decks moved each iteration. A predicted 1-nat gap is about 2.6x the A/A RMS of 0.38. Four problems remain. (1) A live third rival predicts the same outcome as H-objective-mismatch. Winner-only credit discards most of the signal. Only one draw per deck gets credit; no deck gets any when the incumbent wins, which happens for about 25% of decks at ctl479's move rate. Credit falls on the noise-max of 10-game means, and ungated selection moves at the null rate (H24). The head may simply learn less per step: an effective-step-size or dilution effect, like H33's lr, which was never powered. That rival also predicts h_in staying high and the wall cluster unchanged. Nothing in the readout separates 'the K proposals stay jointly useful' from 'the head learns slower'. Accepted-move gain under ungated selection is mostly winner's-curse noise, so it does not separate them either. (2) Two factors change at once: winner-only credit, and Gumbel-top-k distinct first cuts with the first choice removed from the log-prob. The candidate-uniqueness readout (triples sharing their first incoming card, 0.27 now) is pushed directly by the new sampler: distinct outgoing rows. A drop there cannot be credited to the objective hypothesis. (3) The kill rule ('h_in below the control's for 3 consecutive iterations') is uncalibrated. Both arms start at 2.745 and the A/A RMS is 0.38, so three consecutive small deficits early on are likely under noise, and the rule could kill a true positive. (4) It is one reseed, with no decision rule for the zone between the two predictions (h_in 1.0-2.0 at 492). There is also no A/A for 'prop's composition within 0.3 cards a draw'.
required_changes: Add a sparsity- and information-matched control so that 'objective mismatch' can be told apart from 'less signal, slower head'. Use a random-one credit arm: credit one uniformly chosen candidate per deck with the same capped magnitude distribution, zero when the incumbent would have won. Run it at least on C24's bench under null and planted (delta*) rewards beside winner-only and mean credit. If a slot is free, also run it in the loop. H-objective-mismatch then predicts winner-only > random-one on h_in under planted signal; dilution predicts winner-only = random-one.

Separate the two factors. Make the primary in-loop arm winner-only credit with the current i.i.d. sampler, or run the 2x2 (credit x distinct starts) on the bench first. Do not count the first-incoming-card uniqueness readout as evidence for the credit hypothesis in any arm that uses Gumbel-top-k first cuts.

Recalibrate the kill rule to the noise band. Kill only if h_in is below the control's by more than the A/A RMS (0.4 nats) for 3 consecutive iterations, and not before about 486. Keep the wall-cluster >= 75 by 494 condition.

Pre-register the decision for the ambiguous zone. Adopt or advance only if the h_in gap over the control exceeds 2x the A/A RMS at both 492 and 499 and the wall cluster is <= 70 at 499. If h_in at 492 falls in 1.0-2.0, run a second reseed before reading the result. Give an A/A spread for prop composition (ctl479 vs resetcap at 480-499) before using the 0.3-card bar.

Also log the best decks' Energy, Trainer and Pokemon counts and their distance to the human medians as a secondary ground-truth readout. Under Evan's ground truth, a head that stays undecided but keeps adding Energy is not progress.

reviews.reasons: The code supports this at about the stated cost. Step 4 (rl/metagame.py:654-669) builds each deck's advantage with rloo over per-game z. Replacing it is local. The incumbent is in held as an empty-ev pseudo-sample (line 491), and its zero log-prob already gives no gradient. The cand tallies needed for s_win, s_second and the binomial SE already exist (draws[g,a]['sum'/'n'] and pick()'s pb formula at lines 690-695). With about 80% zeros, the few nonzero entries become large, but they are bounded because the cap of 3 is applied before scaling, and Adam normalizes, so no instability is expected. title: Wall-free island: Evan's league of 3 heads with local judging, testing whether the wall attractor is absolute or depends on the field
rivals: H-absolute-attractor: under the current judge the wall plan is what local edits reach from any start; a non-wall island re-forms walls even with no wall opponents, no wall migrants and its own head (in scr-t60gate479 no deck ever left the wall cluster; by 498, 11 of 25 non-walls of 479 and 8 wide entrants joined it through accepted moves; wall #829 beats all 24 lists under this pilot)

H-field-dependent: the walls win because of the field they meet (wall mirrors reward Energy Removal, healing Energy, extra Energy) and spread by competition and by turnover mutants of the best quarter (8 of 16 decks entering the wall cluster as new ids by 498); isolated, a non-wall island keeps its own archetypes
design: Fork runs/screens/scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt, --reseed 2, scr-t60gate479's flags (gate, greedy judge, 60-turn draws, 250 practice, turnover every 5, protect 20), plus --draft-heads 3 --draft-heads-init copy (Evan's league, each head a copy of the 479 head). New: islands from the copy-weighted descriptor at the fork: W1 37 walls, W2 37 walls, C the 25 non-walls plus 8 ten-card mutants of C's best (33). Each island owned by one head; judged games paired within the island; turnover within each island (mutants from its best quarter, wide entrants), no type cap; one best deck swapped between W1 and W2 every 10 iterations, nothing into or out of C; recorded PPO and practice games stay global so the shared pilot sees every type (#137). 20 iterations (480-499). Optional second arm: a 9x11 torus with the non-walls seeded as one contiguous block, 90% of judged games in the 8-neighbourhood and local turnover, read as front speed and reversals.

predictions.predicted: island C's decks with overlap >= 0.5 to the 479 wall centroid rise from 0 to >= 13 of 33 by 499 and C's mean overlap from 0.36 to >= 0.48; C's head's top_in includes the wall core cards by 489; on the torus a wall front advances >= 1 site an iteration with no reversals
C holds <= 3 such decks through 499, mean overlap <= 0.40, and >= 2 clusters of 8+ decks with their own cores (mutual overlap < 0.35); the torus front stalls or reverses

readout: Island C's wall-cluster count and mean overlap with the wall centroid; C's clusters and cores; C's head's top_in and top_out; conversion by accepted moves vs replacement (lineages). Evaluation only: C's 3 best decks vs the 24 lists under pilot-v2 and the run's pilot at 499.
noise_and_power: Global-mixing reference, scr-t60gate479 by 498: 11 of 25 non-walls converted, 16 new ids joined the wall cluster (8 converted wide entrants, 8 mutants), 3 non-walls left. The predictions (>= 13 vs <= 3 of 33) are about 3.5 binomial SDs apart; the overlap bands (>= 0.48 vs <= 0.40) lie outside the control's whole 479-498 range (0.32-0.39). One run decides unless C ends with 5-10 wall-cluster decks.
kill_rule: Stop at 489 if C already holds >= 13 wall-cluster decks (H-absolute decided); stop the torus arm at 494 if walls hold >= 85 sites with no reversal since 484.
cost: About 0.5-1 day of code (descriptor assignment, within-island pairing and turnover, migration; head ownership uses the existing --draft-heads plumbing); one slot for about 2 h, the torus arm another 2 h. C32 can pre-screen islands and the torus.
distinct_from: H37 (a league of heads sharing one pilot, fresh or copied) paired decks at random across the population; H38 scored heads against head 0; H39's cap acts globally. H37's do-not-repeat bars 'any league variant judged by a pilot from the population without changing the judge': this keeps the judge but changes whom decks are judged against, the factor the rivals differ on and the critic's gap ('no current-loop family varies the opponent mix'). No spatial, torus or island matchmaking in the log. Completes Evan's league (row 12, approved 2026-10-20) in its untested form.
rules_check: Human-free and game-agnostic: the descriptor counts copies of copy-limited cards (nonbasic cards in MTG); Evan's own league structure with one shared pilot and heads learned on results.
value: Decides whether population structure can protect non-wall types under the current judge: H-field-dependent makes islands, a torus or the hard cap (C44) worth adopting now, in parallel with judge work; H-absolute-attractor predicts every structure-based diversity mechanism null under J1, as C27 expects, so N7 screens wait for a judge that passes fidelity. Either way Evan's league gets its first fair test.
merged_from: meta: Wall-free island: Evan's league of 3 heads with local judging, testing whether the wall attractor is absolute or depends on the field

reviews.reasons: No earlier reviews to keep. Overlapping families: H37 (league of draft heads sharing one pilot), H38 (exploiters), H39 (type cap), H40 (turnover), H41 (novelty; NSLC local competition listed untested), H36 (deck-owning agents). All H37 tests (017-meta-league3 fresh/copy from 400/440, scr-league479) paired decks at random across the whole population ('all decks still play one another at random', rl/metagame.py lines 45-50), so the opponent mix -- who a deck is judged against (within-island pairing, no migration into C) and descriptor-based head ownership instead of round-robin assign_heads -- is a never-varied factor, matching the completeness critic's gap 'No current-loop family varies the opponent mix'. Grep of progress-log.md for island/torus/spatial/neighbourhood/migration/deme finds nothing (only the card 'Island Cave'). H37's do-not-repeat 'any league variant judged by a pilot from the population without changing the judge' targets leagues expected to fix the walls under the same judge; this is a crucial experiment on whether the attraction is field-dependent, which that ban does not cover. Per-head turnover (H40 do-not-repeat: 017) is reused only as plumbing. Distinct in: node N7 opponent structure; mechanism isolation/local competition; never-varied factor island-restricted judged pairing. Caveat on information value, not distinctness: the main line formed walls from a non-wall field by 160 (H44 DATA) under an earlier pilot, which is prior support for H-absolute; the candidate should cite it and explain what the current-judge version adds.
required_changes: Cite the main line's emergence of walls from a non-wall field by 160 (H44 DATA) as prior evidence for H-absolute-attractor and state that this test differs by using the current pilot and the present non-wall types with no wall opponents.

reviews.reasons: The node and readout match: an N7/N6 population-structure change read by deck readouts (C's wall-cluster count, overlap, clusters, lineages), with human lists used only for evaluation. The two rivals predict clearly different outcomes (>=13 vs <=3 of 33; mean overlap >=0.48 vs <=0.40), and the kill rule at 489 stops only on an early decisive H-absolute result, so it does not bias against slow effects. Five weaknesses remain. (1) A third live explanation predicts the H-absolute outcome: proposal drift. C's head is a copy of the collapsed 479 head, whose incoming choice concentrates on wall cards (0.1-0.3 nats). Under --select-z 1.0 at about 10 games a candidate, noise-accepted moves (H24/H25) can push C toward wall cards with no real judge preference. A rise in overlap therefore does not by itself show the attractor is in the judge. The select stats already log acc and prop: the readout needs the overlap change to the wall core for accepted moves minus proposed moves in C, or a C arm with a reset head. (2) The descriptor can be fooled by staples. Whole-list overlap (rl/decks.py overlap) puts Haymaker against Wigglytuff at a median 0.54 (pokemon_overlap docstring), so a C deck can pass 0.5 overlap with the wall centroid just by adding Oak, Bill, Gambler, Energy Removal and Energy, without Chansey or Snorlax. 'Wall-cluster' needs a core-based definition (Chansey+Snorlax presence, or pokemon_overlap to the wall core) reported next to the copy-weighted overlap. (3) The power claim treats conversions as independent binomial draws. Turnover mutants come from C's best quarter, so one converted top deck spawns converted mutants: counts cluster by lineage and are overdispersed. The 3.5 SD separation is overstated, and there is no A/A of this count. Count conversions by lineage (accepted moves vs mutant descent) and treat 5-10 as undecided. (4) Short horizon: H-field-dependent's '<=3 at 499' could just mean slower conversion, since a wall-free field may give smaller per-move gains. Add a pre-stated extension to 509 if C ends at 4-10, and compare C's overlap slope per iteration with the control's accepted-move slope. (5) The control baseline (0.32-0.39) must use exactly the same measure: mean over all current members descended from the 25 non-walls plus entrants, not the surviving non-walls, whose mean stays low because converts leave the set. The torus arm's front-speed readout has no noise reference.
required_changes: Add a proposal-drift control: report the overlap change (to the wall core) of accepted minus proposed moves in island C every counted iteration, using the existing acc/prop logging, and/or run C with a reset head. Attribute conversion to the judge only if accepted moves exceed proposed ones.

Define wall-cluster membership by core cards (Chansey+Snorlax presence, or pokemon_overlap to the wall core), not whole-list or copy-weighted overlap alone, because shared staples put distinct human archetypes at 0.54 overlap.
Replace the binomial power claim with lineage-level counting (conversion by accepted moves vs mutant descent) and state that 5-10 converted decks is undecided.
Pre-register an extension to 509 if C ends at 4-10 converted decks, and compare C's per-iteration overlap slope with the control's accepted-move slope.
Recompute the control's 0.32-0.39 band with exactly the same membership definition used for C.

reviews.reasons: Rules: no violation. The islands use only card counts; human lists are evaluation-only; one shared pilot is kept, and Evan's league is the base (evan-requests row 12, approved 2026-10-20). Hand-placing islands around a wall centroid is acceptable as a diagnostic. If islands are adopted as a method, the niches must be formed by a learned or automatic rule, not a hand-chosen wall label. Code: the --draft-heads plumbing, per-head ownership, per-head REINFORCE batches and per-head turnover with mutants from the head's own best quarter all exist (rl/metagame.py about 430-445, 650-700, 750-775), and rl/decks.py overlap exists. New work: (a) island assignment replacing assign_heads' round-robin, plus a core descriptor; (b) restructured pairing. Pairs are drawn first (rng.choice(D,2)) and only then is rec chosen per game, so keeping recorded games global while judged games stay within islands means drawing the two kinds separately. Judged games must be allocated in proportion to island size, and the field sample for views (line 483) should become island-local. (c) Migration between W1 and W2 every 10 iterations. (d) Seeding 8 ten-card mutants of C's best (random_changes exists). (e) Logging of per-island overlap, clusters and lineages. That is plausibly 0.5-1 day for the island arm. The torus arm (9x11 grid, neighbourhood pairing, local turnover, front tracking) is about another half day not counted in the cost. Arithmetic error: W1 37 + W2 37 + C 33 = 107, not 99. The 8 mutants must replace 8 walls, so 33/33/33. Dropping --type-cap 0.5 changes one flag against the scr-t60gate479 control; that is fine but should be stated. Machine: one screen slot (~2.7 GB RAM, ~3.5 GB GPU), 20 iterations of ~6 min, about 2 h, within the 3-screen budget; the torus arm is a second slot. Fork files exist (runs/screens/scr-resetcap/population_it0479.pt; scr-t60gate479 snapshots to 494 plus the checkpoint).
required_changes: Fix the island sizes: 37+37+33 = 107 decks. With the 8 C mutants replacing 8 walls, use 33/33/33 (or state which decks are dropped).

Specify that judged games are allocated to islands in proportion to their size and that the draft head's field sample (views) is drawn within the island, while recorded PPO and practice games are drawn globally. This requires separating the judged and recorded pairing loops.
Raise the cost to about 1-1.5 days if the torus arm is included, or drop the torus arm from this candidate.
State that --type-cap is removed relative to the scr-t60gate479 control.
If adopted beyond diagnosis, replace the hand-labelled wall-centroid assignment with an automatic or learned niche rule, to keep the meta level learned and game-agnostic.

title: Hard selection-time type cap on a descriptor that sees the walls: label or substance?
rivals: H-leak: the built cap failed because it was soft and blind: it removed at most 15 decks every 5 iterations against an excess of 23-44 and spared young decks, and its descriptor (Pokemon-name overlap) splits walls into small types (largest 19 at 479, while copy-weighted overlap on copy-limited cards puts 73 decks in one cluster; 41 vs 68 at t60gate 498; 59 vs 80 at ctl 499; scratchpad meta_lens/descriptor.py); a hard cap at selection keeps >= 2 other clusters with their own cores

H-convergent: the shared head and the judge pull every deck toward the wall plan; a hard cap holds the label but not the substance (non-walls crowd under the boundary and pick up the wall core: walls-lite)
design: Gated on C43: run if C43 supports H-field-dependent, else keep it as the diversity guard for the first screen under a judge that passes fidelity. Descriptor: copy-weighted overlap of copy-limited cards (all but basic Energy); clusters by greedy founders in score order at link 0.5, recomputed each iteration. Cap: 0.5 of the population (49 decks), hard: --select refuses a candidate that would move its deck into a cluster at or over the cap. Turnover: over-cap clusters lose their excess first, unprotected, replaced by mutants of the best quarter of under-cap clusters (MUTANT_SHARE 1); at the fork the excess (24 decks) is replaced the same way. Fork 479, --reseed 2, scr-t60gate479's flags with this cap in place of --type-cap 0.5; 20 iterations; control scr-t60gate479.

predictions.predicted: by 499 >= 30 non-walls in the boundary band (overlap 0.35-0.5 to the wall centroid; 13 of 26 at 479, 7-20 under the control over 484-498), non-wall mean overlap >= 0.43 (0.36 at 479), refused moves >= 5 an iteration and rising, <= 1 non-wall cluster of 10+ decks

band <= 20 decks, non-wall mean overlap <= 0.38, refused moves <= 2 an iteration and falling, >= 2 non-wall clusters of 10+ with mutual overlap < 0.35 whose best decks score within 0.05 of the walls against the 24 lists under pilot-v2 (evaluation only)

readout: Boundary band; non-wall overlap with the wall centroid; refused-move count (pressure on the cap); number of non-wall clusters and their cores. Evaluation: best non-walls vs the 24 lists under pilot-v2 and the run's pilot; top-12 distance only as a necessary-condition check. Baselines from scratchpad meta_lens/boundary.py.
noise_and_power: The band and overlap thresholds sit outside the control's whole 479-498 range (band 7-20, overlap 0.32-0.39); refused moves are a count with a natural zero. One run; a second seed only if the band ends at 21-29.
kill_rule: Stop at 489 if refused moves are >= 8 an iteration and the band holds >= 30 (H-convergent decided).
cost: About half a day of code (descriptor and clustering, refusal in pick(), turnover order); one slot for about 2 h; the descriptor already runs in seconds. C32 can pre-screen it.
distinct_from: H39 is the built cap: soft, at turnover only, deck_kinds descriptor, refuted as built; its verifier names a hard selection-time cap and a card-level descriptor as missing variants. Not a rerun of scr-typecap, scr-resetcap or scr-ctl479.
rules_check: A game-agnostic descriptor (copies of copy-limited cards; nonbasic cards in MTG), threshold fixed in advance at 0.5, never calibrated on the human lists; a population rule of the same kind as the existing type cap.
value: Decides whether a cheap population guard can hold diversity of substance: H-leak makes it the default guard and its descriptor replaces the logged type metric (which undercounts walls by 1.4-3.8x); H-convergent retires descriptor caps, so diversity must come from the judge or the head.
merged_from: meta: Hard selection-time type cap on a descriptor that sees the walls: label or substance?

reviews.reasons: There are no earlier reviews to keep. The closest family is H39 (N7, type cap). Its do-not-repeat list covers the soft cap at turnover only (--type-cap 0.5 --turnover-every 5, with or without the reset head or protection), scr-typecap, scr-resetcap and scr-ctl479, and 'a soft type cap with the Pokémon-overlap descriptor (deck_kinds)'. C44 changes two factors that were never varied, and H39's verifier lists both as genuinely untested: (1) enforcement at selection time, where pick() refuses a candidate that would move a deck into a cluster at or over the cap, whereas the built cap acts only at turnover and removes at most 15% every 5 iterations; (2) a card-level descriptor, copy-weighted overlap on copy-limited cards, in place of deck_kinds / pokemon_overlap. The code confirms the built cap acts only in the turnover block (rl/metagame.py lines 755-765) and that pick() (lines 683-697) has no type check. A grep of the progress log for 'hard cap', 'selection-time', 'copy-weighted' and 'refuse' finds no earlier run. The candidate is also distinct from H41's untested 'card-overlap novelty filter on proposals' (a bonus or filter, never run), from H40 (turnover was never isolated) and from H25 (the gate, which stays fixed here as in scr-t60gate479). The run reuses scr-t60gate479's flags, and that control is in H25's do-not-repeat list only as a control, so it is not rerun as a treatment. One caveat for attribution, not for repetition: the design also changes the turnover rule (MUTANT_SHARE 1 and no protection for the excess). That is a third factor changed at the same time, so a positive result could not be credited to the hard cap alone (see the feasibility notes).

The node and the readout match: a population or selection change is read by deck-cluster readouts, and the evaluation against the 24 lists is kept for evaluation only. The rivals are well posed. But several readout thresholds do not separate them as written. (a) The boundary band is compared in absolute counts with a control whose denominator differs. The control has about 19-26 non-walls, with a band of 7-20, so up to about 0.77 of its non-walls sit in the band. The treatment has about 50 non-walls after the fork. H-convergent's '>= 30' (0.6 of non-walls) is therefore less extreme than the control's own range, and H-leak's '<= 20' (0.4) lies inside it. The claim that the thresholds 'sit outside the control's whole range' is false once the counts are normalised. (b) The fork builds the band itself. The 24 replacements are 10-card mutants of the best quarter of non-walls, which are probably the most wall-like non-walls, so many mutants land at overlap 0.35-0.5 at iteration 480 by construction. Without a band and overlap baseline measured at 480 after the replacement, both the predictions and the kill rule can fire on this artifact. (c) Hugging the boundary is the expected behaviour of any constrained hill-climb whose fitness gradient points at the walls. Both rivals accept that the walls are fitter under this judge (wall #829 beats all 24 lists), so the band mostly measures the gradient, not label versus substance. Cores need a substance readout: the non-walls' share of the wall-core cards (Chansey, Snorlax, Energy Removal, healing special Energy) and their Energy count. (d) The refused-move thresholds are not calibrated against the base rate. Under the gate (--candidates 1 --select-z 1.0), scr-t60gate479 moves 13-30 decks an iteration in all (log.jsonl), and only about 0.6 non-walls an iteration crossed into the wall cluster (11 over 19 iterations). With about 50 non-walls that suggests about 1-2 crossings an iteration, so H-convergent's '>= 5 and rising' and the kill rule's '>= 8' are probably unreachable under either rival, and H-leak's '<= 2' is predicted by both. (e) 'Refused' is ambiguous. The design must count only moves across clusters; a wall deck moving within the wall cluster at the cap must not count. (f) The evaluation rule 'best non-walls within 0.05 of the walls under pilot-v2' is a weak bar: pilot-v2 rates the walls only 0.23-0.26 against the 24 lists. It should be read under both pilots against a fixed absolute bar, not only relative to the walls. (g) Cap membership is overlap to a founder, while the readout uses overlap to the 479 centroid (boundary.py); the two can disagree near 0.5. (h) The kill rule decides H-convergent at 489 but cannot decide H-leak, because 'falling' needs a longer window. That asymmetry is a short-horizon bias. One run, with a second seed only for a band of 21-29, is acceptable if the thresholds are first rescaled to fractions with an A/A band; distance RMS 2.0-4.8 is only a side check here.
required_changes: Express the band and non-wall overlap as fractions of non-walls, and set both rivals' thresholds outside the control's normalised 479-498 range (control band fraction up to ~0.77), or compare against a matched control that has the same fork replacement but the soft cap.

Measure the band, mean overlap and cluster count at iteration 480, right after the 24-deck fork replacement, and state the predictions as changes from that baseline, so the mutants' construction cannot decide the outcome.

Calibrate the refused-move thresholds on the control's base rate of non-wall moves into the wall cluster (about 0.6 an iteration in scr-t60gate479, so about 1-2 with 50 non-walls; compute it with lineage.py on every snapshot). Count only moves across clusters, and rescale the kill rule to match.

Add a substance readout for the non-wall clusters: their share of wall-core cards and their Energy and Trainer counts against the 479 non-walls. 'Walls-lite' should mean the core arrives, not only overlap near 0.5.
Replace 'within 0.05 of the walls under pilot-v2' with an absolute score against the 24 lists under both pilot-v2 and the run's pilot, plus distance to the human medians (evaluation only).
Make the kill rule symmetric: decide either rival only after a minimum of 15 iterations, or add an early-stop condition for H-leak as well.

reviews.reasons: Rules: compliant. The descriptor is game-agnostic: copies of copy-limited cards, which in MTG would be nonbasic cards. The 0.5 cap and link are fixed in advance. Human lists appear only in the evaluation. The rule is a population rule of the same kind as the existing --type-cap. It is not learned, but it is no more hand-built than the cap already adopted, and it is simple. Code: feasible at about the stated cost. pick() (rl/metagame.py lines 683-697) takes the list of held candidates, which is [self, one candidate] under --candidates 1. A refusal means computing clusters once an iteration (greedy founders in score order over 99 decks, 99x~50 overlaps, milliseconds) and dropping a candidate whose cluster is at or over the cap and differs from the deck's own. The turnover block (lines 754-777) already has the cap's 'worst of the big type first' ordering and the 'mutants from other types' best quarter' logic, so the new descriptor drops in in place of deck_kinds. The fork-time replacement of 24 decks needs a small new step after the fork loads. Gaps the design leaves out: (1) turnover entrants and fork mutants must also face the cap, since a 10-card mutant of a boundary deck can land in the wall cluster, and the design does not say whether they are refused or redrawn; (2) recomputing founders each iteration can move decks between clusters without any move, so the wall cluster can exceed the cap between turnovers; the design should state how that excess is handled (left until the next turnover?) and log it; (3) MUTANT_SHARE 1 and removing protection from the excess are changes beyond the cap; to keep attribution to the hard cap, keep the control's turnover mix (MUTANT_SHARE 0.25, wide entrants, protect 20) for ordinary turnover and apply MUTANT_SHARE 1 only to the excess, or name it as a factor; (4) the descriptor and boundary scripts cited as 'scratchpad meta_lens' actually live in another session's scratchpad (C:/Users/evanc/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-evanc-Desktop-333/9afecfab-fdea-4a82-8aad-02daab001fd1/scratchpad/meta_lens/descriptor.py and boundary.py) and must be moved into the repo (e.g. rl/metagame.py or notes/scripts) with the same wover definition used in training and in the readout. Budget: one screen slot (~2.7 GB RAM, ~3.5 GB GPU) for about 2 h (20 iterations at ~6 min), plus CPU-only pilot-v2 evaluation at the end; this fits the 3-screen limit. A realistic code estimate is half a day to a day once the fork-time replacement, refusal logging and cap handling for entrants are included. Being gated on C43 (a 3-head island league) means C44 may wait for C43's 20 iterations; plan the slot with that in mind.
required_changes: Specify that turnover entrants and the fork's 24 mutants are subject to the same cap (redraw or refuse), and log how many were redrawn.
Specify how a cluster that goes over the cap through founder recomputation (with no move) is handled between turnovers, and log it each iteration.

Keep the control's turnover mix (MUTANT_SHARE 0.25, wide entrants, protect 20) except for removing the over-cap excess, or declare MUTANT_SHARE 1 and unprotected removal as separate factors, so the hard selection-time cap is the only factor changed against scr-t60gate479.

Move descriptor.py and boundary.py from the other session's scratchpad into the repo, and use one shared wover implementation for the cap and the readout. Use either founder membership or 479-centroid overlap for both, or report the two side by side.
Budget half a day to a day of code including logging (refused moves across clusters, cap excess, entrant redraws), not half a day for the core logic alone.
